author: aniekanasuquookono-web
body:
## What & why

Follow-up to #669, which gated the slash commands and the natural-language link paths. Review of that PR found two more chat paths that write with no permission check, both reproduced against a real database as a Viewer:

- `/create-element ApplicationComponent ...` created an ArchiMate element.
- The decision detector that runs after every successful chat answer created a proposed architecture decision whenever the answer contained words such as "should" or "recommend". An ordinary Viewer question could create a decision record.

This PR is stacked on #669 (base is its branch) and reuses its `user_can_write` / `refuse_unless_can_write`. No new mechanism.

- Every mutating workbench command is gated before its first write: create element, generate viewpoint, generate SAD sections, generate governance pack, record decision, generate work packages, generate roadmap and plateaus, confirm artifact. The two handlers that write directly (`create-element`, `record-decision`) also gate themselves, so any caller is covered.
- Starting or advancing a greenfield or brownfield workbench workflow creates a workspace, so both are gated too.
- `create_automated_action` (bulk update, auto-tag, scheduled report, data remediation) is gated.
- A refusal returns the same permissions message as the agent path and records a `tool_refused` audit row (`via` is `workbench_command` or `automated_action`).
- The decision detector is gated by skipping the record when the acting user cannot write. The chat answer is unchanged and no audit row is written for the skip, so every Viewer answer containing "should" does not fill the audit log. It is not queued for approval: that would need the same new queued operation type as the deferred model-decided link work, and a decision proposed by the model is already created as `proposed`.
- The read-only readiness check is unchanged.

Not in this PR: queueing the model-decided capability link or the detector's decision through the approval queue.

## Tests

- `tests/test_ai_chat_write_gate.py` gains tests, real PostgreSQL: a Viewer is refused on each of the eight workbench commands with no element, decision or workspace artifact change and exactly one audit row; a Viewer cannot start a workflow or create an automated action; a Viewer's question and an explicit "record this decision" create no decision; an Architect is unaffected on create element, record decision and the automatic decision; the readiness check is not refused for a Viewer.
- 12 of the new tests fail without the change and pass with it.
- `test_multi_domain_chat_decision_writes_only_the_canonical_row` recorded a decision with no user; it now uses a user with write access.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests pass locally (`pytest -q`) and new behaviour has a test
- [x] No secrets, internal hostnames/IPs, or real customer data (CI gitleaks gate)
- [x] No `console.log` / native `alert()`·`confirm()` (use `Platform.toast` / `Platform.modal`)
- [x] No raw-string `db.session.execute("…")` (wrap in `db.text(...)`)
- [x] Icon-only buttons have `aria-label`; images have `alt`
- [x] Staged specific files (not `git add -A`)

- the rich catalog, bounds and 7,000-token output ceiling;

There are still two analyst calls per day. The edition guidance carries the opening contract from the PRD §5.1. The prompt's budget sentence no longer names a fixed 500 words; it is 10,994 bytes, under the 11,000 ceiling, so no OD-3 raise was needed yet.

|---|---|---|---|
| Oct 13 (38409951093) | 31,954 | 42,718 | 58,674 |
| Oct 14 CPI (38576783285) | 36,044 | 47,105 | 61,089 |

## Summary
- The builder image build on `main` keeps failing: `next build` is killed with exit 137 ("cannot allocate memory") during compile.
- The Turbopack compile peaks close to the runner's ~16GB, and `NODE_OPTIONS` cannot cap it because it is native code.

## Changes
- Add a 16GB swapfile before the Docker build, for the builder leg only. Other image legs are unchanged.
- The swapfile goes on the first disk-backed filesystem with room to spare (`/mnt`, else `/`), never on tmpfs, and is added next to the existing swap.
- If no disk has room or setup fails, the step only warns and the build runs as before.

author: ashesfall
body:
The patched pretransform in front of the SAME transformer audio autoencoder
folds runs of patch_size samples into the channel axis and unfolds them again.
Both directions were assembled in Java as a layer whose body was a reshape, a
permute of the last two axes, and a reshape -- composition hidden inside a
lambda.

Move that structure into engine/ml/src/main/resources/pdsl/audio/patch_transform.pdsl,
whose patch_encode and patch_decode layers show the fold and its inverse as
three commented data-flow stages built from the existing reshape and permute
builtins (no new primitive; the same permute-then-merging-reshape pattern
sequence_attention.pdsl's split_heads/merge_heads already use). PatchedPretransform.encode
and decode now only bind the batch, channel, length and patch arguments and
load the asset via a buildPatchLayer loader method, so there is one definition
of the structure and it lives in the asset. The encode length-validation stays
in Java. SAMEAutoEncoder is unchanged -- it still calls encode/decode.

Parity is pinned by the existing PatchedPretransformTest, which asserts the
fold's exact element placement and that decode inverts encode against explicit
index arithmetic (a reference independent of the old Java assembly); two new
test methods add an element-level decode pin and a multi-channel/multi-batch
round trip.

author: pocharlies
body:
Deja el OVERVIEW y la ficha como pide el registro de Paseo, antes de hacer el repo público y de fijar el commit en el registro. qa y security anotaron tres afirmaciones imprecisas al revisar #24; las contrasté con el código y las arreglo, y la guía del registro (README y REVIEW.md de `getpaseo/plugins`) aporta el resto.

## OVERVIEW
- **Qué se envía**: solo el texto de la conversación. `conversation()` (`shared/suggest.ts`) quita las llamadas a herramientas, sus resultados y el pensamiento antes de la llamada; el OVERVIEW decía «cada llamada reducida a una línea», que es el paso intermedio de `shared/transcript.ts`. Dicho también el tope (~400 000 caracteres, se pierden los más antiguos).
- **Silencio configurable**: la pantalla ofrece 30 s, 1, 2 o 5 min; el documento de ajustes admite de 15 a 600 s, la pantalla no.
- **Idioma**: la instrucción incorporada pide la sugerencia en castellano y la pantalla de ajustes está en castellano; el OVERVIEW lo dice y apunta a `prompt.txt` para cambiarlo.
- **Capturas**: el texto de la sugerencia en ellas es fijo (copia de prueba sin router, parcheada); el intercambio es real. Se dice debajo de las imágenes.
- **Reglas del registro**: la validación de publicación rechaza `paseo plugin add`, `npm install` y `npm i` en un overview (había uno), y la guía pide sin rayas largas. La sección «Retirement» pasa a «Known limits».

## Ficha
- `paseo-plugin.json`: `media` con `docs/media/pill.png` (miniatura) y `docs/media/prompt.png`, que es donde la guía manda declarar las capturas. Lo acepta el esquema del daemon 0.11.2 (probado con su `readPluginManifest`).
- `package.json`: `docs/media/` entra en `files` para que `deploy.sh` copie a la carpeta desplegada lo que el manifiesto declara (comprobado el copiado con el mismo fragmento de `deploy.sh`).

Sin tocar workflows ni código: riesgo normal.

## Pruebas
`npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (23) y `scripts/check-internal.sh origin/main..HEAD` en local.

author: superfamousguy
body:
## Summary

The black-cat-clapping tee came out looking nothing like the meme: a slim cat with human hands. Four causes:

1. The trend brief was written from Know Your Meme text only and described the cat wrong ("human hands"; the meme has paws).
2. The designer was forbidden to use any frame as a reference, and the spec rules said art must *not* resemble the source.
3. The prompt filled the gaps with invented traits.
4. The designer couldn't download or view its own results, so its review step never ran.

## Changes

- **meme-expert** saves reference stills to `trends/refs/`: it downloads the defining image, checks it, crops out any real person with `ffmpeg`, and records it in the brief's `references`. If only a video exists, it reports the URL so the main session can pull a frame with `/watch`.
- **trend-brief schema**: adds `references` (`path`, `source_url`, `shows`). Required for `emerging` and `peaking` briefs, or the notes say why there is none.
- **designer** uploads the still to Higgsfield as a pose and face reference. It downloads each result, compares it with the still, and regenerates up to three times. It won't design from a brief without a reference.
- **design-spec**: Higgsfield is the default, and hand-written SVG is a last resort when Higgsfield is out of credits or unreachable. Art must read as the meme but be redrawn, with no photo pixels, background, or people. Specs record the reference they used.
- **`.claude/hooks/shell-guard.mjs`**: limits each agent's Bash to exact command shapes. The designer can run two `curl` commands, and the meme-expert can run `curl`, an `ffmpeg` crop, and `rm`, all in fixed paths. Run `node .claude/hooks/shell-guard.mjs --self-test` to test it.
- **black-cat-clapping brief**: corrects the description and adds a user-supplied still, with the person cropped out.

## Test plan

- [x] `shell-guard.mjs --self-test` passes, covering chaining, substitution, path traversal, and wrong-agent cases.
- [ ] In a fresh session, confirm both agents get `Bash` and the new Higgsfield tools. Agent definitions load at session start.
- [ ] Have the designer regenerate `clapping-cat-bad-idea-tee` from the reference and review the output.
- [ ] Have the meme-expert refresh a brief and save a still.

Not included: the generated designs in `designs/`. The tee artwork was rejected and will be regenerated with this process.

author: bhouston
body:
Closes #8.

Adds the opt-in **Experimental power lobe and matched GGX controls** preset to fidelity, live and performance views. Existing renderer pins, default preset and 4096-sample path-traced references remain unchanged. The four new entries start unchecked/excluded from default batches; their preset, explicit renderer selection, live dropdown and explicit CLI arguments enable them.

| Method | Estimator | SSR filtering |
| --- | --- | --- |
| three-pr72-ggx-raw | Stock stochastic GGX control | None |
| three-pr72-ggx-recurrent | Same GGX control | Existing temporal/recurrent |
| three-pr72-power-raw | Biased power lobe / projected stepping | None |
| three-pr72-power-recurrent | Same power estimator | Existing temporal/recurrent |

All four use source pin `fe44dbcdb0cc6a9ffe119b17f6d1e9f305c5ce34` from three.js PR #72, full native trace resolution, one ray, 16-step budget, authored reach/thickness/intensity, clamp off, shared HDR environment and final non-jittered TRAA. The independent pin keeps this investigation separate from subsequent Hi-Z integration. Power reads reprojected previous opaque linear HDR; stock reads current opaque color. Both use the same opaque geometry and downstream transparent beauty. No denoiser algorithm changed. Caller-owned CPU equirectangular HDR textures are borrowed without disposal; unsupported borrowed maps are rejected explicitly. A shared CPU-readable HDR environment bake prevents stock GGX's unsupported-PMREM black-miss behavior. The existing viewer default stays three-dev.

**48 physical-GPU captures** cover all 12 scenes at native dimensions, seed 1 and 64 completed frames. Existing reference images were reused without modification. Provenance records identify NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti, WebGPU, fallback=false, zero shader-validation errors, exact source pin, capture commit, resolution and settings.

| Comparison | Mean full-frame RGB8 PSNR change |
| --- | ---: |
| Power raw minus matched GGX raw | -1.5922 dB |
| Power recurrent minus matched GGX recurrent | -1.5079 dB |
| Existing recurrent filter minus raw, GGX fixed | +0.1907 dB |
| Existing recurrent filter minus raw, power fixed | +0.2750 dB |

These one-seed static observations support keeping the methods experimental. Restricted sampling and missing BRDF/PDF correction deliberately bias energy/lobe shape. Native GGX weights, edge fade, distance scaling, thickness acceptance and step distribution differ. Power shows structured bands/speckles; filtering smooths them and softens detail. Cornell full-frame errors also include missing diffuse indirect lighting with SSGI disabled. No motion-quality or throughput superiority claim is made. The GGX control versus older three-dev includes runtime/composition changes and is not a matched estimator comparison.

[Definitions and reproduction](https://github.com/bhouston/three-ssr-fidelity/blob/ee3be0cc4f9e0b53fd8ae751c6550ed9c0829d06/docs/SSR-EXPERIMENTS.md) · [Per-scene report](https://github.com/bhouston/three-ssr-fidelity/blob/ee3be0cc4f9e0b53fd8ae751c6550ed9c0829d06/docs/SSR-EXPERIMENT-RESULTS.md) · [Scores](https://github.com/bhouston/three-ssr-fidelity/blob/ee3be0cc4f9e0b53fd8ae751c6550ed9c0829d06/docs/data/SSR-EXPERIMENTS.json) · [Capture provenance](https://github.com/bhouston/three-ssr-fidelity/blob/ee3be0cc4f9e0b53fd8ae751c6550ed9c0829d06/docs/data/SSR-EXPERIMENTS-CAPTURES.json)

Columns: reference, GGX raw, GGX recurrent, power raw, power recurrent.

![Roughness comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhouston/three-ssr-fidelity/ee3be0cc4f9e0b53fd8ae751c6550ed9c0829d06/docs/images/power-lobe-roughness.png)

![Metal-hit comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhouston/three-ssr-fidelity/ee3be0cc4f9e0b53fd8ae751c6550ed9c0829d06/docs/images/power-lobe-metal-hit.png)

![Cornell mirror comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhouston/three-ssr-fidelity/ee3be0cc4f9e0b53fd8ae751c6550ed9c0829d06/docs/images/power-lobe-cornell-mirror.png)

Validation: `pnpm build`, `pnpm tsc`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test --coverage --maxWorkers=4` (242/242), image processing (264 comparisons, zero failures), `pnpm site:build` and hardware unified-site smoke pass. The latter exercises fidelity detail, live selection/reset/resize, physical-GPU rendering/capture and GPU-completed benchmark CLI contracts. Lint retains unrelated existing warnings. The initial unrestricted test run timed out in the unchanged CLI process-priority test on this shared machine; the full four-worker rerun passed. Node 26 and pinned pnpm 11.0.8 were used.

Dependency audit reports seven existing advisories (two critical, four high, one moderate) in unchanged simple-git/extract-zip dependency paths. Lockfile changes only add runtime/type aliases; no dependency versions changed. No generated Three.js build outputs are included. Merge with a merge commit only after green checks, as requested by the maintainer.

Final environment validation uses an asymmetric analytic HDR scene: six cardinal directions and one oblique direction agree after the cube/equirectangular/readback/sampler round trip (max RGB error 0.00586, including values above one). This caught and corrected the initial bake yaw/row convention before merge; all 48 captures and scores above were regenerated. Reproduce with `node scripts/verify-ssr-environment.mjs`; the hardware workflow now includes it.

author: jumiknows
body:
Refs #10

## Problem

The team has a broad space-data idea but needs one deliverable product and an actionable implementation queue for Grok Bot and Cursor. Generic maps, mine prediction, and unsupported fire probabilities would spread the hackathon effort across unrelated problems.

## Approach

Define EmberReady as accessible community wildfire awareness: real NASA observations, synchronized historical replay, deterministic place context, and source-grounded Grok Voice. Add the product brief, architecture, shared contracts, checked source references, demo script, honest sponsor-evidence record, Cursor project rule, and Grok handoff. Create 16 implementation tickets under epic #10 and refine the existing scope, scaffold, and release tickets.

## Verification

- Repository checks passed for 37 tracked files.
- All 17 existing tooling regression tests passed.
- Staged diff whitespace check passed.
- Checked the implementation dependency graph for cycles and unresolved ticket references.
- Verified current primary NASA, xAI, NWS, Census, Cursor, and implementation documentation.

## Risks and limitations

This is a planning and handoff change. No application, model, authenticated provider integration, user study, or deployment is claimed. The supplied challenge requires actual implementation in Cursor. Grok Bot is not automatically launched or assigned by these issues. The data and Voice access tasks must run before the demo can be considered viable.

body:

author: pelikhan
body:
## Summary

Add **18 AST-only linters**, an extensible rule registry, and reusable source/sink/filter secret-taint analysis. Rules consume parsed AW or Actions ASTs; file discovery and workflow parsing belong to the CLI adapter. No rule recompiles a workflow, fabricates an execution graph, retrieves secret values, or executes analyzed programs.

- Accept AW `.md`, native Actions `.yml`/`.yaml`, and compiled `.lock.yml` inputs without compilation. AW-only checks inspect authored execution nodes and prompts and retain unavailable generated-flow coverage. Directory scans avoid duplicate lock/source pairs; Markdown never reaches external actionlint.
- Declare supported AST targets, stable IDs, default severities, deterministic value-free JSON diagnostics, cancellation, and independent failure handling. `gh aw lint` runs registered checks alongside actionlint on YAML; `--rules` selects AST-only operation. Existing extension rules default to Actions-only targets.
- Track symbolic flows through expressions, environments, step/job outputs, Bash/sh, files, AW prompts, and explicitly configured JavaScript ASTs. Fix the Gemini inventory API key-in-URL exposure using an authentication header.
- Hide only secret-leak coverage warnings in normal text/JSON output; `lint --debug` restores them. Internal AST diagnostics, actual errors, analysis failures, and other rules' warnings remain intact. Shape-preserving JavaScript object rest avoids contaminating public timeout fields with nested credential environment members while retaining real secret flows and shallow aliases.
- Require positive/negative contracts for every registered linter and supported AST: **86 functional cases** cover strict/non-strict behavior, exact diagnostics, repeatability, and AST immutability.
- Add per-rule performance markers and execution-trace regions, **100 benchmark cases / 300 baseline samples**, and ordinary-test runtime/allocation-growth guards.
- Update CLI/API documentation, threat-spec mappings through version **1.0.59**, and the major changeset. Merge main's test fixes and preserve the concurrent correction for optional malformed AW lock companions.

## Linters

| Linter | AST inputs | Threat mapping | Severity | Observable check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `secret-leak` | AW, Actions | CTR-017 subset | Error; internal coverage warnings visible with `--debug` | Symbolic secrets reaching modeled logs, summaries, outputs, network fields, publication inputs, cache keys, or artifacts. AW-only input retains missing generated-flow warnings. JavaScript is opt-in. |
| `action-pin` | AW, Actions | CTR-002 subset | Strict policy | Immutable remote action, Docker action, and reusable-workflow references. Local references are exempt; authored references are not resolved by compilation. |
| `template-injection` | AW, Actions | CTR-006 subset | Error | Known attacker-controlled expressions interpolated into executable run text, including environment aliases. Quoted shell-variable consumption is not direct interpolation. |
| `workflow-run-scope` | AW, Actions | CTR-021 subset | Error / strict policy | Required upstream workflow selection and positive branch scope, excluding empty, wildcard-only, and negated-only filters. Does not prove complete glob-language trust. |
| `job-timeout` | AW, Actions | CTR-026 subset | Error | Explicit workflow/job timeouts are literal positive integers. Omission is allowed; compiler defaults are not invented. |
| `permission-scope` | AW, Actions | CTR-001 subset | Error / strict policy | Blanket `write-all` declarations and invalid OIDC `id-token: read`. Scoped writes and OIDC issuance are not automatically violations. |
| `version-check` | AW | CTR-018 | Strict policy | Authored configuration explicitly disables `check-for-updates`. |
| `conditional-import` | AW | CTR-020 | Error | Configuration import entries contain `if`, including false/null values. Runtime prompt conditionals are unaffected. |
| `private-to-public` | AW | CTR-031 | Strict policy | GitHub-tool configuration opts out of private-to-public protection, globally or for selected servers. |
| `install-scripts` | AW | CTR-014 | Strict policy | Node runtime configuration enables dependency install hooks. Does not infer arbitrary install commands or imported policy. |
| `allowed-labels` | AW | CTR-015 | Error | Bare `*` in creation/discussion-update label allowlists. Narrow patterns and literal required-label names remain valid. |
| `network-scope` | AW | CTR-011 subset | Strict policy | Bare wildcard network allowances, including alongside `defaults`. Domain wildcards remain valid; omission is not missing-firewall evidence. |
| `push-target` | AW | CTR-012 subset | Warning | Wildcard PR-branch pushes lack authored title/label constraints. Respects legacy aliases and defers absent constraints when imports may supply them. |
| `tool-scope` | AW | CTR-003 subset | Strict policy | Shell refusal conflicts with CLI/gh proxies, minimum-integrity bypass lacks explicit shell intent, or cache memory uses repository-wide scope. Missing prerequisites defer for unresolved imports. |
| `sandbox-config` | AW | CTR-004 subset | Strict policy | Explicit agent sandbox disablement or nonempty internal agent/MCP command, environment, argument, image, or version overrides. Does not prove effective sandbox enforcement. |
| `image-argument` | AW, Actions | CTR-013 subset | Error | Option-prefixed job/service or authored MCP container image operands. No registry queries, inferred package operands, or guessed dynamic image values. |
| `checkout-mode` | AW | CTR-033 subset | Error | Explicit boolean expansion mode, literal list/single-mode conflicts, multi-mode path/allowlist prerequisites, bare allowlist wildcards, and forbidden LFS/submodule/current/wiki options. Runtime selector trust and visibility remain separate. |
| `fork-association` | AW | CTR-034 subset | Error | Explicit fork association admission uses GitHub's uppercase enum. Empty association lists and repository wildcard patterns are valid; generated admission guards are not reconstructed. |

**Strict policy:** error for authored strict AW (the default), warning for explicit non-strict AW, and warning for native Actions where applicable. Missing workflow selection and invalid OIDC reads are always errors; wildcard push-target findings remain warnings. AW-only checks accept a standalone AW AST or a `.lock.yml` companion and skip native Actions without source evidence. CLI/repository overrides and imported configurations are not reconstructed. These are observable subsets, not assertions of full CTR conformance.

## Current analysis results

Both completed scans cover **all 18 rules across 344 compiled workflows and companion sources** on published tree `242e891bfd5c8825b039ff8d1b7e613b67fe06f7`:

| Configuration | Errors | Internal/debug coverage warnings |
|---|---:|---:|
| Default, without native JavaScript configuration | **0** | **472** |
| Native JavaScript compiler and source/runtime mappings enabled | **0** | **633,973** |

Normal default CLI JSON is `[]`. Coverage warnings are normally hidden and restored with `--debug`; the underlying AST diagnostics remain available. The configured run completed all 344 runners and **6,192 rule checks**, with zero runner failures and zero compiler-unavailable/incompatible diagnostics. The other 17 linters report no findings in either scan.

Default coverage gaps are 341 unavailable-JavaScript boundaries, seven other external-command boundaries and 124 unsupported/indeterminate shell boundaries. Earlier source-matched shell/file refinements reduced 1,605 warnings to 472; uninspected helpers were not allowlisted.

The new configured total supersedes the earlier child-tree count of 630,179 after main's runtime/source changes. The 14 historical timeout findings were corrected by preserving JavaScript object-rest member provenance, not by suppressing error diagnostics. author: jeswr
body:
## Summary

Before: 7 ontologies in the fuzz corpora answered `Unknown(Unconfirmed)` although HermiT finds them consistent. In each, a root such as `o` is joined to the elements of an infinite chain, and an at-most restriction applies at every node behind a self-loop, like `∃T.Self ⊑ ≤1 R`. `o` has no `T`-loop. But the copy check behind model confirmation (`counts_copies`) looked only at a clause's concept body, so it treated that at-most as counting the chain's copies at `o` and could not confirm the model.

After: `counts_copies` also skips a clause whose self-loop body fails at the root, as `ni_clause` already does. All 7 are decided and agree with HermiT. `Unconfirmed` on the corpora goes from 7 to 0.

How: a root's self-loops are final in a complete, clash-free graph, and the unravelling keeps roots as they are. So a clause needing `T(x, x)` never applies at a root without the loop, however many copies of its neighbours the model has. The new test `an_at_most_behind_a_missing_self_loop_counts_no_copies` is one of the 7 files. It fails on main and passes here.

Measured against HermiT on the fuzz corpora (about 161k ontologies), compared with main at #7152:
- 7 more files decided, all agreeing with HermiT.
- No regressions, no changed answers, no new disagreement.

How it was checked (local runs):
- `cargo test -p sparq-reason-dl --release --test owl2dl_reasoner an_at_most_behind_a_missing_self_loop_counts_no_copies` fails with `crates/sparq-reason-dl/src` at main and passes at this head.
- The corpora were run through a probe test (`check()` with `Budget::default()` on every `.ttl` in a directory) built from this head and from main, and the answers were diffed per file. They were also diffed against HermiT's (`hermit-oracle.jar` on the same directories).

Addresses #7031

author: jorgesolerrr
body:
The first test of a heavy web test file sometimes hit vitest's 5 s timeout when `bun run check:linux` ran on Jorge's laptop. This caps vitest at four workers.

## Cause

`vitest run` starts one worker per core, less one. The host is an i7-13700H with 6 P-cores, 8 E-cores and 20 threads, so it got 19 jsdom workers. The tests use the CPU the whole time; `apps/web/src` has no dynamic imports, so no module gets transformed during a test. Too many workers for the cores just made every test slower.

I timed the first `manifest-section` test in the check image:

| Workers | First test |
| --- | --- |
| file alone | 0.45 s |
| 4 | 0.87-0.91 s |
| 6 | 1.4-1.6 s |
| 10 (`50%`) | 2.0-3.1 s |
| 19 (default) | 2.0-2.6 s with the laptop cool, 4.8-5.3 s with it hot |

Of three default runs in a row, two failed on the timeout. With 4 to 19 workers the whole suite takes the same 25-29 s, because `onboarding.test.tsx` alone takes 10-18 s.

## Change

`apps/web/vite.config.ts` sets `maxWorkers: Math.min(4, Math.max(availableParallelism() - 1, 1))`. Below four cores vitest's default still applies, so CI's 4-vCPU `ubuntu-latest` runner keeps its 3 workers.

## Checks

`bun run check:linux` passed three runs in a row: 534 of 534 web tests, 26-32 s for the web half.

author: laubaumau
body:
Adds a way to take pages off the public site **without deleting anything**. Follows a full page check of sourcelibrary.org (17 Oct 2026) that found many old, unfinished or internal pages live and indexed. Decided with Laura: nothing is deleted, and hidden pages are visible to **admins only**.

## How it works
One list, `src/lib/page-status.ts`. Unlisted = live. A listed route keeps its file and URL:

| state | admin (session role `admin`/`superadmin`) | everyone else |
|---|---|---|
| `archived` | sees the page + an "Archived since …" bar | 307 to the entry's `sendTo` |
| `internal` | sees the page + an "Internal" bar | signed out → `/auth/signin?callbackUrl=…`; signed in → `/unauthorized` |
| `draft` | sees the page + a "Draft" bar | same as internal |

- **Gate in `src/proxy.ts`**, not the pages: the pages are ISR and a role check there needs `headers()` (dynamic rendering), and a `redirect()` in a streamed page commits a 200 first. `getToken()` runs only for listed paths. Redirect targets are paths built with `request.nextUrl.clone()`, so a partner subdomain is never redirected off itself (tenant-lockdown invariant 1).
- **`next.config.ts`**: listed paths get `CDN-Cache-Control: private, no-store` and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, appended last so they override the 24h Cloudflare rules (e.g. `/about/:path*`). Proxy redirects also send `no-store`.
- **Sitemap** drops listed pages (chunks 0 and 1). **robots.txt** disallows internal and draft; archived stay crawlable so engines follow the redirect.
- **`PageStatusBar`** in the root layout: client component, `usePathname` only, no `headers()`.
- **Why not an `_archived/` folder:** the knip cleanup (#4887) deleted the last one; unrouted code reads as dead. Listed pages keep compiling.

## Tests
`tests/unit/page-status.test.ts` (15): pattern matching (`:name`, `:name*`), every gate decision (incl. editor/tenant roles do NOT pass), same-host targets, robots output, and checks on the real list: archived needs a live `sendTo`; no listed page may be in the sitemap static list, `footer-nav.ts`/header/user menus, or `site-features.json`. Mutation-checked: marking `/about` internal fails the sitemap and menu checks; an archived page pointing at a hidden page fails the successor check.

`npx tsc --noEmit` and eslint clean. Unit suite: 8,434 pass; 3 fail locally on macOS only (`flock`, `/proc`: stale-worker-restart, safe-merge, archive-bulk-scratch-sweep), unrelated.

## Verification
The list ships **empty**, so this PR changes nothing for visitors. A demo build with three sample entries (`/roadmap` archived → `/about`, `/processing` internal, `/ideas` draft) is on `preview/page-status-demo` (never to be merged) for checking signed out, as a reader, and as an admin.

## Out of scope
- Putting real pages in the list: follow-up PRs (internal/draft first, then archived), each a list edit plus a Cloudflare purge of the affected URLs (noted in the file header).
- `/es/…` twins are not matched automatically; list them explicitly if needed.
- `scripts/workers/embed-site-pages.mjs` reads `site-features.json` directly; the test keeps hidden pages out of that file instead.

author: fb-elong
body:
Refs #2889. The first of the five traced shapes on #2889, under the owner decision of 2026-10-17: each gap becomes a registered compiler finding with an independently authored negative benchmark, as a targeted PR into `release/0.5.0`.

## The shape

A specification with row templates in which a column computed after row construction (the column phase) reads a key column declared after it, while at least one row template leaves that key to the column phase. A `rank` or `row_number` key is the common case: a window is never row-local (REQ-1260).

```yaml
keys: [STUDYID, USUBJID, PARAMCD, AVISITN]
columns:
  - {name: ABLFL, type: str, derivation: {flag: "AVISITN = 1"}}
  - name: AVISITN
    type: int
    derivation:
      rank: {method: dense, window: {group_by: [STUDYID, USUBJID], order_by: [ADT]}}
rows: [...]
```

On `release/0.5.0` the compiler admits this. `column_dependencies::analyze` exempts every key from the forward-reference rule. That exemption holds without row templates, where keys are derived before any other column (REQ-0074). With row templates, `Rows::bind` keeps the column-phase assignments in declaration order. The plan's second validation pass (`validate_direct_assignment`) then refuses the read as `PlanError::UnavailableColumn`. The hosts report that as `engine_rejected` (`result_projection`), and the prototype envelope as `("bind", "internal")`.

## The finding

`analyze` now exempts a later key only when the key is derived first: always without row templates, and with row templates only when every template derives the key in the row phase (the key has no column-phase declaration). Any other later key is treated like any other later column. The read fails as `forward_reference` under REQ-0071 ("A reference to a later declared column: fail and report both columns"), at the reading column's operation, with context `{column, dependency}`. This is the registered `ColumnForwardReference` cause, so the diagnostic registry does not change.

A key that every row template derives keeps its current behavior: it is admitted and builds, as the design table on #2840 specifies ("unless the key is row-phase in every template"). Suppose the key is left to the column phase in some template. The reading column is then computed in the column phase in that template too. Had the template derived the reading column in the row phase, the key would be promoted with it, because a default's own reads become defaults (REQ-1260). A key that cannot be promoted, such as a window, would already be refused there as a row dependency on a later-phase value (REQ-0069). So the new finding refuses no specification that the second pass admitted.

## Tests and fixtures

- `rust/crates/yamaa-core/tests/fixtures/column_dependencies.tsv` gains two row-template cases. A later column-phase key gives a forward reference. A later key that every template derives gives no finding.
- `benchmarks/negative-forward-key-reference`: ADaM ADVS built from wide vital signs by two row templates. `ABLFL` reads the dense-rank visit number `AVISITN`, a key declared after it. `expected/error.yaml` is written by hand from REQ-0071. With `AVISITN` listed first, as the How to fix section shows, the specification builds. On `release/0.5.0` this benchmark gives the internal error above.
  - Its empty child builds, because composition orders the child's columns by dependency (REQ-0643). The benchmark therefore carries the same permanent metamorphic exception as `negative-forward-reference`. `tools/tests/test_public_conformance.py` now pins both reviewed exceptions, not just the one.
  - `check` analyzes column order only for formulas in specifications without row templates. The case therefore joins `NOT_REPORTED_BY_CHECK` in the adapters suite, which grows to 23 entries.
- `docs/releases/0.5.0.md` gets a Language note. It needs no migration note: 0.4.0 already refused these specifications, though only with an internal error.

## Checks

All run on Linux x86_64 at this head:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo test --locked -p yamaa-core` | pass (1304 tests) |
| `cargo test --locked -p yamaa-adapters` (including `memory_resolver_benchmarks` and `check_matches_domain_on_validation_benchmarks`) | pass (1125 tests) |
| `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` | pass |
| `cargo fmt --all --check` | pass |
| `make check-lint` | pass |
| `make check-repository` | pass |
| `make docs-test docs` | pass |
| `make test-python`, after rebuilding the extension | pass (893 package and tools tests, plus the installed-host suites) |
| `make test-r` | `R CMD check` Status: OK |
| `python -m yamaa.style benchmarks/negative-forward-key-reference/` | 0 findings |

## Summary

Closes #1507

This PR moves `internal/org`'s store to `internal/org/postgres/`, so the domain package no longer imports `jackc/pgx` (ADR-0069, `stack-go.md` §1). It is the fourth of the ten conversions #1083 covers. It repeats PR #1503 (`deaaf5f072df154342111337ad2792fc8b292b8f`) and the pilot's decisions listed in #1101: package `postgres/`, `Store`/`New`, the aliased import `orgpg`, `queries.sql` and `db/` under the package, and `NewX` stamps kept in the domain. Like `user` (`c6cdb97c5b0d8c68af3b40c4fe350de4232cbf07`), the aggregates the `Store` interface names now carry exported fields named after the old accessors.

## Changes

- **Domain (`internal/org`)**: `Organization`, `Group`, `Project`, `Membership` and `Invitation` now have exported fields. Each takes its accessor's name: `Organization()` → `Organization`, `User()` → `User`, and so on. The accessors are removed. `Invitation.Accepted()` and `Invitation.Expired()` are behaviour, so they stay. `NewOrganization`, `NewGroup`, `NewProject`, `NewMembership` and `NewInvitation` stay in the domain.
- **`checkMemberOrg` → `CheckMemberOrg`**: the store calls this rule, which refuses a Group or Project member that another org owns. Exporting it keeps the rule in the domain and lets the moved store reach it. This visibility change is not in #1101's settled list; see Convention concerns.
- **Store (`internal/org/postgres`)**: `postgres.go` and the five `postgres_<concept>.go` files moved here with `git mv`. `PostgresStore` → `Store` and `NewPostgresStore` → `New`. Domain identifiers are now qualified `org.`, and the row converters fill the exported fields. No query, statement or error mapping changed.
- **sqlc**: `queries.sql` moved. `sqlc.yaml` now points at `internal/org/postgres/queries.sql` and outputs to `internal/org/postgres/db`. I deleted `db/` and regenerated it with `go tool sqlc generate`; the output matched the `git mv`'d files byte for byte.
- **Composition root (`internal/cli`)**: `org.NewPostgresStore(pool)` → `orgpg.New(pool)` in `authority.go`, `controller_proof.go`, `cutover_inventory.go`, `execution.go`, `machine.go`, `serve.go` and `standalone.go`. In files that no longer use `org` otherwise, the plain `org` import is dropped. `standalone_run.go` is not touched.
- **Callers (`internal/api`, `tests/integration`)**: accessor calls became field reads. The compiler located every call site, so only these aggregates' accessors changed. `tests/integration` now uses `orgpg.New` and `*orgpg.Store`. `grnsOf` in `org_store_test.go` was constrained by a `GRN()` method, which a field cannot satisfy. It now takes the three aggregates as a union and reads `GRN` through a type switch, so its call sites are unchanged.
- **Docs**: `domains.md` and `structure.md` now count four of ten converted and name the five domains left. `domains.md` §Store implementation status points the `org` row at `postgres/`. The `ls internal/*/postgres_*.go` sentence now names four packages. `organizations.md` no longer describes `org` as unconverted. Its target paths in #1507 do not list it, but it described the structure this change alters.
- `.mockery.yaml` is unchanged: no org interface's package path moved.

## Verification

Run on `2f85faba4485b174636cca00f93232da5c29bec9`, branched from `d447cb60f99a34e61832bccf617e2936b784bbd3`.

- `go list -deps github.com/garamsh/garam/internal/org | rg pgx` prints nothing, exit 1. Controls with the same command and `rg -c`: `internal/org/postgres` gives 14, `internal/agent` (not converted) gives 14, and `internal/machine` gives none.
- Pure move: `GARAM_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://unused go test -list '.*' ./internal/... ./tests/...` ran before and after, with timings stripped. The diff is one line: `internal/org/db [no test files]` became `internal/org/postgres [no test files]` and `internal/org/postgres/db [no test files]`. No test name changed. The dummy URL only gets past `tests/integration`'s `TestMain`; `-list` opens no connection.
- `make ci` exited 2 on all three runs, each time in `web-test` only. Every target before it passed on every run: `format`, `lint`, `test` (`internal/org`, `internal/api` and `internal/cli` ok), `build`, `check-gen` ("51 generated files, all owned by a generator config"), `check-toolchain`, `chart`, `web-format` and `web-lint`.
  - Each `web-test` failure was vitest's 5000 ms timeout or a `findBy` that gave up, and the failing set changed between runs: 1 test, then 3, then 5. The files included `new-agent-wizard`, `create-policy-form`, `document-panel` and `policy-editor`. The host's load average was 36 to 44 on 12 cores, from other workers.
  - Run on their own with `pnpm --dir web exec vitest run <the three files from the second run>`, they passed: 3 files, 12 tests.
  - `git diff --stat origin/dev -- web api proto` is empty.
  - The `web-ci` targets after `web-test` that the failure skipped, `make web-build web-check-gen`, exited 0.
  - So `make ci` has not passed end to end on this host. A run on a quieter host or in CI is what would settle `web-test`.
- `make db-up integration e2e` exited 0: `tests/integration` ok in 285.5 s, `tests/e2e` ok in 53.1 s. It ran on a separate rootless daemon with `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=garam-1507` and ports `GARAM_DB_PORT=25107`, `GARAM_OPENBAO_PORT=27107`, `GARAM_LOCAL_API_PORT=28107`, `GARAM_LOCAL_WEB_PORT=23107` and `GARAM_LOCAL_METRICS_PORT=29107`.
- Deliberate defect: in `rowToOrg` I swapped `CreatedAt` and `UpdatedAt`, the two `time.Time` fields. `go test -count=1 -run 'TestOrg' ./tests/integration` then failed `TestOrgStore_OrgGroupAndProjectSurrenderTheirTimestamps`. I reverted the swap; it was never committed.
- Not run: `make workload-integration`, `make standalone-e2e` and `make mutation`. This diff touches none of the paths they exercise.

## Conventions consulted

- `docs/convention/README.md`
- `docs/convention/stack-go.md` (§1)
- `docs/convention/git.md`
- `docs/convention/documentation.md` (§GitHub artifacts)
- `docs/convention/style.md`
- `docs/convention/simplicity.md`

## Defaults not taken

N/A. The change takes every default the pilot settled in #1101.

## Restructure rejected

The type switch in `grnsOf` is the one thing this change adds. The alternative was a key function argument, `grnsOf(items, func(o *org.Organization) grn.GRN { return o.GRN })`. That rewrites all nine call sites and adds a closure to each, against three switch arms in one helper. I rejected it.

## Convention concerns

`CheckMemberOrg` is a case #1101's settled decisions do not name: an unexported domain function the moved store calls. The other choice was to move it into `internal/org/postgres`, which would put a domain rule (ADR-0001's organization segment) in the persistence package. I exported it from the domain instead, on the same reasoning that keeps `NewX` stamps in the domain. No convention file is affected.

author: leopalatto20
body:
## Summary

On iOS, every list row's swipe only repeated an item already in its long-press menu. Rows now have a tap and the menu, as on Android. ADR 0005 records the rule.

```diff
 Routine row:   tap = start Workout,  menu = Edit / Duplicate / Delete
-               swipe = Edit
 Gym row:       tap = rename,         menu = Rename / Delete
-               swipe = Delete / Rename
 Exercise row:  tap = open,           menu = Edit / Hide / Delete
-               swipe = Hide
 Routine editor slot: swipe = Remove   (kept: it is the confirmation ADR 0004 relies on)
```

Routine rows still need `deleteDisabled` because `List.ForEach` always offers swipe-to-delete. Wrapping the row in a `Group` to carry it stops SwiftUI from calling `onMove`, so the modifier now goes on the row itself (the HStack in Edit mode, the ContextMenu otherwise).

## Evidence

Driven on the `crowbar-verify` simulator from a fresh install, using real taps:

- **Before:** swiping a Routine row left revealed "Edit"; Gym rows revealed "Delete"/"Rename"; Exercise rows revealed "Hide".
  **After:** a left swipe on each list's row reveals nothing (no new buttons in the accessibility tree). Long-press opens the menu each time, and its actions work: Edit opens the Routine editor, Duplicate adds `Push Day copy`, Rename opens "Rename Gym", Hide sets `exercise.hidden = 1`.
- **Reorder regression check:** with the `Group` wrapper, dragging "Pull Day" above "Push Day" left `routine.position` unchanged, while the same drag on `main` reordered it. With the final code it reorders (`Push Day 0, Pull Day 1` after dragging Push Day up). Edit mode shows only reorder handles, no delete controls.
- Tapping a Routine row still starts a Workout (Gym prompt, then Ledger).
- `bun run check`, `bun run check-types`, `bun test` (389 pass).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Reverting brings the swipes back. No data or schema change.

**Blast Radius:** gestures

iOS only. Anyone used to swiping now has to long-press. Routine drag reordering is the fragile part and was rechecked on the simulator.

Preço no servidor, inativos/publicação futura, estoque, duplicidade, erro de rede, estado do carrinho, frete, idempotência, cancelamento, concorrência e histórico — verificados e cobertos por teste (tabela no doc). Novos testes SQL: histórico no cancelamento, transições inválidas, frete negativo/fora de pedido aberto, snapshot de preço, falta em vários itens sem baixa parcial, FK/CHECK/imutabilidade.

- ⚠️ A correção da Edge Function está no repositório mas **só entra em produção no próximo deploy da função** (não executado).

author: ajisaacs
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes completion publication crashing when its response is an `ActiveSessionRefusal`. A refused turn can settle in storage without delivering a `message.complete` event to its viewer, leaving the UI apparently waiting for the turn to finish. Admission safeguards remain unchanged.

Production path: `gateway/run_inbound.py` returns a refusal from `try_acquire_active_session()`; `gateway/session_ingress.py::execute_admission()` returns it to `gateway/session_authority.py::_drain()`, which passes it into `settle_with_retry()`. `gateway/session_settlement_recovery.py::completion_payload()` puts that response into the completion payload (line 57), before `gateway/session_events.py::SessionEvents.publish()` attempts the failing copy (line 44).

`completion_payload()` puts the response in both `text` and `content`. `SessionEvents.publish()` deep-copies that payload at `gateway/session_events.py:44`. The refusal is a string subclass whose `__new__` requires both `message` and `reason`; inherited string reconstruction supplies only the message. Publication raises:

```text
TypeError: ActiveSessionRefusal.__new__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'reason'
```

Add `__getnewargs_ex__` on the class so Python's reconstruction protocol supplies both arguments. This preserves the string value and machine-readable refusal reason for shallow copy, deep copy and pickle, rather than stripping the reason or special-casing one publication call site. The extended hook also avoids overriding `str.__getnewargs__` with an incompatible tuple return type.

The class's original intent (commit `a5f0fbb26235f8517b153cf26b7db2e24ddc476c`) is preserved: capacity, existing ownership and unavailable coordination remain distinct reasons; uncertainty still fails closed.

## Related Issue

No dedicated issue linked. The regression tests reproduce the missing-`reason` TypeError on tested base `e6cf2a9b1e8f98d40408b09a9a55993c8459b4b4`, including through the real `completion_payload()` → `SessionEvents.publish()` path. This is a unit-level reproduction, not a live-gateway reproduction.

On October 17, 2026, the branch was rebased onto refreshed upstream `main` at `ccc695635094d7615373db267b77f894d978b1a0`. That base still lacks the reconstruction hook. All-state issue/PR searches for `ActiveSessionRefusal` and `deepcopy refusal` were repeated; no direct reconstruction-fix duplicate was identified among the returned results.

Duplicate searches included `ActiveSessionRefusal`, `deepcopy refusal`, `session completion capacity`, and these all-state PR queries:

- `repo:NousResearch/hermes-agent is:pr "ActiveSessionRefusal" "deepcopy"` — no matches.
- `repo:NousResearch/hermes-agent is:pr "ActiveSessionRefusal" "copy"` — no matches.
- `repo:NousResearch/hermes-agent is:pr "session" "deepcopy" "refusal"` — related results, no direct reconstruction fix identified. #127801 concerns authorization-reaction outcomes, not this class or crash.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Security fix
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Tests only
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] New skill

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/active_sessions.py`: four-line reconstruction hook on `ActiveSessionRefusal`.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_active_session_refusal_copy.py`: message, class and reason preservation across copy/deepcopy/pickle for all three refusal reasons.
- `tests/gateway/test_active_session_refusal_completion.py`: real completion-payload construction, publication to an observer and bounded replay for all refusal reasons plus an ordinary successful response.

No cap changes, slot-leak repair, admission-policy changes, deployment, service restarts or dependency-manifest changes.

## How to Test

Provision an independent test environment using the checkout's prepared Python, per CONTRIBUTING.md:

```bash
python -m pm.build_env --source . --out /absolute/fresh/refusal-copy-venv --group dev --group test
export HERMES_PYTHON=/absolute/fresh/refusal-copy-venv/bin/python
export HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0
scripts/run_tests.sh \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_active_session_refusal_copy.py \
  tests/gateway/test_active_session_refusal_completion.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_active_sessions.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_active_session_exclusivity.py \
  tests/tools/test_bot_mode_refusal_contract.py \
  tests/gateway/test_session_event_observer_isolation.py \
  tests/gateway/test_local_viewer_events_turn.py \
  tests/gateway/test_admission_results.py -j 2
"$HERMES_PYTHON" scripts/check --base upstream/main
```

Verified on Linux x86_64, Python 3.14.7, in an isolated PM-built test environment:

- RED: the two new test files against unmodified upstream production code: **12 failed, 1 passed**. Nine reconstruction cases and three completion-publication cases fail with the exact missing-`reason` TypeError; the ordinary-completion control passes.
- Refreshed GREEN after rebasing onto `ccc695635094`, selected eight-file run: **76 passed, 0 failed**, retries disabled. Includes all 13 new cases plus existing admission, ownership/capacity/fail-closed registry, refusal-consumer, event isolation and completion tests.
- Refreshed lint/code health: **12 checks passed**, 0 blocking and 0 advisory findings.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

The full suite, native Windows/macOS execution, model calls and live-gateway deployment were not run. CI has not been dispatched.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide and applicable repository instructions.
- [x] Commit follows Conventional Commits.
- [x] Searched existing issues/PRs and current source/history for duplicates and design intent.
- [x] Only related changes are included.
- [ ] Full test suite passes — not run; selected coverage is recorded above using the canonical runner, not bare pytest.
- [x] `python scripts/check --base upstream/main` passes.
- [x] Regression tests added and proven red on upstream production code.
- [x] Tested on Linux x86_64 / Python 3.14.7.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Reconstruction hook has a docstring; no user-facing documentation change required.
- [x] Config examples: N/A (no config changes).
- [x] Architecture/workflow docs: N/A.
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered: stdlib reconstruction only; native Windows/macOS not exercised.
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas: N/A.

## Risk and Review

The change is class-local and does not weaken admission checks or drop `.reason`. JSON replay retains the existing plain-string wire representation; the test verifies content parity, not a new wire-level reason field. Pickle is exercised only on a locally constructed fixture; no runtime deserialization path is added.

Independent read-only review by Claude Code found no code defects. Its required submission-text findings have been addressed, and upstream freshness, duplicate searches, targeted tests and lint were refreshed afterward. The reviewer inspected existing test evidence but did not run tests itself. No unrelated formatting, secrets, shell execution or external I/O were added.

AI assistance: This patch and its regression tests were prepared with Hermes Agent and independently reviewed using Claude Code.

author: jgaethle10
body:
## EverMaps: build the replacement on Evercraft-owned Forge

**Directive:** No additional legacy-platform spending, builds, connectors, or source-export dependency. This PR implements an independently owned EverMaps foundation from existing first-party Forge infrastructure and permitted public geographic data.

### Working code on this review branch
- `public/evermaps/index.html`, `app.js`, `style.css`: a responsive independent EverMaps map page at **/evermaps/**. Real OpenStreetMap raster cartography with attribution, mouse/touch pan, zoom, regional incident clustering, accessible incident selection, official source timestamps and an explicit preview/safety boundary.
- `systemia/evermaps/incident-source.mjs`: source-qualified NIFC WFIGS public wildfire reports with region-limited request, timestamp and out-status checks, bounded results, single-flight TTL and fail-closed source outages.
- `systemia/evermaps/http.mjs`: **Forge-owned same-origin** GET `/api/evermaps/incidents/pnw` and `/api/evermaps/source-health`, registered in the existing `server.ts` with rate limiting.
- `Dockerfile`: explicit production-runtime copy of EverMaps source adapter.
- `scripts/verify-evermaps-owned-release.mjs`: fails the build if the production `dist/evermaps/` HTML/JS/CSS are missing, too small, refer to the legacy host, or don't link the owned API.
- Dedicated Node tests for source/HTTP and owned web surface, plus frontend script syntax validation, tied into the existing Forge `npm run check`.
- Migration inventory and slice receipt under `systemia/migrations/base44-exit/`. Historical reference only, **not a build dependency**. A full legacy source export is NOT a prerequisite for proceeding.

### Non-negotiable truth and release gates
The map plots **reported incident records**, not active flames, containment certification, burn perimeters, evacuation directions or trail access. NIFC current records can be stale and no reported records does not prove no fires. This is a noindex internal preview. OSM raster tiles are public third-party cartography; approved production scale needs its own tile-service policy.

The public legacy domain has **not** been changed. The owned frontend is a replacement foundation, not the old app repackaged and not the full 3D/Quest/Rewards experience.

### Current status
Draft PR, no merge or deployment. CI must pass full Forge source tests, build-asset verification, Docker smoke, and Systemia release policy. After that, deploy to authorized Evercraft-owned Yard capacity, verify the real HTTPS `/evermaps/` page on desktop/iPhone and rollback, then incrementally enable owned World/VR and additional source layers. **No further legacy builder involvement needed.**

Do not mark the new site live until route and recipient-browser evidence exists.

### Verified CI receipt, October 18 2026
At reviewed head `1efe202d8d5d67f8c6a552663116a04ebe220e39`, **Forge checks**, **World Engine**, and **Base44 exit and KAIDANCE proof** have all completed successfully. Forge checks passed TypeScript/unit/build validation, production Docker packaging, and existing runtime health/discovery smoke tests. The owned EverMaps static assets were required by the production build verifier. **The smoke test did not independently open `/evermaps/` in a browser or prove the new source endpoint at a public Evercraft URL.** This PR remains draft pending owned Yard staging and recipient-browser route verification.

author: sakaeri
body:
## 概要
変更は4つのコミットに分けています。

### 1. 業務報告の修正・差し戻しの改善／募集操作の権限チェック
- **権限の穴を修正**：募集の人数変更・削除・公開募集への切り替え・下書き保存で、「自社の募集か」をサーバー側で確認していませんでした。4つとも確認を追加しました
- **ダッシュボード**：業務報告のポップアップに「時間を直して確認してもらう」を追加しました。時間の入力欄は共通の部品（`WorkReportCorrectionForm`）にまとめました
- **ボタン名の変更**：「差し戻す」→「スタッフに直してもらう」、「修正して差し戻す」→「時間を直して確認してもらう」
- **スタッフ側に「内容が違う」ボタン**：押すと差し戻しの状態に戻り、スタッフが自分で直して出し直せます
- 会社側の時間修正は、提出済み・未承認の報告だけに限定しました

### 2. シフト外の勤務の報告
- スタッフのタイムカード画面に「＋シフト外の勤務を報告する」を追加しました。勤務先は自社か、本人が配属されている依頼主です
- 提出すると裏でシフトを作り（`createdVia=STAFF_REPORT`）、通常のシフトの業務報告と同じ流れ（承認先・給与・請求）に乗せます
- 同じ時間帯にすでにシフトがある場合や、未来の日付は出せません
- 承認待ちの一覧とダッシュボードに「シフト外」の印を付けました

### 3. 依頼主ごとのキャンセル規定
- **設定場所**：依頼主詳細＞単価タブの業務内容ごとに設定します
  - 選べるのは「いつでも可」「締切後はキャンセル料」「締切後は不可」「キャンセル不可」の4つです
  - 締切は「勤務日の◯日前の◯時」で決めます
- **依頼主がオーダーを削除するとき**：確認画面に、派遣元のスタッフ分の扱いを出します
  - 取り消せない分があれば、削除できません
  - キャンセル料がかかる分は、了承したときだけ取り消せます
  - 同じ判定をサーバー側でも行います
- **記録と請求**：取り消しは新しいテーブル `ShiftCancellation` に記録し、キャンセル料はその月の請求書に明細として載ります
- **通知**：派遣元（通知先メールと本部へのプッシュ）に知らせます

### 4. 依頼主に取り消されたときの「調整中」と、電話で受けた取り消しの記録
- **シフトの新しい状態「調整中」（`ON_HOLD`）**：キャンセル規定に「取り消されたときのスタッフの扱い」を足しました
  - 「調整中にする」（請負向け・既定）：休みにはせず調整中にします。スタッフには通知しません。スタッフのカレンダーには「調整中（会社から連絡があります）」と出し、勤務・業務報告の対象からは外します
  - 「そのまま休みにする」（派遣向け）：取り消して、スタッフに通知します
- **派遣元側の表示**：カレンダーに「依頼主取消・調整中」、ダッシュボードの「やること」にも出ます
- **調整中の片付け方**
  - 同じ日に別のシフトへ入れる（振り替える）と、調整中のシフトは自動で外れます
  - 「休みにする」で休みにできます。スタッフに通知するかは選べます
  - どちらの場合も、キャンセル料の記録と請求は残ります
- **電話で受けた取り消し**：自社の管理者が依頼主の現場のシフトを解除するときは、理由（依頼主都合／自社都合）を毎回選んでもらいます
  - 依頼主都合なら、規定からキャンセル料を自動で入れて記録し、請求書に載せます。金額の変更・免除もできます
  - 規定上キャンセル不可の依頼主でも、注意を出したうえで記録できます
  - 記録には、アプリ上の取り消しか電話などで受けたものか（`source`）も残します

## 確認したこと
- `smoke-client-cancel-policy`（26項目）は、次の流れをすべて確認して PASS
  - キャンセル不可で削除できない
  - キャンセル料の了承
  - 調整中になる、メールに調整中と書かれる、スタッフのカレンダーとダッシュボードに出る
  - 振り替えで自動で外れても、キャンセル料は残る
  - 電話の取り消し（理由を選ぶまで解除不可、キャンセル料の自動入力、記録）
  - 調整中を休みにする
  - 請求書の明細2件
- `smoke-unscheduled-workreport`・`smoke-workreport-correction` を含む既存のスモークテスト18本もすべて PASS
- `eslint`・`tsc --noEmit` でエラーなし（警告は既存のもののみ）
- 1 の権限の修正は、コードを読んで確認しました。別の会社のアカウントから実際に操作する再現テストはしていません

## 補足
- マイグレーションが3本あります。シフト外報告のenum値の追加、キャンセル規定、調整中とスタッフの扱い・記録元の追加です
- 「そのまま休みにする」の経路は、コードの分岐としては実装していますが、スモークテストでは通していません

author: tylers2222
body:
Part 1 of 14 of the PR 7 stack (replaces #20). Plan: `~/MonoCode/gigas/monocode-general/projects/change-e/pr7-split.md`.

**Size.** +407/-11 in 11 files, against tyler/main `4ed9767`. Non-test code: +116/-9 (125 lines). Tests: +291/-2. Review rounds: 1.

## What changed

Each session now records which session started it (design 13.2, 13.3). This is level data only. No gate reads it yet; PR 5 of the stack adds the first reader.

- `sessions.lead_session_id TEXT REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`, added by `ensure_session_column` with no version row, plus the partial index `sessions_lead`. `sessions_cwd_cover_idx` gains the column and is rebuilt once when its SQL lacks it, so the sidebar listing stays index-only.
- The write is insert-only through `(SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?)`. A later save never changes the stored lead, and a worker whose lead row is gone saves as a lead instead of failing the upsert. `upsert_session` answers the stored value with `RETURNING`.
- Session summaries, records and metadata answer `leadSessionId`. The web app keeps it on `Session` and sends it on save.
- `sessions.start` from a session that is no Mono chat or habit run names that session as the new session's lead. A Mono's start makes a lead.
- `acceptQuickLaunch` saves the lead before its worker exists whenever the launch names one, through the required `workspace.saveSession`. A lead that is not open, or a save that fails, starts no worker.

Deleting a lead turns its workers into leads. Archiving keeps the link.

## Why

Tyler's levels addendum (`tyler-spec-levels.md`) and the 2026-10-18 size rule. #20 (+8577/-681, 3002 non-test lines) is split into one concern per PR. The level gate, session callers, limits and start rows follow in later PRs of the stack. The approved UI-7 tree (direction B) reads this column.

## How it was tested

- `npm run check` (web and Rust; Rust lib 909 passed) on the rebased head. New: `migrate_twice_leaves_the_lead_session_id_schema_unchanged`, `deleting_a_lead_turns_its_workers_into_leads`, `archiving_a_lead_keeps_its_workers_linked`, `a_worker_whose_lead_row_is_gone_saves_as_a_lead`, `a_later_upsert_never_changes_the_stored_lead`, `record_and_summaries_answer_the_stored_lead_id`. Changed: `list_by_project_is_served_by_a_covering_index` selects `lead_session_id`.
- vitest: sessionStore "sends a worker's lead id with the session"; sessionStoreRestore "a worker's lead" (record, summary); quickLaunchSession "writes a worker's lead id before its first save", "saves the lead before the worker exists", "gives no worker when the save fails", "gives no worker when the lead is not open"; agentApp "names %s that starts a session as its lead only when it is no Mono" (a session, a Mono's chat, a habit run).
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- Mutations: `/tmp/mc947/E/e7-1-mutations.py` removes each fix in a scratch worktree and runs its test. 23 of 23 caught (20 mutations, each named test run under each; output in `/tmp/mc947/E/e7-1-mutations.out`). Examples: the upsert without the `(SELECT id ...)` subselect fails `a_worker_whose_lead_row_is_gone_saves_as_a_lead` on the FK; `lead_session_id = excluded.lead_session_id` fails `a_later_upsert_never_changes_the_stored_lead`; saving the lead after the worker is added fails "saves the lead before the worker exists" with `expected true to be false`; ignoring a false save fails "gives no worker when the save fails" with `promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting`; skipping a lead that is not open fails "gives no worker when the lead is not open" the same way; a Mono start that names its chat fails with `expected 'lead' to be undefined`.

## Review round 1

- m2: rebased onto tyler/main `4ed9767` (#26 took `?25` and record column 22): the lead subselect is `?26` and `get_session_record` reads `row.get(23)`. `record_and_summaries_answer_the_stored_lead_id` passes.
- m1: the lead save moved from App.tsx into `acceptQuickLaunch` (see above).
- n1 (one plain doc comment per field) and n3 (conditional spread, `leadSessionId?: string`) done.
- Follow-up, not one-liners: n2, one `isMonoCaller(id, host)` helper for the four `host.isMono(id) || host.isHabitRun?.(id)` copies with `isHabitRun` required; n4, tests that pin the partial `WHERE lead_session_id IS NOT NULL` clause and that the cover index is rebuilt only once.

## Risks

- `sessions_cwd_cover_idx` is dropped and rebuilt once on the first open after upgrade.
- Until PR 9 of the stack (A3 `worker_cannot_spawn`), a worker that has `/operator` access can still start a session, which then records a worker of a worker. No code reads the level before PR 5.
- A lead that is no longer open in the workspace when its start runs now fails the start, instead of saving a stale snapshot of the caller.
- The lead id is decided in TS here. PR 9b replaces that rule with the Rust gate's answer, which gives the same id for every allowed start.

## Front end

`src/app/App.tsx` changes with no visual change: `launchQuickSession` gives `acceptQuickLaunch` its `saveSession` (`upsertSession` for a session that belongs in history). UI rule: waived by Tyler, in the Monocode General chat on 2026-10-16, for non-visual edits to src/app/App.tsx.

author: zheref
body:
## Why

`docs/PUBLIC-REDACTION.md` § *The rule* says no private repository is named anywhere in this repository's content, and HA-PR-#300 (#289 step one) left item 10 open: the tree's older mentions, written before the guard existed, and the tree check as a lane (#149 criterion 2(b)). This is that item, its own effort as step one's row said. Conjurer.

## How

A one-pass rewrite over every tracked file outside `surfaces/` and `.nen/`: each bare name on the live private list (`gh api 'user/repos?visibility=private'`, indexed, never printed) matched case-insensitively on word boundaries is replaced by its legend placeholder — `<product-repo-A>`, `<product-repo-C>`, `<product-repo-E>` and `<reference-repo>`, the two unmapped roles ruled by the maintainer on 2026-10-17 (`docs/ROSTER.md` § *Rulings of 2026-10-17*, the #289 item 10 row). Skills, `docs/ab/` records, history notes, the CHANGELOG, one changelog fragment and the kagutsuchi worktree self-test fixture, whose directory takes the bracket-free spelling `product-repo-c` (the tenkai fixture changes one comment); both `--self-test`s pass; the mirrors are regenerated. Two shapes stay deliberately: a public repository whose name contains a private one is written as its own name and never composed with a placeholder (the composition would tie the letter to the public name for anyone listing the public repositories — Feitan, round one; PUBLIC-REDACTION § *What is deliberately not redacted* says so now), and the predecessor generator's marker keeps the exact shape limbo matches byte for byte. The tree check lands as the `redaction-tree` lane (`nen shu test --lane redaction-tree`, `bash scripts/private_name_check.sh --tree .`): it needs the live list and the maintainer's ignore file, so it runs on the maintainer's machine, never in CI. Three entries on the live list are ordinary English words used as words (13, 43, 45 by index; `docs/DISCOVERY.md`, `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, 112 ordinary uses) and are left as words. The kazaana skill's verification date on one line was dropped to stay under the 12288-byte ceiling. The `NZ-KWIR` runner labels next to `<product-repo-E>` were tested against that name (initials, camel-case initials, consonant skeleton) and derive from none of it, so they stay. Rejected: rewriting the three words (it would mangle prose) and composing the public name with a placeholder.

## What this changes for you

Reading the history, the A/B records and the skills no longer names a private repository; the placeholders read by role (`<reference-repo>` is the frozen predecessor, `<product-repo-X>` a consuming product). Patch bump 0.112.2 → 0.112.3 (shipped skills changed); the mirrors restamped. **The `redaction-tree` lane reads red until your ignore file carries the three ordinary-word entries.** From a terminal in a Hatsu checkout, each line prints one entry to the terminal (never to a log):

```bash
for k in 13 43 45; do bash scripts/private_name_check.sh --resolve "$k"; done
```

Then add each as its own line to `~/.config/hatsu/redaction-ignore` (`owner/name` ignores that repository only; a bare `name` ignores the word under every owner). The lane then reads green, which is the tree check this PR lands.

## How to verify

1. `git diff origin/fable/kurapika/ha-289-step-two...HEAD -U0 | grep '^+' | grep -v '^+++' | sed 's/^+//' | bash scripts/private_name_check.sh -` → `ok -- no private repository named`; `bash scripts/private_name_check.sh --tree .` → 114 mentions, every one index 13, 43 or 45 (0 with the ignore file in place).
2. `bash scripts/kagutsuchi_worktree.sh --self-test` and `bash scripts/tenkai_adopt.sh --self-test` → 0; `bash scripts/surface_mirror_check.sh .` → all mirrors match; `nen schema check --repo .` → ok.

## Evidence

No user-visible surface changed, so there is no evidence table (prose, a lane and a fixture, UZF-26 exempt).

## Completion checklist

- [x] Required tests — kotoamatsukami: `not applicable — Hatsu declares no general suite`; focused lanes at head: redaction-guard 0, prose-guard 0, surface-mirror-guard 0, plugin-bump-guard 0, tenkai-guard 0, fresh-worktree-guard 0; redaction-tree 1 until the ignore file (above)
- [x] Touched-file coverage — byakugan: `not measurable here` — Hatsu declares no coverage verb
- [x] Adversarial review settled — hanten: Nobunaga · code, two rounds — round one's eight findings resolved at d9a53b35 (Nobunaga-Read: complete at dcb13a6f), round two's veto (the public name restored with the wrong letter case) and its low (the fragment's bump line) fixed at 9635f464, every site now byte for byte the base's token; Feitan · security, two rounds — findings 1, 3 and 4 fixed (Feitan-Read: clear at dcb13a6f), one low left to the maintainer's ruling (four lines list `<product-repo-C>` beside its public sibling; no rewrite hides a name a public repository carries)
- [x] Economics report — `n/a — the economics scope was not raised`
- [x] Every required section present, `## Agent attribution` last — `nen pr body-check` against `contracts/pr-body.requirements.json`
- [x] changelog fragment — `nen changelog fragment-required`: `satisfied`; `changelog.d/ha-289-item-10.md`
- [ ] Bot reviewer rounds (CON-32(b)) — Hatsu's `aiReviewers` is `optional` and the Copilot/Bugbot rounds were declared exhausted on 2026-10-11: readiness is hanten's rounds plus the `nen pr ready` verdict quoted, the CON-32(b) row cited as waived

## Associated issues

**Landing order** (WORKFLOW § *Stacked pull requests* rule 5): this PR now targets `main`; HA-PR-#304 (db4d4808) and HA-PR-#303 (7043bcdf) merged first, and this branch is caught up onto `main` at db86338c; head 9635f464.

| Issue | Scope this PR implements | Merging this |
|---|---|---|
| https://github.com/zheref/hatsu/issues/289 | item 10 — the tree's older private-repository mentions and the tree-check lane | **closes it** — the last item of #289; HA-PR-#304 and HA-PR-#303 have merged |

Closes https://github.com/zheref/hatsu/issues/289

| Agent | Canonical persona / plane | Role and contribution | Evidence |

author: alexander-marquardt
body:
<!-- pr-body-for: branch=issue-17 -->
## What this fixes

Inch-thread socket head, flat head, button head and low head cap screws published `Material` = `Grade 12.9 Alloy Steel`, an ISO 898-1 property class that exists only for metric fasteners. The four families drew their material from one three-entry pool whatever system their standard was in. The pool is now per system (`SOCKET_SCREW_MATERIALS` in `domains/industrial/generate.py`): an inch line draws `Grade 8 Alloy Steel` (SAE J429), a metric line keeps `Grade 12.9 Alloy Steel`.

Refs #17

## Count, before and after

- Before (red commit, `tests/test_catalog_coverage.py::test_no_document_carries_a_grading_from_the_other_measurement_system`, both the committed golden catalog and a fresh build): 240 inch-thread documents publish an ISO property class, all in `screw_socket_head` (95), `screw_flat_head` (55), `screw_button_head` (45) and `screw_low_head` (45). The issue's 318 was measured on an older catalog; the number moves with each regeneration, and this is the count on current main.
- After: 0 inch documents with an ISO class, 0 metric documents with an SAE grade (same test, green on both sources).
- The rebuilt `golden-catalog` has the same 11,765 SKUs in the same order; a python diff of the old and new `flat.jsonl` shows exactly those 240 documents changed (fields `title`, `description`, `text`, `attributes`, `facets`, `price_usd`) and no other.

## The guard

The existing grading-fidelity test (`test_a_bolt_never_carries_a_grading_from_the_other_measurement_system`) is extended in place and renamed `test_no_document_carries_a_grading_from_the_other_measurement_system`; no second test was added. It now:

- scans every published string of every document, not the hex bolt `grade` facet;
- reads a document's system from its own thread designation (`thread_size` / `dia_thread_size`: `M..` is metric, otherwise inch; a document with none, or both, is skipped), so no family list is enumerated and a new family is covered when it publishes a thread size;
- asserts no inch document carries `Class|Grade` 8.8 / 10.9 / 12.9 and no metric document carries `Grade` 2 / 5 / 8;
- asserts the sweep classified more than 1000 documents of each system and that each grading appears on its own system at least once, so a typo in a pattern cannot pass.

The hex bolt's old check (grade facet against `INCH_GRADES` / `METRIC_GRADES`) is covered by the same patterns: `Class 8.8`, `Class 10.9`, `Grade 5`, `Grade 8` each fall under one of the two rules.

## Evidence

- Red: commit 72c89a3 (test only, source unchanged). `agent_pytest tests/test_catalog_coverage.py -k other_measurement` gave `AssertionError: 240 inch-thread document(s) publish an ISO 898-1 property class` for `[committed]` and `[generated]`.
- Fix alone reverted is the red commit itself: its source is the unfixed generator, so the test fails on the generated source and the unfixed golden files.
- Reverse direction bites: with the metric pool temporarily set to `Grade 8 Alloy Steel` (not committed), `-k "other_measurement and generated"` gave `AssertionError: 250 metric-thread document(s) publish an SAE grade`.
- Determinism: `ecom-generate build` twice to two scratch directories, then `cmp` on `flat.jsonl`, `nested.jsonl`, `render.jsonl`, `images.jsonl` between the two and against `golden-catalog/`, and on `stats.json` against the committed one: all identical.
- `agent_pytest` on `tests/test_catalog_golden.py tests/test_catalog_coverage.py tests/test_marking.py tests/test_sku_drawings.py tests/test_price.py tests/test_retail_figures_162.py`: 396 passed.
- This repository has no `scripts/mutant_run.py`, no `scripts/prepush_red_commit.py` and no mypy; none was run.

## Choices worth a reviewer's eye

- Only `Grade 8 Alloy Steel` is added for inch lines, not `Grade 5`. The brief says "Grade 5 / Grade 8"; a Grade 5 socket cap screw is not a product ASTM A574 or F835 describes (those are alloy steel), so publishing one would be new wrong data. Grade 5 is still published on hex bolts and nuts.
- The pool keeps three entries per system so `rng.choice` consumes the same random bits and the rest of the catalog does not move. A first attempt that also made an inch Grade 8 line claim `SAE J429` added a `Standards` value, which shifted the random stream and the SKU count (11,765 to 11,782); that claim was dropped to keep the change to the 240 documents.
- Grade 8 gets its own finish pool (black oxide, zinc plated), Rockwell C36 (SAE J429 is C33-39), price factor 1.1, a section hatch, a fill, and a head marking, because those tables are keyed by material and tests require a hatch for every published material.

## Builds on

- #16 (merged: "Three absent sizes, the customer's thread size, and titles that say what differs"; `gh pr view 16`): it fixed the hex bolt's grade, and this extends its fidelity test to the screw `Material`.
- #99 (merged; touches `set_screws_hex_socket`, price fitting) and #313 (merged; retail `house_styles.py`): both name #17 in their body, neither touches the socket screw material pool or the fidelity test, per `gh pr view <n> --json files`.
- #7 and #22 were not read in detail; the hatch, fill and marking tables this adds a row to are the ones the existing tests (`test_marking.py`, `test_sku_drawings.py`) require every published material to appear in.

Docs-Impact: README.md "Finish and hardness follow material and grade" names the per-system scale; `docs/drawings.md` walkthrough shows `Grade 8 Alloy Steel` for the inch `5/16-18` screw it describes.

author: matt-dean-git
body:
Two pkg/mcpserver tests failed by chance, on main as well as on #250's head. Both are fixed in the test files only (no product code, no build tags, no exports). This unblocks #250's full-package gate (`go test -race -count=3 ./pkg/mcpserver/...`), which both round-2 reviewers could not get green because of these two tests.

Base: main 0df84b0f229cc7b3d664a25c21d705cdb2fa0ca0.

## 1. TestApprovalRepliesAndReceiptsCarryNoArgumentValues (approval_gate_test.go)

How it failed: the privacy check walks every string in the reply and in the recorded receipt input and fails if one contains the planted argument value "777". The receipt input holds `token_id`, which is the first 12 hex characters of a hash of the token, different on every run. Whenever it contained 777 (about 1 run in 400) the test failed with `doc1[0].token_id carries a call value ("777")`. No argument value had leaked.

Fix: `token_id` joins the fields that are checked for their shape (`approval_id`, `receipt_id`, ...) and is not searched for argument values. Its shape check is strict: it must equal the identity the test works out from the token itself (a hash of the decoded identifier and signature). The test also fails if no `token_id` was seen, so the check cannot pass by not running. Every leak assertion on every other field is unchanged.

Permanent case: the test is now two subtests, "any token id" and "token id contains the planted digits". The second searches for a variant of the harness token (one extra non-narrowing `expires` caveat) whose id contains 777, so the id is 777-bearing on every run.

Reproduction on main's walk (the new subtest against main's unchanged assertion code):
```
approval_gate_test.go:454: doc1[0].token_id carries a call value ("777")
--- FAIL: .../token_id_contains_the_planted_digits
```
After the fix, same subtest: PASS. Mutation check: making the expected id wrong fails both subtests with `token_id has the wrong shape`.

## 2. TestStreamableRedirect_OtherPortIsDifferentOrigin (transport_redirect_test.go)

How it failed: the fixture built the redirect target as `"http://" + host + ":" + port + ...`. `url.Hostname()` returns the host without brackets, so when the test servers bound the IPv6 loopback (httptest does that when the IPv4 bind fails) the target was `http://::1:PORT/...`, an invalid URL. The transport then refused with "invalid location" instead of the different-origin refusal the test asserts.

Fix: `net.JoinHostPort(host, port)`. The different-origin assertion is unchanged.

Permanent case: the test is now two subtests, "ipv4 loopback" (127.0.0.1) and "ipv6 loopback" ([::1]), each starting both servers on that address through a small helper (the subtest skips if the host has no such loopback address).

Reproduction on main's string join (the new ipv6 subtest against main's unchanged line):
```
missing "upstream redirect status 307 to http://[::1]:52637 refused" in streamable HTTP POST http://[::1]:52639: upstream redirect status 307 has an invalid location
--- FAIL: .../ipv6_loopback    (ipv4_loopback: PASS)
```
After the fix: both PASS. `-race -count=50 -run TestStreamableRedirect_` passes.

## 3. tool_names_budget_test.go:45 (no change)

Line 45 is `r3Setup(t, nil)` in TestBudget_AQueuedListDoesNotWaitForTheViewLockPastItsBudget; the "incomplete fixture" is r3Setup's `setup: N of 9` check. Run alone on a quiet machine (load 1.39, TIME_WAIT 10 at start), race build, `-count=200`: 200 of 200 passed, 0 failures, exit 0. So it does not fail without port exhaustion; the failure Sol saw happened in a run with socket exhaustion (EADDRNOTAVAIL elsewhere in the same run). Nothing changed.

## Gates (load average 1 minute and TIME_WAIT logged before each; all quiet: load under 8, TIME_WAIT under 2000)

| gate | load1 | TIME_WAIT | exit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gofmt -l on the two changed files: empty | 1.74 | 587 | 0 |
| go vet ./... | 1.74 | 587 | 0 |
