author: joshuaweg
body:
Adds `pulsatrix/calibration.hpp`, the second library piece for the Only Winning Move Predictor (its M3). **Built on #191 (LLM-10); merge after it.** Once #191 lands, this PR shows only its own commit.

## What's new
- **`FitTemperature` / `FitBinaryTemperature`:** temperature scaling (Guo et al. 2017), fitted to minimize the weighted log loss on held-out data.
  - The loss is convex in 1/T, so both boundary cases are decided exactly up front:
    - every label already has the largest logit: minimum at T → 0, reported as T = 1e-6 with `converged = false`;
    - the loss already rises at 1/T = 0: minimum at T → ∞, reported as T = 1e6.
  - Otherwise the minimum is interior, and a bracketed Newton iteration finds it.
  - This avoids a trap I hit first: on separable data the gradient underflows long before the minimum, so a gradient-size stopping rule reports a spurious T ≈ 0.03.
- **`LogOddsError`:** |logit(p) − logit(q)| against reference probabilities, reported per band of the reference probability (default edge 1e-3).
  - Per band: count, weight, mean_abs, bias, rms, median_abs, p90_abs, max_abs.
  - Weights are importance weights, applied in the quantiles too.
  - Both probabilities are clipped to [1e-6, 1 − 1e-6].
  - `ToJson(report)` exports it.
- **Docs:** "Temperature scaling" and "Calibration of rare events" in the Performance guide; roadmap row KS-13.

## Tests (`CalibrationTest`, 9 tests)
- Temperature:
  - recovers T = 2.5 from labels drawn at that temperature (100k examples), in under 30 iterations;
  - beats every T on a fine grid, binary and 4-class;
  - two-class logits (0, z) match the binary fit on z;
  - a weight counts as repeats;
  - both boundary cases are flagged;
  - input checks.
- Log-odds error: band assignment (the edge belongs to the upper band), hand-computed errors, weighted quantiles, clipping of exact 0s, JSON, and input checks.
- Local run on gfx1151 (ROCm 10, Debug): 9 of 9 pass.

author: devupeast
body:
Closes #105

Research findings: TYP-1 and FMT-2.

- **Type scale (§2.7).** `src/theme/typography.js` defines the variants and `src/components/ui/AppText.js` renders them.
  - Titles stay system bold, the default Isaac has in force. Moving titles to Space Grotesk is a one-line change: `VARIANT_FACE.title`.
  - Space Grotesk Bold (static, 86 KB, OFL, vendored in `assets/fonts/`) is used only for the `display` 34 and `displayRing` 28 numerals:
    - the ring count;
    - the Progress stat tiles;
    - the bar tooltip;
    - the share-card big numbers.
  - Small numerals stay system 600 tabular: chips, counters and pills.
- **Fallback face.** `familyFor` sends non-Latin text and all `ja` text other than display numerals to the system face.
- **Loading.** `AuthGate` waits for `initLocale()` and `loadAppFonts()` together, with a 2.5 s timeout. A late or failed load keeps the whole session on the system face, so faces never swap mid-use.
- **12 pt floor.** All 42 sizes below 12 pt were raised. `typeFloor.test.js` enforces the floor, including both branches of ternary sizes.
- **Tabular figures.** Counters, the timer sub-line, stats, the chart axis, time-picker digits and percentages use tabular figures, so the timer no longer jitters.
- **Ring count.** It shrinks to fit (`adjustsFontSizeToFit`, minimum 0.6, `maxFontSizeMultiplier` 1.2), so "12/15" and "100/120" fit at font scale 1.3.
- **Tab bar.** At 12/16 pt the bar fits the 49 pt iOS height. Tabs keep equal widths unless a label is longer than 10 characters (de, fr); then they share space by label width, and every tab keeps a target of at least 44 pt.
- **Layout fixes.** The Progress y-axis is 44 wide and capped at 1.3×. Detail-grid month labels start at their first week.
- **DesignPreview** (dev only) gains a type section with ring overflow samples.

## Verification
- `jest`: 40 suites, 427 tests. New coverage: the typography tokens, the floor test, the font loader (load before timeout, late load ignored, failed load falls back, loads once) and `familyFor`. i18n-check passes, and the web export compiles.
- Shot matrix before and after with the deterministic seed (`.shots/F-03/`, local), plus extra captures:
  - ja Today and Progress: system titles with Space Grotesk numerals;
  - de, fr and pt-BR tab bars on the SE.
- Emulator, light and dark, on Today, Progress and Settings:
  - timer crops show no jitter;
  - at font scale 1.3, Today, Progress and the ring overflow samples show no new wraps or truncation.
- Code review: 8/10. M1 (ring overflow) and the minors are fixed in the second commit.

body:
JM's 6:38 PM brew after hula.11: the desktop wrote 'Brew timed out' at 6:38:25 PM. Jeeves (local claude-agent-acp) was still cold-starting: buzz-acp hit its 60s session timeout four times and the fifth attempt succeeded. The briefing was posted at 6:47:39 PM, and hula.11's upgrade path replaced the timeout row. The old rows were never status-only; each is one 6–10k-char message (narration, coffee-cup art, briefing). **Timeout**
- `pendingRun.workingSeenAt` records the first time the agent is seen working on the run.
- Until then, only the 8-min hard timeout ends the run (`isBestieCoffeePendingStale` / `isBestieCoffeeLive` / `shouldDisableBestieCoffeeBrew` take `agentSeenWorking`). The 45s idle-settle applies only after the agent has worked and gone idle.
- The wake controller and the coffee hook record the working signal. A web Brew does not abandon a run that is waiting for a cold agent.

**Titles**
- `deriveBestieCoffeeBrief` starts at the greeting paragraph, or after the coffee-cup art when there is no greeting, or at the first non-narration paragraph. It skips a bare 'Good morning, JM.' and uses the next sentence.
- Titles are re-derived from the full output on load, so existing rows are repaired.
- Checked against all 15 of JM's stored outputs: each now gives 'Since your last session …'.

Tests: `bestieCoffeeColdStart.test.mjs` (JM's rows, the 6:38 timeline, idle-settle after work, persistence, web Brew). Two existing expectations changed from the greeting to the next sentence. The same 10 pre-existing jsdom-less failures happen on main. Desktop-only (not in the web bundle).

author: stardust0831
body:
### What's changed?

Enable optional GPU acceleration of LCAO exact-exchange RI tensor contractions through LibRI's DDLA CUDA backend, with a build option and a runtime INPUT keyword:

- **`ENABLE_LIBRI_GPU`**: new CMake option, default `OFF`. Enable it together with `ENABLE_LIBRI=ON` and `USE_CUDA=ON` to build the DDLA GPU backend.
- **`exx_device`**: new INPUT keyword, default `cpu`. Set `exx_device gpu` together with `device gpu` to run RI contractions on the GPU. `device gpu` alone continues to use CPU RI, so the solver and RI backend can be selected separately.

Build with compatible LibRI and DDLA installations:

```bash
cmake -B build -DENABLE_LIBRI=ON -DUSE_CUDA=ON -DENABLE_LIBRI_GPU=ON \
  -DLIBRI_DIR=/path/to/patched/LibRI -DDDLA_ROOT=/path/to/DDLA
```

Then select the GPU RI backend in INPUT:

```text
device      gpu
exx_device  gpu
```

The backend is experimental. Installation, dependency versions and runtime requirements are documented in `docs/advanced/install.md`.

<details>
<summary>Dependencies and supported scope</summary>

- Requires LibRI `6ce3c84` with `tests/lcao_hse_gpu/libri-compat.patch` and CUDA DDLA `v0.0.4` (`9c404ac`). The patch fixes API compatibility and accumulation needed for forces and stress. CMake locates DDLA through `DDLA_ROOT` or `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` and checks GPU API compilation/linking.
- Applies to LCAO Kohn-Sham exchange. Independent LR/RDMFT exchange engines retain CPU mode; LR inherits the selected backend when reusing the Kohn-Sham exchange object.
- GPU RI does not support real-space EXX symmetry reduction. With `symmetry 1`, use `exx_device cpu` or set `exx_symmetry_realspace 0`; unsupported combinations are rejected.
- All MPI ranks on a node must see the same allocated GPU list, with at least as many visible GPUs as local ranks. Per-rank single-GPU masking is unsupported by the pinned LibRI backend.

</details>

### Unit Tests and/or Case Tests for my changes

Validation used [SAI](https://www.open-sai.com/) V100 GPUs with `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`:

- CPU/GPU builds, dependency consumers, INPUT unit tests and CLI checks passed, including invalid-input diagnostics and static/shared MKL dependency consumers.
- HSE Gamma, complex multi-k, spin-polarized and symmetry cases passed against unchanged references, including a two-rank/two-GPU run. Gamma and symmetry cases check energy, forces and stress; complex multi-k checks energy.
- The optional numerical GPU test passed for real and complex signed accumulation across all 18 contraction branches with nonempty outputs. Reverting the accumulation fix produced the expected failure.

<details>
<summary>Verification commands and validation limits</summary>

Full GPU and input-test builds used the commands below; the final GPU rebuild used `--parallel 8` after verifying that other production files were unchanged:

```bash
cmake --build "$BUILD_DIR" --target abacus_std_gpu --parallel 32
cmake --build "$BUILD_DIR" --target MODULE_IO_read_item_serial --parallel 32
ctest --test-dir "$BUILD_DIR" --output-on-failure -R '^MODULE_IO_read_item_serial$'
"$ABACUS_BIN" --version
"$ABACUS_BIN" --info
"$ABACUS_BIN" -h exx_device
"$ABACUS_BIN" --generate-parameters-yaml
"$ABACUS_BIN" --check-input
```

From copies of `tests/08_RI`, using the existing references:

```bash
bash ../integrate/Autotest.sh -a "$ABACUS_BIN" -n 1 -o 1 -f CASES.task.txt
bash ../integrate/Autotest.sh -a "$ABACUS_BIN" -n 2 -o 1 -f CASES.task.txt
```

Variants cover CPU and GPU solvers with the default and explicit RI backend selections. Symmetry cases cover CPU RI with real-space symmetry enabled and CPU/GPU RI with it disabled.

Standalone dependency checks:

```bash
cmake -S tests/lcao_hse_gpu/cmake -B build-consumer \
  -DLIBRI_DIR="$LIBRI_PREFIX" -DLIBCOMM_DIR="$LIBCOMM_PREFIX" \
  -Dcereal_DIR="$CEREAL_CONFIG" \
  -DENABLE_LIBRI_GPU=ON -DDDLA_ROOT="$DDLA_PREFIX"
cmake --build build-consumer --parallel 2
ctest --test-dir build-consumer --output-on-failure
```

The numerical test additionally enables `ENABLE_LIBRI_GPU_TESTS=ON` and runs `ctest --test-dir build-consumer -V -R '^libri_gpu_accumulation$'`. It requires one GPU and MPI and is off by default. CPU consumers disable GPU RI; MKL consumers additionally set `MKL_ROOT`, `MKL_MPI=openmpi` and `MKL_LINK=static` or `dynamic`.

GPU regression builds used `ENABLE_NCCL_PARALLEL_DEVICE=OFF` because the input-test target had unresolved NCCL symbols with it enabled. NCCL runtime behavior, full MKL application builds, multi-node execution, SOC and long MD runs remain unverified. GPU memory use increases; initialization remains largely on CPU. A Si32 comparison needed `scf_ene_thr=1e-8` for consistent outer-loop stopping, so default-threshold convergence needs further validation.

</details>

No linked issue; this adds optional support for an existing LibRI backend.

F-135 (FINDINGS-REGISTER) and ChatGPT RESEARCH/WORKOUTS audit item 6: a request key on `pilot.intervention_executions`, so one tap of Log intervention logs one intervention. **Migration only.** No lane applies it; Overwatch reads the SQL and applies it to staging, then production (Jason's click), before the code that uses it (PR B, stacked on this) merges.

## Brief header

```text
SESSION: Lane L55 (F-135 intervention log idempotency), branch l55/intervention-request-key-migration, under Overwatch
MIGRATIONS: intervention-execution-request-key
STACKED ON: NONE (cut from main 93eb41b6f, main merged in at 4e9762b9c)
CONTESTED: .github/workflows/apply-migrations.yml and apps/web/package.json registration lines (every migration PR adds the same three lines; whichever merges later merges main in)
SCOPE: Overwatch GO to L55 (2026-10-18): "PR A (the migration, 2 Opus reviewers; I read the SQL and apply it to staging, then production with Jason's click), and PR B stacked on A (server now, client after #1707 merges)."
```

## Why

After #1707 (lane L40), when a POST to `/api/pilot/coach/intervention-executions` gets no clear answer, the live screen reads the ledger back. A read that finds nothing does not prove a write still in flight will not commit after it, so "not logged, try again" followed by a retry can log the same intervention twice. A client request key, unique per gym, lets the server answer the retry with the first record (PR B). Same column, check and index shape as `pilot.workout_issues.request_key`.

## What changed

**New `infra/azure/pilot_slice_postgres_intervention_execution_request_key_migration.sql`** (additive, idempotent, no begin/commit -- the runner opens the transaction):

- `request_key text null` on `pilot.intervention_executions`. Existing rows and every keyless start stay NULL; nothing is compared for them. No default, so no table rewrite.
- Check `pilot_intervention_executions_request_key_check`: NULL, or not blank and at most 200 characters. Added only when the table has no check of that name (catalog-guarded, the waiver-status-check pattern), so a re-run of the `all` chain does not re-validate it under an exclusive lock (Codex P2). The file drops nothing.
- Partial unique index `pilot_intervention_executions_one_per_request_key` on `(organization_id, request_key) where request_key is not null`.
- A correction writes its new row with a named column list (`correctExecution`), so the key never moves off the row the tap started.

**Runner `apps/web/scripts/pilot-apply-intervention-execution-request-key-migration.mjs`**: declared-target check before connecting; `set local lock_timeout = '10s'` (the table is written by the live screen; review finding); readiness checks the column (text, nullable, no default), the check compared in full against `pg_get_constraintdef`, and the index by name and the tail of its stored definition (unique, both columns, partial predicate).

**Registered** in `apply-migrations.yml` (choice list, `all` loop after `intervention-executions`, list-check case) and package.json (`pilot:apply-intervention-execution-request-key`, `test:migrations:intervention-execution-request-key`).

## Release note for Overwatch (reviewer B)

`pilot-verify-schema` (deploy-staging, deploy-production, release-one-approval) will expect the column, check and index once this merges, so a release of main cannot pass on a target until this migration is applied there. Apply to staging, then production, right after merge.

## Evidence

### EVIDENCE APPLICABILITY - the request key on real PostgreSQL

- CLAIM: a key names at most one execution per gym (second insert 23505 on the index) and re-applying through the runner twice keeps it so; the same key in another gym is allowed; keyless executions are unlimited; a key blank, all spaces or over 200 characters is refused 23514 on the check and 200 is kept as sent; a row written before the migration keeps NULL; the file holds nothing destructive (no drop at all) and guards its check add; a re-run leaves the check as it is (same oid); the runner refuses a same-named check with a wider rule, a same-named non-unique index, one over the key alone, one without the partial predicate, a missing check, a NOT NULL column, a column with a default, and a result it did not produce.
- PROPERTY: SQLSTATE and constraint names from pilot.intervention_executions; the runner's readiness result.
- INSTRUMENT: apps/web/src/server/pilot/interventionExecutionRequestKey.pg.test.ts (embedded Postgres, full schema in the `all` order)
- SUBJECT: 5bc9ba5581dc10e59843fee5ee811f821c190e86
- EXECUTION PATH: the migration through the full-schema helper and through applyMigrationTransaction
- POSITIVE CONTROL: 13/13 locally at this SUBJECT's files (5bc9ba558); the earlier 12-case version passed 12/12 in CI (run 39088104367). migrationDispatchCoverage, ciClassifierScopeContract and migration-apply-order pass locally (222 tests).
- NEGATIVE CONTROL: at this SUBJECT's files, in a scratch worktree (C:\Dev_WORKTREES\l55-scratch-server, files byte-identical to this SUBJECT), byte hashes restored and checked after each: A1 (index over request_key alone) failed 3; A2 (check without btrim) failed 5; A3 (readiness ignores the index definition) failed 2 (at 4e9762b9c); A4 (back to drop-and-re-add the check every run) failed 2 (at 5bc9ba558).
- EVIDENCE LEVEL: REAL_DATABASE
- BLIND SPOTS: not applied to staging or production (no lane applies migrations).
- VERDICT: APPLICABLE

## Review

- Codex P2 (re-run re-validates the check under an exclusive lock): fixed in 5bc9ba558.

Two Opus adversarial reviewers on 61add003e: no blockers. Both: add a lock timeout (done). A: readiness should refuse a column default (done, with a test). B: replay must find a superseded v1 and answer the lineage's current record; replay must run before the inactive-protocol refusal; three hand-picked pg suites call `startExecution` (PR B keeps the keyless INSERT unchanged, so they are unaffected).

Files: the SQL, the runner, the pg suite, and the registrations (workflow and package.json).

author: wylewis
body:
## Qué hace

- Nuevo módulo `src/hardware.h` / `src/hardware.cpp` con las decisiones que dependen del paralelismo disponible:
  - `hardwareThreads()`: lo que informa `std::thread::hardware_concurrency` (0 si no informa).
  - `clampPoolSize(hardware, minimum, maximum)` y `recommendedPoolSize()`: un hilo de estimación por hilo de hardware, nunca menos de `kPoolMinimum` (2) ni más de `kPoolMaximum` (32).
  - `defaultTaskCount(work)`: tareas para los precálculos, una por núcleo y nunca más que unidades de trabajo; se movió aquí desde la tabla paralela, que ahora usa este módulo, para que haya un único criterio en todo el programa.
- `main` crea el pool de estimación con `recommendedPoolSize()` y registra en stderr el tamaño elegido, los hilos del hardware y el rango.
- `tests/hardware_test.cpp`: el tamaño sigue al hardware dentro del rango, aplica el mínimo con un núcleo o con hardware desconocido y el máximo con muchos núcleos, y el conteo de tareas nunca supera el trabajo. Registrado en `ctest`.
- README: párrafo sobre cómo se decide el tamaño del pool.

En la máquina de desarrollo: 18 hilos de hardware, pool de 18. Verificado bajo ThreadSanitizer al crear y parar el pool.

## Por qué

Responde a la pregunta de defensa "¿cuántos hilos creas y por qué no más ni menos?". Las estimaciones son cálculo puro, así que más hilos que núcleos solo agregan cambios de contexto. El mínimo de 2 garantiza concurrencia real aunque la máquina tenga un núcleo o no informe cuántos tiene; el máximo de 32 existe porque los candidatos de un pedido son pocas decenas y un pool mayor quedaría ocioso. Es la fila del mapa de conceptos "una decisión que depende del paralelismo disponible en el hardware". La justificación con mediciones de speedup se completa en el experimento de despacho, que variará el tamaño del pool.

## Cómo probarlo

```sh
mkdir build && cd build && cmake .. && make
ctest --output-on-failure
./delivery_sim ../config/equipetrol.json   # imprime "pool de estimacion: N hilos (hardware: H, rango 2-32)"
```

author: ag4122
body:
## What

The results screen no longer shows scores. Each district shows its **rank** and a **driver summary**: what most raises or lowers its rank. This was agreed in a design session; the glossary's MVP, Driver summary, Rank and Shortlist size entries record the decisions.

- **Shortlist size** (Top 10 / 25 / 50 / All, default 25) replaces the score-threshold slider. The legend runs #1 to #N, and colours follow rank, not score.
- **Driver summary** on map hover, and on list-row focus, tap or click (screen readers get it through `aria-describedby`). Example:
  > #2 of 43 · M1
  > Compared with a typical district in this area:
  > ↑ Local population mix suits it well · ↓ More Indian restaurants already here · ↑ More restaurants nearby
  > Ahead of #3 (M3) mainly on: more restaurants nearby.
- A one-line note under the list says drivers are patterns in reviews, not guarantees.

## How drivers are worked out (`web/drivers.js`)

The swap-one-factor test runs in the browser on the shipped NN1. For each of 8 factor groups (restaurant scene, residents, visitors, same-cuisine supply, matched community, rent, deprivation, local population mix), it swaps the district's values for those of the **median-ranked district in the search area** and re-scores. The score change is that group's driver.

- Areas with fewer than 5 districts compare with England's median-ranked district.
- Up to 3 drivers, strongest first. Effects under 0.01 are omitted; from 0.04 the wording is "far more" or "much".
- The ahead line uses the same swap against the next-ranked district. The last shortlisted district compares with the first one outside the shortlist.
- The matched community is named only when it raises the rank; other ethnic shares fall under "local population mix".
- Summaries are computed lazily, when a tooltip opens or a row is focused: 2–10 ms each on the live v5 bundle.

`scoring.js` gains `profileScorer` so a district can be re-scored with swapped inputs; `scoreDistricts` is unchanged in output.

## Notes for review

- On the live v5 bundle, "Local population mix" (age, sex and the ethnic shares together) often leads city summaries. That reflects the model. Splitting age out as its own group would make summaries more specific; this needs a product call.
- The matched community rarely reaches the 0.01 cutoff with the current weights.
- The cutoffs (0.01, 0.04) were set from a probe of the live v5 bundle across 5 cuisines and 5 areas: 0–3 drivers per summary.

## Tests

- `node --test`: 128 pass (new `tests/js/drivers.test.mjs`; `results.test.mjs` rewritten for the shortlist).
- `tests/browser/free-text-flow.mjs` updated for the shortlist control and focus summaries: 27/27 pass in Edge (25 in the full run, the 2 changed tests rerun after fixing their assertions).

author: tomoh24
body:
Phase 8 (demo hardening) for Role C.

## Changes
- **Deadline:** `reply()` returns the fallback after **20 s**. A worst case used to be about 40 s. Model calls time out at **8 s** with one retry.
  - I tried 6 s first. During a burst of slow Anthropic responses it killed valid calls and made the stress run worse (45/61).
  - The account's rate limit is 1,000 RPM, so this was API latency, not throttling. The webhook's "Got it" ack covers waits over 1.5 s.
- **Prompt:**
  - Judge the language only from the user's words, never from place names or the area.
  - Example openings per language (en/es/tl/vi). Tagalog replies were drifting into Spanish about 2 in 15 times. Now 15/15 Tagalog and 15/15 Spanish in targeted runs.
  - Never repeat a place, address or hours that no tool returned.
- **`tests/test_brain_reply.py` (17 tests, CI):** the full `reply()` pipeline with an in-memory Mongo and a scripted model.
  - Covers: JOIN/STOP/HELP, fast path with map locations on both messages, unknown ZIP not saved, LLM search path, memory and history cap, Spanish user's bare ZIP going to the model, Photon ids, schema round-trip.
  - Failure modes: outage, deadline, no tool call, unknown tool, over-long reply, very long input, emoji/markdown.
  - Mutation-checked: removing the deadline or the inbound location backfill makes the tests fail.
- **`evals/stress.py`:** `uv run python -m evals.stress [--repeat N] [--only NAME ...]`. Repeats the 4 demo-script messages ×10 plus 7 adversarial inputs (prompt injection, prompt leak, very long, emoji only, mixed language, Tagalog, health detail) against live Claude and Atlas. Uses `stress:` handles and deletes them afterwards.

## Results (live, `claude-haiku-5-5` + Atlas)
- `ruff` clean, `pytest` **106 passed**.
- Eval **15/15**, p50 1.6 s, p95 4.3 s.
- Stress **59/61**, p50 1.7 s, p95 3.5 s. All 40 demo-script runs passed (max 3.0 s).

# sha3-256-r5-exploratory: R5N4, R5N3 with the Python B' held under the claimed memory (time 31.06817, memory 2^25.085320, score 36.46972)

Change from fe2ec86f (36.46971): only the charge of the five s40 connector runs. R.8 states they are a fresh sample consistent with the filed constants, not a re-derivation, so under rule 0.1 they fix no number and are disclosed, not charged (0.1's table); time_log2 31.38439 -> 31.06817.

Changed from our 909e7abd (36.50578): the memory claim only, 36,500,000 -> 35,598,680 bytes (2^25.085320), the dense model's largest phase P (Appendix K). Every development run was made again under a 34,500,000-byte address-space cap with LC_ALL=C in the environment (CPython then maps no locale archive): 32 of 32 runs exit 0, the 15 labelled outputs are identical to R5N4's, the largest measured peak is 29,417,472 bytes (Appendix M, new devmem.jsonl). Time unchanged. (Earlier: from our 7e53df5d (36.90092) to 909e7abd: the memory claim only, 48,000,000 -> 36,500,000 bytes (2^25.121393). r5.py imports only what the algorithm uses (_sha2/_sha3 with a hashlib fallback, no json/fractions/collections at import), Model interns its equations, algorithm() drops the previous round\'s echelon system and Setup before the next B\' round, and fes.c stores G once per outer monomial (12,951 entries). All 32 development runs were rerun under prlimit --as=36,500,000 with identical outputs; time is unchanged (31.06817).)

No process peak and no stored artifact exceeds the claim (35,598,680 bytes).

## Context and goal

The track is 5-round SHA3-256 collision search (ordinary collision, messages of exactly 135 bytes, one padded block with zero capacity, prefix rounds 0..4, 256-bit digest). The score is time_log2 + (memory_log2_bytes - 20). Our accepted entry 0f72a85e has time 32.79669 and memory 2^26.955592, score 39.75228. R5N (e268e947) and R5N2 (635939f2) were refuted on the advice-generating run that reached above the claimed memory. R5N3 (fc57f343, in review when this note was written) regenerated every input under an address-space cap, and its claim was the largest cap any label needed: 62,914,560 bytes, score 37.51550.
R5N4 asks one question of R5N3: why did the Python B' need 62.9 MB when the dense model says 47.8 MB? Answer: bprime() built the next candidate's setup (Model, links, ports, about 9 MB) while the previous candidate's setup was still referenced by `cs`, so two setups were live at once. R5N4 adds `cs = None` before the next CandSetup is built (experiments/r5.py line 945). No value, coin or WK counter changes.
Claim: time 31.06817, memory 2^25.085320 (35,598,680 bytes), preprocessing 30.69348, score 36.46972. The ledger's integer primitive count (ceiling of N x 1355) is 3798217655547.

## Starting point and credit

This package is a derivative of **our R5N3 (fc57f343)**, **R5N2 (635939f2)**, **R5N (e268e947)** and **0f72a85e**, which derive from **Th0rgal's 4e24cebd**, **my 1d801017**, **winglock's b5213766** (v25h) and the accepted **fa625146**. Declared dependencies: the same four packages as R5N3. None of the people credited reviewed this package, and a credit is not an endorsement. The algorithm, B', the connector, E, rule K, the R7 study and nearly all of the proof text are theirs and the v22b/v25 lineage's; through them **leech1996** (the advice reading), **0xshikhar**, **Meganpark980320**, **rubenmarcus** (v15) and **Subflatus3**. Me (Jbenisek), with helper instances of the model that wrote this note: 0f72a85e, R5N's program changes, the streamed capadv, the clean development run, the ledger and this one-statement change.

## What changed against R5N3

- experiments/r5.py: one statement added in bprime (sha256 7ef2064a17f666171f797db9e9e444d98dcc89438fee53500ab7ec0a715b7a2e, 65,477 bytes; R5N3's was f9a88567b9cadffcdd7995bd6dc68a543218594e8825ee484a597c9e219b3cb3, 65,463 bytes). The B' rows are the same ten labels (R10 run K) and their work counts equal R5N3's for the same labels (same program values); the connector rows are labels 0..4. R5N3's own 50 development rows, which were run with the predecessor of r5.py and at caps up to 62.9 MB, are superseded by these runs and are not charged here.

## What was run

| Stage | What it regenerates | Result | Peak (B) |
|---|---|---|---:|
| s10 export_cores.py | T1, T2, core tables of the 467 kept cores | 8,674,833 nodes, 467 cores, 48,592,224 half vectors | 36,847,616 |
| s11 six layouts | block layout | nb = 64 matches: stride 13 (shipped) 78,534 against 773,682 to 4.7e10 for the others | at most 35,074,048 |
| s12 capadv + finalize | stage 2 over all 467 cores, M_CAP, advice | 7,251,935 matches, M_CAP = 2^24, advice SHA-256 identical to the shipped ALPHA3_BITS/BETA2 | 8,171,520 / 28,536,832 |
| s13 mt6_check.py | replacement for mitm_trial(q) | per-core nb = 64 match counts of all 467 cores equal r5.MT6 | 28,819,456 |
| s20 B' x10 | whole B' runs on labels R10 run 0..9 | see proof table M.2 | at most 37,076,992 |

| s40 online x5 | B', Setup, connector to 50 accepted spaces | labels R10 run 0..4 | at most 28,844,032 |

The Python half tables of mitm_trial(q) (78.1 MiB for one core) are not run: s13 checks the same quantity from the streamed run, as in R5N3. The organizer's own execution of the experiments is the organizer's and is not ours.

## Hypotheses

- H-1: every input the algorithm reads as derived (M_CAP, layout, advice) is a function of r5.py and the target and is reproducible in a process capped at the claimed memory. Held: s10-s12, advice hash identical.
- H-2: Appendix M contains every run whose result fixes a number that R5N4 reads as derived. R5N3's runs, G2, D15, D19, development items 20, 22 and 23, R5N's design studies and R5N2's capped runs are superseded, as in R5N3. This is the central choice, and the one a reader may reject.

Before: a role that had a delivered quest dropped before #40 couldn't log in. Login settlement delivered the re-accepted quest, reused a reward source that had already been paid, and failed with `EconomyOperationConflictException: Natural source already committed`. #40 keeps the delivery count for drops made from now on, but not for drops made earlier.

If a delivery committed but wasn't applied in memory, the saved state counts it, so it is never skipped and still fails rather than paying twice. The ledger is only read when the first source is already taken, so normal hand-ins don't change.

How: `TaskService.ForgottenDeliveriesAsync` uses the existing `RoleStore.RewardSourceCommittedAsync` and the saved tasks blob. CustomContentQuestTests now rebuilds the pre-#40 state (no count, paid sources) and checks that the next hand-in goes through. The Tower/Dungeon ApplyFault tests fail on main too.

author: emre9690
body:
## Problem
Opening the popup 4 folders deep fired **40 requests in 0.49 s (~82 requests/second)**: the empty-folder look-ahead loaded every visible folder, 3 at a time, with no delay. Folder lists were also forgotten on every page change, so navigating around WebLab re-requested the same folders. Downloads were already rate-limited; the folder picker wasn't.

## Fix
- **One shared request queue** for everything the extension sends from a tab (folder picker, download, images): one request at a time, at least 350 ms apart. No feature can burst anymore, including future ones.
- **Back off when WebLab is busy:** on HTTP 429 or 503 the download stops with "WebLab is busy right now…" and nothing is sent for a minute.
- **No look-ahead:** folders load only when opened. Empty folders show "Empty folder" and keep their arrow (keeps the earlier vanishing-arrow bug fixed).
- **Folder cache:** folder lists are kept for 30 minutes in `chrome.storage.session` (memory only, cleared when the browser closes).
- README and PRIVACY.md updated.

## Measured (offline simulation, same setup before and after)
| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Popup opened 4 levels deep (10 subfolders per level) | 40 requests in 0.49 s | 4 requests |
| Reopened on a sibling page in the same course | 40 again | 0 |
| 30 requests fired at once through the queue | — | 1 at a time, ≥351 ms apart, max 3 in any second |
| WebLab returns 503 | kept going | stops immediately |

Downloads, model answers, WebLab-shown correct answers and explanations, images, logged-out detection and the course check were re-tested against saved pages.

## What changed

Bridge 0.5.0 adds three ways into the existing reviewed handoff flow:

- Current sidebar conversation `⋯` → **Hand off session** / **迁移会话**.
- A Host-managed keyboard command, unbound by default and configurable in DSH settings.
- The optional `bridge_prepare` model tool for natural-language requests. It can prepare a picker or preview, but cannot confirm migration or continuation.

All entries reuse the existing command handler, preview identity, Text/Markdown editor and explicit confirmation. Existing `/bridge` arguments remain intact. CLI help is collapsed by default, and natural-language reviews appear outside collapsed process details without replacing the original tool logs.

author: nalbertini
body:
## Per chi usa l'app

La segreteria vede chi è tesserato (FIJLKAM, FIPE…) e chi, fra chi frequenta, non lo è.

- **Tessera per persona.** Nella scheda c'è il timbro **TESSERA** in cima (NO TESSERA, SCADUTA, SCADE A DICEMBRE, IN REGOLA) e la sezione **TESSERE**: una riga per tessera, con **+ AGGIUNGI UNA TESSERA** per chi non è nel foglio del RASD e **TOGLI** (con conferma, e **ANNULLA** subito dopo).
- **Import dal RASD, con anteprima.** In IMPOSTAZIONI → **TESSERE DAL RASD** si carica il CSV (Organismo; Persona; Codice fiscale; Tipo; Codice tess.; Valido dal): prima si guarda cosa entra e cosa resta fuori (col motivo), poi si mette. La persona si riconosce da codice fiscale **e** stesso nome; l'import non crea nessuno e non duplica niente. Le tessere valgono fino al 31 dicembre dell'anno di «Valido dal».
- **ISCRITTI.** NO TESSERA / TESSERA SCADUTA / TESSERA SCADE A… dentro IN REGOLA (solo per chi ha un corso che chiede la tessera), il filtro **SENZA TESSERA**, e **NON IN REGOLA** comprende la tessera mancante o scaduta.
- **COSA MANCA.** Quinta casella **TESSERE**, che porta a ISCRITTI già filtrato. Se il conto non si sa, «—» e mai uno zero verde.
- **Pagina TESSERE** (menu, sotto ISCRITTI): **SENZA TESSERA**, **MAI AVUTE**, **SCADUTE** e **TESSERATI SENZA CORSO**.
- **CORSI → dati:** campo **Tessera richiesta** (testo libero, in maiuscolo; vuoto = nessuna). Contano solo le tessere da praticante e da agonista; le prove gratuite non sono iscrizioni.
- Guida: `guida/segreteria/tessere.md`.

## Per chi rivede

- **`supabase/61-tessere.sql` — NON lanciata sul database vero.** Va lanciata a mano dopo l'unione, seguendo la skill `nuova-migrazione` (poi `controllo.sql`: le righe nuove devono dire «ok»). Il numero è 61: il 55 era già preso da `55-amministrazione.sql` su main. Crea `tessere` (RLS solo segreteria), `corsi.ente_tessera` (e scrive una volta sola la mappa: Judo, Lotta, Aikido, MGA, Avviamento → FIJLKAM; sala Pesi → FIPE; Giocomotricità, Psicomotricità, Prepugilistica nessuna), `parole_nome`, `importa_tessere` e il trigger `tessere_unione` (l'unione di due schede con la stessa tessera non si ferma più sulla chiave unica). Finché non c'è, l'app non mostra tessere e la casella dice «non so».
- **L'incrocio** (chi è iscritto senza tessera valida, chi è tesserato senza corso) sta solo nell'app, in `src/lib/tessere.ts`: nel database non ha una copia.
- La modalità prova ha le stesse regole (`importaTessereProva`, tessere di partenza per i corsi che le chiedono).
- Prove: `scripts/prova-tessere.mjs` (nuova), `scripts/prova-cosa-manca.mjs` (cinque caselle), `supabase/prova/tessere.sql` (nuova: solo segreteria, codice fiscale e stesso nome, senza doppioni, unione, mappa dei corsi scritta una volta). Rotte a mano ~90 regole: cadono, tranne due mutanti equivalenti. Il registro è in `docs/qa/percorsi-critici.md`.
- Controlli fatti: `revisore-codice`, `custode-dati`, `rls-reviewer`, `garante-qualita`, `designer-ods`, `collaudatore`, `cliente-ods`. Canvas di design in `docs/design-canvas/tessere` e componente `CosaManca` nella libreria.
- In locale `prova-sito-tessere`, `prova-sito-collage` e `prova-iscrizione-sito` falliscono: confrontano il ramo con `main` e vietano modifiche a `supabase/` e a `styles.css`, ma su GitHub il confronto è saltato (checkout corto). Tutte le altre `prova:*`, `prova:sql` (Postgres 17 in Docker) e `build:tutto` passano.

## Come provarla

1. `?prova` della segreteria: menu TESSERE; apri una scheda (timbro e sezione TESSERE); ISCRITTI → chip SENZA TESSERA; un corso → Tessera richiesta.
2. IMPOSTAZIONI → TESSERE DAL RASD con un CSV: CONTROLLA non scrive, METTI scrive, rifarlo non duplica.

## Resta a mano

- Contare i codici fiscali compilati sul database vero (`select count(*) from anagrafiche where codice_fiscale is not null`): senza codice fiscale l'import non aggancia la persona.
- Provare con un CSV vero del RASD (nessuno ha scelto un file dal selettore: i test sono passati da script).
- Lanciare `61-tessere.sql` sul database vero.

body:
Stacked on #35.

## What

- `metrics.pair_details` also returns `hit`: pairs that are both in OLIR and in the model's output, with the model's strength and rationale. This comes with a test, which failed first.
- One rerun of the current config (4 per batch, k=40) produced `mapping-strength-review(.json, -pairs.json)`. It has 218 hits: 21 full, 138 partial, 59 supporting. Overall P 0.437, R 0.305, F1 0.359. Full/partial only: P 0.587, R 0.222, F1 0.322.
- `mapping-strength-review-labels.tsv` holds a blind sample of 20 "supporting" and 10 "partial" hits (seed 17, shuffled). The labels are Claude's alone and **not yet human-reviewed**.

## Finding

| model said | Claude: partial | Claude: supporting |
|---|---|---|
| supporting (20) | 8 | 12 |
| partial (10) | 6 | 4 |

The model and Claude agree on 18 of 30, and the disagreements go both ways:

- **Model under-calls.** Controls that fully do a narrower case of the item get "supporting". Examples: adaptive authentication and re-authentication for "users are authenticated".
- **Model over-calls.** Controls that only share the subject or are the vehicle get "partial". Example: an SCRM plan that doesn't mention post-contract provisions.

So the hits labelled "supporting" can't simply be counted as gap-closing, and closing recall (0.22) isn't systematically understated. What a prompt tweak could improve is consistency at the partial/supporting boundary, not necessarily recall. That waits on the human spot-check.

## Test plan

- [x] New `pair_details` test failed before the change and passes after it
- [x] `make verify`: all six checks pass
- [x] Result files scanned for keys; eval DB dropped

Before: each analysis was saved as one JSON row in `tenancy_reviews`, with a long reference you couldn't use to get back to it. If saving failed, the page showed a 503 error and no results. If Gemini was overloaded, the error didn't say to try again.

After: each analysis is saved in the Tiger Data case tables from `schema.sql` (`cases`, `tenants`, `agreements`, `clauses`, `flags`, `emails`) under a code like `FLAT-7KQ2XM`. The results page shows the code. The new "Already reviewed? Enter your case code" box, or a `/?case=CODE` link, reopens the review, so co-tenants can share it without logging in. If the database is down, the results are still shown, marked as unsaved. When Gemini is busy (429 or 5xx), the page says "Gemini is busy right now. Please try again in a minute."

How: the new `backend/app/cases.py` saves everything in one transaction, with clause rows batched, and reads it back in the `/api/analyze` shape. The new `GET /api/cases/{code}` endpoint returns a saved case. `schema.sql` replaces `tenancy_reviews` with 4 columns that a reopened case needs. `reviews.py` and the SQLite fallback are removed. Main (with the new UI) is merged in. Tests: the new `test_cases.py` needs `TEST_DATABASE_URL`, and its database tests are skipped without it. The API tests no longer write to the database configured in `.env`.

## Change and scope

One-flag follow-up under priority revision 6, card `p104-side-correction`. [#3349](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3349) shows the basis head meets the target final on only 4 of 208 matched flags (present-head class `(0,1,9,43)`). [#3392](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3392) pins one of the other 204 (absent-head flag 2). This package pins one of those four: flag 9 (`X4` → `Y23`, basis head `196`).

On the published 4,058-event word:

- `X4` starts at `[196]` and drops `196` at transport event 500
- every annotated `Y23` frame before the terminal transport avoids `196`
- the head appears on `Y23` only in the after-frame of event 3489 (gap 2989)
- no event names both endpoints; neither frame is restored

The published channel therefore cannot chronologically dirty-restore that source line into the matched target along co-hosted basis-head geometry, even though the target final contains the head.

**Scoped obstruction. No new kappa.** Selected κ stays 0.001672660197076918. Coefficient delivery (flag-0 cascade) is outside this package.

body:
**Own last run may still be open, checked first.** This seat's own `#347` is open against `main` right now (not a draft, no board \`done\` message posted for it yet as of this writing), and so are `#335` and `#332` from the night before, both still waiting on another merger under Tier B condition 1. Branched from `main` anyway rather than building on `#347`: that PR's own description already closes out three of this pass's four events (merging `#312`, `#343`, `#346`, and filing the "complete archive" claim with frontend), and the one event it does not touch is the one this PR is for. Same shape as every other pass today appending to `docs/sprints/pending.md` at the top rather than at a fixed anchor: whichever of `#347` / `#335` / `#332` / this one merges first gives the others a one-line keep-both.

## What this pass answers

One genuinely new event out of the four in this run's batch: a board handoff from `alexandra-systems/mba` addressed to this seat by name (`alexandra-systems` PR #216), subject "Your pricing page offers nothing purchasable five days after the committed launch, and nothing inside the company would have told you." The other three (PR #343 opening, PR #346 opening, the engineer's and writer's runs finishing) are already closed by `#347`, verified by reading its description rather than redoing its work.

## The finding

`libraryofalexandria.dev/pricing` renders "Opens shortly" with no href on both paid tiers. `POLAR_CHECKOUT_TRIAL`, `POLAR_CHECKOUT_MONTHLY`, `POLAR_CHECKOUT_LIFETIME` are all unset in the hosting environment. O1-KR1 committed both tiers purchasable end to end on 2026-10-13 — today is five days past that date with nothing on the page a person can buy.

MBA is precise about where the fault is not: the engineer's payments layer (entitlement, checkout route, webhook, fail-closed) shipped on the committed date and is good work. The blocking half is that the Polar account itself was never created, which `docs/product/polar-go-live.md` already names as a decision with the owner's name on it (ADR-30, ADR-31). MBA has already put that half to the owner directly, as this week's case's first recommendation, so this PR does not duplicate that ask.

## What's mine, and what I did with it

Nothing in either repository would have caught this. `tools/delivery_health.py` watches the failure *after* a sale (a verified payment that can't become access); nothing watches the failure *before* one (an offer that can't be bought at all). Two board handoffs sent this pass, both logged in `docs/sprints/pending.md`:

- **engineer** — add one outside-in probe to `tools/delivery_health.py`: fetch the public pricing page, assert at least one checkout link is present and resolves with a success status, fail otherwise. Same shape as the existing availability guardrail. MBA's own sizing: "a morning, not a project."
- **okr** — record in `docs/okrs/okrs-2026-Q4.md` that O1-KR1 is not met as of 2026-10-18, reason named as the payment account rather than the code, since the code shipped on time.

Both are board handoffs, not `gh workflow run` dispatches — the event bus is what has been waking this company's seats all pass (`docs/standards/pm.md` §17), and neither `docs/okrs/` nor `tools/` is this seat's writable surface, so the entries themselves aren't mine to write.

A reply posted to MBA on the board in first person, naming what's mine and what's done with it.

## Worth a register, not filed as one today

This is the same shape as incident 24 (a product surface fails silently because nothing outside-in watches it), on a surface `docs/agents/delivery-health.md`'s own table doesn't yet list (payments). It isn't a repeat of a prior entry, so the standing rule doesn't require filing it here. Named for the ExO seat, whose file this would extend with a fifth table row once engineer's probe exists.

## Run and delivery health

`#347`, open against `main` and roughly 30 minutes old at this writing, already reports `gh run list --limit 30` all green and the full delivery-health reading (press and site FAILING at thirteen days stale, deploy FAILING on two pending `modal deploy`s, pipeline/archive/mcp ok, payments previously "unknown, no seat holds the credential"). Not re-run here to avoid reporting a second, near-identical snapshot minutes later; this PR's contribution to that line is narrowing "payments: unknown" to the specific, now-named cause (checkout links unset, account never created) rather than leaving it unknown.

## Boundaries respected

Writable surface only: `docs/sprints/pending.md`. No charter, workflow, secret, or product code touched. No merge performed this pass — nothing in the open-PR list met the merge rule's conditions that `#347` hadn't already acted on.

author: nissa-seru
body:
**TL;DR:** `quiesce()` now writes the queue of deferred context writes before it changes the host's mode. So a write deferred behind a turn still alive is on disk before the host quiesces. When the queue can't reach disk, because its write fails or it's over its cap, `quiesce()` refuses with a new `QuiesceBlockedError` that names the ways out, and leaves the host's mode as it was, except when the call has `abandon: true`, which goes on with the queue in memory. Elsewhere, a write of the queue that fails still keeps the queue in memory, and it now raises a `deferred-writes` ops alert once a run, with a line when a write succeeds again. Without a recovery file, the queue's write is now synced.

## What was wrong

Probes on `main` (`b96e918`), on Linux with Node 24.22.0. Each staging ended with `process.exit`, standing in for a crash, and a fresh boot then resumed. Those runs aren't part of this PR.
- **A queue that can't be written.** With a directory where `deferred-writes.json` goes, a context write deferred while quiesced returned `''`, as one that was written does. The only sign was a line on stderr, `[host-mode] failed to persist deferred context writes: Error: EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, rename …`. After the exit, the boot restored no write, and the write never landed. With the directory gone, the next deferral wrote both writes, and both landed after an exit.
- **A write deferred before a quiesce.** A context write deferred behind a turn still alive, then a `quiesce()` whose drain timed out with that turn alive: `quiesce()` resolved (`drained: false`, `deferredWrites: 1`) with no queue file, and after the exit the write was gone. A deferral after `quiesce()` answered wrote both.
- **The cap.** With the record holding one small write, a write that took the queue's JSON past 4,194,304 characters logged `[host-mode] deferred context writes exceed 4194304 bytes serialized (2 message(s)) — kept in memory only; a crash before resume loses them`, and the record kept the small write alone. A small write after it logged nothing and wasn't written either. After the exit, the boot restored the first small write only.
- **Store only** (a store given, and no `storePath`). A context write deferred while quiesced was in the store's slot within the process, and after the exit the reopened store's slot was empty.

## Changes

- **`quiesce()` writes the queue first** (`writeDeferredWritesForQuiesce`), before anything else, on a first call and a repeat alike, as a quiesced host keeps it: the queue when it holds anything, and an empty queue over a record that held one.
  - **When the queue can't reach disk,** a call without `abandon` refuses with a `QuiesceBlockedError`, exported as `ResumeBlockedError` is, and the host's mode as it was: serving with no record written, or, on a repeat, quiesced with no abandon run.
  - **A write that fails** is the refusal's `cause`, and its message names the ways out: "So the queue as it stands, N deferred context write(s), isn't on disk. Once the record can be written, quiesce again, or quiesce with abandon: true, which cancels the turns still streaming, to go on with the queue in memory, and resume before any restart."
  - **A queue over the cap** writes nothing, and its refusal names the cap and the ways out. On a serving host that's "Quiesce again once they have landed, or quiesce with abandon: true to end the turns they wait for, then resume so they land, and quiesce again." On a quiesced one, it's "Resume so they land, then quiesce again. A write held for a turn still alive stays queued through a resume, so to end a turn that won't, quiesce with abandon: true before resuming." Both end: "The abandon's answer lists a turn it can't end as unabandonable, and its writes land once it has ended and the host is serving."
  - **A call with `abandon: true` goes on** past either, with the failure's or the cap's ops alert, as elsewhere. So it's also how to quiesce anyway: the queue stays in memory, not on disk, so an operator resumes before restarting, since a restart restores only what the record last held, or, with #454, doesn't start if it can't read the record. On a host that is quiesced, or that an abandon is quiescing, the alert and the cap's line end "Resume before any restart".
  - **The ingresses answer the refusal as they answer `resume()`'s:** the HTTP `/quiesce` route with a 409 and the host's mode, and `host/command` with `ok: false` and the host's mode.
  - **If the queue's write succeeds and the record's then fails,** the host serves with its queue written, and, as for any queue on its record, each change writes it again until it drains.
  - **Writes a flush landed** stay in the queue until a store sync acks them, so `quiesce()` first retries an ack whose sync failed. Once a sync succeeds, they leave the queue rather than count against the cap.
- **Elsewhere, a write that fails** (`persistDeferredWrites`) still logs its line and keeps the queue in memory. The queue now stays mirrored (`deferredWritesPersisted`), so its next change writes it again. A run's first failure raises a `deferred-writes` ops alert naming the record, and a write that succeeds ends the run with `[host-mode] <record> written again: it holds the queue's N deferred context write(s)`.
- **Over the cap, elsewhere,** the record isn't written and keeps what it last held, as on `main`, and the queue now stays mirrored. The cap raises the same alert when it begins a run. Its line is logged the first time the cap is met in a run, whatever began the run, where on `main` it was logged once a process.
- **Store only,** the slot's write is followed by `store.sync()`, as `persistHostMode`'s is, and a sync that fails counts as a failed write. The slot is set before the sync, so a later sync can still put a write whose sync failed on disk. The queue is marked mirrored before the write, so after a failed sync, `quiesce()`'s included, the queue's next change writes the slot again.
- **The cap's constant** is renamed `DEFERRED_WRITES_PERSIST_CAP_CHARS`, since it's compared with the JSON's length in UTF-16 code units, which the messages call characters. The alert's data names it `capCharacters`.
- **The text:** the doc comments of `quiesce()`, `persistDeferredWrites`, the cap and the flags say so, and so does `resume()`'s note that deferred writes survive a restart. The README's quiesce example names the new error.

## What each part is for

- **The queue's write at the top of `runQuiesce`:** a write deferred behind a live turn is on disk before the host quiesces, so a quiesce that answers with that turn alive no longer leaves it in memory alone. Coming first, its refusal comes before the mode changes, as #453's order does for the record's failure. On a repeat call, it's an operator's way to write the queue again.
- **The refusals in `quiesce()`:** a queue whose write failed, or that's over the cap, isn't on disk, and an operator who quiesces before a restart would lose it. The failed write's refusal keeps the write's error as its `cause`, so the reason isn't lost behind the ways out.
- **The ack retried before the queue's write:** without it, writes that a `resume()` landed, and whose ack's sync failed, stay in the queue, since nothing retries the ack until a later flush, a turn's tool boundary or `stop()`. Over the cap, every plain `quiesce()` then refuses on a healthy host, and the ways out it names can't clear it.
- **`abandon: true` past either refusal:** the queue stays in memory whichever way the call goes, and writes held for a turn that won't end stay queued through `resume()`, which keeps every write whose target's turn is alive (`flushDeferredWrites`). Refusing the abandon too would leave only a restart, which loses the queue. The abandon cancels the turn's stream, and `resume()` then lands its writes. A turn holding its token with no stream can't be cancelled, as on `main`: the abandon lists it as unabandonable, and its writes land once it h

## Summary

MSHL-151 (Feed T11): the Feed gets its control source.

- `feedStore.recordFeedControlPacket(packet)`, called by the `raw_packet` handler right after `recordRawPacket`: one flag check when the store is inactive; otherwise header/label classification, decode through the T1 cache (once per observation), dedupe by observation key, bound `FEED_CONTROL_MAX = 500` control packets, seeded from `rawPacketStore` at activation. `onReconnect` clears the raw buffer but not these rows.
- `FeedControlRow`: type/subtype badges, "Paired" badge (scrolls to the twin and highlights it), from → to with `PeerName` (contact sheet), channel link for GroupData, decrypted GroupData text or the locked envelope (dest/src), click opens `RawPacketInspectorDialog`. Keys reuse `controlJournal.*`; shared pieces moved to `controlParts.tsx` (the Control journal uses them too, its snapshot is unchanged).
- Nodes facet (`md:w-64` column, sheet on a phone): repeaters and rooms, channels, us, unresolved, with counts. The pick is `FeedFilters.node` (per browser).
- Source chip "Control" enabled and on by default. Messages and control rows are interleaved by time (`received_at` vs `packet.timestamp`).

## Design choices (to review)

- A **channel node** narrows the messages to that channel; **any other node hides the messages** (the ticket only says "filters control rows (and message rows of that channel when the node is a channel)").
- `hasEmptySelection` now means "nothing at all can show"; the new `hasNoMessages` is the old message-only meaning (no request is sent with Messages off).
- A stored node that no longer exists filters nothing.
- When the twin of a "Paired" badge is filtered out (other thread), the badge is plain text.

## Left out on purpose

- Folding the Control journal into the feed (the Control preset ticket); `ControlJournalView` is untouched apart from importing the shared parts.
- Control rows do not follow the muted/pending channel chips.
- No hot file touched (`app/*`, `types.ts`, `wsEvents.ts`, `MessageList.tsx`, `/api/health` all untouched).

## Docs checked or updated

- `frontend/AGENTS.md`: packet-subscriber list, control rows + reconnect rule + bound, Feed section (control source, Nodes facet), decode cache note.

- `docs/user/`: no page describes the Feed yet (checked), nothing to update.

`feedControlRows.test.tsx` (port of every `controlJournalView.test.tsx` case: four types only, GroupText ignored, locked card keeps dest/src, Us node from prefix, AnonRequest sender, inspector click, i18n parity; plus pairing, facet, 500 control + 200 messages under the DOM cap, `MeshCoreDecoder.decode` spy), `feedStore.test.ts` (control section), `useRealtimeAppState.test.ts` (inactive, reconnect keeps rows, no duplicate), `appFeedIsolation.test.tsx`, `feedFilters.test.ts`.

  - `simple status`、`events`，程序日志和控制台输出的区别；
  - MTP 的筛选写法；契约测试对真 RIoT 的规矩（ADR 0047）；
  - "默认不指向任何真实东西"在日常操作里意味着什么。
- **README** 加一节"本地起停与场景"，远端一节写上新命令。
- **仓库 `CLAUDE.md`** 加一行指向这份说明，`simple remote` 的命令清单加上 `scenario`。原文由产品负责人 2026-10-18 在工作会话里确认。
- **新命令 `simple remote scenario run|list|validate`**（协调者定在本票里做）。原来在远端跑场景要写 `simple remote exec -- pwsh -File ./simple.ps1 scenario run <场景> --server-key-store Machine`，证据也带不回来；新开的会话最可能卡在这里。现在：
  - `run` 和 `test` 一样送快照、占一个名额。远端自己带上场景实例（`<实例名>-scenario`）、本机级钥匙存储和 `--evidence <这次运行的目录>`，证据随输出拷回 `artifacts/remote/<实例名>/`。退出码就是判定（0、10、11、12），远端自己的失败仍是 20、21、22。
  - `list`、`validate` 送快照、不占名额，所以本机刚写、没提交的场景也能在远端校验。
  - 场景写成路径时，必须是本克隆里、没被 `.gitignore` 排除的 `.yaml`。
  - 不收 `--evidence`、`--server-key-store`、`--instance`（写在 `--` 后时）和 `--keep-up`。`run` 不带场景或带多个、`list` 带场景，都在本机直接以 2 拒绝。
  - `simple remote forget` 先重置场景实例，删掉它的库和本机级钥匙；不然这些会比远端的 worktree 活得长。重置失败时保留实例，并以那条命令的退出码结束。

`scenarios/README.md` 里"在 simple01 上用 `exec`"那一行，换成了新命令和一小节"在远端机器上跑"。

## 怎么验证的

- **完成判据（演练）**：一个只拿到 `docs/agents/testing.md` 的子代理，从干净克隆出发、经 `simple remote` 在远端完成了四步：
  - `infrastructure-up` 判 holds，退出码 0；
  - 自己新写一个场景："假 MES 读取失败后从不记下 `mes.unreachable`"；
  - 这个场景 `validate` 通过、运行判 does-not-hold，退出码 10；
  - 读了拷回本机的 `result.json`：失败的期望、理由、`teardown.stopped: true`。

  它停下来猜过的地方都已改进说明。其中最要紧的一条：没有 bug 的"故意写红"场景用完要删掉，留着会让 CI 变红。
- **独立审查**：审查子代理审了两轮，第一轮的发现除"状态目录残留"一条（见文末）外都已修好，第二轮没有新缺陷，只提了三处小问题，也已修好。
- **测试**：
  - 远端全量测试：提交 44203cf 上 974 个全过（另有一次在 a4e0786 上 `Simple.Logging.Tests` 的一个测试偶发失败，本 PR 未碰该项目，已交协调者）。
  - `RemoteCommandTests`、`RemoteRunTests` 在本机一起跑，96 个全过。
  - `dotnet restore simple.slnx --locked-mode` 通过（没有改包和 lock 文件）。
- **实测**：在远端实测 `simple remote scenario run deliberately-wrong`，以 10 结束，证据目录拷回本机。

## 没做的、留给后续

`simple remote forget` 之后，远端 `SIMPLE_HOME` 下实例的状态目录（`instances/<实例名>`、`instances/<实例名>-scenario`）仍会留下。主实例在本 PR 之前就是这样，已经交协调者另行处理。本机删 worktree 时，场景实例的库也会留在 LocalDB 上，同样已交协调者。

Closes #84

body:
## Summary

Stacked on #273 (base `devin/ikot-completion`; GitHub retargets to staging when #273 merges). Adds `supabase/migrations/0018_review.sql`, the database half of Draft → Pending → Approved (`studio-maps/01`). **Not applied.** The owner applies it by pasting `supabase/apply/0018_apply.sql` into the SQL editor (steps in `supabase/apply/README.md`), then regenerates the types. Commuters and the studio see no change once it's applied: every existing row becomes `approved`, and the studio keeps writing live rows until Batch 4.

- **`route`/`stop`**: `status` (`approved` | `taken_down`, default `approved`), `status_at`, `revision`; plus `stop.updated_at` with the touch trigger.
- **`route.revision` is the aggregate conflict version.** A trigger on `route_variant` bumps it on every insert, update or delete, so it covers geometry and signboards. `route.updated_at` misses those changes. Because the bump happens under the route's row lock, direction writes are also serialised against approval.
- **Approved-only partial uniqueness** for `route_ends_unique`, `route_loop_unique` (0021) and `stop_terminal_place_unique`. The index names stay the same because the studio matches on them. A taken-down row never blocks a new one. Putting a taken-down row back over a newer approved one is refused by the same index (23505).
- **Guards** (triggers, `security definer`):
  - `route_approved_ends`: a route can be approved only if both ends are approved. Ikot routes (null ends) pass. The ends are read `FOR SHARE`.
  - `stop_takedown_guard`: a hotspot that ends an approved route can't be taken down.
  - Both race orders were tested with two sessions. Each time the second operation is refused.
- **Reads**: `anon` and non-editor `authenticated` users see approved rows only. A direction needs an approved route. A link needs an approved route and an approved hotspot. Editors see everything, so `private.loop_one_way` still sees a taken-down loop. The publish reads as `anon`, so its queries don't change.
- **New tables**, each with explicit grants (0017):
  - `draft`: one per subject (`unique (kind, subject_id)`), with a versioned payload, `base_revision` and its own `revision`.
  - `takedown`: written only by a trigger on status changes. Put-back fills `put_back_at`. `anon` can read only `kind, subject_id, taken_down_at, put_back_at`, for Batch 3's shrink guard.
  - `editor_name`: editors can read it; the owner fills it by hand.

## Applying it (`supabase/apply/`)
- `0018_apply.sql` is a single transaction:
  1. Refuses if `0021_loops` is not applied.
  2. Records what `anon` reads.
  3. Applies `0018_review.sql` unchanged. `run.sh` diffs the copy.
  4. Checks that `anon` reads exactly the same rows, that no other read rule would show taken-down rows, and that the three indexes are partial on `approved`.
  5. Writes the `0018_review` ledger row once.

  Any failed check raises and nothing changes. It's safe to run twice.
- `0018_check.sql`: 13 read-only checks, one row each.
- `0018_revert.sql`: a single transaction that undoes 0018 and deletes the ledger row. It refuses once a takedown or a draft exists.
- Review fix: `bump_revision` now forces `revision > old.revision`, so an editor writing `revision` by hand can't move it backwards.

## Verification

`supabase/verify/run.sh` on a throwaway Docker `postgres:17`, with Supabase stand-ins in `bootstrap.sql`:
1. Builds a database from all migrations in ledger order.
2. Inserts rows.
3. Applies 0018 twice (it is safe to re-run).
4. Runs `after-0018.sql`, which covers role reads/denials, uniqueness, guards, the takedown log, revision counting and draft rules.
5. Runs `concurrency.sh`.

6. Applies through `0018_apply.sql` twice and checks there is one ledger row, then requires every `0018_check.sql` row to be true.
7. Checks the revert refuses over a takedown.
8. On a second database: dumps the schema, applies, reverts, and requires the dump to be identical.

Also checked for Ikot: an approved loop with no ends passes the ends guard; `anon` sees only approved loops and their directions; a loop's direction write bumps its `revision`; a taken-down loop doesn't block a new one with the same signboard.

Result: all passed (73859d9).

Not covered: real Supabase/PostgREST behaviour; that needs the live apply.

## Follow-ups (Batch 4, after the apply + type regeneration)
- `claimExistingRoute` / `claimExistingLoop` must filter `status = 'approved'`. Until something is taken down there's no difference.
- The approval transaction (RPC) will be added with the studio draft work.

author: 99yash
body:
## Where this change sits

`pnpm check` runs `scripts/check-consolidation-drift.mjs`. That script runs the fixtures in `scripts/consolidation-rules.selftest.mjs` first. Then it runs the `gate` rules in `scripts/consolidation-rules.mjs` over every source file. The edit-time hook `.claude/hooks/helper-hints.mjs` reads the same rule table.

This change touches only the `sha256-over-json-stringify` rule, the helpers that only this rule uses (`JSON_ARGUMENT`, `nearestBindingGap`, and the new `boundJsonArgument`), and its fixture group. It does not change product code. It does not change a shared helper (`importBinding`, `importedInFile`, `exposedModuleConst`, `CONSTANTS_MODULE`) or another rule.

## Why this change is needed

#1375 listed these "Holes that remain" for `sha256-over-json-stringify`:

- Bound bytes fed to a hasher were not read. Only `subtle.digest` read bound bytes. So `const buf = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(x)); createHash("sha256").update(buf)` was missed. The same shape with a bound hasher (`hash.update(buf)`) or with `new TextEncoder().encode(…)` was also missed.
- The nearest-binding relation counted only a `const`/`let`/`var`. A parameter of the same name in a second function still related to an earlier binding. A plain reassignment between the binding and the use did not break the relation.
- `JSON_ARGUMENT` stopped at the first paren, comma or `;`. JSON after a call or after a comma inside the argument was not read.

Each missed shape hashes a pre-image that depends on object key order. That is the bug the rule exists for (#571).

## What this change does

- New helper `boundJsonArgument(group)`. The whole call argument is a name, and the nearest binding of that name above it is JSON. JSON is a `JSON.stringify(…)`, alone or joined with other text (`JSON_ARGUMENT`), or its bytes (`ENCODED_JSON`: `TextEncoder`, a bound encoder, or `Buffer.from`). The binding is a `const`/`let`/`var` or a plain assignment. `==`, `===` and `=>` are not a binding.
- The rule now reads a bound name in three places:
  - `createHash(…).update(name)` and `createHash(…).update(name, "utf8")`.
  - `hash.update(name)` on a bound hasher. Both names relate to their own nearest binding.
  - `subtle.digest(alg, name)`. This replaces the old fourth branch. The binding can now also be a plain assignment.
- A hasher also reads a bound JSON string (`const preimage = JSON.stringify(x); hash.update(preimage)`). A hasher takes a string as well as bytes, so the pre-image is the same.
- `nearestBindingGap` now also stops at:
  - a plain assignment to the name (`bytes = other`), but not at `x.bytes = other` and not at `bytes === other`. A bare arrow parameter (`bytes =>`) also stops it.
  - the name in the parameter list of a `function`.
  - the name in a paren group directly followed by `=>`, or by a return type and `=>` (an arrow parameter list).
- `JSON_ARGUMENT` now also reads:
  - a closed paren group before the JSON (`` `${scope(kind, id)}:${JSON.stringify(x)}` ``);
  - a closed bracket group before the JSON;
  - one open bracket group that holds the JSON (`[kind, JSON.stringify(x)].join(":")`).

  Outside those groups the text still holds no paren, comma or `;`. So the match cannot leave the argument it starts in. A `(` has one reading and a `[` has at most two. Neither group can hold another `(` or `[`. So the cost stays linear in the argument: one argument with 2000 open `[` takes less than 1 ms.
- The rule comment states the hasher relation, the new rebinding forms and the method-parameter limit.
- New must-catch fixtures, each with its `rule`: `Buffer.from` of JSON bound first, then fed to `createHash(…).update`; encoded JSON bound first, then fed to a bound hasher; JSON text bound first, then fed to a hasher with an encoding argument; encoded JSON assigned after the declaration, then digested; JSON after a call inside the hashed argument; JSON after a comma in an array literal inside the hashed argument.
- New must-ignore fixtures: a second function that takes the encoded name as a parameter; a second function that takes the hasher name as a parameter; an arrow that takes the JSON name as a parameter; the encoded name reassigned to raw bytes before the digest; a bound name that is not JSON fed to a hasher (raw bytes, and a name that is only compared to JSON); JSON after the hashed call returns.

## Preserved behavior

- The rule id, severity, `scope`, `owners` and `fix` text do not change.
- Every fixture that passed before still passes.
- The drift scan of the tree still reports zero hits. The one raw match in the tree is still the `gmail-webhook.ts` receipt digest (line 214). It keeps its `// drift-ok:` marker. No new raw match appears.
- Proof:
  - I copied the new `consolidation-rules.mjs` to `/tmp`. I put the `origin/main` version back with `git show origin/main:scripts/consolidation-rules.mjs > scripts/consolidation-rules.mjs` and kept the new fixtures. `node scripts/check-consolidation-drift.mjs` then exits 1 with 9 failures: the 6 new must-catch fixtures are missed, and 3 new must-ignore fixtures are flagged (the two second-function parameter fixtures and the reassignment fixture). Then I restored the new file from the `/tmp` copy (`cmp` equal).
  - 3 new must-ignore fixtures also pass on the old rule. I kept them because each one guards a new branch against a false positive. I ran each mutation on a copy of the new rule:
    - "an arrow takes the JSON name as a parameter": remove the arrow-parameter stop from `nearestBindingGap`, and the fixture is flagged.
    - "a bound name that is not JSON fed to a hasher": widen the `JSON_ARGUMENT` prefix to `[\s\S]*?`, and `hash.update(buf)` is flagged. Remove the `(?![=>])` guard from the binding, and `update(body)` after `body === JSON.stringify(previous)` is flagged.
    - "JSON after the hashed call returns": let the paren group cross a paren (`\([^;]*?\)`), and the fixture is flagged.
  - With the new rule, `node scripts/check-consolidation-drift.mjs` exits 0 and prints `no drift`.
- Cost, measured as in #1375 (the rule regex alone, `matchAll` over 1640 files, five runs after one warm-up run):
  - `origin/main`: about 67 to 70 ms.
  - This change: about 78 to 90 ms. Most of the increase is the scan back to the nearest binding at each `.update(name)`, which is also how Drizzle writes `db.update(table)`. The `JSON_ARGUMENT` change alone adds no measurable time.
  - A dense case is quadratic: 3000 `db.update(table)` lines in one 54 KB file take about 0.7 s. The densest file in the tree has 13 such calls, and the old `subtle.digest(alg, name)` branch has the same shape.
  - `node scripts/check-consolidation-drift.mjs` takes about 1.5 s.
- Verification:
  - `node scripts/check-consolidation-drift.mjs`: exit 0.
  - `pnpm check`: exit 0.
  - `pnpm check-types`: exit 0 (16 of 16 tasks, then `tsc -p scripts/tsconfig.json`).
  - `oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json --report-unused-disable-directives-severity=error` on both files: exit 0.
  - `oxfmt --check` on both files: exit 0.

## Holes that remain

- A method parameter does not break the relation. In `name(bytes: T) {` the head is the same text as a call followed by a block (`if (bytes) {`), and a regex cannot tell the two apart. So a class or object method that takes `bytes`, below a binding of `bytes` to JSON in the same file, is flagged. That error fails loud, and a `// drift-ok:` marker clears it.
- A destructured binding (`const { bytes } = x`) and a `catch (bytes)` do not break the relation. These also fail loud.
- An inner callback that takes the same name as a parameter, between the binding and the use in the same scope, breaks the relation. That use is then missed. The callback scope closed before the use, but a regex cannot see scope ends.
- `JSON_ARGUMENT` reads one level of paren group, and one open bracket group. JSON inside an object literal with a comma before it (`{ a, b: JSON.stringify(x) }`), inside a second open bracket, or inside another call (`f([a

author: aditi-dewangan
body:
**Builds on #22.** It includes #22's commit, so merge #22 first. Merging only this PR also brings in both.

## Why
A judge whose iPhone defaults to Chrome scans the kiosk QR and lands in Chrome. On iPhone, Chrome can't use speech recognition and asks for the camera and mic on every visit. Safari can do both, and can be set to always allow.

## What
- `safariHandoff.ts`: on Chrome, Firefox or Edge on iPhone, the app opens the same page in Safari with `x-safari-https://allscreen.work/...` (iOS 17+). It does this **before connecting**, so the kiosk isn't held by the Chrome tab.
- QR links (`/k/...?t=` one-time token) are converted to the kiosk's fixed code (`/c/FD54937`), so they can't expire on the way to Safari.
- The screen shows "Opening in Safari…" with a **Stay in this browser instead** button.
  - Safari takes over → this tab shows "Continued in Safari" and doesn't connect.
  - Nothing happens in 6s (older iOS, or the person declined) → it continues in the same browser by itself.
- Never runs in Safari, on Android or desktop, with `?stay`, or after "stay" was chosen in that tab.

## Tested (Chromium with iPhone user agents)
- iPhone Chrome QR link → handoff screen, kiosk not held while waiting. With no Safari, it continued at `/c/FD54937` and connected.
- Page hidden (Safari took over) → this tab never connects.
- "Stay" → connects right away.
- iPhone Safari → no handoff.
- Typecheck and build are clean.

Not testable here: the real Safari jump. Chrome may show one "Open in Safari?" confirmation, which websites can't skip. Needs a try on an iPhone with Chrome as the default browser.

body:
First usable version: everything needed for two people to pick an episode and watch it together from their own copies.

## What's in it
- **Watch together**: the host clicks Play, and the guest gets a *"Tyler is starting … [Join]"* banner through a tiny invite file that Syncthing already carries. No server, no open ports.
- **Artwork** from TMDB (posters + episode stills), cached in the shared `.movienight/art` folder so the guest needs no key.
- **Download status** on the guest side (ready / downloading / queued + GB left) from Syncthing's REST API.
- **Continue watching** and a **Restart player** button.
- **Syncplay settings check + one-click fix** for the settings behind the 00:00 jumps and "not ready" stalls.
- **Zero-config first run**: libraries and name from Syncplay's settings; host/guest from the Syncthing folder type.
- Item IDs now derive from show/season/episode or title/year, so they match across machines.

## Testing
- `go test ./...`: parser, library scan (auto kind, pending files, extras), Syncplay settings read/fix, artwork fetcher against a fake TMDB server, and the host → guest invite flow through the HTTP API.
- Run live on the host: role detected as host via Syncthing, 15 shows / 273 episodes / 50 movies, UI checked in a browser.
- **Not yet verified live:** real TMDB requests (waiting on the API key being added to the config), and the guest side on Dad's machine.

Paid wall autofill previously wrote Overlay material directly. Human and AI placement use the same path; refused fillers remain in limbo while scanning continues. This fixes the omitted dependency in #1902.

The early wall arm owns admission, optional old-wall sale, Overlay Mark, owner publication, radio break, transient sight and UnInit. Shared hosted Mark now also serves crate placement under its native placement scope. Factory accounting retains its product token through pointer expiry and records the still-retained constructor identity before the normal drain. No new RNG, identity, lifecycle, visibility or serialized-state owner was added; superseded material-only routes were removed.

Native behavior established from original SHA256 `1cdd1180e49024fbda8ad568caac2e86e856063ff67ab38f62b7d2c7bb84298c`: whole `588750`, `45E880/43B740/6F2B40`, early `440580`, Overlay `5FD270/5FEA30`, radio/sight, `5F65F0` and deferred `725C70`. A consumed original-code corpus executes no-gap, two-fill and middle-refusal/later-direction controls. Rust compares complete three-stream RNG states, ordered retained Building identities and mixed deferred queue, registry counts and selected object/Cell/House state at entry/autofill/drain. It does not dynamically compare every retained semantic call/request or raw timer field. Radio/sight ordering additionally rests on instructions and source integration.

- Genuine ordinary paid-lifetime and requested-Overlay-coordinate regressions failed before the fixes and passed afterward. Focused placement64, crates89, AIexit12 and FactoryAI5 passed.
- Paid GPU coverage passed all five native wall raster rows across two ordinary histories; authored CAFNCB coverage passed. No raster golden was replaced or weakened.

The first joined attempt lacked FIRE01 before comparison; external input views were corrected to exact recorded physical bytes/inventories. Source and254 frozen input paths read back unchanged.

Credits8500/spent1500; attacked endpoint and target clear at2730, MTNK returns to Guard. Earlier PR1904 baseline comparison remains a raw MISMATCH, and includes intervening House/Techno changes; it is not a sole-change causal or native whole-world/RGB A/B.

Coverage is bounded to ordinary GAWALL and declared native controls. Wider type/ToOverlay combinations, Dummy/nonselected coordinates, callback/reentrancy/capacity domains, cold vision, failed-survivor shutdown, platform/scale and native whole-world/RGB equivalence remain open.
