body:
## 目的

Issue #420「多言語と公開記事のXML sitemap生成を整備」を実装する。公開状態の URL だけを `<loc>` に載せ、`lang` 別の alternate と各 route の `rel="canonical"` と整合させる。i18n route が未着地の現時点では、日本語（`lang="ja"`）1 言語で単体完了させる。

Refs #420

## 実装

| ファイル | 役割 |
| --- | --- |
| `src/http/seo/sitemap.ts` | 依存ゼロの純粋モジュール。静的 inventory（`SITEMAP_ENTRIES`）、生成 family（`SITEMAP_DYNAMIC_ROUTES`）、除外理由つきの `SITEMAP_EXCLUSIONS`、XML / robots.txt レンダラ。 |
| `src/http/seo/router.ts` | `GET /sitemap.xml` / `GET /robots.txt`。DI seam（`createSeoRouter(loadProjects)`）。 |
| `src/http/seo/README.md` | 契約と各ガードの責務。 |
| `src/portfolio/{contract,load,schema}.ts` | `PortfolioLoader.listPublishedProjectIndex()` を追加。 |
| `src/server.ts` / `src/http/hono.ts` | `EXTERNAL_BOUNDARY_PREFIXES` に `/sitemap.xml` と `/robots.txt` を追加（完全一致）、seo router を mount。 |
| `src/routes/index.tsx` / `src/routes/tools.index.tsx` | canonical 未宣言だった公開 route に `rel="canonical"` を追加。 |
| `scripts/check-sitemap-route-coverage.test.mjs` | route 被覆ガード（`pnpm run test` に配線済み）。 |
| `scripts/make-sitemap-verification-report.mjs` | スクリーンショットの再現可能な生成元（#452 と同じ流儀）。 |
| `AGENTS.md` §3 | 依存方向表に `http/seo -> portfolio` を追記。 |

### 設計判断

**なぜ Hono が持つのか。** TanStack Start 1.168 には raw response を返す route primitive が無く、route file では XML body を返せない（route は必ず document shell を通る）。ADR-0002 §2 が「SSR パイプラインが答えられないもの」を Worker entry 側の分岐としているため、そこに乗せる。これは ADR-0002 の re-evaluation trigger「TanStack Start が first-class HTTP-route primitive を出す」と同じ出来事で、primitive が入ったら `src/routes/` に戻す（コメントに明記）。

**公開可否フィルタは portfolio 側にだけ置く。** sitemap 側で SQL を再掲すると公開境界が二重化する。`listPublishedProjectIndex()` は `status='published' AND visibility='public'` の 2 列だけを 1 クエリで返し、JavaScript 側の `isVisible` でも再確認する（defence in depth）。Draft / unlisted / archived はこの.obligation に入らない。

**多言語（hreflang）。** 全公開 route が `lang="ja"` 1 言語なので、各 `<url>` は `xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang="ja"` の自己参照を 1 つだけ持つ。存在しない言語を捏造しない。locale 付き route が来た場合は entry ごとに alternate を増やすだけで、`<loc>` と同じ entry から alternate を導出しているため hreflang が双 reciprocity になる。

**canonical 整合。** 「`<loc>` は必ずそのページの canonical URL」という契約を成立させるため、canonical を宣言していなかった `/` と `/tools` に `rel="canonical"` を追加した。ガードが route source の canonical literal と照合するため、以後は二重管理にならない。

**`/tools/$slug` は除外。** route 自身が `robots: noindex` を宣言している。sitemap に載せたら指しているページと矛盾する。`/tools`（index）自体は公開・canonical なので掲載する。

## 受け入れ条件の対応

| 条件 | 対応 |
| --- | --- |
| draft / 未掲載 / 404 URL が載らない | ①`listPublishedProjectIndex` の `status='published' AND visibility='public'` + JS 側 `isVisible`（実 D1 で draft/unlisted/archived 3 種を検証）。②route grammar に一致しない slug（`../etc/passwd` / `Nested/Slug` / 空 / 先頭ハイフン / 129 文字）は builder が drop。 |
| 1 Issue = 1 PR で独立検証可能な fixture / 表示または report | `sitemap.test.ts`（純関数の document 契約）／`router.test.ts`（DI fixture の HTTP 契約）／`portfolio/load.test.ts`（実 D1 の公開境界）／`check-sitemap-route-coverage.test.mjs`（route 被覆）／コミット済み WebP スクリーンショット。 |
| 現行 route / framework 契約を保持し未完成 feature に依存させない | 新規 route 0、既存 framework API の変更 0。i18n route に依存せず hreflang は 1 言語のみ。 |
| 誤検知と未実装 route を無言の合格にしない | 被覆ガードが `src/routeTree.gen.ts` の全 route を「静的掲載 / 生成 family / 理由付き除外」に分類し、未分類があれば失敗。逆向き（実在しない route の掲載）も失敗。`<loc>` と route 宣言 canonical の不一致も失敗。**ガードを実際に壊して red になることを確認済み**（`/design-system` を inventory から外して 1 failing で、元に戻して 5 passing）。 |
| 導入範囲の test / CI 実行結果と環境を記録する | 下記「検証」。 |

## 検証

### ローカル（cheap checks のみ）

| コマンド | 結果 |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm exec biome format --write` / `lint`（変更ファイル） | pass |
| `pnpm run architecture:check` | `obligation boundaries OK` |
| `pnpm run test:wiring:check` | `all 39 scripts/*.test.mjs files are reachable from a test entry point` |
| `node scripts/check-d1-sql-binding.mjs`（release-0-6-3 取り込み後に追加されたゲート） | `no interpolated D1 statement in src/` |
| `node --experimental-strip-types --test scripts/check-sitemap-route-coverage.test.mjs` | 5 pass / 0 fail |
| `pnpm exec vitest run src/http/seo src/portfolio/load.test.ts`（workerd） | 3 files / 64 tests pass |
| `pnpm run typecheck`（host semaphore 経由） | pass |

### CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` の `validate` ジョブ（= `validate:integration`）が最終 head で **success**:

- run: https://github.com/rebuildup/my-web-2026/actions/runs/39094337751
- head: `9facfd286db625d60be2325a9aa9a8feefb4928a`
- `vitest run`: **39 files / 509 tests passed**（うち `src/http/seo/sitemap.test.ts` 22 tests、`src/http/seo/router.test.ts` 6 tests）
- `node --test scripts/check-sitemap-route-coverage.test.mjs`: 5 subtests ok（CI の Node 22.18 でも通ることを確認）
- 上流 (#452) が追加した `scripts/check-d1-sql-binding.mjs` / `check-d1-sql-binding.test.mjs` 10 tests も pass

Note: base の `release-0-6-3` は本作業中に #539 で前進したため、途中 head で conflict になり `origin/release-0-6-3` を merge した（`package.json` の `test` script は双方のステップを保持、conflict 解消後に再 push）。

## スクリーンショット

![sitemap.xml をブラウザで開いた様子](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rebuildup/my-web-2026/9facfd286db625d60be2325a9aa9a8feefb4928a/docs/verification/seo/sitemap-browser.webp)

- 保存先: `docs/verification/seo/sitemap-browser.webp`（Issue が要求する `docs/verification/seo/sitemap-browser.png` の **`.webp` 代替**。PNG は同等の内容で 2 倍以上のサイズになり、リポジトリを無意味に膨らませるため。#452 と同じ判断）
- 生成コマンド: `pnpm run verify:sitemap-screenshot`（= `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/make-sitemap-verification-report.mjs`）
- 何を描くか: 出荷する `src/http/seo/sitemap.ts` を **リポジトリ自身の fixture**（`PORTFOLIO_SEED`）で描画し、ローカル HTTP サーバで `application/xml` として配信したものを Playwright chromium（E2E と同じもの）で 1280x1600 で撮影。
- オフラインで実行する理由: `pnpm run dev` は Infisical 経由（ADR-0015）なので検証生成物から依存を外す。document builder は Worker が配信するものと同一の純粋モジュールなので、描画されるのは出荷バイトと同一。
- secret を一切読まない / Cloudflare リソースに触らない / `.tmp/` の中間物のみ（WebP だけ commit）。
- 期待結果: 静的 6 件 + fixture プロジェクト 6 件 = `<url>` 12 個。各 `<url>` は `https://rebuildup.dev/…` の `<loc>` と `hreflang="ja"` の自己参照を持つ。`/admin*` と `/tools/<slug>` は含まれない。fixture 行に `updated_at` が無いため `<lastmod>` は出ない（「推測しない」挙動）。
- 本番での再現: `curl -sS https://rebuildup.dev/sitemap.xml | head -30` / `curl -sSI https://rebuildup.dev/sitemap.xml` で `content-type: application/xml; charset=utf-8` と `cache-control: public, max-age=300, must-revalidate` を確認できる（マージ後に production へ出た時点から有効）。

## 既知の制約

- **production 反映は merge 後。** 本 PR は release-0-6-3 へ merge されるまで production には効かない。`/sitemap.xml` は Worker entry の prefix 一覧による経路。
- **`SITEMAP_ORIGIN` と route head の canonical literal は 2 箇所。** 建築上の都合（route 層は `http` 層を import しない、ADR-0002 §1「両層は互いに import しない」）。被覆ガードが両者を照合するので silent な drift は起きないが、origin を変えるときは route 6 ファイルと sitemap module の両方を触る必要がある。
- **`/design-system` の掲載判断。** 公開・canonical・nav リンク済みだが「内部向け showcase」という性格もある。technical には indexable なので掲載している。除外する場合も `SITEMAP_ENTRIES` から 1 エントリ消すだけで、被覆ガードは「未分類 route 」として red になる（黙って消えることはない）。owner 判断が必要なら本 PR で変える。
- **`lastmod` は portfolio detail にしか付かない。** 静的ページに対応する更新時刻の source of truth がリポジトリに無いため、`lastmod` を推測せず省いている。
- **`Cache-Control` は 5 分。** sitemap の鮮度と origin 負荷のトレードオフ。project 数や crawl 頻度を観測してから調整する。
- **production D1 の実データは未確認。** 公開境界は実 D1 の unit test で担保しているが、`/sitemap.xml` が本番で何件になるかはマージ後に確認が必要（fixture での 12 `<url>` は seed ベースであり、本番の件数ではない）。

author: dotcoocoo
body:
## What and why

A move that Shift kept level, upright or diagonal left that line when it snapped. With View › Snap to Grid on, a level Shift-drag with the Selection tool also moved the selection up or down onto a gridline, and Snap to Pixel, Smart Guides and Snap to Point moved it off the line in the same way. Each axis snapped on its own after Shift had constrained the move. The reference app's help says that Shift constrains a move "so that they move in a precise horizontal, vertical, or diagonal direction", and that snapping helps "position objects as you move them" ([Move objects](https://web.archive.org/web/20250115013546/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/moving-aligning-distributing-objects.html)). The page does not say how the two combine, so this change follows VectorCraft's own rule: the move stays on its line and slides along it until it snaps.

- With the Selection tool, and with Group Selection and Direct Selection moving whole objects, a Shift-constrained move slides along its line. With Snap to Grid or Snap to Pixel, the move slides along the line by the shorter of the two distances that put it on a gridline or a whole pixel on either axis. A level or upright move snaps on its own axis only.
- With Smart Guides on, the bounds line up with the other objects, or space evenly with them, only on the axes the line runs along. The grabbed point stops where the line passes an anchor or crosses a ruler guide, with Smart Guides off (Snap to Point) or on.
- Moves without Shift snap as before. Direct Selection drags held by an anchor already kept to the line (#886) and are unchanged.
- `docs/target-app-parity.md` has one line for it under "Drawing aids". No command, string or reply changes.

## How it was tested

New tests, each failing on `main`:
- `select::tests::a_shift_move_snapped_to_the_grid_stays_on_its_line` (vectorcraft-tools): level, upright and diagonal moves with Snap to Grid
- `select::tests::a_shift_move_snapped_to_pixels_stays_on_its_line` (vectorcraft-tools): level, upright and diagonal moves with Snap to Pixel
- `select::tests::a_shift_move_lined_up_by_smart_guides_stays_on_its_line` (vectorcraft-tools): level, upright and diagonal moves with Smart Guides, and the guide lines of the level and upright ones
- `select::tests::a_shift_move_spaced_by_smart_guides_stays_on_its_line` (vectorcraft-tools): a level move with Spacing Guides
- `select::tests::a_shift_move_snapped_by_its_grabbed_point_stays_on_its_line` (vectorcraft-tools): an anchor and a ruler guide with Smart Guides off, and a ruler guide with Smart Guides on
- `direct::tests::a_shift_move_of_objects_snaps_along_its_line` (vectorcraft-tools): Group Selection and Direct Selection with Snap to Grid
- `tests::a_shift_move_snapped_to_the_grid_stays_on_its_line` (vectorcraft-engine): a Selection tool move through the session

Targeted checks on the final tree: `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` on vectorcraft-tools and vectorcraft-engine; `cargo test -p vectorcraft-tools`; `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo xtask brands`, `layers` and `assets`.

On Windows 11 (x86-64) with rustc 1.99.1, on top of `main` at `299a4b3` with #2837 merged in:
- `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=<craft-fonts checkout> cargo xtask ci` passes its 10 steps: 8,084 tests passed, 0 failed, 12 ignored.

`main` at `299a4b3` fails two vectorcraft-svg tests on Windows, `a_missing_link_warns_and_keeps_a_placeholder_in_its_box` and `import_never_reads_or_runs_scripts`, which #2837 fixes. Without it the gate stops at `test` on those two.

`git merge-tree` reports no conflicts with `main` at `299a4b3` or at `5e68106`.

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, brands, layers, wasm).
- [x] No panics in shipped code: no `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!` or
      `unimplemented!` outside tests, and no unchecked indexing on data from files, parameters or
      messages. Errors are returned as `Result` and shown to the user
      ([why and how](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/main/docs/development.md#robustness-vectorcraft-never-crashes)).
- [x] Clean-room: nothing copied from Adobe products or GPL/AGPL code ([AGENTS.md](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/main/AGENTS.md)).
- [x] Every new asset has a row in `ASSETS.md`.

author: lifeline4603
body:
## Summary
This PR refactors the server restart client-side animation sequence to use a more maintainable data structure and fixes a syntax error in the server restart command validation.

## Key Changes
- **Refactored animation data structure**: Replaced the sparse `repAlphas` table with a sequential `steps` table that contains all animation frames in order, making the sequence easier to understand and modify
- **Integrated sound effects into steps**: Moved sound effect logic from conditional checks into the step data itself, allowing each animation frame to optionally specify which sound to play
- **Simplified animation loop**: Removed conditional checks for specific repetition numbers; sound playback is now determined by the presence of a sound file in the current step
- **Fixed syntax error**: Added missing `then` keyword in the server-side admin check condition
- **Improved code clarity**: Added a comment explaining the step structure (one entry per 0.5s tick with alpha values and optional sound)
- **Fixed file formatting**: Added newline at end of client file

## Implementation Details
The animation now follows a clearer pattern:
- Steps 1, 3, 5: Red overlay with alarm sound
- Step 6: White flash with explosion sound
- The sequence is now defined declaratively rather than through sparse indexing and conditional logic

author: gmh5225
body:
## Problem

In android_server, libc++abi's `__cxxabiv1::readEncodedPointer` printed `__builtin_trap(); /* unresolved indirect branch */` instead of its switch on the pointer encoding. Every program that links libc++abi statically has this function.

```
and   w8, w1, #0xf            // guard value: the low 32 bits, masked
cmp   w8, #0xc
b.hi  default
adrp  x9, table
and   x8, x1, #0xf            // index: the whole register, masked again
add   x9, x9, :lo12:table
ldrsw x8, [x9, x8, lsl #2]
add   x8, x8, x9
br    x8
```

## Cause

The precise guard inference (`JumpTableResolverGuardAlias.cpp`) asks whether each guard node is the table index. For a node with a definition, it proves this by occurrence identity: the index at the table read must be the value that same definition produced. Here the index comes from a second `and`, so that proof cannot hold, and no guard bounded the index. The table was refused.

A plain value comparison would not have helped either. The two values are `(w1 & 0xf)` widened to 64 bits and `x1 & 0xf`. The resolver names the entry value of each register width with its own root, and it had no rule relating a masked narrow lane to the mask of the whole register.

## Fix

- The guard batch already keeps a value-comparison fallback for a narrow lane of an extension writer, evaluated only when the occurrence proof fails. A definition that ANDs a value with a constant now gets the same fallback.
- The value matcher (`JumpTableResolverSlice.cpp`) accepts, under zero extension only, `zext(x' & c) == x & c` when the mask `c` fits in the narrow width and `x'` is the low lane of `x`:
  - the masks are compared by value, after widening any constant narrower than its operation (its top bit must be clear);
  - `x'` is the low lane of `x` when it equals `x`'s low slice, or when both are entry roots of one root block whose registers share a container and start at the same byte (`w1` and `x1`).

Sign extension does not commute with masking this way, so the sign-extension checks are unchanged.

## Result

Per-function decompiles of every function with an indirect jump in nine binaries (android_server, armlinux_server, android_x64_server, android_x86_server, android_server32, armlinux_server32, mac_server, mac_server_arm, AArch64 libc.so.6), dev vs this branch:

- android_server: unresolved branches 2 → 1. `readEncodedPointer` gets `switch (encoding & 0xF)`. Its labels are 0, 4 and 0xC, which share the 8-byte read, then 1, 2, 3, 9, 10 and 0xB, and a default: exactly the entries of the 13-entry table that differ from the default target. The three words after the table are not read.
- Every other output in the nine binaries is byte-identical, and the decompile times are unchanged.

## Tests

- `JTE_AArch64.MaskedLaneGuardBoundsAWideMaskIndex` uses `test_jumptable_masked_lane_a64.s`, the shape above with a 13-entry table. The three words after the table would name addresses far outside the code if read as entries. The test requires exactly the 13 decoded targets, so the 16-entry bound the mask alone allows fails it, and no unsafe branch.
- Mutation checks: without the fallback, or without the matcher rule, the table is refused and the test fails.

## Validation (local)

- NeverDJumpTableTests: 541/541.
- NeverDLiftTests, 16 shards, on dev df14bd4c9: 7248 passed, 16 failed. These are the same 16 tests that fail on dev without this change (listed in #1272).
- `check_clang_format.py` clean.

author: stefan-azentrius
body:
The status column shows how much of the plans' limits is used, for both providers, below the hardware and like it. Meters that are nearly full turn red. No outgoing connection and no login: both sources are local.

## What it shows

- Per provider a title with how old the values are ("… plan usage · 2 min ago") and one row per window (5 h, Week): a bar, the percent used and when the window starts again ("until 07:47" within a day, "until Thu" after that).
- A window whose reset time has passed counts from zero.
- A model's own weekly limit (such as "Fable") shows only once it needs attention, so the column stays short.
- Hardware and plan rows share one grid (subgrid), so the bars line up; each section stands under the same line as the signature.
- When an alert above leaves too little room, the gauges give way and fade out at the bottom (like a full column) instead of pushing the signature off the screen. The display measures again when the fonts are loaded or the window changes size.

## Levels

The context meter and the plans' limits share two levels (`ui/src/levels.ts`): grey up to 79 %, attention from 80 %, red from 90 %. The app compacts the context at about 97 %, so a session at 97 % was only yellow before.

## Where the values come from

- **The desktop app:** it gives its sessions a tool, `mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__get_usage`, that reports the account's limits. When a session calls it, the `PostToolUse` hook (which the hub already receives) carries the answer as `tool_response`: JSON in a text block, `plan.windows[]` with `label`, `percentUsed`, `resetsAt`. A parser in `hub/plans.ts` checks it with zod and keeps only percent, window, reset and the model of a model's own limit; the session's context in the same answer is dropped. `hook-input.ts` is unchanged and still drops every tool output.
- Sessions call the tool on their own almost never, so the README suggests a line in the user's own instructions that has them call it at the start of each task. Any session's call updates the values, as the limits are the account's.
- **Codex:** it writes `rate_limits` into every `token_count` entry of its transcript (`primary`/`secondary`, each `{used_percent, window_minutes, resets_at}`). The context reader already reads these transcripts after Codex events and now also passes on the newest limits (`codexPlanOfLine` in `hub/context.ts`), ordered by the line's timestamp.
- `PlanBook` (`hub/plans.ts`) keeps the newest values per provider and remembers them in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\stellwerk\plans.json`, checked with zod when read, so the display has them after a restart.

Looked at and not used: the status line JSON has the limits too, but the desktop app does not run a status line (probed); the app's own usage history is written only when it quits; asking the web service directly would need a new destination and a login.

New: `test/plans.test.ts` (both sources, the book and its file, the display's rows and texts, the levels) and end-to-end tests in `test/hub.test.ts` (a usage tool call through the hook to the state; a Codex event to the state and again after a restart from the file).

author: devnexsler
body:
## What

A prospect reply (`inquiry_reply` / `showing_offer`) the agent executes is refused once, before preflight, when another wake already sent that recipient a customer reply in the previous 72 hours. The refusal:

- names the earlier reply: `RECENTLY ANSWERED: <recipient> already got a reply <N>h ago (action <id>, wake <n>, <intent>): "<text>"`
- lists it in a new `recently_answered` field (omitted from the wire when empty)
- carries the existing `override`. The agent either answers `confirm` decision `no` (recorded as `agent_declined`, a deliberate no-send) or sends the override with a reason. Nothing is dropped silently.

## Why

- Wakes 27331/27332 (2026-09-28): one tour request arrived on two lanes, and the prospect got two different slot lists four minutes apart.
- Wake 28084 (2026-10-09): Amy McDermott sent her TenantCloud inquiry again. It was answered a second time, in different words, 27 hours after wake 27994's reply.

Byte-identical idempotency cannot catch a re-worded repeat.

## When the agent is not asked

- The trigger is a staff directive or a schedule (`zoho_cliq`, `hermes_schedule`, `internal_qualification`).
- The trigger arrived after the newest such reply and is not an exact repeat (ignoring whitespace and case) of an inbound from the same sender in the 72 h before that reply. A genuinely new question gets its answer.
- The row is an override or stale-context successor, which is already the agent's answer.
- The worker or Restate background paths are running (nobody to ask).

Backtest over 30 days of production replies: 22 of 690 would have been asked. Without the trigger rule it would have been 418.

## Comm-Data-Store

No change needed. `reject_outbound_action` and `override_outbound_action` (migration 251) already accept any rejected `detail_code`.

## Tests

GitHub Actions is billing-blocked, so all results below are from local runs:

- `tests/unit/outbound_gateway/test_recently_answered.py`: 11 tests. They fail with the check disabled and pass with it.
- `tests/integration/test_gateway_recently_answered.py`: 6 tests on real PostgreSQL, using the production rows of both incidents.
- Unit suite: 1844 passed.
- Integration: the same 57 tests fail before and after this change (harness schema drift, e.g. `outbound_alias_is_hub`). The 6 new integration tests pass.
- Ruff and pyright: clean on the changed files. `main` is already not `ruff format` clean, so unrelated files were left alone.
- Live read-only run of the lookup SQL:

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The shared runtime configuration owner silently skips its mandatory schema read when a replacement Gateway omits config.schema from its method list. UI and Gateway ship as one install/version; current coupling policy forbids this older-Gateway fallback.

## User Impact

Unsupported version skew reaches the existing visible schema-error state instead of silently retaining an old schema. Normal replacement still refreshes config and schema. Connected-client admission, read scopes (including scope-less access policy), current-request checks, config drafts and all write/settlement behavior stay unchanged. No rendering, style or visible-copy change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the mandatory-method advertisement skip and its import, and replace the obsolete compatibility comment. The existing loadConfigSchema owner records request failures; reconnect schema refresh now follows config refresh so the config success cannot erase that schema failure. This is a narrow shared-owner area in the mandatory-method fallback family, split under the campaign's area rule: four net production lines removed, eleven net test lines added. No parallel error owner or new state.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- An unsupported mismatched Gateway lacking config.schema now receives the request and reports its missing-method error through existing lastError; the previous schema is retained. The gate originated in f8ba65636c23/#125492, whose scope-access and scope-less policy are preserved. Its method-list fallback was compatibility rationale/test evidence, not a cited human incident; current UI/Gateway coupling explicitly retires that fallback.
- Reconnect's schema refresh follows that reconnect's config read, not an arbitrarily superseding read. An unsupported mismatched Gateway combined with another overlapping refresh may still overwrite its old error or delay this refresh; reload/explicit schema refresh recovers. We accept that edge instead of introducing latest-read arbitration or another error-state owner. A second review's P2 proposed that additional coordination; declined under the best-effort doctrine, not claimed fixed or clean.
- Hosted review's distinct disposal P2 is also declined: an already-started reconnect read may finish and attempt a harmless schema read after disposal. Publishing is disabled, listeners detached, writes disposed and server authorization retained. No write or security authority is lost; we accept this recoverable read rather than add another lifecycle guard.
- No security guard, permission, connection/request lifetime, mutation authority or write settlement is removed. No config/schema/protocol/persistence/dependency/SDK change. Phase E standalone memory backend/factory/registry/expiry/federation/tests remain untouched.

## Evidence

- Current owner, full companion suite, state model and harness, determining schema operation and direct caller frames inspected. Canonical core descriptor unconditionally registers config.schema with operator.read; actual handler returns the runtime schema. No optional plugin/config registration is involved.
- Migrated owner-level reconnect regression fails pre-cut because lastError stays null (one intended failure, 37.15s Vitest/52.43s wrapper). Independent review found that a later config success could erase an earlier schema failure; the deferred-config regression reproduced it in the gate-only proposal (25.65s Vitest/35.13s wrapper). Sequencing the existing reads fixes that loss without new state. Final owner and state-model suites:37/37 passed in37.50s Vitest/56.26s wrapper; changed case52ms. Retains normal replacement, scope denial, scope-less access, stale-result exclusion, dirty-draft and write settlement proof. No new seam, sleep, retry, timeout, skip or suppression.
- Final full two-file/five-dataset independent review completed, final source verification successful. Its remaining P2 for overlapping superseding reads is explicitly declined above; the first ordering finding was reproduced and fixed. A subsequent mechanical default type-argument removal fixes the owned lint diagnostic without behavior change. Targeted graph reports36 existing parse5/MCP dependency diagnostics, none in changed paths: NOT a local type pass. A proof-config ambient root omission was corrected using the existing modal-dialog owner. Corrected canonical type-aware lint, formatting54ms and whitespace passed. Mandatory suppression guard14/14 passed in94.92s Vitest/126.68s wrapper; no suppression/baseline/budget changes. Exact-head hosted ci:full is the broad/UI-browser gate; no local build/E2E/live/performance claim. Only an import edge is removed, so no new runtime cycle/component can arise. Plain TypeScript owner remains plain TypeScript; no reactive/render lifecycle machinery added.

Release-note context: surface missing mandatory config schema methods instead of silently skipping their reads on reconnect.

Exact-head CI39093563678: production/test types, lint and selected boundary suites passed. One MCP conformance E2E job failed finding an inner iframe, plus its aggregate gate; the pinned runtime-import closure excludes both changed files and the fixture supplies only gateway/theme context, so campaign path-based attribution treats this as inherited. No matching-main signature or local E2E pass is claimed. Full per-job failure and superseded metadata-cancellation accounting is recorded in the landing evidence comment. No CI rerun, rebase or confirmation push.

author: noahhendrickson
body:
Adds `--day=YYYY-MM-DD` to `scripts/crawl-perk-popularity.ts`. It samples the `--hours` (default 24) before 06:00 UTC on that day, which is the window the scheduled daily crawl that day would have had. Days that were missed, or that came before the daily crawl existed, can then be filled in without overlapping days already saved.

The data repo's Action gets a matching `backfill_days` input. It crawls the listed days one after another in a single run (separate runs would cancel each other's queue slot), never overwrites a day already saved, and pulls before pushing so it can't collide with the scheduled run.

**Tested:** a 40-player run with `--day=2026-10-15` sampled matches from 2026-10-14 07:35 to 2026-10-15 05:19 UTC, inside its window, with combos counted. `tsc` and eslint are clean.

author: nvorkinn
body:
The notice board looked up its own postcode on postcodes.io (or Kartverket for a Norwegian one). That was the renderer's last direct call to an upstream API. A new provider, `provider-locations`, now looks each postcode up once for every screen, and the board reads the answer from the store. After this the renderer talks only to the store and the broker, and a test checks that.

## What changed

**`provider-locations`** (`providers/src/countdown_providers/locations/main.py`, entry point `countdown-provider-locations`, compose service `provider-locations`)
- Reads `v1:sub:postcode`. A UK postcode goes to postcodes.io (`notices.location.lookup_postcode`), a Norwegian one (four digits) to Kartverket (`notices.norway.lookup_norwegian_postcode`). It writes `v1:location:<keys.place(postcode)>` (new `keys.location`) as a `StoredLocation`, `store/location.py`:
  ```json
  {"fetched_at": "2026-10-18T12:00:00Z", "postcode": "SE17 3LL", "found": true,
   "location": {"postcode": "SE17 3LL", "latitude": 51.48873, "longitude": -0.09766, "country": "England", "region": "London", "admin_district": "Southwark"}}
  {"fetched_at": "...", "postcode": "ZZ1 1ZZ", "found": false, "location": null}
  ```
- **Timing:** the TTL is 7 days. Each answer is rewritten every 5-minute cycle and asked for again once a day. A new postcode is looked up at once, because the broker's nudge runs a cycle on every config save.
- **Unknown postcodes:** a postcode neither service knows is written explicitly as `found: false`.
- **Failures:** a lookup that fails isn't written (or the last answer stays), and it's tried again next cycle. A "not found" for a postcode that was found before (a terminated one) doesn't unplace it.
- **Logging:** nothing logged names a postcode or anything worked out from one. Errors are logged by type plus HTTP status, and urllib3 is turned down to ERROR.

**Renderer** (`notice_board_client._ensure_location`)
- Reads the key instead of calling postcodes.io or Kartverket:
  - **Missing key** (or an unreadable store): `Couldn't look up the postcode yet`, as before. It reads again after `LOCATION_RETRY`, now 1 minute instead of 10, since a store read costs nothing upstream.
  - **`found: false`:** "Unknown postcode", as before.
  - **Found:** the board builds the same sources from the stored `Postcode`: bank-holiday division, Met Office source, floods, TfL roads, and MetAlerts' point-in-polygon place.
- The renderer's direct lookup path is gone. `lookup_postcode`, `lookup_norwegian_postcode` and the parsing helpers stay, because the provider uses them.
- **Logs:** the success line no longer names the area, Met Office region or bank-holiday division. `region_for`'s "no region" warning no longer names the district.

**Docs:** there's a key-table row and a "Locations" section with deploy steps in `providers/README.md`. The "Enabling in production" list now says a renderer asks no API at all.

## Tests
- **Parity, from fixtures.** `tests/fixtures/locations.json` holds postcodes.io's and Kartverket's answers and the stored value for five postcodes:
  - an English one, `SE17 3LL`
  - a Scottish one, `EH1 1YZ`, so the bank-holiday division is exercised
  - a Norwegian one, `0150`, so MetAlerts' polygon filter is exercised
  - an unknown UK one, `ZZ1 1ZZ` (404)
  - an unknown Norwegian one, `0001` (no addresses)

  `tests/fixtures/locations_board.json` is **recorded from the old code before I changed it**. For each postcode it has what the board built and showed from the same answers: its location, every source with its division, region and key, and the notices or message, with the same notices stored for both runs. `test_locations.py` runs the provider through the runner into fakeredis, then runs the board with every request refused. It checks the result is exactly the recorded one. I checked that dropping `location.country` from the bank holidays fails the Scottish case.
- **No network in a full render cycle** (`test_e2e_render_cycle.py::test_a_full_render_cycle_reaches_nothing_but_the_broker`, UK and Norway):
  - The setup is the real `DisplayLoop` with departures, weather, energy, Spotify and its cover, plus the notice board with a placed postcode. Sockets are refused and recorded, below `responses` (`socket.connect`, `connect_ex`, `create_connection`, `getaddrinfo`). The test also asserts that no request went anywhere but the broker.
  - One thing is stubbed: Material Symbols, a font the renderer downloads from GitHub once and keeps on disk. It isn't an API.
  - With main's `notice_board_client.py` put back, both cases fail, on the postcodes.io and Kartverket URLs.
- **Provider tests** cover the stored values, Kartverket's query, look-up-once / rewrite / daily refresh, failure and retry, keep-on-failure, found-then-not-found, not-found-then-found, a non-postcode, the runner writing the keys with the TTL, and the urllib3 retry warnings. They also cover nothing logged naming a postcode, its district, region or coordinates at DEBUG through the runner.
- **Board tests** are rewritten to the store: missing key then retry, an unreadable store, unknown, and placed without logging where.

**Checks:**
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean.
- With countdown-api main (`--remote`, as CI builds), the only failures are main's 179 font-download tests, the same set as on main.
- main is merged in, with #203's `Tfl.app_key` test fixes.

## Merge and deploy order
- **No contract change.** It doesn't depend on countdown-api or auth-broker. `v1:sub:postcode` (auth-broker #174) is already deployed.
- **Conflicts with #204 (no-postcodes-in-logs):** both change `_ensure_location`'s log lines, `region_for`'s warning and the matching tests. #204's `test_no_place_in_logs.py` also tests the board's old lookup-failure path, which this removes. Merge in either order; whichever goes second resolves it. I own this side.
- **Deploy:** the provider and the renderers that need it ship in the same release. The deploy starts `provider-locations` with the other providers, and its first cycle writes the keys within seconds. Until a board's key is there, the board says it couldn't look the postcode up yet: it keeps its other notices, has no place-based ones, and reads again each minute. **Before relying on it**, check on the host that there's a key for each member of `v1:sub:postcode`:
  ```sh
  docker exec redis sh -c 'REDISCLI_AUTH="$REDIS_PASSWORD" redis-cli -h 127.0.0.1 --scan --pattern "v1:location:*"'
  docker exec redis sh -c 'REDISCLI_AUTH="$REDIS_PASSWORD" redis-cli -h 127.0.0.1 SCARD v1:sub:postcode'
  docker logs --tail 20 countdown-renderers-provider-locations-1   # why one is missing
  ```

## Judgment calls
- **I store the parsed `Postcode` fields, not postcodes.io's and Kartverket's raw answers.** The two answers have different shapes, and the conversion already exists (`lookup_norwegian_postcode` builds a `Postcode`). So one shape serves both countries, and the renderer needs no parser for either. It's data, not rendered text.

author: asinglesprinkle
body:
Teaches the Jira board to cut a slice under an Epic: a pre-flight that refuses a project it cannot file into or an unreachable Epic before anything is created, children carrying `fields.parent`, the label and an ADF body, `Blocks` links, the cut note as a comment, and the Epic's move by transition.

## Changes

- Jira's `ticket_filing` now reads the project's statuses and the Epic to settle a private `Settled` filing, and `Boards` carries its own `Filings` so a Jira destination that exists no longer reaches `cut` as absent.
- Jira's `create_ticket` files a draft as one POST under `fields.parent` with the label, `accountId` assignee and ADF body, answers the key as id, identifier and browse URL, and transitions a child landing outside `new`.
- Jira's `create_relation` writes each edge as one `Blocks` issueLink POST with the blocker as `inwardIssue`, and `comment_on_brief` says a cut or skip note as an ADF comment on the Epic, answering the comment's id; neither is retried.
- Jira's `move_brief` moves the Epic by transition: the one whose `to.name` matches the name given — trimmed and case-folded, never by category — is posted by its id, and no match answers `false` with nothing posted.
- Added flow tests driving `warlock draft <jira-scope> <key>` through one whole cut against the in-memory `Calls` stand-in: the request order, the printed identifiers, and the cut note read back through `cut::noted`.

## Testing

- New `tests/jira.rs` cases assert the pre-flight's two reads by method, path and body — the ready filing, a project that is absent or has no `new`-category status, a propagated Epic absence, malformed answers and that every call is a GET under `/rest/api/3` — plus a `tests/cut.rs` case that the brief key reaches the pre-flight first.
- New `tests/jira.rs` cases drive the create by method, path and body — the parent from the filing, the exact field set, the status read back, the transition chosen by `to.name` and never by category, a workflow that reaches no such status, and a refused create, refused move, malformed answers and the no-retry call counts; `create_ticket` moved from the untaught list into `every_verb`.
- Added jira.rs tests driving both verbs against the `Calls` stand-in by method, path and body — the link's direction, a refused link and a refused note each left unretried, a note that answers no id, and a round trip where the ADF a note went up as comes back through `fetch_brief` and is read by `cut::noted` as a settled cut and a settled skip.
- New `jira.rs` tests cover the Epic's move by method, path and body on a default workflow, the `false` answer with nothing posted, the choice by name against two `indeterminate` destinations, both `cut::finish` lines, a refused move reported in Jira's words and not retried, and a transitions read with no list as malformed.
- Three tests in `mod jira` of the planned flow tests covering the cut's request order (pre-flight, a create and status read per draft, the link, the comment, the Epic's move), the identifiers and settled-slice lines printed, and the ADF note body reading back as the slice and its issues.

## Review notes

- `issuetype` is written as `Task` by a new `TASK` constant: Jira requires the field on a create and no curl in the ticket says which type a child was filed as, so a site that renamed Task refuses the create in its own words. A transition Jira refuses propagates out of `create_ticket` after the child already exists, so such a cut refuses with an issue standing — the same shape as a create that fails partway through a slice.
- `comment_on_brief` reads the answer's `id` leniently and answers the empty string when it carries none, rather than raising `Malformed` as the other creates do: no caller reads the value, and a note that landed must not be reported as failed. `create_relation` always answers the empty string because Jira's 201 for a link carries no body — a caller that starts reading that string gets nothing.
- The transition read-choose-post step is now one private `Jira::shifted`, shared by `move_brief` and by the move `create_ticket` makes of a child that landed outside `new`: a change to how a transition is chosen or posted changes both callers.
- The slice's drafts come from `drafting::stub_answer`, which yields exactly one edge after de-duplication, so the order assertion covers one `issueLink` POST rather than several; link bodies and direction stay asserted in `tests/jira.rs`.

author: samoylenkodmitry
body:
Stacked on #1739: the commits of #1736 to #1739 show here until they merge.

## Cause

`LayoutState::place` noted every node a layout pass moved in the context's moved-node `HashSet`: about 50 inserts a frame on a scrolled lazy list. Each take then drained the set into a list, which clears every control byte of the table.

## Change

- Placing is the only way a node is noted as moved. The node now keeps `moved_noted_in`, the take of the moved list in which it was last noted. A second note in the same take is one comparison, and the list is a `Vec` that each take swaps out.
- Takes are numbered on the thread (`ThreadCells::moved_scene_node_takes`), so two app contexts never share a number, and a node placed in another context is never skipped.
- The other dirty-node sets keep their hash sets: their notes come from many sites.
- New test `a_node_moved_again_before_a_take_is_reported_once_and_again_after_it`.

## Measurement

`cranpose-app-shell` bench `scroll_frame` under callgrind on samarch (x86), on top of #1739:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| total instructions | 421,180,665 | 414,269,322 (-1.6%) |
| `LayoutState::place`, inclusive | 13.0M | 8.0M |

## Tests

- `cargo test -p cranpose-ui -p cranpose-app-shell -p cranpose-render-common` locally.
- clippy on ui, precommit gates.

author: mostafammy
body:
🚨 **Severity**: MEDIUM

💡 **Vulnerability**: 
The `CreateSuggestionSchema` and `CreateUniversitySchema` schemas used Zod's `z.string().url()` to validate user-provided URLs (`sourceUrl` and `website`). However, `z.string().url()` only verifies that the string matches a generic URL format and does not restrict the protocol schema. This allows malicious users to supply URLs like `javascript:alert(1)`, which, if rendered unmodified in an `href` attribute (e.g., in `SuggestionReviewDialog` or university detail pages), can execute arbitrary JavaScript in another user's browser, leading to Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).

🎯 **Impact**:
If an attacker submits a suggestion or university payload with a `javascript:` URL, administrators or users interacting with the submitted data could click the link and unwittingly execute attacker-controlled scripts in their current session context.

🔧 **Fix**:
Chained `.refine()` to the `z.string().url()` validations in `src/schemas/suggestion.schema.ts` and `src/schemas/university.schema.ts` to explicitly enforce that valid URLs must begin with either `http://` or `https://`.

✅ **Verification**:
- Automated test suite passes (`SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION=1 pnpm test`).
- Type check passes (`pnpm type-check`).
- The fix prevents payloads containing `javascript:` from successfully parsing through the affected Zod schemas.

author: dotcoocoo
body:
## What and why

Dragging a user slice's edge or corner handle with the Slice Selection tool never snapped, while drawing a slice with the Slice tool snaps to the grid, to whole pixels, to the art and to the ruler guides. The reference app's help says of slices drawn with the Slice tool or made from a selection or from guides: "you can move, resize, and delete them in the same way as other vector objects", and "To resize a slice, select the slice with Slice Selection tool, and drag any corner or side of the slice" ([Slices and image maps](https://web.archive.org/web/20260311095240/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/slices-image-maps.html)). The page does not say how a slice's handle snaps, so the rule here is VectorCraft's own: the handle snaps as the Slice tool's drag does.

- The handle drag gathers its targets when the handle is pressed and snaps what the handle moves through `PointSnap::snap_scale`, which the Selection and Free Transform tools' bounding-box handles use (#2715): to the nearest gridline with View › Snap to Grid, to whole pixels with Snap to Pixel, to the art and the artboards with Smart Guides, and with Smart Guides off to the art's anchors and the ruler guides with Snap to Point. The Smart Guides lines and labels show during the drag.
- Then a shown, unlocked ruler guide within 5 px moves the side or corner onto it, as the Slice tool's `snap` moves a drawn slice's corner. Shift still keeps the proportions, and Alt still resizes about the center.
- `docs/target-app-parity.md` has one line for it under Drawing aids. No command, reply or string changes: the drag still previews `object.slice.setRect`.

Moving a slice with the Slice Selection tool does not snap yet; this change covers its handles.

## How it was tested

New tests in vectorcraft-tools, each failing on `main`:
- `slice::tests::slice_handles_snap_to_the_grid_and_to_pixels`: a side and a corner land on the grid, Shift keeps the proportions, Alt mirrors the other side about the center, and a corner lands on whole pixels.
- `slice::tests::slice_handles_snap_to_the_art_and_the_ruler_guides`: a side lines up with another object's edge and its guide shows until release, a corner lands on an anchor with Snap to Point, a side follows the pointer with both off, a ruler guide takes a side with Smart Guides on and off, and a guide takes a corner's x while the grid takes its y.

Targeted checks on the final tree: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo clippy -p vectorcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p vectorcraft-tools`; `cargo xtask brands`, `layers` and `assets`.

On Windows 11 (x86-64) with rustc 1.99.1, on top of `main` at `299a4b3` with #2837 merged in:
- `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=<craft-fonts checkout> cargo xtask ci` passes its 10 steps: 8,079 tests passed, 0 failed, 12 ignored.

`main` at `299a4b3` fails two vectorcraft-svg tests on Windows, `a_missing_link_warns_and_keeps_a_placeholder_in_its_box` and `import_never_reads_or_runs_scripts`, which #2837 fixes. Without it the gate stops at `test` on those two.

`git merge-tree` reports no conflicts with `main` at `299a4b3` or at `5e68106`.

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, brands, layers, wasm).
- [x] No panics in shipped code: no `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!` or
      `unimplemented!` outside tests, and no unchecked indexing on data from files, parameters or
      messages. Errors are returned as `Result` and shown to the user
      ([why and how](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/main/docs/development.md#robustness-vectorcraft-never-crashes)).
- [x] Clean-room: nothing copied from Adobe products or GPL/AGPL code ([AGENTS.md](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/main/AGENTS.md)).
- [x] Every new asset has a row in `ASSETS.md`.

author: nyaromesama
body:
Line numbers are on master `97cd13f3`.

## Summary

`processActionsWithZkSigs` trusts the prover's `signers[]` instead of running `ecrecover`. Two checks that the sig path makes on-chain were left to the circuit alone on the ZK path. This PR adds both on the contract side, so the ZK path no longer relies on the circuit being bug-free for them.

The SP1 program does not produce either case (I executed it on such inputs; see Tests). These are defence-in-depth guards, not a fix for something reachable with the current program.

## What differs today

**1. Zero signer**
- Sig path: `_verifySignatureMem` treats the recovered signer as the owner only when `signer == owner && signer != address(0)` (CawActions L1560).
- ZK path: `_zkProcessOneGroup` checks `signer == owner` only (L556).
- `CawProfileLedger.ownerOf` returns `address(0)` for a token that is authenticated but whose owner was never synced (Ledger L68–77, and the `_setOwnerOf` comment around L636–640). That comment gives "ecrecover cannot produce address(0)" as the reason this is safe. The ZK path does not go through `ecrecover`, so a zero signer would match that token's "owner" and its actions would run with owner authority.

**2. Contiguous cawonces in a batch-sig group**
- Sig path: `_unpackBatchGroup` reverts `NonContiguousCawonces` (L829; also L1125).
- ZK path: `_zkApplyOne` checks the sender only (L621).
- The program asserts contiguity (`zk/sig-recovery/program/src/main.rs` L131–135), but the contract did not.

Why the program never emits either: `ecdsa_recover` panics on an invalid signature (main.rs L50–58) and derives the address from a recovered public key, and `zkProgramVKey` is immutable.

## Fix

- `_zkProcessOneGroup`: revert `InvalidSig` when the group's signer is `address(0)`. This is the same error the sig path uses for a zero signer (L1586).
- `_zkProcessOneGroup` reads the group's first cawonce with a new `_peekCawonce` (fixed offset 17, the same way as `_peekSenderId`). It passes `cawonce0 + i` to `_zkApplyOne`, which reverts `NonContiguousCawonces` on a mismatch, right after the `MixedSenders` check. A single-action group always matches.
- No storage changes. Both checks run before the race-loss skip, so a malformed group reverts instead of being partly skipped.

## Tests

New `test-foundry/ZkPathSignerGuards.t.sol` uses `MockSP1Verifier` and the same setup as `SessionProfileScoping.t.sol`:

| test | master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| contiguous batch group (5, 6) executes | pass | pass |
| non-contiguous batch group (5, 7) reverts `NonContiguousCawonces` | **fail** (both actions executed) | pass |
| owner signer executes | pass | pass |
| zero signer on an authenticated token with no owner reverts `InvalidSig` | **fail** (the action executed) | pass |

Full forge suite (forge 1.8.5, solc 0.8.30, `--evm-version prague`):
- this PR: 260 passed, 10 failed, 1 skipped (271)
- master: 256 passed, 10 failed, 1 skipped (267)
- The 10 failures have the same names on both. They are the existing `SigVsZkDifferential` `setUp` ("mockActionsA nonce mismatch") and the 9 `StorageLayoutSnapshot` tests, which need `forge` on `PATH` for their ffi script; that was not available in my environment.

Size and gas:
- `CawActions` runtime size: 24,148 → 24,210 bytes (+62; 366 bytes left under EIP-170).
- Gas on the ZK path, from the tests above: +227 for a 1-action group, +379 for a 2-action batch group.

SP1 program, executed (no proving) from the master source (this PR does not touch it) with `sp1up -v v6.0.1` and `sp1-sdk` 6.1.0 as locked. This is a local build, so its vkey is not the deployed one; it checks the program source, not the deployed ELF:
- Controls (a single action, a batch group with cawonces (5, 6)) commit the expected `signersHash`.
- A validly signed `ActionBatch` with cawonces (5, 7), `r = s = 0`, `v = 29` and `v = 0` each commit nothing.
- 16 random `(r, s)`: 12 commit nothing, 4 recover a non-zero signer, none recover `address(0)`.
- The guest's panic message was not in the log, so which assert fired for (5, 7) is inferred from the input (it differs from the (5, 6) control only in the second cawonce).

Not run: the Truffle JS tests (`test/zk-*.js`), which need a local chain.

## Notes

- The deployed `CawActions` is immutable, so this takes effect on the next deployment only.
- Not changed: on the ZK path a cawonce that is already used skips that slot rather than reverting the batch (by design, L585–593). For a batch-sig group this means part of one signed `ActionBatch` can execute. That only happens if the same sender signed two different actions with the same cawonce. I left it as it is; mentioning it in case it should match the sig path's all-or-nothing behaviour for batch groups.
- Overlap: none of the 184 open PRs touches `solidity/contracts/CawActions.sol` (checked against every PR head; as a positive control, a synthetic commit editing the same line conflicts in `git merge-tree`).

body:
## What and why

The Mac's launchd unit runs `kbf daemon --driver native`, but `native-macos` built and tested only `kbf-daemon`. Nothing ran the `kbf` binary on macOS. Its `main` has to hand a helper's command line to the helper (`kbf_node::dispatch_helpers()`) before clap reads `__keeper` or `__as-user` as a mode; that was checked only on Linux, and only for the keeper.

## What changes

- `crates/kbf-cli/tests/macos_daemon.rs` (`cfg(target_os = "macos")`; compiles to nothing elsewhere):
  - `check_args_accepts_the_units_words_and_refuses_a_renamed_flag`: `kbf check-args daemon <the unit's words>` exits 0; the same words with `--data-dir` spelled `--datadir` exit 2.
  - `kbf_answers_as_a_keeper`: `kbf __keeper group` prints its READY line and SIGKILLs its own group when stdin closes.
  - `kbf_answers_as_the_pools_as_user_step`: `kbf __as-user` with no words exits 126 with the as-user usage line, not clap's exit 2.
  - `kbf_daemon_starts_as_the_units_words_start_it`: `kbf daemon` with the unit's argv (one word per argument, `https://localhost:<port>` for `--server` and `--cas`, no `--tls-server-name`, `--data-max-bytes`, two `--label`s), in the unit's working directory with its `HOME`, against kbf-node's fake front. Asserts `Hello` with node `node-1` and drivers `["native"]`, runs an action the front starts, SIGKILLs the daemon, and asserts the action's leader and child end (the keeper is `kbf` re-run as `__keeper`).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: one step in `native-macos`, `cargo test -p kbf-cli --test macos_daemon --locked`. The job's `if:` is unchanged.
- `crates/kbf-cli/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`: dev-dependencies `futures` and `kbf-front` (the fake front is kbf-node's `tests/front/mod.rs`, included by path); tokio's `sync` feature named in dev-dependencies; `kbf-driver-container` moves to a Linux-only dev-dependency section. That crate does not compile on macOS (`st_dev` is `i32` there), and cargo builds every dev-dependency for any test target, so without the move `cargo test -p kbf-cli --test macos_daemon` could not build on the runner. Only `tests/storage_and_daemon.rs` uses it, and that file is already Linux-only.

## Tests and planted defects

Run on Linux with a temporary copy of the test file gated `cfg(unix)` (not committed), under the local-compile lease:

| Defect (via `git apply`, reverted with `git apply -R`) | Result on Linux |
|---|---|
| Baseline | keeper, check-args, daemon tests pass; as-user fails (its dispatch exists only on macOS) |
| Remove `dispatch_helpers()` from `kbf_cli::main` | keeper test fails ("did not answer as a keeper"); daemon test fails (times out waiting for the action's files: the keeper start is refused) |
| Rename `--data-dir` in kbf-node's flags (`long = "datadir"`) | check-args test fails (`unexpected argument '--data-dir'`); daemon test fails (the daemon exits 2, no `Hello`) |

Not run on macOS by me: the as-user test, and every test of the file against the real native driver. The as-user test is covered by reasoning only: with `dispatch_helpers()` removed, `kbf __as-user` goes to clap and exits 2 with `unrecognized subcommand` (observed on Linux, where the dispatch does not exist), so the test's `Some(126)` assertion fails. Those run in `native-macos` on this PR (label `macos`).

Also: `cargo clippy --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p kbf-cli --bins --test macos_daemon -- -D warnings` is clean (type-check only; no link), Linux `clippy -p kbf-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean, and `kbf-it`'s `repo_lints` and `layering` pass.

author: theleoborges
body:
Fixes #13.

**Before:** on the Browserbase API host (CDP enabled), `extensionId` was stripped only from bodies that were JSON-typed, under `COATCHECK_MAX_SWAP_BODY_BYTES`, un-encoded and parseable. Any other body streamed through unchanged — so a JSON session config sent as `text/plain`, gzip-encoded, or padded past the cap could have carried the extension parameters to Browserbase.

**After:** every request body to an adapter host is buffered regardless of `Content-Type`.
- Parseable JSON is inspected and stripped even when labelled `text/plain` or unlabelled.
- A body that can't be read — `Content-Encoding` present, over the cap, or not parseable — is refused with `403` + `X-Coatcheck-Denied: uninspectable-body` and the tunnel is closed; nothing is forwarded.
- `multipart/form-data` (session file uploads) is the one shape forwarded uninspected: no server reads a multipart body as a JSON session config. Flagging this carve-out explicitly as the one judgement call in the PR.
- No change when CDP is disabled.

**Tests** (`server.test.ts`, 7 new): gzip / malformed / oversized → 403 + nothing upstream; `text/plain` and no-`Content-Type` JSON → stripped; multipart → forwarded byte-for-byte; CDP off → unchanged streaming.

**Docs:** README (CDP step 1, request bodies), `THREAT_MODEL.md` (property table + "second routes" gap), `clients.md`, `design/cdp-broker-login.md` ("As built" paragraph previously documented the fail-open), `design/cdp-injection.md`, `CLAUDE.md` code map.

author: willfulbard
body:
## Summary
Throttles the public registration endpoint's anonymous POST steps per client address (10 a minute by default, `CAMPHORIC_REGISTER_RATE`). This curbs junk registrations and using the confirmation email as a spam relay. The GET, signed-in users (the importer, bulk tools) and the PayPal/card capture are exempt. The capture is exempt because a 429 there would throw away the payer's approval. No CAPTCHA (SPEC DR-125).

## How
A `ScopedRateThrottle` (scope `register`) on `RegisterView`; `get_throttles` skips the exempt cases. A 429 says in plain words to wait N seconds, and the register pages already show it. `NUM_PROXIES` defaults to 0, which ignores `X-Forwarded-For`; the Ansible env sets 1 for nginx. Counts are per gunicorn worker, so a shared cache is a follow-up.

## Testing
Server tests check where the throttle applies: the limit, the plain 429 message and `Retry-After`, the exemptions, and which address is counted with and without a proxy. The test runner now empties the caches before each test, including under `--parallel`. Without that, about 30 existing register tests got 429s. Full suite, flake8 and the migrations check pass.
- `tests.test_views.RegisterThrottleTests.test_throttled_past_the_rate` (added)

body:
## What

ADR-0187: the upgrade suite planned, and Latest ≠ Newest's scope stated. Nothing is built.

**The suite**, twenty-nine proposals UPG-01 to UPG-29, read against the tree:

| Disposition | Proposals |
| :--- | :--- |
| Done | UPG-11 (ADR-0097, 0098, 0102, 0104, 0105) |
| Planned, in order | M10 a reward past the trial (UPG-03); M11 learning that sleep keeps (UPG-04); M12 couplings over long runs (UPG-02, its layout first); M13 a lookahead (UPG-08); M14 synthesis in sleep (UPG-09); M8's tool broker; M15 language that says what it does not know (UPG-05, UPG-06) |
| After the broker | UPG-07, UPG-10, UPG-15, UPG-16 |
| Deferred, each with what would bring it | UPG-01, 12, 13, 14, 17, and 18 to 29 |
| Not adopted by any round | the claims and probability figures; unreproduced figures; GPUs, AVX-512, RDMA and NVMe paging on the hot path; self-change beyond `REGISTRY`; loops that do not end by construction |

Each planned item enters by a decision ADR of its own that writes a hypothesis before any run, and is then measured by one round.

**What the suite gets wrong about the tree:**
- UPG-02's bytes are `v_slow`'s, and the modulator's `[32..36)` is not reserved.
- `OBJECTIVE_EPISTEMIC_GAIN = 2` collides with `OBJECTIVE_REHYDRATIONS`.

**Latest ≠ Newest is kept.** It governs what the tree depends on, not what the engine does.
- A mechanism enters by an ADR and a measured round.
- The project's documentation tools are admitted by ADR-0008 and ADR-0185.
- A brief's "nothing else is adopted" is its `## Not empowered`.

The maintainers chose to change the wording in this pull request: `CLAUDE.md`'s principle 4, a "what the rule does not govern" in §2.1, and `briefs/README.md`'s standing-directives row.

## Changes

- `docs/adr/0187-the-upgrade-suite-planned.md`, accepted.
- Whitepaper 4.121.0: Appendix C's M10 to M15, §2.1, and section 9's row.
- `CLAUDE.md`, `briefs/README.md`, the index and `CHANGELOG.md`.

author: lesnolie
body:
## Goal
ChatGPT Web can initiate a first native Codex Desktop `$magpie-codex-collab` collaboration (no app-server required), retain the correct ChatGPT chat identity, and avoid duplicate executions.

## Implementation
- Add opt-in execution-capable `codex_collab_start` (MCP tool #17). Requires existing Magpie local Codex enable + non-read-only permission and only accepts Codex Desktop registered project names.
- **Current ChatGPT conversation URL is NOT exposed via MCP**: without an explicitly supplied exact URL returns `needs_chat_url` with no task created or local action. Never infer from title, old conversation or another tab.
- Persist immutable launchId, taskId, target chat URL and goal for idempotent first start. One-stage launch receipt says `opened_unconfirmed` / `queued_unconfirmed`, NEVER claims actual execution. A retry cannot open a second Codex window or deliver a second queue message.
- For first start, Windows uses `codex://threads/new` with absolute project path (only in local process), prefilled Skill instructions; user **must press Send** in Codex Desktop. The returned MCP JSON never exposes local project paths.
- Once the *native* Codex Skill verifies the ChatGPT workspace/browser URL and registers its thread UUID locally, later starts in the same chat may use `codex queue --thread ...`. A successful queue exit only means the message was stored, not consumed; no automatic fallback.
- Native Codex Skill now understands START MODE, launchId and target chat and will not modify source until Magpie MCP project verification and exact URL checks are complete.
- Clear stale native thread IDs when switching chat conversations. Remote cannot activate a chat or bind an arbitrary thread.
- CLI command `link-thread` is local only; v0.4.8 existing handoff remains.
- Updated README and Magpie UI with pairing and limitations; automated tests for auth gating, link encoding, first launch, invalid URLs, queue receipts, thread changes, idempotency and cross-platform checks.

## Limitations
End-to-end Codex Desktop UI and in-app browser behavior needs a real Windows acceptance test; GitHub Actions mock the OS opener. A deep link only PREFILLS a prompt. Queue acceptance does not confirm Codex executed it, and unloaded/goal-mode threads may require user intervention. Existing Cloudflare Access authentication stays required.

## Validation
Node unit/integration tests on Windows and Ubuntu via Actions.

body:
<!--
Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/126479
-->


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed `CREATE TABLE` and `ALTER TABLE` accepting a MergeTree table (with `flatten_nested = 0`) whose non-flattened `Nested` column, named with the prefix of a flattened `Nested` group, writes its streams into the files of other columns. Parts inserted into such a table could not be read.

### Description

On 26.8.16.41 and 26.9.19.9, after `SET flatten_nested = 0`, `CREATE TABLE t (n.a Nested(x UInt64), n.b Array(UInt64), n.a.x UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple()` is accepted, and after an `INSERT`, `SELECT n.a.x FROM t` fails with `Too many marks in file .../n%2Ea%2Ex.cmrk2` (`CANNOT_READ_ALL_DATA`): the element `x` of `n.a` and the column `n.a.x` are written into one file. A debug build aborts the `INSERT` in `validateColumnOfFixedSize`. `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` has the same gap.

With `share_nested_offsets` on, `checkColumnFilenamesForCollision` checks `Nested::collect(...)`, which removes a non-flattened `Nested` column whose name prefix is a flattened group without uniting it into that group, so the streams of that column were never checked while the part writer still writes them. The check now includes such columns.

Their array sizes are written to the group's `n.size0`, so `n.a Nested(x UInt64), n.b Array(UInt64)` is refused too, as `n Nested(a UInt64), n.b Array(UInt64)` already is. That schema could not be read with `SELECT *` or merged anyway (`There is no subcolumn a in type Nested(b UInt64)`). With `share_nested_offsets = 0` it stays allowed. Existing tables still load and only log the error, as for the other collisions.

The new test fails on master (the first `CREATE` is accepted) and passes with the fix.

The same gap in `Log` and `TinyLog` is fixed in #126479. The draft #119329 rewrites these lines and would replace this change.

body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
Search returns the raw vector similarity score from AI Search (`scoring_details.vector_score`). Retrieval is pure vector. The worker asks for the top 50 chunks by vector similarity (`retrieval_type: "vector"`) and sends `reranking: { enabled: false }`. `MIN_SEARCH_SCORE` stays 0.6. The worker drops scores under 0.6, drops `llms.txt` index files, keeps the highest-scoring chunk per page, and sorts by similarity, highest first. `k` defaults to 50 and is capped at 50. The calling agent decides relevance.

These scores are a record, not a gate. They were measured on 2026-10-19 against the live `design-guide` AI Search instance, using the request the worker now sends. That request is 50 candidates, `retrieval_type: "vector"`, `reranking: { enabled: false }`, and query rewrite off. It sends no keyword match mode and no fusion method. The same local filter then drops scores under 0.6, drops `llms*.txt`, and keeps one chunk per page. The deployed Worker was not queried.

Pure vector did not change the junk result or any first page. It did raise how many real pages clear 0.6. Every chunk in this run has a `vector_score`. The earlier hybrid run spent part of the 50 slots on keyword-only chunks, so those slots now hold extra vector hits. Top scores and first URLs match the hybrid table. `asdf qwer zxcv 99999` still returns 24 pages at 0.6465. The floor stays 0.6.

**The 0.6 floor keeps every real query in this set. It also lets one nonsense query through.**

q01 to q10 and the six held-out queries each return between 7 and 33 pages at or above 0.6. Three nonsense queries return nothing. `asdf qwer zxcv 99999` returns 24 pages, and its top score of 0.6465 is the highest score among the nonsense queries.

| Query | At or above 0.6 | Top score | First URL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| q01 form errors | 18 | 0.7065 | https://www.patternfly.org/components/forms/form/design-guidelines |
| q02 toast vs alert | 24 | 0.7330 | https://ix.siemens.io/docs/components/toast/code |
| q03 modal focus | 19 | 0.7266 | https://www.patternfly.org/components/modal/html |
| q04 button hierarchy | 24 | 0.7334 | https://ix.siemens.io/docs/components/button/code |
| q05 empty table | 29 | 0.7400 | https://cloudscape.design/patterns/resource-management/view/table-view/ |
| q06 skeleton or spinner | 24 | 0.7329 | https://design.gitlab.com/components/skeleton-loader/ |
| q07 date input | 16 | 0.7614 | https://ix.siemens.io/docs/components/input-date/code.md |
| q08 confirm delete | 20 | 0.6975 | https://cloudscape.design/patterns/resource-management/delete/delete-with-simple-confirmation/ |
| q09 data table | 7 | 0.7962 | https://primer.style/product/components/data-table |
| q10 Paste button guidance | 11 | 0.6467 | https://ix.siemens.io/docs/guidelines/language/menu-functions-and-ui-labels/button-labels |
| q11 zzqxv quantum flux capacitor sandwich | 0 | 0.5554 | none returned |
| q12 best recipe for banana bread | 0 | 0.4703 | none returned |
| how does Paste say to use buttons | 28 | 0.6992 | https://paste-dsys.com/introduction/for-engineers/quickstart |
| form validation paraphrase | 21 | 0.7265 | https://cloudscape.design/patterns/general/errors/validation/ |
| skeleton or spinner paraphrase | 29 | 0.7269 | https://primer.style/product/components/ |
| confirm before delete | 10 | 0.7051 | https://cloudscape.design/patterns/resource-management/delete/delete-with-simple-confirmation/ |
| cloudscape table guidance | 14 | 0.7174 | https://paste-dsys.com/components/table/api/ |
| primer dialog guidance | 33 | 0.6768 | https://ix.siemens.io/docs/guidelines/language/forms-and-form-fields/helper-info-text |
| purple elephant tax law on mars | 0 | 0.5305 | none returned |
| asdf qwer zxcv 99999 | 24 | 0.6465 | https://ix.siemens.io/docs/components/chat-input/guide |

A row with `none returned` shows the highest raw vector score in the 50 candidates. That score is under 0.6, so the worker would return nothing. Every other top score is the first page the filter keeps. On `cloudscape table guidance`, the highest raw score is still 0.7684 and the filter drops it as an llms index file. The first kept page is the Paste table API at 0.7174.

Highest nonsense score: **0.6465**, on `asdf qwer zxcv 99999`.

**Decision (Simon, 2026-10-18):** ship as-is with raw vector similarity and the 0.6 floor. The calling agent filters relevance. Known: `asdf qwer zxcv 99999` clears the floor at 0.6465. Accepted, no floor change.

## Review notes

1. A follow-up that completes one branch no longer marks the seed complete. Pruning and clearing the frontier wait until no unstaged, unattempted frontier URL remains. The new test failed with `action: enqueued` while the alert URL was still unstaged. It now continues from that URL.
2. Staged crawl URLs and frontier links use the same trailing-slash key. Each start URL is recorded. Two capped jobs in a row failed by starting at the alert page twice. They now start at the alert page, then the modal page.
3. Shared nav links are inserted once. Twenty-five pages with the same 40 links used to issue 1025 inserts. They now issue one multi-row insert, and a later tick skips the links already stored.
4. The named-system boost and path affinity are gone. Search returns vector similarity in score order. The calling agent decides relevance.
5. `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` stay off the frontier, out of the index, and out of citations. Citations keep the highest vector-similarity chunk per page.
6. `how does Paste say to use buttons` returns 28 pages at or above 0.6. The first URL is the Paste quickstart at 0.6992. That is the live vector score, not a pinned page.

## Grit blockers

1. **Named-system order and path affinity are gone.** Simon removed the ranker in this PR. Search returns vector similarity, and no page is pinned first. Live `Paste button guidance` puts `https://ix.siemens.io/docs/guidelines/language/menu-functions-and-ui-labels/button-labels` first at 0.6467.
2. **A capped chain does not prune.** `capped_any` is set on the discover run before the follow-up replaces the job, and a later completed job does not clear it. The run stays incomplete, so pruning does not run and the seed refresh is not recorded. A sitemap-only page stays. Pruning only pages proven gone still needs a complete live map, which a capped crawl does not have, so the safe choice is to never prune after a run that was ever capped. Test: `does not prune or record a refresh when a capped chain's follow-up completes`.
3. **A failed follow-up start does not drop the chain.** A follow-up start has its own five-failure budget, separate from poll errors. Under that budget the tick retries the same URL. The fifth failure records the URL as attempted and the same tick starts the next frontier URL. After three skipped URLs the run ends incomplete, enqueues the staged pages, and does not prune. A 401 or 403 ends the run in that tick. Staged pages stay. Test: `retries a failed follow-up start, then skips that url and keeps staged pages`.
4. **Query strings do not each start a crawl.** Frontier keys drop the query string and the hash before storage and before a start is chosen, so `?tabId=` variants share one path. Tests: `does not start a crawl per query-string variant of the same path` and `does not pick a query-string variant when the path was already staged`.
5. **A 10,000-page ceiling is not a finished refresh.** The run stays incomplete and not Live, does not prune, and does not write the seed refresh or the seed hash. It records a cap defer instead of treating the partial index as done for 30 days. The first incomplete run waits one hour. Consecutive incomplete runs then wait 6 hours, 1 day, and 7 days. A complete run clears the defer. Test: `does not record a seed refresh when the run hits the page ceiling`.

## Scheduled recrawl

`FRESHNESS_MS` stays 30 days. The tests are in `test/scheduled-recrawl.test.ts`. They drive `fillTick` on `*/5 * * * *` with the full 14-s

author: youknowone
body:
Blackhole, bridge and resume fixes that bring these paths closer to PyPy. Most items come from the Codex parity findings filed as #2396–#2429.

## Guard failure and bridges
- **Uncaught exception on a bridge source.** `trace_and_compile_from_bridge` no longer blackholes this failure. It records `GUARD_EXCEPTION` through `execute_ll_raised(constant=false)` + `handle_possible_exception`, then closes with `compile_exit_frame_with_exception(last_exc_box)` (`pyjitpl.py prepare_resume_from_failure` / `finishframe_exception`). The FINISH argument is the symbolic guard result, not a constant of one exception instance. A hot loop raising a distinct `ValueError(k)` 400 times compiles one bridge, and every caught exception carries its own `k`.
- **`must_compile` key.** It hashes a TY_REF `GUARD_VALUE` value by its pointer bits (`compile.py must_compile`, `lltype.cast_ptr_to_int`). That makes the counter follow an object that a minor collection moves, so `guard_failures` depended on the nursery size: across `PYPY_GC_NURSERY` 256KB–16MB, `synth/inheritance_dispatch`, `synth/type_name_attr_fold` and `synth/classmethod_type_dispatch_hot` read 602–1000, 1414–1707 and 201–265. Each now calls `gc.collect()` before its loop and declares `requires-modules=gc`. That pins them at 602, 1414 and 201 at every nursery size, and the cranelift core build, which has no `gc` module, skips them. `inheritance_dispatch`'s baseline moves from 764 to 602; its loops (1) and bridges (3) still equal pypy3's `jit-summary`.
- **Trace-too-long check.** `TraceCtx::is_too_long` also tests the trace's tag overflow (`pyjitpl.py blackhole_if_trace_too_long`).
- **Bridge frame sub-walk.** `drive_bridge_frame_subwalk` keeps every consecutive helper/operator tail. Before, a second tail overwrote the first.

## Tokens and jitdrivers
- **Every JitCellToken names its jitdriver.** `make_jitcell_token` takes the driver descriptor's index, falling back to `active_jitdriver_sd` (`compile.py make_jitcell_token`). `compiled_meta_for_bridge_source`, `jitdriver_index_for_failed_token` and the eviction path expect that index instead of defaulting to driver 0.
- **`redirect_call_assembler` refusal.** `attach_procedure_with_redirect` panics when the backend refuses it, as `x86/assembler.py redirect_call_assembler` asserts. The uncalled `MetaInterp::redirect_call_assembler` is deleted.
- **Segmented-trace FINISH.** It expects the attached `exit_frame_with_exception_descr_ref` instead of minting a fresh descr (`pyjitpl.py _create_segmented_trace_and_blackhole`). pyre's port also expects the host `assertion_error_typeptr` hook, which pyre always installs. The generic majit `create_segmented_trace` keeps `ConstInt(0)` for a host that installs none, since that FINISH is unreachable.

## Reading guard values and resume data
- **`jf_guard_exc`.** `handle_fail_propagate_exception` reads it without clearing it (`llmodel.py grab_exc_value`).
- **Unstamped live ref box.** `MIFrame::ref_value_for_blackhole` returns null for it, matching the int bank, so `copy_data_from_miframe` writes every present register (`blackhole.py _copy_data_from_miframe`).
- **Int virtual.** `DirectVirtualsCache::live_ptr` returns the raw-buffer address (`resume.py getvirtual_int`). Pending-field replay used to write 0 for it.
- **String concat resume.** The VStrConcat/VUniConcat arms root `left` across the decode of `right` and reread it before `bh_call_r` (`resume.py concat_strings`).
- **Asserts instead of skips.** `store_live_frame_array_slot` asserts a live array and an in-range slot (`virtualizable.py write_boxes` / `write_box_at`). `bh_setfield_gc_{i,r,f}` assert a non-null struct (`llmodel.py bh_setfield_gc_*`).
- **Const refs in snapshots.** `snapshot_tagged_to_box` no longer remaps a Const ref onto an InputArg holding the same address, and `ref_liveness_to_tagged` tags a live InputArg or non-constant register as a box (`resume.py ResumeDataLoopMemo._number_boxes` keys on box identity).
- **New test.** `test_get_iter_seeds_sparse_inputarg_positions` covers `TreeLoop::get_iter` seeding the iterator cache at each surviving inputarg's position (`opencoder.py TraceIterator.__init__`).

## Deleted
- **`PyreJitState`'s `materialize_virtual_ref*` overrides.** Also their `alloc_zeroed` helpers (`materialize_virtual_object` / `_struct` / `_raw_buffer`, `write_field_bytes`) and the tests that exercised only them. They had no production caller: guard failures resume through `eval.rs DirectVirtualsCache`, the `ResumeDataDirectReader` analog, which already allocates through the GC.
- **Native-entry probe.** `native_entry_args_intact`, `opcode_clobbers_native_entry_args`, `first_unsafe_native_entry_pc` and the `NATIVE_ENTRY_UNSAFE_PC` cache had only test callers.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p majit-metainterp` (dynasm)
- `cargo test -p pyre-jit -p pyre-jit-trace` (`dynasm,prepass,pyre-module`)
- `python3 pyre/check.py --backend dynasm`
- `python3 pyre/extra_tests/run.py --gated-only --dynasm-only`
- The fold census is unchanged.

body:
## What changed and why

Check A4 in `db/31_verify_ingest_crm_records.sql` compared `cma.ingest_connection(text)`'s `proconfig` to the exact 0006 value `search_path=pg_catalog, cma`. Addition 0008q (`db/76_audit_hardening.sql`, section 7, finding DB-08) sets `pg_catalog, cma, pg_temp` on purpose, on this function and on `cma.find_tenants_for_identity(text, text)`. So the prod run of `31` on 18 October 2026 stopped at A4 (`FAIL A4: ingest_connection must pin its search_path`), and because of `ON_ERROR_STOP` it never reached block B. Dev and prod both hold the new value, so the problem is the stale verifier, not the database. A4 now expects `search_path=pg_catalog, cma, pg_temp` once `cma.schema_migration` holds `0008q`, and `search_path=pg_catalog, cma` before that. It uses the same pattern as `57` for 0008h (`if exists (select 1 from cma.schema_migration where version = '0008h')`).

The diff is in `db/31_verify_ingest_crm_records.sql` only (6 lines added, 2 removed):
- one declaration `v_path text` in block A's `declare` (the expected value, used by the check and by its message)
- one comment line naming 0008q, `76`, DB-08 and the reason (`pg_temp` last, so a temporary object can never shadow `cma`)
- the expected value picked from `cma.schema_migration`
- the message keeps its text and adds the expected value: `FAIL A4: ingest_connection must pin its search_path (expected search_path=pg_catalog, cma, pg_temp)`

**An exception to "never edit a verify script that has run".** This verifier is adjusted in place for a later addition, as `27`, `57` and `61` were (README, Data model sections for 0005a, 0008g and 0008i). No new check for `find_tenants_for_identity`: `77` A5 already covers every SECURITY DEFINER path.

## How it was checked

All runs were on a PostgreSQL 16 that I started in Claude Code's container. As in the earlier night runs, it had a local `public.uuidv7()` stand-in, because 16 has no `uuidv7()`. **4. Provoked run.** I ran a temporary copy with `verify.provoke` set to `true`, made with the same `sed` as `run_migration`, with `ON_ERROR_STOP=0`. Exit 0.
