author: joethompson1
body:
## Summary
Defines the standard formats ("contracts") for the data passed between Safe Context's parts, so they can be built separately without mismatching:
- **Policy:** what the dashboard sends to each laptop (which data types are green, yellow or red, and what to do if checking fails).
- **Events:** what each laptop reports back to the dashboard. Counts only, never the actual text.
- **Hook messages:** what Claude Code sends to our local checker, and the allow/block answers it expects back.

It also proposes the **default list of data types** every new company starts with.

## Needs human input
- **Approve the default data types** (3 green, 4 yellow, 3 red). See the table and 3 questions in [this comment on #2](https://github.com/SafeContext/safecontext/issues/2#issuecomment-6245163595). Don't merge until the team agrees.

## Issue
Closes #2

## Area
contracts (shared formats used by every part), plus tiny updates to detectors and agent

## What changed
- **Policy rules:** if checking fails, the default is **block**; only green data types can be allowed through; every data type must be unique.
- **Defaults:** 10 starter data types (e.g. Customer names → replaced with `customer_1`; API keys → blocked).
- **Privacy built in:** reports to the dashboard reject anything that isn't a count or an id, so prompt or file text can't leak, even by mistake.
- **Claude Code messages:** match Claude Code's docs exactly. When a prompt is blocked, the user's text isn't repeated back.
- **Safety net:** a test checks the plugin talks to the checker at the right address and still blocks if the checker is down.
- **Python copies:** the same formats, exported for the ML side.
- **Checker uses the shared settings:** the local checker now takes its address and port from the shared formats instead of its own copy, so they can't drift apart (from Claude's review).

## How it was checked
- [x] `pnpm check`: all 4 packages pass
- [x] Tests: 23 passed (formats), 2 passed (detectors), 1 passed (checker: `/health` matches its format), 2 passed (dashboard)
- [x] Built the checker and started it; `/health` answered correctly
- [x] Claude PR review: 1 nit, fixed

## Follow-ups
- Dashboard browser tests need Playwright's test browser downloaded once per machine (`pnpm --filter @safecontext/dashboard exec playwright install chromium`); worth adding to the README setup.
- Otherwise none. Once merged, the agent (#9), term lists (#8), dataset (#11) and database (#18) can start.

author: prabirshrestha
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"prabirshrestha"} -->
_Requested by **Prabir**_

Before: `embed`/`embed_many` read the whole response body with `response.text()`, however large. A broken or hostile embedding server (or a proxy in front of it) could make the client hold an unbounded reply in memory; a request timeout limits time, not bytes, and chunked replies have no `Content-Length` to check.

After: the body is read chunk by chunk up to `EmbeddingOptions.max_response_bytes` (default 256 MiB, enough for about 2,000 float vectors of 3,072 numbers). A larger body fails with `Error::InvalidProviderResponse` after reading at most the limit. `EmbeddingOptions::builder().max_response_bytes(n)` sets it.

How: `read_limited` in `providers/openai_embeddings.rs` replaces `response.text()`. Found in a review of an app that uses this crate for embeddings. `EmbeddingOptions` gains a public field, so struct literals need `..Default::default()` (they already do since 0.8.0 added `media_format`).

body:
## Problem

The inventory stack quantities were initialized through two steps (`useState` plus a `useMemo`) that added pointless indirection, and the loop pipeline's `verifier` role had only a vague prompt. There was no written, repeatable review procedure, so verification quality depended on whoever ran it.

## Solution

In plain terms: the app now loads the saved inventory once, cleanly, without the extra memo layer. And the verifier now has a real checklist and skill file so it reviews every change the same five-axis way instead of guessing.

### Changes

- `src/App.jsx`: resolve inventory quantities in a single lazy initializer instead of `useState` + `useMemo` over a value that never changes; drop the now-unused `useMemo` import and extra blank lines.
- `skills/verifier/SKILL.md` (new): the five-axis review method (correctness, readability & simplicity, architecture, security, performance), severity labels, the exact procedure, and the `APPROVE`/`REJECT` output contract.
- `opencode.json`: `verifier` agent prompt and description now point at `skills/verifier/SKILL.md` and the `code-review-and-quality` skill.
- `STATE.md`: mark C1 merged, record the verifier re-run on C1, and add the deferred two-sources-of-truth finding to the Watch List.

### Testing

- `npm run build` passes.
- `npm test` passes 24/24.

### Notes

- No GitHub issue linked.
- Verifier sub-agent is still permission-blocked in headless runs; the C1 verification was executed inline.

## The ruling (SIP-0110 §A.8)

- **No automatic expiry** while the deploy has one operator. It is revisited if the deploy gains users.

body:
## What changed

The first Mutation run after a merge opened #244: 27 mutants survived in the findings tool that #240 added. This change answers all 27.

- **Deleted, 19 survivors.** The type guards in `findings.ts` and `results.ts` checked the shape of JSON that this repository's own jobs write, so no input could reach their false branches. They go, and the reports and the plan are read the way the footprint tool reads its own tools' JSON.
- **Moved, 4 survivors.** `index.ts` ran as a separate process, so Stryker saw no test reach it. The command now lives in `main.ts` and is tested in-process over planted results. `index.ts` only hands it the process.
- **Killed by tests, 4 survivors.** One test now checks the whole issue body for a mutant on line 2. It holds the opening text, the blank lines between sections, and where a line starts.
- **A gap the rewrite closed.** Each job's report is read by its shard's name, as `stryker.shards.json` names it. A job that finished without a report is now written to the issue as broken. Before, it counted as zero mutants and could have closed the issue.

The run after this merge should find no survivor, and its issue job then shuts #244 and names this merge.

## How to see it

Nothing in the app changes. After the merge, the Mutation run on main judges the lines this change edits, and should clear #244 by itself.

## What the checks proved

- A local Stryker run over the four files killed all 135 mutants. That is every mutant in them, not just one per line.
- The 20 tests in `tools/mutation-findings` pass, and so do all 1,037 unit tests, typecheck, lint, knip, spelling, complexity, duplication, claims and counts.
- A two-axis review (standards and spec) found no blocking issue. Both reviews noted the `dir === undefined` check in `judgedFrom`. It stays: dropping it leaves a mutant that no test can tell apart from the original.

author: pascalandy
body:
## Problem

#47 fixed a race between `Output.Write` and `Output.Err` with a mutex, because a handler that outlives its time may still write while the extension answers. `just test` never runs the race detector, and no test makes the two calls meet, so removing the mutex would pass every check. The cost of about 3 seconds in the old issue was measured on an old commit.

## Solution

- **`TestOutputErrDuringFailedWrites`** in `sdk/command/answer_test.go`. Each of 100 rounds makes a new `Output` on a file opened read-only, so every write fails. One goroutine writes, which records the error, while another reads it with `Err`. Each round checks that `Err` reports the error
- **`just race`** runs `go test -race ./sdk/... ./internal/...`. `just check` runs it after `just test`, so `just signoff` runs it too
- **The scenarios keep their mode.** `./sdk/...` and `./internal/...` hold no testscript scenario: `cmd/ncly`, which runs `TestScripts`, and the extensions stay out of the race run. `just test` does not change, so it still builds and runs the scenarios without `-race`
- **Docs.** "Local release preparation" in M00, the one doc that lists the tools of the full local check, adds that the race detector of `just race` needs a C compiler on Linux

A first version of the test ran 4 writers and 4 readers on one `Output`, and the race detector missed the race in 1 of 10 separate runs without the mutex. The error is written once, and many reads of the same word can push that write out of the detector's history. A new `Output` per round puts each write beside the read that races with it. That version failed 30 of 30 separate runs without the mutex.

## Proof

Every run below is at `57df4c4`, with a clean tree before and after. A review fix in #171 then restacked this layer: `57df4c4` is now `fe9805c`, with the same diff, and the head is `cec8c7e`, which only adds the M00 sentence of Docs. So this evidence still covers the code. The mutex came back with `git checkout`, and the defect is not in the diff.

**Negative control on om1.** `Write` and `Err` of `Output` temporarily lose their mutex. Without `-race`, the test still passes, which is why the gate needs the detector. Under `-race`, it fails with the race of #47:

```text
-		o.mu.Lock()
-		o.mu.Unlock()
-	o.mu.Lock()
-	defer o.mu.Unlock()
$ go test -count=1 -run ^TestOutputErrDuringFailedWrites$ ./sdk/command
ok  	github.com/pascalandy/nicely/sdk/command	0.027s
--- exit 0
$ go test -race -count=1 -run ^TestOutputErrDuringFailedWrites$ ./sdk/command
==================
WARNING: DATA RACE
Write at 0x00c0000eb3d0 by goroutine 30:
  github.com/pascalandy/nicely/sdk/command.(*Output).Write()
      <checkout>/sdk/command/answer.go:34 +0xa4
  github.com/pascalandy/nicely/sdk/command.TestOutputErrDuringFailedWrites.func2()
      <checkout>/sdk/command/answer_test.go:24 +0x71

Previous read at 0x00c0000eb3d0 by goroutine 31:
  github.com/pascalandy/nicely/sdk/command.(*Output).Err()
      <checkout>/sdk/command/answer.go:49 +0x34
  github.com/pascalandy/nicely/sdk/command.TestOutputErrDuringFailedWrites.func3()
      <checkout>/sdk/command/answer_test.go:25 +0xe
...
--- FAIL: TestOutputErrDuringFailedWrites (0.00s)
    testing.go:1867: race detected during execution of test
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/pascalandy/nicely/sdk/command	0.189s
--- exit 1
$ just race
...
--- FAIL: TestOutputErrDuringFailedWrites (0.00s)
    testing.go:1867: race detected during execution of test
FAIL	github.com/pascalandy/nicely/sdk/command	0.196s
error: Recipe `race` failed on line 151 with exit code 1
--- exit 1
```

Without the mutex, 30 separate runs of `go test -race -count=1 -run '^TestOutputErrDuringFailedWrites$' ./sdk/command` failed 30 of 30. With the mutex, the same 30 runs passed 30 of 30.

**macOS.** On the mbp (mbp16, macOS 14.6.1, Darwin arm64, Go 1.27.1), in a detached worktree at `57df4c4`. nicely is `mini = false` in fleet's `repos.toml`. `go env` gives `CGO_ENABLED=1` and `CC=cc`, which is Apple clang 16.0.0 (clang-1600.0.26.6). `just race` passed every package. The same control failed 30 of 30 separate runs with `WARNING: DATA RACE` and `race detected during execution of test`, and with the mutex back, the runs passed 30 of 30. `just check` passed there too, with `go test -race ./sdk/... ./internal/...` among its steps.

**cgo and the C compiler.** On Linux, `-race` needs cgo: on om1, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -race ...` answers `go: -race requires cgo; enable cgo by setting CGO_ENABLED=1`. om1 has `CGO_ENABLED=1` and `CC=gcc`, GCC 16.2.1. On macOS, Go has not needed cgo for `-race` since Go 1.20: on the mbp, the same call with `CGO_ENABLED=0` passed.

**Durations**, measured at `57df4c4`, except the base row:

| Run | om1 (Linux amd64) | mbp (macOS arm64) |
|---|---|---|
| `just race`, build cache warm | 1 to 3 s | 4 s |
| `GOFLAGS=-count=1 just race`, tests not cached | 3 s | 3 s |
| `GOCACHE=<empty folder> just race`, race build from scratch | 11 s | not measured |
| `just check`, Go caches as they are | 17 s | 82 s, its first run there, with module downloads |
| `GOFLAGS=-count=1 just check` at `57df4c4` | 59 s, then 62 s | not measured |
| `GOFLAGS=-count=1 just check` at `4877e25`, the base without `just race` | 59 s, then 57 s | not measured |

On om1, the two heads alternated in one checkout, so both used the same build cache. The race run adds about 3 seconds to an uncached check, within the noise between runs.

## Disposition

Closes #52. Every Done when item holds:

- A test of `sdk/command` makes failed writes to `Output` meet reads by `Err`
- `go test -race ./sdk/... ./internal/...` is on the path of `just check`, and the testscript scenarios keep their build and their run without `-race`
- Without the mutex, the test fails under `-race` with a detected race. With the mutex, it passes. The defect is not in the diff
- The race run passes on Linux and on macOS. The report names the Mac and confirms cgo and the C compiler
- `just check` passes with the mutex, and each duration above was measured on the tested commit

No real race showed up: every package of `./sdk/...` and `./internal/...` passes under `-race` on both machines.

## Checklist

- [x] 1. Spec: n/a, the card adds a check and no command, flag, JSON key, or code of `ncly`
- [x] 2. Scenario: n/a for a `.txtar`, since `ncly` does not change. The targeted test fails under `-race` without the mutex, as shown above
- [x] 3. Code: the test passes with the mutex
- [x] 4. Text: n/a, no user-facing string
- [x] 5. Checks: `just check` passes
- [x] 6. Verify: n/a, the card reaches nothing that the scenarios replace
- [x] 7. Docs: n/a for a milestone status, since no milestone card owns #52. "Local release preparation" in M00 now says that the race detector of `just race` needs a C compiler on Linux (`cec8c7e`). README.md is unchanged, because a user sees no change
- [x] 8. Sign off: `just signoff` passed on `cec8c7e`, the head of this PR

Plain stack on `main`, bottom to top: #198 (#95), #202 (#132), #203 (#171), #204 (#131), #205 (#52). GitHub runs a closing keyword only for a pull request whose base is the default branch, so each PR must target `main` when it merges.

author: kazu-2020
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"kazu-2020"} -->
_Requested by **matazou** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01JuAUmWGW99LKkKCiUtiYLT?thread=cmsg_01JuAUmWGW99LKkKCiUtiYLTAYw5WDuGgvyT5ZQ71Wc9v8)_

Before: on the writer, the commit of one `remove_member` took 39 s at x8 (39M cells) and 205 s at x32 (157M cells). The x32 peak memory was 12.3 GB, and with a standby on the same 15 GB VM the writer ran out of memory.

After: the same commit takes 0.17-0.26 s at x8 and 0.99-1.41 s at x32, and the peak memory does not grow.

When a member went, `journal._cell_changes` used the by-id compare. That compare made Python dicts of every cell of each input Metric on the dimension, old and new (36.0 s of a 36.7 s commit at x4 in cProfile). The record then had 0 cell rows.

How:
- `journal._renumbering` gives the old member number and the new member number for each dimension. `Store::diff_cells` maps the old keys while it merges, with `merged_iter`, so the memory is O(diff).
- `Store::remove_member(.., last)`: if the last member goes, no numbers close up, so only its cells go and the untouched segments stay shared.
- `journal.structure` skips the dimensions that did not change.

## Record format change (please check)

The cells of a removed member, and member-type values that point to it, are no longer written as `[key, old, None]` rows. Replay already skipped these rows, and `cell_history` cannot ask for a gone member. A reader of the records outside the engine loses these rows.

## Measurements (writer only, FileJournal, one new empty Employee member)

| Case | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| x8, last member | 39.0 s (36.6-43.8, n=6), peak +2.5 GB | 0.17-0.26 s (n=8), peak +0 |
| x32, last member | 205 s (n=1), peak 12.3 GB | 0.99-1.41 s (n=3), peak +0 |
| x8, member in the middle | 38.6-40.7 s | 0.81-0.89 s, +290-350 MB for a short time |

The x8 runs alternate between main and this branch. Details are in the project note `notes/remove-member-perf.md`.

## Tests

- 2 new tests in `tests/test_journal.py`: a removal with renumbered member-type cells, and a removal of the last member followed by a new member that takes its number.
- rust 1029 and reference 1029 pass. `test_pg_journal` passes 65/65 with RustFS. cargo test, clippy `-D warnings` and pyflakes are clean.

## Known limits

- A removal from the middle stays O(all cells on the dimension) in Rust.
- `Store::remove_member` with `values=true` still rebuilds the whole store.

## What

- **`Containerfile`**: Debian slim + the linux binary (glibc), no `ENTRYPOINT`, root, so GitLab CI can use it with a plain `image:`. Written for buildah/podman *and* Docker BuildKit (no `RUN`, so arm64 builds without emulation), built from the release archives rather than the sources.
- **CI** (`build.yml`): `test-image` builds it with Docker, podman and buildah on every run and smoke-tests both images (including building the README and changelog pages inside them); `merge-release` now waits for it. `image` (releases only) pushes `linux/amd64,linux/arm64` to `ghcr.io/jetbrains-markdown-cli/jetbrains-markdown-cli` as `X.Y.Z`, `X.Y`, `X`, `latest`, and warns if the package is not anonymously pullable.
- **Dogfood**: the release job converts `CHANGELOG.md` with the published image (`docs/changelog.yaml`) and attaches `CHANGELOG.pdf`, next to the `README.pdf` made with the action.
- **README**: new *Container image* section with `docker`/`podman` usage and a two-job GitLab CI example (convert, then print to PDF with Chromium).
- **`feat: --no-raw-html`** (own commit): found while dogfooding. `CHANGELOG.md` mentions `<style>` in plain text, which was passed on as HTML and hid the rest of the page, so the PDF was one page long. `--no-raw-html` / `raw-html: false` (pandoc's `markdown-raw_html`) shows HTML as text; `docs/changelog.yaml` uses it.

## Verified

- `linuxX64Test` green (new tests for the switch and the changelog page); both pages built with the new binary, `CHANGELOG.pdf` printed with Chromium (2 pages, tags visible as text).
- Image built with podman and `buildah --platform linux/arm64`; the CI smoke test run locally with podman. Real BuildKit is only exercised by the new CI job.
- The GitLab CI example ran on gitlab.com in a temporary private project (image from its registry): both jobs green, 17-page PDF. The project was deleted afterwards. `chromedp/headless-shell` hangs on `--print-to-pdf` and `zenika/alpine-chrome` runs as non-root and cannot write the artifacts, hence Chromium on plain Debian.

## Before/after merging

- **Merging releases automatically** (`merge-release`): this has `feat`s, so it will make a release (1.2.0) and publish the image for the first time.
- A new ghcr package starts **private** and its visibility can't be set from a workflow: after the first release set `ghcr.io/jetbrains-markdown-cli/jetbrains-markdown-cli` to *public* in the package settings (the `image` job prints a warning until then; the release does not fail).
- Then check: `podman pull ghcr.io/jetbrains-markdown-cli/jetbrains-markdown-cli:latest`, `CHANGELOG.pdf` on the release, and re-run the README's GitLab example against the ghcr image.

author: mattbaconz
body:
# phonton-cli v0.25.1 — Local runs survive a busy laptop

0.25.0 recommends `qwen3.5:4b` for 4-6 GB GPUs, but on exactly that hardware
local goal runs often stopped halfway with `resource_pressure`. 0.25.1 lets a
model that is already loaded in VRAM keep working when the rest of the
machine is busy.

## A loaded model keeps working

`phonton goal --local` refused every model call once available host RAM fell
below 1.5 GiB, even when the exact calibrated model (same digest, same
context) was still loaded entirely in VRAM. That reserve covers starting the
runtime. A model that is already loaded holds its host memory, and the
available-RAM reading already excludes it, so the check counted that memory
twice. Running the project's checks between model calls, such as an offline
`npm ci` and jest, was enough to trip it with a browser and chat apps open.

A call to a copy held entirely in VRAM now needs 512 MiB of free host RAM.
On Ollama 0.34.2 with an RTX 4050, loading `qwen3.5:4b` at 16384 tokens took
about 700 MiB of host RAM; a later 7,000-token call to the loaded copy loaded
nothing. Everything else still fails closed:

- a cold load keeps the 1.5 GiB reserve (2 GiB when the model is partly
  offloaded to the CPU);
- a resident copy that is partly in RAM keeps the 1.5 GiB reserve;
- a loaded copy with another digest or a smaller context gets no exception
  and is admitted like a cold load;
- an unknown memory reading still stops the run before inference.

Residency is still checked again immediately before each call; it is an
observation, not a reservation.

In the 0.25.0 Aider Polyglot run on a 16 GB RAM, 6 GB RTX 4050 laptop, this
check ended 18 of 51 Phonton runs, including 13 of 17 JavaScript runs, about
100 seconds in, after the jest checks.

## Tests

- `018f0b0` adds a repro: at that commit the run ends `resource_pressure` where `review_ready` is expected. `5a04d53` makes it pass.
- fmt and clippy `-D warnings` pass locally. The full workspace suite runs here in CI, because Bitdefender quarantined cargo.exe on the dev machine.

author: aminwoo
body:
## Summary
- **The problem:** the clock model charges each action of a team on turn on both boards a fixed `TeamMoveTimeMs`. For the move being searched, a front end often knows its real cost: nachos budgets lead-cost moves at half its usual time, while `TeamMoveTimeMs` is the median of past moves. So every root child was valued at the wrong lead, and that decides who may sit afterwards.
- **New UCI option `RootMoveTimeMs`** (default 0, which keeps the old behaviour). The root team's next action costs this amount when it is charged. Every later action in the tree keeps the usual move time.
- **How `TimeState` carries it:**
  - it's a next-move time that the team's next action uses up, whether or not that action costs lead;
  - `can_sit_through` counts it for the first action;
  - `exact_key` includes it only when it's set, so states without it hash exactly as before.
- **Background searches** (`go background`) run from the opponents' side, so `run_background_search` drops the next-move time.

The front-end half is in nachos: lead-cost moves are no longer extended, and they send their budget plus the measured delivery overhead, capped by the partner's median.

## Tests
- `TimeStateTest`, for both teams:
  - a paid action uses up the next-move time;
  - so does a free one;
  - the other team leaves it untouched;
  - sit-through counting;
  - dropping it leaves the plain clock.
- Clock key: set only at the root, and identical to a plain clock once used.
- UCI: the option sets and clears the next-move time, and persists across `position` and `ucinewgame`.
- `RootMateSearchTest.TheRootActionPaysItsBudgetAndOnlyIt` (descent level). It searches a root where white is on turn on both boards with an 800 ms lead. Charged the usual 1000 ms, black may sit after the root move; charged a 400 ms budget, white still leads. Every expanded child is checked against the clock key at the lead after the root action. I confirmed it fails if the descent ignores the budget.

Results:
- TensorRT build: 432 pass, 1 skipped (already skipped before).

author: zcsizmadia
body:
Closes #277

## What

ChaCha20 now computes several keystream blocks at once with the cross-platform `System.Runtime.Intrinsics` API (`src/SshSharp/Crypto/ChaCha20.Vector.cs`):

- **Lane layout (word-sliced):** vector N holds state word N of consecutive blocks, one block per 32-bit lane (lane j = block counter + j). The rounds are the scalar rounds applied to all lanes. Rotations by 12 and 7 use shifts, and rotations by 16 and 8 use constant byte shuffles. Each group of 4 words is then transposed into 16-byte rows per block (constant shuffles and selects) and XORed with the input.
- **Path selection:**
  - 8 blocks (`Vector256`) when it is hardware accelerated, on .NET 10 only. On .NET 8 the JIT doesn't inline the 8-block output stage, which made that path slower than 4 blocks.
  - Otherwise 4 blocks (`Vector128`: SSE on x64, AdvSimd on Arm64).
  - Otherwise the scalar code. Big-endian machines also use the scalar code.
  - Whole groups of 8 blocks, then of 4, take the vector code. The tail (fewer than 4 blocks, possibly partial) takes the scalar block function.
- **Counter:** the 64-bit counter carries from the low word into the high word per lane with a compare mask, with no branch. It wraps at 2^64 like the scalar code.
- **JIT tiering:** the kernels use `AggressiveOptimization`. With tiering, the measured time varied 2x between runs depending on the tier.
- **Poly1305 is unchanged.** It is now the larger share of a packet (about 10 of 17.9 µs for 16 KiB). The portable vector API has no 32x32->64 lane multiply, so vectorizing it would take x64- and Arm64-specific intrinsics. The numbers and options are in `docs/benchmarks.md`.

## Numbers (i7-12800H, Windows 11, `--job medium`)

| | Runtime | Before | After |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| ChaCha20 32 KiB | .NET 10 | 49.4 µs (663 MB/s) | 16.6 µs (1,979 MB/s) |
| ChaCha20 32 KiB | .NET 8 | 40.4 µs (811 MB/s) | 22.0 µs (1,493 MB/s) |
| chacha20-poly1305 packet seal, 16 KiB | .NET 10 | 35.4 µs (463 MB/s) | 17.9 µs (915 MB/s) |
| chacha20-poly1305 packet seal, 16 KiB | .NET 8 | 30.5 µs (537 MB/s) | 21.3 µs (769 MB/s) |
| seal + open, 16 KiB | .NET 10 | 70.4 µs | 36.5 µs |
| seal + open, 16 KiB | .NET 8 | 64.1 µs | 44.0 µs |

## Safety net

- **Differential tests** (`Crypto/ChaCha20VectorTests.cs`):
  - Paths 8, 4 and 1 are each forced explicitly through an internal overload, so every path runs on every CI platform.
  - Every length from 0 to 2000 with random keys and nonces.
  - Counters around 2^32 and 2^64, with the wrap landing in each lane.
  - A 1 MiB + 37 B buffer, separate and in place.
  - An independent check of the carry and the wrap against the block function.
  - Per-kernel group counts, and the path selection truth table.
- **RFC 8439, framework AEAD and Wycheproof vectors pass.** The framework AEAD comparison now includes lengths that hit the vector paths.
- **Timing test** (`--timing 15000`), |t| on .NET 10 / .NET 8:
  - key, dispatched: -0.42 / -0.03;
  - key, 4 blocks: -1.33 / 0.69;
  - data: -0.20 / 1.21.
  - Fix in the harness: the fixed class used to reuse one cached array, which showed as a false t = -16.9 on 1,000-byte inputs. It now gets a fresh copy per sample.
- **Stryker** (`chacha20-poly1305` scope, net10.0): 87.74 % (403 killed, 5 timeouts, 57 survived).
  - Every survivor in the ChaCha20 files is equivalent: `>>` to `>>>` on `ulong`, an exception message string, a scalar loop `<` to `<=` that XORs 0 bytes, and removing the 8-block call (the 4-block kernel then produces the same bytes).
  - The other survivors are existing ones in the unchanged `Poly1305.cs` and `ChaCha20Poly1305OpenSsh.cs`.
- **Build:** the full suite passes on net8.0 and net10.0, `dotnet build -c Release` has 0 warnings, the AOT smoke test publishes and runs, and the docs build has 0 warnings.

author: mohanraj00
body:
Fixes #301

On the 0.9 held-out set, admit rejected 85 baseline and 98 runner candidates with `VALUE_NOT_IN_EVIDENCE`, and the value was the cited number times a scale (#297). The documents write the scale as `£m`, `£'000` or `€70,471m`, and SPEC §4.1 did not read these forms. This PR does not measure the rule. A new set must measure it, not the 0.9 set.

## Decision

`k`, `m` and `bn` count as a scale only directly next to a currency sign. I reuse the signs that §4.2 already lists: `$`, `€`, `£`, `₹`.

- §4.1, scale suffix: a number with a currency sign directly before it gets a scaled value when one of these suffixes is directly after it: `k`/`K` (10^3), `m`/`M` (10^6) or `bn`/`Bn`/`BN` (10^9). `€70,471m` is 70471000000. A candidate with the number as written gets `SCALE_WORD`.
- §4.1, currency scale: `£m`, `$bn`, `£'000` or `£’000` is a heading scale on any line, also on a line with a tab. It reaches the lines with tabs after it, as "(in thousands)" does.
- §4.6, `scale` role: an item can hold a currency scale. The item fails when a scale word lies between it and the value. It also fails when a currency scale with another power of ten lies there. The second `£m` of `\t£m\t£m` does not stop an item on the first.

The rule is strict. `70 m` and `5m` stay as written, because a bare `m` can be metres. `£5 m` (a space before the m), `£ 9m` and `£5mm` also stay as written. A scaled candidate there gets `PART_MISSING` with `scale`.

## Vectors

I wrote the vectors by hand in the first commit (b03750a), before the code:

- `60-currency-scale-suffix`: the scale suffix, and the negative cases `70 m`, `5m`, `£5 m`, `£ 9m`, `£5mm`.
- `61-currency-scale-heading`: tabbed `£m`, `£'000` and `$bn` headers. A `£m` with no table after it, a bare `(m)` and `£ m` reach no number.
- `62-currency-scale-item`: scale items with currency scales. An item fails when it ends after the value or when `£bn` lies between it and the value. A bare `(m)` gives no scale.

## Checks

ruff, ruff format, mypy and pytest pass: 1421 passed, 18 skipped. `examples/irs-590a` rebuilds with no change.

This PR changes how groundgate reads documents, so it needs a security review.

author: jessegrabowski
body:
`Import.timeraw_gEconpy` replaces the four `Import` benchmarks and times `import gEconpy` in a fresh interpreter. Its untimed setup first imports every runtime dependency the installed gEconpy declares in its package metadata, so the timed import covers gEconpy's own modules. The old benchmarks all measured the same full-package import after evicting gEconpy from `sys.modules`.

Added `BuildMemory` and `BuildStatespaceMemory`, which report the peak bytes `tracemalloc` traces during one model build. Their `setup` runs one untimed build first. asv runs a `track_` benchmark in a fresh process, and the first build there also allocates lazily imported modules and one-time caches. On gEconpy main that first `BuildStatespace` build traced 241 MB, against about 4 MB for later ones.

`tracemalloc` traces Python and NumPy allocations. It doesn't see memory used by subprocesses, such as C compilation.

A quick asv run against gEconpy main reports `timeraw_gEconpy` at 95 ms, `BuildMemory` at 1.8 to 7.0 MB across the model ladder, and `BuildStatespaceMemory` at 3.5 MB.

author: nissa-seru
body:
## Problem

An adapter can return a `stopReason` that membrane doesn't map, such as `'error'`, without a `providerStopReason` (#154). `mapStopReason` normalizes it to `end_turn`, as it should, since callers switch on a closed union. But `details.stop.providerReason` came only from `providerStopReason`, so the token itself was dropped, and nothing in the response showed that the stop wasn't a clean end of turn. A caller that refuses a failed stop by its `providerReason`, as anima-research/agent-framework#380 does for `'error'`, accepted it.

By our reading of all eight built-in adapters, each returns `providerStopReason` beside any token membrane doesn't map, so only adapters from outside membrane reach this.

!Closes #154.

## Changes

- **`providerReasonFor`** settles the token `details.stop.providerReason` carries for an adapter's result: its `providerStopReason` when that's a token, and otherwise its `stopReason` when membrane doesn't map that token. A `stopReason` membrane maps, given alone, still leaves `providerReason` unset. Only a non-empty string counts as a token, in either field.
- **It runs where an adapter's result enters membrane:** in `complete()`, and in `streamOnce`, which every `stream()` and `streamYielding()` round goes through. That's before membrane's own stop can replace the adapter's `stopReason`: a stop sequence that `LocalStopSequences` or the XML tool loop finds in the text makes it `stop_sequence`. The places that build `details.stop` read `providerStopReason` as before.
- **The texts say what `providerReason` carries now:** the docs of `StopInfo.providerReason` and `ProviderResponse.providerStopReason`, the default arm's comment, and both lines it logs. The first said `providerReason` was present only when the adapter supplied the raw token, and the second, after 64 tokens, that it carries each.

## What callers notice

- A response whose adapter returned an unmapped `stopReason` without `providerStopReason` now carries that token as `details.stop.providerReason`. Its `stopReason` is still `end_turn`, or `stop_sequence` where membrane found a stop sequence, and the token is still logged once per process. The token may be the adapter's own word rather than the provider's.
- When the adapter gives a `providerStopReason`, `providerReason` still carries that, so an unmapped `stopReason` beside a different `providerStopReason` doesn't reach it.
- A `providerStopReason` that isn't a non-empty string, such as `null` or `''`, now counts as none: the field is a string, omitted when no reason was reported. It was reported as `providerReason` as it came, so where a built-in adapter passes on a server's empty stop token, `providerReason` is now unset. An empty or non-string `stopReason` isn't carried either.
- Otherwise the built-in adapters' responses don't change: they return `providerStopReason` beside any token membrane doesn't map. Tests show that through membrane for `openai`, `openai-compatible`, `openrouter` and the Responses API, and they pass with `main`'s `membrane.ts` too. For `anthropic`, `bedrock`, `gemini` and `openai-completions` it's our reading.

## What each part is for

**What it's for:** an unmapped stop token given without `providerStopReason` was dropped, so the response read as a clean end of turn. The fix keeps it where callers already look for the provider's word.

1. **`providerReasonFor` and `isStopToken`** (10 lines of code and their doc comments) are the rule, in one place. It asks `mapStopReason` whether a token is one it maps, since that switch maps each token it knows to itself, rather than listing the mapped tokens a second time. It keeps `providerStopReason` first, so an adapter's report of the provider's own word still wins. It counts only a non-empty string as a token, so a `null` from a JavaScript adapter or a server's empty token isn't reported as one.
2. **The two doors** (one line each): `complete()`'s and `streamOnce`'s. Settling the token where the result enters means a stop membrane finds afterwards can't drop it, and four stream loops need no call of their own.
3. **The texts** said `providerReason` was present only when the adapter supplied the raw token, which no longer holds.
4. **The tests** (+111 lines in one file): the three entry points in both tool modes, a stop sequence membrane finds, the adapter giving both fields, the five other tokens membrane maps, and the null and empty values.

**Not taken:**
- Documenting that an adapter must set `providerStopReason` beside any token membrane doesn't map, the issue's other option. Nothing would hold an adapter outside membrane to it, and one that missed it would still read as a clean stop.
- Reading the token at each of the five places a response's stop is built. By then a stop sequence membrane found has replaced the adapter's `stopReason`, so the token would still be lost there.
- A separate field for the adapter's own token. It would keep `providerReason` to the provider's word, but a caller would read two fields to learn one thing, and agent-framework#380 would have to change to read it.
- A new `StopReason` member for an unmapped token, which would change the closed union every caller switches on.

The source is +55/−11 in three files, and 14 of the 55 added lines are code.

## Tests

In `tests/unit/stop-reason-loudness.test.ts`, `an unmapped stop token the adapter gives without providerStopReason`, with an adapter built on `MockAdapter` that returns `stopReason: 'error'` and no `providerStopReason`:
- `complete()`, `stream()` and `streamYielding()`, each in native and XML tool mode: `stopReason` and `details.stop.reason` are `end_turn`, and `details.stop.providerReason` is `'error'`.
- `stream()` and `streamYielding()`, each in native and XML tool mode, with a stop sequence in the adapter's text that membrane finds itself: the response is `stop_sequence`, with that sequence as `triggeredSequence`, and `providerReason` is still `'error'`.
- Through all three entry points, an unmapped `stopReason` beside a different `providerStopReason` gives the `providerStopReason`.
- A `null` `providerStopReason` beside `'error'` gives `'error'`. An empty `stopReason`, and a number as one, give no `providerReason`.
- Each of `max_tokens`, `stop_sequence`, `tool_use`, `pause_turn` and `refusal`, given alone, gives no `providerReason`. `pr56-review-boundaries` already holds that for `end_turn`.

Runs at `c5f58ede` on Linux, Node 24.22.0, from a clean `npm ci`:
- `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean, and `stop-reason-loudness`, `pr56-review-boundaries` and `stop-reason-log-cap`, the three test files that name `providerReason` or the unmapped-reason log line, pass 147 of 147.
- With `main`'s `src/membrane.ts` and this branch's tests, 11 fail: the six cases through the three entry points, the four with a stop sequence membrane finds, and the `null` `providerStopReason`. The rest pass on `main`, as they should.
- Taking out each of nine pieces on its own, with the rest in place, fails at least one test: either door left as it came; `streamOnce`'s reading the stop after `LocalStopSequences` replaced it; a `null` `providerStopReason` counted as given; a token that needn't be a string, or may be empty; any token but `end_turn` counted as unmapped; any token carried, mapped or not; and an unmapped `stopReason` put before `providerStopReason`.

The head, `442c5807`, changes only the changelog fragment's wording after `c5f58ede`. CI's [run](https://github.com/antra-tess/membrane/actions/runs/39100496146) at `442c5807` typechecked, built and ran the suite on Node 22.12.0, 24 and latest on Ubuntu, and on 22.12.0 and latest on macOS. Each passed 2625 of 2625 tests in 134 files, against 2604 of 2604 on `main` `a6037789` ([run](https://github.com/antra-tess/membrane/actions/runs/39091768985)). The 21 more are this change's new tests.

## Not verified

- **No live provider, and no adapter from outside membrane.** The new cases use a stub adapter built on `MockAdapter`.

@KakarottoCake **Draft: code done, needs a Wii (and a Wii U) with the adapter.** Split out of #115, which covers controls files, shake, Wii Remote rumble and the Bluetooth diagnostics.

## What it does
The GameCube controller adapter for Wii U now plays in GameCube games. This matters most on a Wii U, a Wii Mini and a Family Edition Wii: none of them has GameCube ports, so the adapter is the only way to use GameCube controllers there.

- **Menu side** (`TakeGcAdapterForGameCube` in `wii/launch/boot.cpp`, `take_adapter_handle` in `wii/hooks/padhook.cpp`):
  - Settings > GameCube adapter decides, with the rules Wii games follow (`settle_gc_adapter`), applied to the menu's IOS, which GameCube games keep. On a Wii U that is IOS 58, so **Automatic** works there.
  - The menu opens `/dev/usb/hid` before the hand-over, and passes the handle, HID version, adapter device and rumble in `rwp_gc_launch`. The handle comes from the launch's own v5 handle when there is one, else a fresh one after libogc's USB lets go, the same as for Wii games.
- **Plugin** (`gcnative.cpp`): places the adapter's state (`gc_gcad`) in MEM2, only when the menu passed a handle.
- **Blob** (`runtime/gc/gc_gcad.c`, new):
  - Runs the same driver as Wii games (`runtime/rtgcad.c`) from `PADRead`, with polled IPC.
  - Replies that nothing was waiting for are routed between the adapter and the Wii Remotes (`gc_ipc_route`). `gc_ipc_send` now takes the context instead of `gc_bt`.
  - The adapter's controllers take ports by `gc_ports.h`'s rule before the Wii Remotes fill what is left. A real pad in a Wii port keeps its port. **GameCube rumble** reaches the adapter.
- **Trace:** new words `gcad` (link << 24 | version << 16 | ports filled << 8 | device), `gcad_reports` and `gcad_error`.
- **Docs:** GUIDE (controllers in GameCube games, the adapter section, Experimental), ARCHITECTURE and MAP.

## To do from the first list
- [x] Real GameCube ports: #91's rule (real pads keep their ports) is on main, and the earlier trace showed a remote moving to port 2 when Dolphin's pad held port 1. Still needs a real pad on a Wii.
- [x] The adapter in GameCube games, as Wii games get it.
- [x] Mixing: the real ports first, then the adapter's controllers, then the Wii Remotes.
- [x] L+R+Z+Start to leave: it is checked on the final pad status, after every fill, so it works from any controller kind.

## Testing
- Dolphin, Melee from the gcn card:
  - With **Automatic**, the adapter stays off and the game runs as before.
  - With **On**, the blob gets the v5 handle. The trace reads `gcad=0x500ff`: link NONE, because Dolphin lists no adapter. Melee runs to its progressive-scan question with 4503 pad reads and no exception.
- Host: 74 suites pass. The new `gcgcad` suite runs `gc_gcad.c`'s port filling and rumble on the host. It covers adapter controllers on their own ports, a real GameCube controller keeping port 1 while the adapter's moves to port 2, all four ports taken, stale reports, not set up yet, and rumble through the moved port, with rumble off and a WaveBird. Breaking the port bookkeeping makes it fail.
- Wii build clean (only the two expected warnings).
- **Not tested: a real adapter.** Dolphin has none.

## Needs a Wii / Wii U
1. A Wii U (or a Wii with the adapter) on **Automatic**, with a GameCube game from the SD card:
   - Does a controller in adapter port 1 play as port 1?
   - Does rumble work?
   - Does L+R+Z+Start go back?
2. A Wii with a real pad in GameCube port 1 and an adapter pad in adapter port 1: the adapter pad should move to port 2.
3. With a problem report afterwards, `sd:/riftwii/gc/trace.bin` has the `gcad` words (link 3 = reports flowing).

## Context size
The blob's context is now a fixed 0x600 bytes, with the size in a defines-only `runtime/gc/gc_layout.h` that `gc_entry.S` includes. A new field only has to fit, which is checked; the size and the assembly's `.fill` no longer change. #114 (GameCube games from USB) is stacked on this branch.

## Cost
About 8.5 KB more blob in MEM1 for every GameCube game. The adapter's state goes in MEM2, and only when there is an adapter.

## Self-review
- The request struct grew in the middle, which is safe because a plugin must carry the DOL's exact build stamp.
- `settle_gc_adapter`'s RVZ exclusion belongs to Wii games on d2x, and GameCube RVZ games don't go through d2x, so they get the adapter.
- Demo mode becomes On for GameCube games.

author: casperleerink
body:
Step 2 of #283: a parent's own ports are ends of its connections, so the keyboard, the mic and a child's numbers go where a parent wires them.

## What changed
- **Own ends:** an end without `child` is a port of the parent itself, with the same key per kind as a child's.
  - `from: { port: "audio" }`: what reaches its audio input. `from: { notes: "notes" }`: what reaches its notes.
  - `to: { port: "audio" }`: what it plays, through its own `sound`, which stays the last stage of its output. One connection for the common chain.
  - `to: { number | bang | notes: "x" }`: an output `x`, which its own parent connects like any child port.
  - tsc refuses a wrong pair. An undefined `child` is reported as a problem; it does not quietly become an own port.
- **Every TS tool has `notes`:** effects and parents too. `onNotes` and `send` without `child` mean the same for every kind. An effect's sound follows the newest held note, as a source does.
- **Arrangement:** an instrument track has its own `notes` input, where its clips and the keyboard meet. Every child that takes notes hears them, including TS effects, parents, and plugin effects (MIDI sidechain, as in Reaper). After a device with latency they arrive that much early, because events are not delayed. This is documented and tested.
- **Keyboard at the top:** it plays every top-level instance that takes notes, as a track plays each of its devices, instead of the first one by name. `Keyboard::play_into` takes a list of ports. A test proves two top instances get the key and the pedal on the same frames. Re-measured: top parent 6.90 → 6.93, Crow Hill ×4 8.01 → 8.11, both within run-to-run noise; no audio code changed.
- **Core:** `AudioThru` and `EventThru`, pass-through processors for a port that many connections meet at.

## What it removes
- `ownSound`, and the six port structs and two enums, now one `End`.
- The step-1 keyboard path to Bun (`hear_keyboard`, the transport's hearing state, `Keyboard::take_heard`).
- The "an effect has no notes" refusal.
- The rules "a parent hears its sound, not its notes" and "mic only into a top effect".

## How it was verified
- **New tests** (`own_ports.rs`), each with the CLAP and VST 3 test plugins where a plugin is involved:
  - The live keyboard at the top plays a plugin child through the parent's notes. The render is sample for sample the one the plugin gives at the top, key and pedal on the same frames.
  - The mic into a parent reaches its child.
  - A child's number passes out of a parent inside a parent.
  - An effect hears its track's clip, also across a bypass.
  - An undefined child is a problem.
- **Updated tests:** effect and latency tests, now that plugin effects hear notes. `sdk-types.ts` covers the own ends.
- **Checks:** fmt, typos and clippy pass. 1438 tests of the touched crates pass. The new, effect and latency tests also pass with `RTSAN_ENABLE=1`.
- **Example tools** (written from the agent doc alone):
  - A top parent with the real VST 3 Crow Hill piano as child `keys`, driven by the live MIDI input: first sound on frame 1069 both through the parent and at the top. author: justgooogleit
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"JustGooogleIt"} -->
_Requested by **Ashwin** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01HchedVUpyNe3TAVEjrKUoF?thread=cmsg_01HchedVUpyNe3TAVEjrKUoFF32icfLmAthbsHRFjthiKv)_

Before: to shop something seen in a video, you screenshot it yourself, open ClipCart, and upload the file.

After: pause the video, click the ClipCart toolbar button, **Shop this frame**, drag around the piece, **Open in ClipCart**. The studio opens with the cropped frame uploaded and detection running, as if you had uploaded it there.

The extension uses only existing endpoints. It opens a tab on the ClipCart origin and runs `POST /api/sessions` and `POST /api/media/uploads` there as same-origin requests, so the browser's own `cc_owner` cookie and the `X-ClipCart-Request` guard work unchanged. Nothing reaches ClipCart, and no model is called, until **Open in ClipCart**.

**How:** a Manifest V3 extension in `apps/browser-extension/` (plain JS, no build step) with a popup, an extension-owned crop preview and a settings page for the ClipCart address. Permissions are `activeTab`, `scripting` and `storage`, with host access to `127.0.0.1` and `localhost`. It handles unsupported pages, capture failures, black (protected) frames, cancelled crops, duplicate clicks and an unreachable server. Install and test steps are in `apps/browser-extension/README.md`; the contract and the requested backend change are in `apps/browser-extension/HANDOFF.md`.

**Provenance (HANDOFF change B), now implemented in this PR:** `POST /api/media/uploads` takes optional `sourceUrl` and `sourceTitle`. A capture is stored as `sourceType: "browser_capture"` with the page URL and a cleaned title, and the studio shows "Browser capture · {title}". The extension sends both, and the preview tells the user so. Plain uploads are unchanged.

**Tested** in Chromium 141 against a fixture server on `integration` a1741a8: 5 unit tests and 11 end-to-end steps pass. Automation can't click Chrome's toolbar, so the test copy of the manifest adds `<all_urls>` in place of the `activeTab` grant, and the video is a static page showing a real fc01 frame. README "Testing" lists what was real and what was substituted. A real toolbar click in desktop Chrome hasn't been tried yet.

## Review update (backend lane, after #15, #16 and #17 merged)

**Merged** `integration` 60c06d7 into this branch. Then:
- **Provenance** (327864e):
  - **Backend:** the upload route validates `sourceUrl`. It must be http(s) with a host, no credentials and a valid port, and at most 2048 characters. Anything else returns 422 before the body is read. The title is cleaned and capped at 300 characters, and a title without a URL is rejected.
  - **Contracts:** `MediaAsset.sourceTitle` and the `browser_capture` source type, regenerated additively.
  - **Studio:** the "Browser capture · {title}" label.
  - **Tests:** `tests/api/test_capture_provenance.py`.
- **Extension fixes** (a7e360c):
  - **Concurrent sends:** `send()` checked its in-memory guard only after two awaits. Two simultaneous sends for one capture, for example from a duplicated preview tab, made **2 uploads and 2 sessions**. The worker now claims the capture synchronously, and the same reproduction makes 1 upload, with the second message refused as "in progress".
  - **Sent before navigating:** a successful upload is now recorded as sent before the studio tab is touched. If the user closed the helper tab mid-handoff, the studio opens in a new tab, and a Retry can't upload the frame twice.

**Checks on this branch:**
- **Backend suite:** 282 passed, 1 skipped.
- **Web:** `tsc -b` and `vite build` are clean.
- **Extension unit tests:** 5 of 5 pass.
- **End-to-end:** 12 of 12 steps pass in Chrome for Testing 155 against a fixture server. The new step covers simultaneous sends, and the upload step now also checks provenance and the studio label.
- **Load unpacked:** the shipped folder loads with no errors, and the popup reports the server as ready.

**Reviewed and fine as is:**
- **Same-origin handoff:** the content-script fetches carry `cc_owner`, and `X-ClipCart-Request` needs no CORS. `sessions/resume` sorts by `createdAt`, so the studio opens the capture's session.
- **Capture permissions:** `activeTab`, `scripting` and `storage`, plus host access to loopback only, where a pattern without a port covers every port. Other hosts are optional and requested from a user gesture.
- **Failure handling:** health check, permission prompt, upload errors and closing the helper tab on failure.

**Still to do:** a real toolbar capture from a playing video in desktop Chrome. Keep this PR unmerged until that's done.

Before: base HP was the only balance knob, so it ran backwards: Sigrun had 4110 HP while Anvil had 780. Win rates on main had drifted to 26–86% (Orrin 86%). Afterburner's 5-damage-per-Fire blast was busted. A handful of cards (Arterial Strike, Overcast, Tempest, Archmage, Storm Mind) dominated.

After:
- Base HP follows body type: brawny 2200–3000 (Anvil, Aldric, Brakka, Mordrek, Bram), medium 1750–2150, slight 1300–1700.
- Afterburner has no blast. Burning out 40 Fire gives 3 seconds of double attack speed, and every hit scorches for another 30% (shown in orange). The fighter is wreathed in flames while it lasts, and burning more than 40 Fire makes it last longer.
- Strike's trigger passive is +3% attack damage per card instead of +1% attack speed, since Fire already covers speed.
- Card pass: top cards toned down, weak ones buffed.
- Gladiators win 39–56% across 4000 bot matches. Nightshade (39%) and Haze (41%) trail; everyone else is 43–56%.

How:
- `HP_BANDS` and `body` in `characters.js`, plus a new ability power stat (`stats.ap`) shown on the pick screen. `tools/autotune.mjs` moves HP inside the band and puts the rest into ability power. Hand kit changes cover what that couldn't (Orrin, Rook, Mordrek, Bram, Cinder, Sigrun, Haze, Nightshade, Kael, Twinfang, Brakka, Glacia).
- Engine:
  - New Afterburner (`FIRE.rush` 1, `FIRE.scorch` 0.3). Cooling Draught now shortens the enemy's Afterburner.
  - `STRIKE_AD`.
  - `ARCANE_CAP` = 25: Arcane gives ability power for at most 25 stacks.
  - Evasion passive is +5% Focus per card.
- Cards:
  - Nerfed: Arterial Strike, Overcast, Archmage, Storm Mind, Tempest, Evergreen, Last Stand, Pained Insight, Titan, Juggernaut, Undying Spite.
  - Buffed: Pandemic, Ember Heart, Reflective Plating, Thundercrack, Bloom Burst, Frostbite, Thermal Shock, Molten Armor, Phantom, Flurry, Mana Shield, Ice Armor, Guarded Swing, Barrier.
- `src/ai/cardValues.js` is regenerated with `tools/cardvalue.mjs`, so bots value the new numbers.

Note: balance is sensitive to how bots draft. Regenerating card values alone moved some gladiators by over 10 points, so bot sims are a guide, not ground truth.

## Goal

Reduce the architecture model drift that #824 reports on main. Refs #824.

## Scope

- `.archcontext/model/` through archctx 0.8.1 ChangeSets.
- `docs/architecture/`: provider projection output, and hand-written module citations.
- `docs/architecture/.projection-manifest.json`.
- No source, script or test file changes.

## Changes

- The owner decided on 2026-10-18 to exclude `docs/architecture`, `docs/researches` and `.ai/harness` from ownership. Contract Assets now has these three source exclusions. The `.ai/harness` includes and two explicit document includes are removed. All 180 tracked paths in the three trees now resolve with no owner.
- 59 observed cross-capability dependencies are now declared: 38 runtime and shared-helper imports, and 21 verification consumers. They use `depends-on`, not invented direct calls.
- Envelope and binding selectors now name the functions that make the calls.
- Hand-written citations in 17 module pages now name current files or symbols. Historical references point to verified Git objects.
- The index inventory states the final counts: 28 capabilities, 56 components, 286 relations, 36 flows.

| Debt kind | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| unowned-path | 202 | 27 |
| undeclared-dependency | 59 | 0 |
| stale-anchor | 57 | 0 |
| flow-proof-failed | 10 | 6 |
| Total | 328 | 33 |

## Remaining (stays in #824)

- 27 unowned paths outside the three excluded trees. They need an owner decision. Examples: `docs/images/*`, `docs/plans/*`, `references/*`, `src/cli/commands/retention.ts`, `src/effects/artifact-retention.ts`, `src/core/tools/catalog.ts`.
- 6 selectors stay unproven. The calls go through dependency objects, or one file has a function and a property with the same name. CodeGraph has no direct edge for them. No required flow step uses them.
- 19 citations stay unchecked: 14 ambiguous short paths and 5 JSON selectors that the checker does not support.

## Verification

All checks ran on `77c2a230` with a fresh temporary HOME. archctx is 0.8.1. CodeGraph is 1.6.2.

- `archctx validate --format json`: valid, 0 errors.
- `archctx flows check --json`: 106 of 112 selectors proven, 0 unproven selectors used by flows.
- `repo-harness architecture-projection anchors --json`: 0 findings in 1,093 citations.
- `repo-harness architecture-debt --json`: 33 items.
- `repo-harness architecture-projection check --json`: `noop`, freshness ok, no human actions.
- `bun run check:type`: exit 0.
- `bash scripts/check-ci.sh affected --base origin/main`: exit 0, 197 test files (190 parallel, 7 serial), `[ci] OK`.

## Risk and rollback

- Model and documentation only. The edit guard and `state resolve` read the model. Paths in the three excluded trees now have no owner, so ownership checks no longer report them.
- Rollback: `git revert <squash-commit>`, then run `repo-harness architecture-projection apply`.

Fixes restart probing for anonymous buyers (Esha's S1 ask, \"Decided with Vivan: buyer identity\").

When ChatGPT/Claude send no buyer_id, the gateway mints `anon_<random>` per chat, so a new chat reset the start limit, buyer memory and the jittered endpoint.

- `probeId()` (store.ts): every `anon_` id maps to one shared `anon` bucket per product. `memoryKey`, the StartLimiter key, `buyerEndpoint` and the jitter key all use it. Jitter stays deterministic for the shared bucket.
- Named and simulated buyer_ids are unchanged (their own bucket).
- `ExchangeResponse.buyer_id` echoes `ctx.buyer_id` so the gateway/model can send it back. E1-owned `exchange/types.ts` only; shared contract untouched (`MakeOfferOutput` is non-strict).
- Test: different `anon_` ids on the same product: later chats never beat the first one's last offer, the shared 4/day start limit trips on the 5th anon chat, and a named buyer is unaffected.

Note: the shared limit is 4 starts per product per day across **all** anonymous chats. If demo traffic opens many anon chats on one product, raise it (`START_LIMIT`) or have the gateway pass a stable id.

author: jayhemnani9910
body:
## What

`llmfit serve --unix-socket <path>` removes whatever is at `<path>` before binding. That clears a stale socket left by a previous instance, but it also:

- deletes a regular file given by mistake:

  ```
  $ echo "important notes" > notes.txt
  $ llmfit serve --unix-socket ./notes.txt
  $ cat notes.txt
  cat: notes.txt: No such device or address
  ```

- unlinks the socket of a server that is still running. A second `llmfit serve --unix-socket a.sock` takes over the path; once it stops, the first server is still running but `curl --unix-socket a.sock` gets "Couldn't connect" (exit 7).

Both on v1.1.17 and main.

## Change

Before binding, the path is removed only if it is a socket and connecting to it is refused (no listener). A regular file or a live socket makes `serve` fail with `<path> exists and is not a socket` or `<path> is in use by another server`, and nothing is deleted. Any other connect error (for example permission denied on another user's socket) is reported instead of deleting the socket. The connect is async with a 1 s timeout: a live server whose accept queue is full makes connect pend or fail with `WouldBlock`, and both count as in use. This needs tokio's `time` feature in `llmfit-tui` (no new dependency). The stale-socket case from #671 (a pod volume across container restarts) still works: connecting to a dead socket fails, so it is removed.

## Tests

New `remove_stale_socket_keeps_files_and_live_sockets`: a regular file and a socket with a live listener are kept and reported, a socket whose listener is gone is removed, a missing path is fine. With the old unconditional delete it fails at the first assertion.

`cargo test`: all green (llmfit bin 144 passed vs 143 on main). `cargo fmt --check` clean. `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features`: 61 warnings, the same set as main.

Manual check with a debug build: a listener with a full queue gives `is in use by another server` in under 1 s; `serve --unix-socket ./notes.txt` exits 1 with `exists and is not a socket` and the file is intact; a second `serve` on a live socket exits 1 with `is in use by another server` and the first one still answers `/health`; after killing a server, a new `serve` on the leftover socket starts normally.

A symlink at the path is now refused too, where it used to be replaced.

author: p-w-rs
body:
## What this brings (gateway 0.6.0)

Everything since main: **accounts** (the 0.4/0.5 work) and the **v2 rework** on top.

### Accounts
- Separate identities as `KIND:NAME`: several GitHub accounts, Hugging Face, Pijul (the Nest and self-hosted), SSH hosts, Azure / Databricks (Entra sign-in), the ASI ML Catalog, container registries.
- Tools that run as the right account: `git` (all of git), `gh`, `git_mirror`, `git_identity`, `hf`, `pijul`, `ssh_exec` / `ssh_copy`, `databricks`, `mlcat*`, `registry`, `account_list`.
- A credentialed runner: env allowlist, a private ssh-agent per call, a one-call credential helper, hardened git config, scrubbed output.

### v2
- **One strict mode, always on**, installed as a normal plugin: the rules live in the plugin's own hooks, and nothing is written to settings.json.
- **Short typed commands**: `/gate:add`, `update`, `delete`, `enable`, `disable`, `block`, `list`, `export`, `import` (plus `help` and `log`). Claude guides a setup with question pop-ups, and values are typed only in a **native dialog** (macOS, or zenity/kdialog), or at `gateway finish GRANT` in a terminal when there's no screen. The web form and the v0.5 `/gate:secret|sudo|account` commands are gone.
- **The gateway's own SSH config**: routes (LAN, then away), one host identity across routes, host-key policy (pinned / ask / accept-new), key rotation, opt-in connection reuse (`/gate:enable reuse ssh:NAME`), `ssh_hosts`.
- **Export / import**: one passphrase-encrypted age file (full or shareable copy), validated and summarized before it merges.
- **Per-account switches**: `/gate:enable exec|delete|write|read KIND:NAME [always]`, `/gate:disable`, `/gate:block` (read-only).
- The skills are for Claude only, so the slash menu shows only the commands you type.
- README rewritten for newcomers; ARCHITECTURE and CLAUDE.md updated.

## Testing
- `pixi run test`: 793 passed, 0 failed (hermetic: throwaway vaults, fake dialogs/browser/sudo, local sshd and HTTP servers). Each phase's security properties are mutation-checked.
- `claude plugin validate` passes for the plugin and the marketplace.
- Live on macOS (desktop app): every account kind; push, PR and mirror; setups through the dialogs; ssh exec/copy/sudo and reuse; export and import; the switches.
- Not yet live: ssh routes (no LAN route to test against), Linux end to end, the ACR token exchange.

author: midego1
body:
# Summary

Lets soiguru.com know who is signed in and keep saved places in the account, sends visitors back to the public page after signing in, and gives the sign-in, register and sign-out screens the SoiGuru look.

## Related Issues

Spec: `docs/spec/058-soiguru-accounts/spec.md`. Public-site side is in the companion PR from `claude/soiguru-astro-cloudflare-deploy-18er0p`.

## Description

soiguru.com is static and has no accounts. This app already has register, sign-in, password reset, verification, 2FA and the `favorites` table, but the public site could not see the session, sign-in never returned to soiguru.com, and the screens still showed template copy.

## Changes Made

- [x] `GET /api/soiguru/me`: signed-in state, name, initial, admin/owner flags, saved slugs. Credentialed CORS only for `PUBLIC_SITE_ORIGINS`; no e-mail or ids.
- [x] `POST /api/soiguru/saved`: add/remove saved slugs (known listings only). 403 for foreign origins, 401 when signed out.
- [x] `/return?to=`: 303 back to a public-site URL, else the public home (no open redirect).
- [x] `/auth` shell in the SoiGuru look; sign-in and register cards reuse the template credentials form (new `hideHeader` prop) and social buttons; the switch link keeps `callbackUrl`.
- [x] `/auth/signout`: server-action sign-out, then back to the public page.
- [x] Middleware keeps `/auth/signout` for signed-in users and honours a safe relative `callbackUrl`.
- [x] English and Thai texts (`soiguru.account`, plus missing Thai form strings).

## Screenshots / Videos

Checked locally in a production build at 1280px and 390px: sign-in, register, sign-out, forgot password, Thai sign-in.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature

## Implementation Details

The session cookie is `SameSite=Lax` on owner.soiguru.com. soiguru.com is the same site, so a credentialed `fetch` sends it. NextAuth only redirects within this origin, so every return to soiguru.com goes through `/return`.

## Testing Instructions

- `tsc --noEmit` passes; eslint on changed files has no errors; `next build` passes.
- Against `next start`: `/api/soiguru/me` returns `{"signedIn":false}` with CORS for `https://soiguru.com` and no CORS for other origins.
- `/return` sends `https://evil.example`, `//evil.example` and `javascript:` to `https://soiguru.com/`.
- `POST /api/soiguru/saved` returns 401 signed out and 403 from a foreign origin; the preflight returns 204 with credentials allowed.

## Deployment Notes

No new env vars. `PUBLIC_SITE_ORIGINS` (default `https://soiguru.com,https://www.soiguru.com`) is shared with spec 056. Social buttons appear only for providers whose client ID and secret are set.

## Checklist

- [x] Spec, index row and `docs/log.md` entry
- [x] No new dependencies

## Additional Context

Forgot password, new password and verification keep their template cards inside the new shell.

author: techrote
body:
Closes #13

## Summary
- Implement the seeded, bounded DRIFT granular engine with six note streams, deterministic per-stream Poisson scheduling, four grain windows, scatter controls, source-bank regeneration with a 50 ms crossfade, and a five-band morphing formant bank.
- Add wind, howl, field, and held-gust controls, complete parameter registration, bounded telemetry, eight packaged factory presets, and `drift --list-presets`.
- Clarify the DSP and live-map contracts in `docs/rag/08-DRIFT-SPEC.md`; record the prepass and provenance.

## Validation
- `python tools/check.py --package all --packaging` — 446 tests passed (kit 339, AURORA 38, LOOM 44, DRIFT 25); all four wheels built, installed into a clean environment, and passed metadata, import, resource, version, and preset-list checks.
- `python -m compileall -q drift/src/trio_drift` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- DRIFT's dense six-stream/96-grain test completed below its 10-second bound with counted pool drops.

## Contract changes
`docs/rag/08-DRIFT-SPEC.md` now records source-color regeneration at block boundaries with a 50 ms crossfade, field density/source-position mapping, gust and smooth-wind density factors, and sample-offset scheduling behavior. Factory preset documents omit `field.x` and `field.y` so map coordinates remain live performance controls. No instrument architecture or sound identity was changed.

## Limitations and manual checks
No physical audio, MIDI, or terminal hardware checks were exercised; qualification is device-free. DRIFT's terminal UI and skins remain in TRIO-014 scope.

## Provenance
Codex desktop, GPT-6 (exact configuration unavailable); Git/GitHub CLI, PowerShell, Python 3.12.10, NumPy 2.4.3, SciPy 1.17.1, pytest 9.1.1, setuptools 84.0.0, and wheel 0.48.0. An independent review tier was unavailable, so I performed a fresh highest-effort self-review against the complete issue, RAG contract, diff, package boundaries, and platform/packaging effects.

author: zaida-3do
body:
## What

R2 of wave 5: the per-user NSIS installer, with everything the app launches bundled. Built on `release/v1` after S1 (#82) and S2 (#89). Builds locally with `npm run build:installer` (not published, no updater, no signing).

- `host/app/tauri.conf.json`: `bundle.active`, NSIS only, `installMode: currentUser`, version **1.0.0** (release/v1 only, never forwarded). Resources: `worker/src` (staged at run time), `worker/package.json`, `helpers/package.json` and `helpers/{usage,titles,autocomplete}/src`, laid out the way the host looks (`<install folder>/helpers/<name>/src/main.ts`, and the helpers' own `../../../worker/src` imports). Installer hooks file: `host/app/windows/installer-hooks.nsh`.
- Root `package.json`: `build:installer` (`tauri build --bundles nsis`).
- `checks/e2e/w5-installer.e2e.ts` (new, reads files only): bundle on, NSIS, per-user, no updater, version 1.0.0 on release/v1; **every `helpers/<name>/src/main.ts` is a bundled resource** and the worker is; every relative import in a bundled file lands inside the bundle. Mutations: removing the titles resource fails the helper test and the import test; removing `worker/src` fails the worker assertion.
- Docs: `docs/handover-v1.md` install section and known gaps (from the S1/S2 PR bodies), `docs/patrick-retirement-checklist.md`, the `CLAUDE.md` "Installer" row.

### Two Rust fixes outside my territory (flagged on f0a2deb7 and ccb2e018; no reply, so I made exactly these)
They are why wave 4's "the installed app has no usage helper / titles" MUST-FIX was not just a bundling question. I found them by smoke-testing the installed app.
1. `host/crates/workers/src/stage.rs`: Tauri's `resource_dir()` is a Windows verbatim path (`\\?\C:\...`); Node cannot run a script given that way (`EISDIR` on `C:`), so every helper spawned from it died instantly ("the helper's answer was not JSON"; chats stayed untitled). New `plain_path()` strips a `\\?\` + drive prefix (leaves UNC and ordinary paths alone); `default_source` uses it. Test `a_verbatim_resource_folder_becomes_a_plain_drive_path`.
2. `host/crates/usage/src/helper.rs`: `helper_script(debug)` passed `resource_dir = None` to `default_source`, so in release it returned `None` and the meter said "Helm could not find its usage helper" whatever was bundled. A release build now looks beside the executable (where the installer puts the resources). Logic split into `script_beside` with a unit test.
No new dependency, no other crate touched; `host/app/src/main.rs` unchanged.

### Installer decision: install folder
Tauri's per-user default install folder is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Helm`, which is also the profile folder (D-P4), so program files and data would share a folder. `installer-hooks.nsh` moves the default to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Helm` (a folder the user picks, and an earlier install's folder, are kept; the empty old default is removed). The setup's directory page still shows the old default text first. Proposed overlay row: "NSIS per-user installer without updater (D-H6 deferred to M13); install folder `Programs\Helm`".

## Smoke test from the INSTALLED app (Calliope, final head 17dde07, build:installer then `/S` install)
Launched `Programs\Helm\helm.exe` with `HELM_PROFILE_DIR` on a scratch folder and WebView2's debug port, real `claude` (release builds ignore `HELM_TEST_CLAUDE`), DOM reads only:
- usage meter live: `Plan usage: 5-hour window 10%, Weekly window 65%` (3 of the 5 runs after the two fixes showed live numbers);
- a new chat got an automatic title: `Title: Keyboard focus rings in desktop apps`;
- the chat round-tripped with the real claude (one-sentence answer, status idle).
- Uninstall (`uninstall.exe /S`): program folder, registry entry and Start-menu shortcut gone; a file placed in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Helm` stayed.
- Upgrade over an existing install kept `Programs\Helm`.

Honest notes: (a) the usage meter showed "unavailable: Claude Code reports no plan limits" in 2 of those 5 runs; the same helper run from the repo gives the same cold-start answer, Claude Code 2.1.289 answers its first `get_usage` without limits some of the time, and the UI then polls only every 10 minutes (`ui/src/usage/store.ts` `POLL_MS`). Not a packaging problem; follow-up: re-read after about 15-60 s on `no_limits`. (b) The automatic title keeps a literal "Title: " prefix (cleaning in `helpers/titles`). body:
## 🗒️ Description

### What
- Refined bot event classification in `resolve_event_policy` to distinguish between autonomous partner bots authoring PRs (`cline-cloud[bot]`, `google-labs-jules[bot]`) and internal/suppressed loop bots (`hannibal-hub-agents[bot]`, `coderabbitai[bot]`).
- Added an immediate short-circuit in `execute_agent_event` when `policy.mode == Mode.IGNORE`, returning empty actions and preventing session allocation or conversational dispatch fallthrough.

### Why
- On PR #389, Cline opened a PR with author login `cline-cloud[bot]`. The recently added unified policy layer blanket-matched all `*.endswith("[bot]")` logins into `Mode.IGNORE`.
- Because `policy.mode` was not `Mode.FORMAL_AUDIT`, `execute_agent_event` selected the `conversational_runner` and fell through to `_post_conversational_reply`, posting the raw audit JSON directly into the PR comments thread as an unformatted issue comment instead of a structured GitHub Pull Request Review (`pr.create_review`).
- Furthermore, events resolved to `Mode.IGNORE` should never invoke runners or dispatch conversational comments.

### How
1. In `src/webhook_agent/core/policy.py`:
   - Imported `is_hannibal_bot_login` from `bot_identity.py` to suppress internal app loop events.
   - Defined `PARTNER_BOT_LOGINS` (`google-labs-jules[bot]`, `cline-cloud[bot]`, etc.) and `SUPPRESSED_BOT_LOGINS` (`coderabbitai[bot]`, `github-actions[bot]`).
   - Allowed PR lifecycle events (`canonical in FORMAL_REVIEW_EVENTS`) from partner bots to resolve to `Mode.FORMAL_AUDIT`, ensuring zero-bypass code reviews.
   - Preserved review-intent comment triggers for partner bots while suppressing unprompted bot comment chatter.
2. In `src/webhook_agent/core/execution.py`:
   - Added an immediate early-return guard checking `if policy.mode == Mode.IGNORE: return []` right after policy resolution.
3. In `tests/unit/core/test_execution.py`:
   - Added unit test coverage for partner bot PR audits, review-intent comments, unprompted bot comment suppression, own-bot loop suppression, and the `execute_agent_event` short-circuit guard.

body:
Arm swings could leave sleeve and outline pixels in the idle body, split the painted elbow, or move a support hand after the arm had already been solved. Several source wrists also pointed to boots, capes or tails. This change registers the actual hands for every articulated form/facing and moves the complete indexed sleeve through a continuous skin. Original fingers retain weapon contact; duplicate procedural fists are removed.

Two-handed grips and weapon bounds are solved together before the final elbows. The painted chest follows physical shoulder yaw, including the two intermediate Brakk slash frames found by full-cycle movie validation. Evolved skeleton staves keep their staff identity. Bloomkin's fairy skin keeps its authored hands and wings without an extra caster arm pair. Expanded recoil coverage also fixes folded short natural legs during hit/stagger. Both offline HTML files are rebuilt.

### Artwork and visual evidence

Reviewed all 41 families, three source forms and eight facings (984 cells). The 12 independent-arm families are knight, orc, dwarf, troll, elf, caster, fox, goblin, minotaur, skeleton, rogue and frostelf (288 bind cells). Natural/winged families, variants, occluded limbs, costumes and original palette indices retain their authored skinning paths. The fairy proxy exception is documented.

- [Review index and all family sheets](https://github.com/DCardimen/AutoB/blob/feat/complete-authored-arm-animation/public/arm-animation-review/index.html): 41 original/current sheets and 36 arm ownership, isolated torso and swing sheets. Run `node scripts/serve-arm-review.mjs` and open `http://127.0.0.1:3048` for the linked players with byte-range seeking. Both players and all 98 review links were checked.
- Full normal-speed movies: [Wild](https://github.com/DCardimen/AutoB/blob/feat/complete-authored-arm-animation/public/arm-animation-review/wild/all-companions.mp4), [Warden](https://github.com/DCardimen/AutoB/blob/feat/complete-authored-arm-animation/public/arm-animation-review/warden/all-companions.mp4). Each player supports native 64px and enlarged family views.
- Decoded intermediate Brakk slashes: [Wild](https://github.com/DCardimen/AutoB/blob/feat/complete-authored-arm-animation/public/arm-animation-review/wild/decoded-critical-slash.png), [Warden](https://github.com/DCardimen/AutoB/blob/feat/complete-authored-arm-animation/public/arm-animation-review/warden/decoded-critical-slash.png). Decoded action/recoil/fall samples and source/offline desktop/phone combat recordings are included beside the players.
- [Exact results and source fingerprints](https://github.com/DCardimen/AutoB/blob/feat/complete-authored-arm-animation/public/arm-animation-review/verification.json), [implementation and reproduction](https://github.com/DCardimen/AutoB/blob/feat/complete-authored-arm-animation/docs/ARM-ANIMATION-OVERHAUL.md).

### Validation

- Every one of the 89 roster entries: 302,600 poses across 17 states, eight facings, five phases, all evolution inputs and both evolved paths; 115,600 arms and 8,774,295 owned arm pixels checked, zero failures.
- Full movie cycles: 484,128 rendered poses, 566,784 final bone-length checks, zero stretched arms or clipped pixels. Both 164-second movies decoded at 1x; 272 native/enlarged state/facing samples, every family enlarged, no browser errors. Original/current sheets and decoded pixels were visually inspected.
- 29 targeted anatomy, raster connectivity, deformation, grip/carry and weapon tests; 13 final contract/palette/Brakk tests; 15 relevant gait/leg tests passed. Expanded natural deformation covers 35,496 poses and 26,205,840 positive-area source quads.
- Decoded part export validates all 984 cells, exact indexed reassembly and palette preservation. No production skeletons or debug leg volumes; assertion thresholds were retained.
- 32 delivered combat encounters cover all 89 characters in source and isolated offline mode, plus both evolved paths for articulated roster entries. Additional source/offline contact, stride, training-glade and default desktop/phone combat checks pass with no page errors or external offline requests.

The complete unit run initially passed 60/63 files. The expanded 17-state run exposed the natural recoil fold fixed here; its full deformation file and related tests pass on rerun. Two existing failures remain: 48 coalcrab/mireclaw contact cases in `combat-spacing.test.js`, and the shield-counter balance expectation in `overhaul.test.js`. Both reproduce identically in an isolated checkout of base `45b6859`; baseline and current logs are included. The entire game suite is therefore not claimed green. No disconnected, stretched or clipped arm is known in the validated coverage.
