author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

ComfyUI workflows often chain multiple LoRAs or use different combinations at different samplers. SGLD currently rejects multiple dynamic adapters on the same target, and its ComfyUI LoRA loader does not expose the merge mode. This adds multi-adapter dynamic execution and a mode selector on the existing loader.

## Modifications

- Add `merge_mode=dynamic|merge` to `SGLDiffusion LoRA Loader`, defaulting to `dynamic`, including older workflows that omit the field. All loaders chained on one MODEL must use the same mode; separate MODEL branches can choose independently.
- Forward the selected mode through the existing sampler-time binding, so switching modes on the same adapters reconfigures the shared worker.
- Accumulate every dynamic adapter's delta and output offset with its own rank, alpha, and strength, preserving the existing single-adapter computation path.
- Clear old adapters on the first matching adapter for each layer, and finalize cached merges even when the last adapter does not cover that layer. Update all adapter strengths during dynamic reactivation.
- Document the compute and BF16 rounding tradeoffs; retain compact regression coverage.

## Accuracy Tests

After rebasing onto main (`e5dc10e73b`), **131 tests passed** on H200 (CPU and CUDA); pre-commit passed on all changed files. Coverage includes:

- Existing single-adapter numerical regressions.
- Multiple dynamic adapters with different ranks, alpha values, strengths, and output offsets, for ordinary and stacked matrices in exact/lossless modes.
- `A -> A+B -> B -> no LoRA`, mode changes, partial layer coverage, and strength reactivation.

Full H3 workflow output-quality validation is still pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked end to end. Dynamic mode adds per-adapter forward computation; merge mode trades adapter binding work and weight rounding for less per-step computation. Full H3 workflow timing and multi-GPU validation remain pending, so this PR is a draft.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Update documentation.
- [ ] Provide full workflow accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

author: reserendipity
body:
## 为什么

本机跑不了 tarpaulin（不支持 Windows），所以「哪一行没覆盖」只能从 CI 取回来看。而现有的 Codecov 上传**一直因为缺 token 而失败**（`fail_ci_if_error: false` 把它盖住了），不是可靠来源 —— 前面十几轮阈值上调，我都是靠 grep CI 日志里 tarpaulin 的逐文件明细表反推的。

## 改动

在 `rust-test` job 里、`cargo fmt check` 之后加一步：

```yaml
- name: Upload Rust coverage artifacts
  if: always()
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: rust-coverage-report
    path: |
      ./src-tauri/coverage/lcov.info
      ./src-tauri/target/tarpaulin/*.json
    retention-days: 14
    if-no-files-found: warn
```

- `if: always()`：即使 `--fail-under` 失败也照样上传（红的那次报告才是要看的）
- `if-no-files-found: warn`：不让「没跑覆盖率」的 job 因此变红

## 价值

- 之后任何一次 CI 都能直接下载 lcov，用本地脚本算出**精确到行**的未覆盖清单，不用再靠日志表格估算
- 14 天保留，够跨 PR 对比「这批测试到底覆盖了哪些行」

## 验证

- YAML 解析通过，pre-commit `check yaml` 通过
- 本 PR 的 `Rust Tests` job 应能看到 `rust-coverage-report` artifact

body:
## What

A per-product **Agotado** switch for the inbox sales agents (Rafael 2026-10-18).

- **Owner:** Configuración › Agentes › ② Productos que vende › **¿Hay stock?** lists each product as «Disponible / Agotado». A sold-out product can take an optional **Vuelve aprox.**: a date (today to +180 days, Costa Rica time) or a short note with no numbers.

  - Stock 0 also counts as sold out, but only when the store tracks stock (at least one product has stock > 0).
- **Agent:**
  - Never shows or quotes a sold-out product's price, and never closes the sale for it. A code step plus the validator check `sold_out_offered` enforce this.

  - Offers an in-stock alternative, and drops combos that name the sold-out product.
  - If the customer accepts the alternative, the agent closes the sale normally.
- **SQL 055** (`InventoryItemAvailability`): additive, gated `BETSY_V2_APPLY_FILES=055`, RLS on. Until Rafael applies it, nothing changes and the list stays hidden.
- **API:** `PATCH /api/chat/agents/[id]/inventory` needs update_config, same-origin, rate limit and a strict body. The product must be in this agent's list and this tenant. Every change is audited.

- **Advisor:** GO with changes; all applied.

author: agent-kortix
body:
## Review in 60 seconds

- **What:** the transcript capture and the inbox transcript read warned on the *expected* states of a sandbox that is stopped, gone, or cold — proxy 503/404/502 on the sub-agent walk, platinum `expose -> 409` auto-stop, read-budget timeouts. Both reads fail open by design; the warn was a false alarm, not a fault. One classifier (`apps/api/src/projects/lib/runtime-read-failure.ts`) now splits expected from unexpected, expected logs info, unexpected keeps its warn.
- **Bounded walk:** a dying box made one prod capture pay 60 consecutive failed child reads (one per sibling). `readChildTranscripts` now stops the walk only when the runtime cannot serve any transcript (`unavailable`: 5xx, timeout, dead connection, proxy-no-row) and lets the next capture or the unread chain take the rest; a per-transcript 404 (`missing`) does **not** stop it — one gone child must not starve the siblings after it, including a running sub-agent's transcript.
- **Nothing behavioral for users:** every read fails open exactly as before (`read: false`, `null` capture, mirror untouched) — log triage plus the bounded walk. Every new test fails on the trunk and passes here.
- **Fixes:** KRTX-2723 (package for KRTX-2368 + KRTX-2349).

**Risk:** low — log-level split plus a bounded walk on a fail-open path; every read's return contract is unchanged (`read: false`, `null` capture, mirror untouched). ## Summary

The transcript capture's sub-agent walk and `readInboxTranscriptState` warned on the expected states of an idle-session sandbox, and the capture's outer catch warned ~10×/h with `sqlstate=unknown` and no error attached (~17,701 lines in four days). Prod ClickHouse evidence: `[transcript-mirror] sub-agent read(s) failed` 637 warns over 10-14→10-18 (503 ×313 = box stopping mid-turn-end because the stop flow captures before `provider.stop`; 404 ×248 = sandbox row / child transcript already gone, `[proxy] no sandbox row`); `[session-lifecycle] inbox transcript read failed` error mix 10-13→10-15 dominated by `platinum POST /v1/sandboxes/<id>/expose -> 409` (Platinum auto-stops idle boxes) and `The operation timed out.` (~228 of the window's lines), the measured `expose -> 429` rate limits (2 lines in the wider window) staying warn-worthy.

Control-plane answers (`PlatinumHttpError`) are expected only for 404/409/5xx — the measured `expose -> 429` rate limit and any 401/403 stay warn-worthy (pinned by test). Deliberately no error-`code` check: these catches also wrap database work, and Postgres errors carry `ECONNRESET`/`ECONNREFUSED` as `code` — a database outage must keep its warn (pinned by test).
- `session-transcript-pages.ts`: the first-page non-ok throw is `TranscriptReadError(status)`; message text unchanged so existing log patterns keep matching.

- `session-transcript-capture.ts`: the per-capture line goes through `childReadFailureLog`; the outer catch classifies — expected → info `capture deferred` with `{error, sqlstate}`, unexpected → warn now carrying the real `error:`.

_Requested by **Enzio** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_012j8YkbmEZ13dFctEmDHtyy?thread=cmsg_012j8YkbmEZ13dFctEmDHtyyEpLdHt8PDNAPdNxY2Zo53c)_

Before: the reminder only appeared while the tracker was open on screen or in a background tab, so phones that had left the page never got it.

After: each phone that installs the free ntfy app and subscribes to the family's topic gets a push notification at the due time, even with the tracker closed. The notification has **Fed** and **Snooze** buttons that open the app. Settings gains a "Reminders when the app is closed" panel that shows the topic and has a copy button.

How: whenever someone logs, edits or deletes a feed, snoozes, or changes settings, that phone books the next reminder on ntfy.sh, using the `At` header for the due time and the fixed sequence ID `next-feed`. A new booking with the same sequence ID replaces the earlier one on the server, so only the latest due time fires. When a notification button opens the app, the app waits for the shared log to load before applying Fed or Snooze, so the action reaches everyone. The topic is `ari-feeds-<family id>`.

Tested in headless Chromium with ntfy and Firestore faked. Setup and new feeds book a reminder 3 hours out with Fed and Snooze links, and opening the `#snooze` link records the snooze in the shared log and re-books. I couldn't reach ntfy.sh itself from the test machine, so the first real check will be on a phone.

# O que mudou?
Implementação da suíte de testes de unidade para a camada Web (MockMvc) voltada ao AgendamentoController, isolando integralmente as regras de negócio do AgendamentoService via @MockBean. A abordagem blinda o principal fluxo de marcação e gestão de consultas da aplicação, assegurando que o roteamento das requisições, as validações de payload (@Valid), a conversão de parâmetros de data (@DateTimeFormat), a paginação (@RequestParam) e a extração do usuário logado via @AuthenticationPrincipal operem com estabilidade e retornem os códigos de status HTTP apropriados.

Adicionalmente, foi incluída a dependência spring-security-test no pom.xml para viabilizar a injeção do contexto de autenticação e manipulação segura de CSRF no ecossistema do MockMvc, além da configuração de mocks para dependências de infraestrutura de segurança (JwtService e TokenBlocklistService) requeridas pelo filtro de segurança da aplicação.

# Tarefas Relacionadas
Issue: [Test] Criar testes para camada Web (MockMvc) para AgendamentoController #424
Outras dependências: Nenhuma

# Mudanças Realizadas
Testes de Camada Web para AgendamentoController:

- Implementação da classe AgendamentoControllerTest no diretório src/test/java/br/org/apae/atendimento/controllers/ utilizando @WebMvcTest(AgendamentoController.class) e MockMvc, cobrindo 10 cenários organizados semanticamente via @Nested e @DisplayName.
- Isolamento da camada de serviço: Utilização de @MockBean para simular o comportamento de AgendamentoService, garantindo testes focados estritamente na camada de transporte HTTP e validação de contratos.
- Validação de Segurança e Autenticação (HTTP 401): Garantia de que requisições desprovidas de credenciais nos endpoints GET e POST /agendamento sejam rejeitadas com status 401 Unauthorized.
- Cobertura de Criação (POST /agendamento): Validação de fluxo de sucesso com status 201 Created retornando o contrato AgendamentoResponseDTO e repasse correto do ID do usuário autenticado; validação de falha de validação com status 400 Bad Request ao omitir campos obrigatórios ou enviar data no passado violando @FutureOrPresent.
- Cobertura de Edição (PUT /agendamento/{agendamentoId}): Validação de caminho com sucesso retornando 200 OK e validação de payload inválido retornando 400 Bad Request.
- Validação de Paginação e Conversão ISO de Data (GET /agendamento): Validação da leitura dos parâmetros de paginação padrão (page=0, size=10) e customizados; validação do parse da anotação @DateTimeFormat(iso = DateTimeFormat.ISO.DATE) convertendo string ISO para LocalDate com retorno íntegro da estrutura de Page<DiaAgendamentoResponseDTO>.
- Cobertura de Exclusão (DELETE /agendamento/{pacienteId}/{agendamentoId}): Validação de resposta 200 OK com corpo textual "Agendamento excluído" e verificação via Mockito verify() do repasse exato de usuarioId, pacienteId e agendamentoId.
- Cobertura de Conclusão (PATCH /agendamento/{pacienteId}/{agendamentoId}/concluir): Validação de resposta 200 OK com mensagem "Agendamento concluído" e verificação da chamada ao método de conclusão do serviço.

# Ajustes de Infraestrutura de Teste:

- No pom.xml: inclusão da dependência org.springframework.security:spring-security-test em escopo test.
- No AgendamentoControllerTest: configuração de mocks para JwtService e TokenBlocklistService para permitir a inicialização íntegra da cadeia de filtros do Spring Security no contexto fatiado do WebMvc.

author: jbonofre
body:
Permet de facturer automatiquement une ligne (ex. : traitement des déchets) sur chaque prestation comportant une intervention sur un bateau ou un moteur.

Un produit du catalogue peut être marqué « Ajouter automatiquement aux interventions ». Dès qu'un forfait ou un service est ajouté à une prestation, ce produit est ajouté en ligne (quantité 1) s'il n'y figure pas déjà, les montants sont recalculés et un message le signale. La main d'oeuvre passant toujours par un forfait ou un service, c'est ce qui sert de déclencheur.

- Backend : nouveau champ `ajoutAutomatiqueIntervention` sur `ProduitCatalogueEntity`, pris en compte à la modification du produit.
- Catalogue : case à cocher sur la fiche produit (catalogue et fiche ouverte depuis une vente), étiquette « Auto. interventions » dans la liste.
- Prestations : ajout automatique au recalcul des lignes, quel que soit le mode d'ajout de l'intervention (sélection, modale, package, forfaits proposés pour le bateau).

Comportement :
- une seule ligne par prestation, quel que soit le nombre d'interventions ; la quantité reste modifiable ;
- une ligne retirée à la main n'est pas remise, sauf si une nouvelle intervention est ajoutée ;
- les prestations existantes ne sont pas modifiées à leur ouverture ;
- le comptoir n'est pas concerné.

À noter : un tel produit n'étant pas géré en stock, il s'affiche « 0 en stock » sur la ligne et compte dans les alertes de stock de l'accueil (règle actuelle `stock <= stockMini`), comme tout produit sans stock aujourd'hui.

Tests :
- `ProduitCatalogueResourceTest` : enregistrement du marqueur à la création et à la modification.
- `vente.test.tsx` : ajout automatique avec un forfait, pas d'ajout sans intervention, pas de réajout après suppression manuelle.
- Rendu vérifié dans Chrome (build + API simulée).

## 概述

Closes #313

父跟踪为 #300；本 PR 只关闭目录子项。

## 范围

- **范围内，已完成：** 精确的管理员九字段 DTO、10/20/50/100 分页与真实总数、完整条件 PUT/DELETE、缺少文件禁止启用、移除取消零写入、删除空末页回退、UTF-16 标题和整数边界。
- 冲突保留草稿及原版本，管理员对照回读结果后明确采用新条件；若单元已删除则保留原目标和草稿，明确选择其他单元后才切换；响应丢失、取消和 5xx 标为未知，不自动重放 POST/PUT/DELETE。已确认写入后的读取失败单独反馈。
- 所有目录、教材与单元请求和清理均检查目标、请求及会话代际；首次写入的共享 CSRF 读取也继承当前目标保护，旧请求不能跳转或阻塞新目标的首次写入，已完成的 Cookie 对仍可复用；等待共享 CSRF 时取消立即反馈，后续令牌到达也不会发出已取消的写入。
- 前后端登录返回白名单仅增加精确的 `/books/<safeId>/audio`；保留旧路径及编码、控制字符、外站、query/hash、反斜杠、越界长度和 traversal 拒绝。原始 API ID 仅编码一次。
- **本次刻意不修：** #314 负责网页上传/替换和未知上传核对，#315 负责教材播放器与真实 S3 网页整链；本页没有占位按钮。词汇发音的外部上传边界保持。没有另行发现需登记的独立缺陷。

## 契约与兼容性

- **保证什么、不保证什么：** 遵循 #300 唯一事件模型的目录部分；结果只作用于当前目标和会话，不猜测服务器提交/回滚，不自动覆盖冲突。刷新后不恢复内存草稿，文件状态不代表对象可读。
- **HTTP API / JSON / 认证行为：** 只消费现有 `/admin/*`，沿用服务器管理员角色和 Cookie CSRF；仅增加上述精确登录返回路径，没有向网页提供 Bearer/S3 凭据。
- **SQLite 数据、配置与部署：** 无 schema、migration、配置、存储目录或服务器目录行为改动。
- **前端与浏览器兼容性：** 沿用 Vue/Element Plus 与既有布局，键盘可操作，关闭弹窗恢复焦点，行内 aria-live；窄表内部可键盘横向滚动。
- **英文使用者文档：** README、frontend guide、TextbookAudio、Testing、Deployment 与 HostedLoginReleaseNotes 同步实际已开放阶段，并保留 #299 新增的公共 API 内容。

author: 99yash
body:
## Where this change sits

Alfred has two edit-time hooks for coding agents in `.claude/hooks/`. `helper-hints.mjs` names the canonical helper when an agent is about to write an idiom from `scripts/consolidation-rules.mjs`. `recall.mjs` injects repo lessons from `.lessons/` at session start, on a prompt, and before an edit. The AST rules in the oxlint plugins (`scripts/oxlint/alfred/`, `scripts/oxlint/anti-slop/`) run only in `pnpm lint`.

## Why this change is needed

- No settings file registered either hook, so neither ran. `.gitignore` has `.claude/*` and un-ignores only `hooks/` and `skills/`. Thus `.claude/settings.json` was ignored and did not exist. `~/.claude/settings.json` has no such hooks. But `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/reference/shared-helpers.md`, and `scripts/consolidation-rules.mjs` said that the hint hook runs while an agent writes code.
- Two consolidation rules moved into the oxlint plugin (`no-function-wrapper-shim`, `sha256-over-json-stringify`). The plugin README said "The edit-time hook does not read this plugin". So those rules gave no feedback until `pnpm lint`.

## What this change does

- Adds `!.claude/settings.json` to `.gitignore` and tracks `.claude/settings.json`. The file has only a `hooks` block and no permissions. Personal permissions stay in the ignored `settings.local.json`. It registers:
  - `helper-hints.mjs` on `PreToolUse`, matcher `Edit|Write|MultiEdit`;
  - `recall.mjs session-start` on `SessionStart`, `recall.mjs prompt` on `UserPromptSubmit`, and `recall.mjs pre-edit` on `PreToolUse` (`Edit|Write|MultiEdit`);
  - the new `lint-on-edit.mjs` on `PostToolUse`, matcher `Edit|Write|MultiEdit`.
  - Each command is `node "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/hooks/<file>`.
- Adds `.claude/hooks/lint-on-edit.mjs`. After an agent writes a `.ts` or `.tsx` file under the repo, the hook runs `node_modules/.bin/oxlint` from `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` with the root `.oxlintrc.json` and the `pnpm lint` flags, on that one file. It gives the diagnostics as `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` with `hookEventName: "PostToolUse"`. It writes each rule in config spelling (`alfred/sha256-over-json-stringify`), so the agent can write a correct disable comment.
- Decision: the hook reports all rules, not only `alfred/*`. Each rule in `.oxlintrc.json` is at `error`, and the tree has zero violations. So each diagnostic on the file is one that `pnpm lint` will reject. A filter to `alfred/*` would hide the anti-slop rules, which are also silent at edit time. With no filter, a new rule in either plugin, or a new core rule in the config, gets edit-time feedback with no table to keep in step.
- The hook is advisory. It always exits 0. It prints nothing when the file is clean, when the path is not `.ts`/`.tsx` under the repo, when the file does not parse yet (a diagnostic with no rule code), when the oxlint binary or the config is missing, when oxlint runs past 5 seconds, or when its output is not JSON.
- Updates the docs so they are true: the alfred plugin README, the `CLAUDE.md` bullet, `docs/reference/shared-helpers.md`, and the `scripts/consolidation-rules.mjs` header. Each one now says that the hooks are registered in `.claude/settings.json`, and that Claude Code asks each user to trust project hooks.

Verification (each hook driven by hand with a hook JSON payload on stdin):
- `lint-on-edit.mjs` on a planted `packages/http/src/` file with `createHash("sha256").update(JSON.stringify(x))` reports `alfred/sha256-over-json-stringify` and `anti-slop/no-object-parameters`, both on line 3. Median 285 ms over 9 runs (max 317 ms). A clean file (`packages/http/src/index.ts`) prints nothing in a median of 281 ms. A syntax-error file, a `.md` path, a project with no oxlint binary, and stdin that is not JSON all print nothing and exit 0. The planted files are deleted.
- `helper-hints.mjs` with `err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)` names `toMessage` (44 ms).
- `recall.mjs` gives the lessons index on `session-start`, a matching lesson on `prompt`, and a glob-matched lesson on `pre-edit`. Each takes about 100 ms.
- Each command string in `.claude/settings.json`, run through `sh -c` with `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` set, exits 0 and emits its event name.
- `pnpm check` exits 0.

## Preserved behavior

- No product code changes. No runtime package changes.
- `pnpm lint` and `pnpm check` stay the gates. The hooks only add context. They cannot block an edit.
- `.claude/settings.local.json` and every other path under `.claude/` stay ignored.
- `helper-hints.mjs` and `recall.mjs` do not change.

Residual risk:
- Claude Code runs project hooks only after a user trusts them, and it asks for review when they change. Until a user accepts, the hooks do not run.
- `.agents` is a tracked symlink to `.claude`. Tools that read `.agents/settings.json` now also see this hooks block.
- An agent that edits a file that already has a lint error sees that error after each edit. Today the tree has zero errors, so this happens only after a new violation.
- Each `.ts`/`.tsx` edit costs about 0.3 s for the lint run. Each edit also starts two short Node processes before the write (about 0.1 s each).

author: elektronaut
body:
### What and why

Phase 0 of the CBM-II plan: `KernalTrap::IEEELayout` no longer hardcodes the PET's VIA and PIA addresses. Its line handling (`time_serial_byte`, `attention`, `byte_sent`, `release_attention`, `listen_to_talker`, `release_serial_lines`) runs the steps of a new `lines:` field (`IEEELines`), each step an `IEEELineStep`. A step either writes a value to an address, or reads the register, keeps the bits its mask names and ORs a value in, or only reads it. The PET's three layouts share `PET_LINES`, which holds the same reads and writes in the same order as before. The CBM-II will give its KERNALs their own lines on TPI1 and the CIA, including the CIA ICR read its timer start ends with (hence the read-only step).

### Verification

- `bin/machine_diff disk --family pet --against origin/main` (LOAD"*",8 through the IEEE traps): 10 checkpoints match on the 8032, 2001 and 3032.
- A CRuby run of an 8032 with a host directory that types `10 print 42`, `save"t",8`, `new`, `load"t",8`, `run`: the same RAM and register digest every 250K cycles, the same screen and the same saved file on this branch and on origin/main's `lib/`.
- `bin/testbench --pet selftest/`: 10/10 PASS (`pet-pass.d82` included), on CRuby and on the Spinel build (`rake spinel:testbench[testbench-pet,selftest/]`: 0 changed).
- Spinel at `SPINEL_REF`: `pet_boot` and `pet_snapshot` match CRuby.
- `bundle exec rspec spec/badline/kernal_trap spec/badline/pet`: 633 examples, 0 failures, four of them new for `IEEELineStep`.

### Notes for reviewers

The step and run methods are named `act_on` and `run_steps`. A step method named `apply` made Spinel refuse `pet_snapshot.rb` at `snapshot/vice/pet_restore.rb:49` and `:92` ("a String is passed through a proc or Method read out of a slot that holds other values"). That is the same-name cross-talk between unrelated user methods seen before (`Restore.apply`), so the name was picked to avoid it rather than worked around.

author: tahubcs
body:
## Problem
Migrations reached Supabase only when someone remembered to apply them by hand (`dotnet ef database update` or the `docs/schema` scripts). Meanwhile Render deployed the API on every commit to `main` by itself. A merge could therefore start an API whose schema didn't exist yet.

## Solution (ADR-044)
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: a new job, `deploy-api`, runs **only on pushes to `main`**, after `verify` and `api-image` pass. It:
  1. builds an EF Core migration bundle (building needs a connection string, so it uses a dummy that is never contacted),
  2. trusts the Supabase root CA, since the connection uses `SSL Mode=VerifyFull` as on Render,
  3. applies pending migrations using `DATABASE_MIGRATION_CONNECTION_STRING`,
  4. calls Render's deploy hook with `ref` set to the same commit.
  It runs in the GitHub environment `api-deploy`, one deploy at a time, and is never cancelled partway through a migration. If either secret is missing, it fails with a clear message.
- `render.yaml`: `autoDeployTrigger: "off"`, so Render no longer deploys by itself.
- Docs: ADR-044 in `DECISIONS.md`. Setup and rules are in `DATABASE.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md` and `TESTING.md`, and `HANDOFF.md` is updated.

EF stays the only migration history, and the API still never migrates on startup (ADR-007). The environment is called `api-deploy` because GitHub environment names ignore case and Vercel already uses `Production`.

## Validation
- `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` passed. Both YAML files parse, and `deploy-api` has the intended `needs`, `if` and `environment`.
- Built the migration bundle locally. Confirmed that it reads `ConnectionStrings__Database` when it runs, not the build-time dummy (I tried it against an unreachable host), and that it exits 1 when no connection string is set.
- No application code changed, so no tests were added. The job itself can only run after merge.

## Migrations / environment
No new migrations. Requires the GitHub environment `api-deploy` with the secrets `DATABASE_MIGRATION_CONNECTION_STRING` (session pooler, same value as Render's `ConnectionStrings__Database`) and `RENDER_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL`, plus Render auto-deploy turned off.

## Known limitations
- **Merging this PR runs the job for the first time** against Supabase. Before merging, run `dotnet ef migrations list --project app/api` against Supabase (read-only) and confirm that no migration already in the database shows as pending.
- From now on, each migration must work with the API version that's already running: drop or rename columns only after a deploy that no longer uses them. Rollback stays manual.
- The bundle hasn't been run against a real database, and the deploy hook call hasn't been tested outside CI.
- The web app still deploys from Vercel on merge, separately from this job.

author: motioneso
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3543. On an account that has never chatted, a first message like "remind me in 2 minutes to stretch" failed with "I couldn't save that reminder".

**Root cause.** Main is only created when a chat session with the model starts. Reminders (and the classifier gate) answer before that session starts. Their thread lookup found nothing, the turn was bound to no conversation, and the reminder writer refused to save without one.

**Fix.** Choosing a turn's conversation now opens one when the account has none, through the same helper the session launch already used. Main therefore exists before anything answers the first turn, whichever path answers it. No reminder-only special case.

**Behaviour change to note.** On a fresh account the classifier gate and its shadow check now see the new conversation's id instead of none. One unit test pinned the old timing; it now asserts gate, shadow and launch all bind the same new conversation, and that it is opened exactly once.

## Tests

- New integration test `tests/integration/chat-first-reminder-fresh-account.test.ts` (real database, real chat runtime): a fresh account's first turn is a reminder; it saves to a newly opened Main with its delivery job, the model never starts, and the next normal turn joins the same Main. Observed failing before the fix with the exact user-facing message ("I couldn't save that reminder..."), passing after.
- New unit test in `tests/unit/chat-reminder-turn.test.ts`, observed failing without the fix.
- Narrow script `pnpm test:chat-first-reminder` runs the new integration test with the existing reminder save tests (14 passing).
- Related unit suites: 29 files, 669 tests passing (includes the chat server boot test).
- Full local gate: green. The full run passed everything except 7 email tests, because the local stand-in mail server was down; it was restarted and those two files were rerun on their own and passed (19 of 19). CI's browser suite is not part of the local gate.

## Live proof

Scratch instance from this branch: own throwaway database, API, worker and web from source (not dev, not prod). No model configured; PR 3540 is not merged, so no model was used.

1. Signed up a fresh owner through the real sign-up screen and skipped setup. The account had zero conversations.
2. The chat drawer shows "Connect a provider" with no composer, because no model is connected. So the first message, "Remind me in 2 minutes to stretch", was posted from the signed-in page to the same endpoint the composer uses. Reply: "Okay. I'll remind you in 2 minutes: stretch" (before this fix: "I couldn't save that reminder").
3. After reload, the drawer shows the message and reply. The database holds exactly one conversation, which is Main.
4. The real worker delivered it two minutes later. The drawer shows "Reminder: stretch" in Main; the reminder row is "delivered" and points at Main.

App map: no screen, setting or navigation changed.

## Release note

Category: Fixed
Title: First reminder on a new account saves
Description: A reminder asked for in a new account's very first chat message is now saved and delivered instead of failing.

author: language-app33
body:
## 0.453 — a card that has climbed every level is reviewed on its top level only

**What changes for learners**
- Once a card has passed every level below its top one (Learnt, Cleared, or back on its top level after a slip there), a session asks it only its top questions: writing the word from its meaning, from its picture, and so on. It no longer gets easy recognition questions.
- Such a card comes up when one of its top questions is due, not when an easy one is. Only the due ones are asked, two at most per session; the rest wait for the next session.
- Missing a top question twice in a row keeps the card on its top level until it's answered right again. The easy questions don't come back.
- These cards are no longer used as extra tiles in other words' "Match the pairs".
- What a card shows, the progress figures, and how Learnt is earned are unchanged.

**Trade-offs**
- A word with no recorded phrase is no longer asked to be heard once it is past its lower levels. Writing it is the check.
- "Get started" asks only easy recognition questions, so on a deck that is mostly past its lower levels it comes out short, or says there is nothing to practise.
- Someone practising many times a day meets such a card in more sittings, one question each time instead of two. The number of questions about it stays about the same: around 4 a day, against 4.2 before, at fifteen sittings a day.

**To check by hand**
- A Learnt word that is due, in a session: only its writing questions should come up, never "choose the meaning".

## Also included
- New tests for each rule above.
- Existing tests whose setups assumed a fully climbed card is asked everything now seed their cards below the top, or count what a card is still asked.
- A bug found while testing is fixed: a card that had just reached its top level was being counted as new, which let too many new words in at once.
- The one-place README summary of this rule came after this pull request was merged; it is in #91.

## What was checked
- `npm run check` passed on the pushed version: lint, types, all 1,703 tests, the smoke test, and the build.

author: aiordanescu
body:
## Problem

US users saw British spellings: Practise (the workspace tab), colour, recognise, centre, grey, cancelled. The interface text is plain English, mostly British with some US, but Lingui's config labeled it `en-US`, and the extract runs with `--overwrite`, so the en-US catalog was always a verbatim copy of the source. Making `en-GB` the source instead would also be wrong: upstream's en-GB catalog has 20 real British translations of US spellings in the source (Behavioral to Behavioural, Color to Colour, Organization to Organisation), which an en-GB source would overwrite.

## Change

- `sourceLocale` is now `en`. Lingui doesn't need a catalog for it, so no new file; en-US and en-GB are both translations and are no longer overwritten.
- `tooling/locales/english.ts`, run by `pnpm lingui:extract` before the PDF translations: en-US entries that are empty or still copies of the source get the source in US spelling; en-GB entries that are empty get the source as it is. Anything else is a real translation and is kept.
- The spelling map is explicit: -ise/-ize stems (words that are -ise in US English, like advertise or revise, are excluded), -our, -re, doubled l, grey, catalogue, judgement and similar. Placeholders and escapes are never rewritten. US to British isn't attempted, since practice and practise depend on noun or verb.
- Result: en-US 25 entries in US spelling; en-GB keeps its 20 British translations and fills its 51 empty fork strings; message ids and the other 53 catalogs are untouched; PDF section titles and Present unchanged. A second extract changes nothing.

author: simlarsen
body:
## Telemetry simplicity audit

The maintainer's ask, applied to Logs, Traces, Metrics, Exceptions, Profiles, RUM, Services, Dashboards, SLOs and LLM observability: a setting whose description explains two modes becomes plain choices with one line each, the default first; forms ask less; an empty first-run page offers one clear next step.

### What changed

**Settings that explained their own modes are now plain choices** (shared Radio, one line per answer, the default first). Stored values are the enum values they always were: API, Terraform and existing records are unchanged.

| Where | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RUM > Replay Policy > Edit Policy | *When to upload a recording*, *Masking mode* and *Consent* were dropdowns whose one description listed every mode; the dialog said *Edit RUM Application* | Two, three and two answers with a line each; *Ignored error patterns* is asked right under the trigger, and only under *On error or frustration* (the one trigger it changes); the dialog says *Edit Session Replay Policy*; an emptied number box saves what its placeholder says instead of failing the save |
| Logs / Traces > Drop Filters (create and Edit Action) | *Action* dropdown, description explaining Drop and Sample | *Drop* / *Sample*, each with its line; *Sample Percentage* says "10 keeps one in ten" |
| Logs / Traces > Scrub Rules | *Scrub Action* dropdown, description listing Redact, Mask and Hash | Three answers, each with its line |
| SLO create (More fields) and Settings | *Window Type* and *Multi Monitor Mode* dropdowns with long two-mode descriptions | Two answers each; Multi Monitor Mode says it only matters with more than one monitor |
| Metrics > Pipeline Rules | *Match Condition* All/Any explained in one sentence; long field help | Each answer with its line; short help on rename, attribute and redact fields |
| SLO > Burn Rate Rules | *What It Declares* had two switches (Create Alert, Declare Incident) that could both be off ("This rule would do nothing") | One question, **When it fires**: *Create an alert* (default), *Declare an incident*, *Both*. No answer opens nothing. *Enabled* is on the edit form only, as on every rule form. Answers worded as the monitor recommendations' own alert/incident choice |

**Empty first-run pages offer the next step**

- Logs, Traces, Metrics and Exceptions explorers: an empty list that nothing narrows (no chip, no search) says "No logs here yet / Logs appear here as soon as your apps send them" with **Set up logs** (opens the Setup Guide tab) and, on a range shorter than a week, **Show the past week**. A list a filter or search emptied keeps its "try adjusting filters" line. Exceptions shows this only when the project has no exception at all (one count request); an empty Unresolved list in a project with exceptions is good news and keeps its message. Only the product pages pass this; embedded logs/traces (service, host, incident tabs) are unchanged.
- Services: an empty list says services appear once apps send telemetry, one per `service.name`, with **Set up telemetry** beside Create Service. Create Service asks for the `service.name` with an example; Description folds beside Labels.
- RUM Applications: the list describes itself in plain words (no `browser.*` / `device.*`); the guide under an empty list no longer says the list is empty a second time.
- SLOs: the six status tiles (all zero) no longer sit above an empty list; they show once there is a live SLO.

**Translations**: 60 new Dashboard keys in all 16 locales. Existing keys drawn beside the new choices that were still English (*Create an alert*, *Declare an incident*, *Both*, *Not required*, *Set up tracing*) are translated where they were untranslated, so no choice group is half English; the sample percentage help quotes the translated *Always*.

**Docs (17 languages, line for line)**: `slo/burn-rate-alerts` (When it fires, Enabled on the edit form, the table and tip), `slo/introduction` (when the tiles show), `telemetry/session-replay` (ignored error patterns asked under *On error or frustration* only). `docs:localize-anchors` changed nothing.

### Decisions

- Choices keep the stored enum values; the burn rate choice is form-only and writes the two existing columns (`shouldCreateAlert`, `shouldCreateIncident`), read with the worker's defaults.
- First steps only when the list is empty and unnarrowed, only on product pages.
- Docs italics of replay option names (_Always_, _Mask all text_ ...) stay English in translated docs, the existing convention SessionReplayPlaybackAssetsDocs pins for Persian.
- Orphaned old description keys stay in the locale files: deleting translated keys needs an i18n baseline reset that would collide with the two audits running beside this one.

### Shared files touched

- `packages/Common/UI/Components/LogsViewer/LogsViewer.tsx`: new optional prop `emptyContentWhenUnfiltered`, exported `isNarrowedByReader`.
- `packages/Common/UI/Components/LogsViewer/components/LogsTable.tsx`: new optional prop `emptyContent`; the default empty block is drawn like every other explorer's (search icon, "No logs found", hint) instead of a boxed upper-case monospace card. This is a visual change for every logs list.
- (UI review) `LogsTable.tsx` also exports `getLogsTableEmptyHint`: a host message that only restates "No logs found" gives way to the list's own hint.

### Seen and left (recommendations)

- **Create Service Level Objective** button: long; pinned by docs and E2E. Suggest **Create SLO**.
- Log/trace pipeline Remap switches *Preserve Source* / *Override on Conflict* still explain two modes each (docs pin them in 17 languages).
- Metrics query "rate" switch and the dashboard trace chart "count every span" switch explain two modes each.
- Dashboard data source *Additional options* and session replay origins/selectors/patterns are raw JSON.
- The reseller "telemetry features are disabled" message is copy-pasted on 6+ pages.
- RUM side menu has two Documentation items; the Enterprise upsell sits inside the Retention Overrides card.
- Radio titles that are enum values (*Rolling*, *Calendar Month*, *Any Monitor Down*, *Monitor Seconds Average*) and the replay field titles are still English in several locales: translating them changes what the SLO and replay docs must say in 16 languages. Good next translation pass.
- The Replay Health page draws its policy labels in English only.
- Dashboards and LLM observability: audited; their empty pages already lead to a next step, no change. (Profiles: changed in the UI review below.)
- For simplicity-audit-infrastructure: a resource's Overview has an *Explore telemetry* card that repeats the side menu, and two Details cards whose rows are mostly empty.

### Tests

- New: `App/Tests/Dashboard/TelemetrySimplicityWiring` (first steps on product pages only; every new line translated in 16 languages; old two-mode descriptions gone), Common `TelemetryFirstSteps`, `TelemetryListFirstSteps`, `LogsViewerFirstSteps`, `BurnRateDeclaresChoice`, `SessionReplayPolicyChoices`, `DropFilterViewAction`.
- Updated: SLO form and burn rate suites, `TelemetryDataRuleForms(Render)`, `MetricAndRecordingRuleFormsRender`, `SloSettings`, `SloStatusSummaryCards`, `LabelsFormFieldGuard`, `LongFormStepsGuard`, `ExceptionsLandingNavigation`, `SloDocsFacts`, `TelemetryAdminDocsFacts`.
- E2E: offline `SloBurnRate/BurnRateRules.spec.ts` walks When it fires (11 passed, 86 s with the fixture build); offline `SessionReplay/ReplayPolicy.spec.ts` gains the choices test (5 passed, 29 s). Deployed `Tests/Dashboard/LogDropFilters.spec.ts` and `Slo.spec.ts` now use the radios; **not run on a full stack**.
- Mutation checks: 8 single breaks (trigger rule, burn rate columns, search narrowing, tiles, services route, product-page wiring, a missing translation), each caught.

### Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` Dashboard, `npm run compile` App, E2E `tsc`: pass. Common `compile-tests`: pass (app part re-checked after a typing fix

author: crispstrobe
body:
The agent worked through the 56 files where our staff-1 onsets disagreed with Verovio's timemap, sorting reading errors from oracle artifacts.

**Reader fixes** (each has a regression test in `musicxml_timing_test.dart` that fails without it):
- Voices 1–4 now claim their slots before a voice past 4, so a piano's voice 5 no longer takes voice 1's slot and runs the bar long. This was the most common cause.
- A `<time-modification>` without `<tuplet>` (half-note tremolos) is now timed. New `TupletSpan.hidden` means nothing is drawn, and the writer writes it back.
- An unprinted note keeps its time as a hidden spacer.
- A fifth voice's note moves to a slot that is free at its onset.
- A bar rest gets its written length next to another voice, unmetered.
- A whole rest in a longer bar (4/2) rests a whole note, not the bar.
- A typeless rest that fills its bar is read as the bar rest.
- Unpitched notes with no display position, or in chords, are kept.
- Quarter-tone alters are read and written as microtonal accidentals.

**Oracle normalisations** (each with its reason in the test):
- Bars start together across a system, as Verovio times them.
- Cross-staff notes may match on the part's other staves.
- Unprinted notes and unpitched pitch 0 are allowed for.
- Rolled chords across both staves get 3/8 of a quarter of slack.

22 files are set aside, each with a written reason, as Verovio misreading them; they don't count as agreeing.

The onset floor goes from 1689 to **1709**. Symbols: 1687 (floor 1681). 14 files remain, with reasons:
- maxima (no model value);
- malformed sources;
- parts in different meters;
- five simultaneous voices.

author: asafyish
body:
Addresses #415. Depends on the streaming infrastructure in #453.

Draft until #453 lands. GitHub currently shows the dependency commits too; the [grep-only comparison](https://github.com/asafyish/just-bash/compare/262a17b28b1729842720e348e5f860b32d5c7b08...codex/grep-streaming-followup) isolates the 6-file follow-up. Once #453 lands, rebase the follow-up commits onto main; no separate pipeline implementation is proposed here.

`grep -rn MATCH /src | head -40` currently reads all 2,000 files in the regression fixture. Stream per-file output through the existing `ctx.stdio` API and discover recursive files lazily, so downstream closure stops both file reads and traversal. `egrep` and `fgrep` use the same implementation.

Keep operand/traversal order, duplicate operands, filename prefixes, context/count/list output, and diagnostics already encountered before a broken pipe. Both buffered and streaming execution retain bounded 50-file parallel reads. Results are emitted before discovering the next batch, preserving full-search throughput while stopping unneeded later batches. Stdin and each individual file still use the existing whole-input matcher; no filesystem API, regex semantics, or pipeline infrastructure changes.

Validation: 503 grep/pipe and comparison tests pass (8 existing skips). The early-stop regression fails on the base branch. A parallel-read regression also protects full-consuming pipelines from serialized remote file reads. Build, typecheck, formatting, banned-pattern checks and knip pass. Broader suite: 15,702 pass; four unrelated xz/tar tests also fail on the unchanged base in this local environment (98 existing skips).

author: xeiculy
body:
## 背景

O2 のリハーサル（#41）は本番と同じ環境で測る必要があるので、先に本番の環境を README の「本番の環境を一から作る」のとおりに作った。デプロイしたあと、ホストのログインから最終ランキングまでを通して確かめた。T7 で決めたログの見方（Workers Logs と、本番中の `wrangler tail` の保存）と、受入基準の Cookie・WebSocket・Service binding の確かめ方は、まだ手順書になかった。

本番の環境（この PR の外で、手で作ったもの）:

- D1 `zubakui`（`--location apac`、`running_in_region` は APAC）。マイグレーションは workflow の `migrate` で当てた
- 本番用の GitHub OAuth App と、`zubakui-api` の4つのシークレット
- GitHub の Environment `production` の `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`・`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`
- deploy workflow の `all`（run 39106289615、`main` の b868770）で3つの job とも成功
- 許可リストに自分（GitHub の ID は文字列で `'106128913'`）
- 本番は `https://zubakui-web.xeikit-app.workers.dev`。Workers Free のまま

## 変更内容

- スクリプト: root の `logs:api`・`logs:web` から、各パッケージの `logs`（`wrangler tail --env="" --format json`）を呼ぶ。保存先の `logs/` は `.gitignore` に入れる
- `tools/docs-check/test/scripts.test.ts`: README と手順書の `pnpm [-s] [--filter <名前>] run <スクリプト>` を拾い、そのパッケージにスクリプトがあるかを確かめる。1つも拾えないときも落とす。文書の一覧は `documents.ts` に出し、`links.test.ts` と共有する
- `docs/runbooks/logs.md`（新規）: ダッシュボードでの見方（`$metadata.error EXISTS`）、本番中にファイルへ残す手順、残るもの・残らないものの表。README の手順書の表からつなぐ
- `docs/runbooks/deploy.md`: 「デプロイのあとに確かめる」を足す（state とログインの Cookie、ホスト用の WebSocket の Cookie、CSP、通しで遊ぶ、tail と Observability）
- 作る途中で分かったことを手順書に反映
  - D1 の作成: 「設定ファイルに足すか」は既定が yes で、Enter だけで ID が書き込まれる。`--update-config=false` で聞かれないようにする（wrangler 4.149.0 のソースで確かめた）
  - `wrangler secret put`・`list` に `--env=""` を付け、`env.e2e` による警告を出さない（`d1 execute` は警告が出ないので、そのまま）
  - `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` は `openssl rand -base64 32 | … secret put` で流し込み、画面に出さない。パイプで渡した値は末尾の改行が削られる
- `CLAUDE.md`: 本番の URL・作り方・ログの見方と、確かめた wrangler の振る舞い

## テスト方法

1. `make check` が通る（手元で確認済み。テスト 1082件）
2. `logs:api`・`logs:web` を `package.json` に足す前は、`scripts.test.ts` の該当の3行だけが落ちた（手元で確認済み）
3. 本番で確かめたこと（2026-10-18）
   - `callback/github` の要求に `__Secure-better-auth.state` が付き、ログインできた。`__Secure-better-auth.session_token` に `HttpOnly`・`SameSite=Lax`・`Secure` が付いた（Chrome の開発者ツール）
   - `ws/host` の要求にログインの Cookie が付いた。tail で、API の Worker に `cookie`（`REDACTED`）と本番の `origin` が届いていた（Service binding を通しても届く）
   - ホストのログインから最終ランキングまで通せた。CSP の違反はなし
   - tail と Workers Logs に、例外とエラーは0件。tail の出力でも `redact_query_string` で URL のクエリが消えていた
   - `zubakui-api.xeikit-app.workers.dev` は 404（`workers_dev: false`）

- #97: 部屋が終わったあとの回答者の画面の「最終の結果はスクリーンで発表されています」が事実と合わない（通しの確認で見つけた）

author: kushagra281
body:
Search terms
- keep short body words (eye, ear, leg, arm, dry, gas); stem coughing/cough etc.
- "worse"/"better" are no longer thrown away: they become modalities used in ranking
- negations ("no thirst", "None", severity answers) are not searched as symptoms
- synonym groups incl. Boericke-era vocabulary (coryza, lachrymation, eructation)
- no more arbitrary "first 10 terms" cut-off; short words match at word start only

Ranking and scoring
- rubrics are ranked locally by how many of the patient's keywords they match (plus "must match two keywords" queries) instead of the first 40 deepest rubrics
- scoring weights each rubric by that relevance, so remedies that merely appear in many loosely related rubrics stop winning by volume
- remedy names are normalised before grouping; duplicate sentences scraped from both source sites count once; rubrics flagged is_eliminating are never used
- UI category labels map to real section/heading patterns (Respiration, Hands/Legs & Back, Urinary System ...); no match -> retried without the section filter

Reliability
- removed the blocking Groq call whose result was never used
- DB lookups are chunked and paginated (no silent 1000-row cap)
- empty/failed lookups are no longer cached for 15 minutes
- if nothing is found AND a DB call failed, the API returns 500 (UI shows an error) instead of "No matching remedies found"; missing SCRAPER_SUPABASE_* env vars now fail loudly instead of silently querying the wrong database
- scoringService imported a RubricRemedyRow type that was never exported; defined it

Frontend
- questionnaire answers are sent with their question context ("worse light"), negative and severity answers are dropped

Tests: npm test (keyword extraction + search pipeline against a fake network)

body:
The growth field on main coarsens into a few large loops, leaving broad empty regions. This growth-only refinement sustains a much finer, interconnected Physarum-inspired mesh through extended viewing.

- Raise the full mobile field to 384 × 264 and the favourable population from 28,672 to 70,963. Retain 50,176-agent intermediate and 31,539-agent constrained tiers.
- Shorten sensors (4.3 → 3.6), narrow their angle (0.417 → 0.25 rad), soften turns (0.95 → 0.70 rad), increase deposition and reduce spatial diffusion. Keep live agents, wrapping boundaries and continuous reorganisation.
- Cache fixed pixel data, fit canvas backing size to its displayed resolution, and avoid per-agent random selection when following trails. Field state remains shared across the lab/expanded view, Replay and resize.
- Preserve visitor resets, inline sliders, notebook history, the complete experiment flow, scientific rules and all four outcome categories. No dependencies or deployment settings change.

### Visual evidence

[New 20-second video](https://github.com/Jiaqi-Hu111/Blue-Green/blob/refine/dense-physarum-field/docs/review/dense-network/after.mp4) · [Previous version video](https://github.com/Jiaqi-Hu111/Blue-Green/blob/refine/dense-physarum-field/docs/review/dense-network/before.mp4)

| Previous | Revised |
| --- | --- |
| ![Previous](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jiaqi-Hu111/Blue-Green/refine/dense-physarum-field/docs/review/dense-network/before.png) | ![Revised](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jiaqi-Hu111/Blue-Green/refine/dense-physarum-field/docs/review/dense-network/after.png) |

[Review notes, additional screenshots, exact parameters and measurements](https://github.com/Jiaqi-Hu111/Blue-Green/blob/refine/dense-physarum-field/docs/dense-network-review.md). Compared directly with the instructor’s [reference video/article](https://www.pavelp.cz/posts/eng-cpp-slime-mold-simulation/), with actual browser captures and extended fields inspected through 7,000 steps.

Raw-field diagnostics at a fixed threshold count 261 enclosed gaps at step 720 versus 23 before, and 265 at step 3,000 versus 5 before. These are artistic topology diagnostics, not biological measurements. A new regression checks that even the constrained tier sustains a connected open mesh; increasing opacity alone cannot pass it.

### Validation

- **26 unit tests passed**; all **24 Chromium scenarios verified** locally across a full run and focused recheck.
- Production build and `git diff --check` passed.
- Replay/Skip remains exact and deterministic. The test allows 15 seconds for reconstructing the larger field in short work slices; it keeps the same step-count, clipping and profile assertions.
- Pause/Play, ongoing evolution, expanded-view continuity, resize without changing field state, fresh visitors, inline recipes, notebook retention, all outcomes, reduced motion, fallback and deployment-update checks verified.
- The PR workflow reruns the complete suite independently.

Local production-build six-second samples at 390 × 844: 1× CPU selected 70,963 agents, 4× selected 31,539. Both had frame interval p50/p95 of 16.7/16.8 ms; maxima were 33.3/33.4 ms. Work p95 was 13/18 ms, and Pause round trips were 55/256 ms. These are desktop Chromium emulation observations, not physical-phone benchmarks or frame-rate guarantees. The throttled engine advances fewer simulation steps per second.

Review only; do not merge automatically. Production main remains unchanged by this branch.

`nvmath-python` pinned `cudaPackages_13_1` because it needs CUDA >= 13.1, but < 14. CUDA 13.0 and 13.1 cannot target Jetson Orin, so `cudaCapabilities = [ "8.7" ]` throws and aborts the nixpkgs CI evaluation.

Now it uses the default package set and marks the package broken outside the support range, just like `cupti-python`.

author: jasondorjeshort
body:
T114: Route to here, from where the phone is (wave 16). The owner on 0.1.8: "there's no way to pick our current position as the starting point". A long-press now offers **Route to here** first. It plans at once from the phone's position to the pressed point, in the card's last mode, for walking too. The route card names both ends, and From can be changed.

## What changed

- **Long-press card** (`tracking/LongPressMenu.kt`): Route to here, Waypoint here, Route from here, Cancel. Route from here keeps T45's two long-presses. After Choose on map, the next long-press goes to the route.
- **Origin** (`routing/RouteOrigin.kt`, pure, tested): the newer of the recorder's last fix and the map's device fix when the route is planned (the recorder's on a tie), as `Tracking.dropWaypoint` picks "here".
- **Stale fix: 120 s.** An older fix still plans, and the card adds its age ("Your location, 14 min ago"). Why 120 s: two minutes at a walking pace is about 170 m, inside the 300 m route snap, so a younger fix starts on the same trails.
- **No fix** (`routing/RouteSession.kt`):
  - Location on and permitted: the card says "Waiting for your location...", looks every 500 ms, and plans on the first fix.
  - Location off, or no permission: the card says so and offers Turn on location. That opens the permission prompt, or else the phone's location settings (the app's settings page when the prompt was refused for good).
  - A long-press still opens the card meanwhile, so Route from here works.
- **Route card** (`routing/RouteControls.kt`):
  - From and To lines. A fix reads "Your location"; a point reads its coordinates.
  - Change opens Your location, Choose on map and Swap, as far as the card allows (`fromChoices`).
  - Try Crow when no path is found; its notice shows under the chips once chosen.
  - Go comes first among the actions; the action row wraps.
- **Off-network origin** (`routing/OffNetwork.kt`): when the start is the phone's position, the message says "of your location" and drops the "Long-press closer" advice.
- **Camera fit** (`RouteSession.fitCamera`):
  - It now waits 250 ms for the finished card to be measured. It used the planning card's height (244 dp against 286 dp), which left the start, the fix, under the card.
  - Once the fit lands, it drops its padding and keeps the same view. MapLibre keeps a bounds fit's padding on the camera, so every later move (a map link, recentre) centred in the padded box.
- **Unsaved route file** (`SessionRoute`, ADR 0033): optional `startFix` and `endFix` keys; still version 1. A file from before reads as two points, and an older build ignores the keys. Tested.
- **Debug routes**:
  - New: `POST /route/to?lat=&lon=[&mode=][&wait=1]`, `POST /route/from?open=1|0` and `?choice=here|map|swap[&wait=1]` (409 when the card does not offer the choice now), `POST /map/longpress/to`.
  - `GET /route` `ui`: `from`, `to`, `fromOpen`, `fromChoices`, `location`, `waitingForFix`, `routeTo`, `lastFit.paddingDropped`.
  - `GET /map/longpress`: `actions`, and `lastAction` `routeTo`.

**Edits outside Owns (named):**
- `MapController.startDeviceLocation` (T115's), one filter: request every provider the phone has, enabled or not. With the location setting off at start, the map never heard a fix after it was turned on, until a restart. That left Turn on location dead.
- `tools/android-ui.py` (the named cross-edit): a `route_to_here` helper and a `route-to` step in `features`, run before the route step (Keep's trip fit in `Trips.kt` still keeps its padding), plus the docstring.
- `docs/reference/release-realism.md` (T115's): one clause naming the step.

**Docs:**
- `android-debug-routes.md`: the Routes and Waypoints lines.
- `android-app.md`: a "Route to here" section.
- `PLANNING.md` › Routing: a paragraph.
- The finding is resolved and promoted, with its row in `findings/README.md` updated.

The idea file is untouched (T118's).

## What was run and seen

AVD `dystopo35-T114`, debug build unless noted, Rainier pack, public places only.

- **Fresh fix:** injected Paradise (46.7864, -121.7366), long-press Panorama Point (46.8024, -121.7289), tap Route to here.
  - `GET /map/longpress`: `lastAction` `routeTo`.
  - `GET /route`: `ui.from` `kind` `fix`, lat/lon equal to the fix, `ageS` 33.
  - The route is 2953.3 m, +401.6 m, via Skyline Trail, Alta Vista Trail, Skyline Trail (the routing tour's numbers).
  - Card screenshot viewed: "From: Your location", "To: 46.80240, -121.72890".
- **Stale fix:** the same fix, 154 s old. "From: Your location, 2 min ago", `stale` true, 2953.3 m. Screenshot viewed.
- **Location setting off, cold start:**
  - `noLocation` with the message and Turn on location. Screenshot viewed.
  - A real tap opened the system Location page.
  - The setting was then turned on (the emulator GPS at Paradise). The first fix planned the waiting route after 8.6 s (17 polls), 2953.2 m. Before the MapController filter fix, no fix ever arrived.
- **No fix yet** (empty test providers, location on):
  - "Waiting for your location..." (screenshot viewed).
  - A long-press meanwhile opened the card (`routePhase` `waitingFix`).
  - The first provider fix planned it after 20.1 s (40 polls), 2953.3 m.
- **No permission:**
  - `noLocation` (`location` `noPermission`).
  - Turn on location by tap showed the system prompt (screenshot viewed).
  - "While using the app" led to a plan after 23.2 s, 2953.2 m.
- **From choices:**
  - Swap: 2982.3 m, +0 / −401.2 m, "To: Your location".
  - Your location: back to 2953.3 m.
  - Choose on map, then a long-press at 46.7686, -121.7295: 5849.3 m from that point (the card read "Route: choose the start", "Long-press the start point").
- **No path** (fix at the tour's Comet Falls off-network start):
  - "No trail or road within 0.2 mi of your location. Nearest: Van Trump Trail, 0.2 mi to the west. To start on it, raise Route snap in Settings to 0.3 mi."
  - Try Crow offered. Crow gave 1572.5 m, +297.9 m (the tour's crow line), with the notice. Both screenshots viewed.
- **Two `POST /map/longpress` calls** (with `/route` between): Paradise to Panorama Point, 2953.3 m, +401.6 m.
- **Font scale 1.0 and 2.0**, all viewed, nothing clipped:
  - The help pop-up (`POST /help/open?key=longPress.menu`).
  - The long-press card (it wraps to two rows at 2.0).
  - The route card with the From choices open.
  - The location-off card.
- **Routing tour** (`android-ui.py routes`): 11/11 ok, 3 grand-canyon lines skipped (no such pack on this account).
- **Device tour:** 10/10 (sheet viewed).
- **Release build by taps** (`android-ui.py features`, x86_64 release APK, `-PdystopoVersionCode` = commit count): 13/13 steps ok.
  - `route-to`: "From: Your location", "To: 46.80241, -121.72892", 1.8 mi · +1318 ft · 1:16 hike, line drawn (3139 samples).
  - The `route` step after it got the same numbers, so the dropped padding left its presses where they belong.
  - The first run, before the padding fix, had route-to after Keep, and its press landed 0.008° south: exactly the 135 dp centre shift of `Trips.kt`'s 110/380 dp fit.
- **Tests:** `HelpRegistryTest`, `RouteOriginTest` (new), `OffNetworkTest`, `SessionRouteTest` green; `user-text-check.py` 0 hits; `./gradlew check` green after the rebase onto main with T116 to T118.

## New or changed user-visible strings, and whose convention each follows

| String | Where | Convention |
|---|---|---|
| "Route to here" (first on the card) | long-press card | Destination first, as with Google, Apple and HERE's "Directions", Organic Maps' "Route to", Locus and CalTopo's "Navigate to"; "here" as in our "Waypoint here" |
| "Route from here" kept, third | long-press card | Organic Maps' "Route from", OsmAnd's "Directions from" |
| Help `longPress.menu`: "A long-press on the map opens this card. Route to here plans a route from where you are to the point; Change on the route card starts it elsewhere. Waypoint here marks the point with a waypoint you can name. Route from here starts a route at the point

author: sattasai
body:
The automatic school connection form sent `Origin: null` because its page used `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`; the authorization API correctly rejected the POST and left users on the API error page. Use `same-origin` on the form page to retain its Origin while withholding the state-bearing URL from other origins. Allow the exact evaluation origin in CSP form-action so the callback redirect can complete. Keep no-referrer on authorization and callback responses and retain strict Origin checks.

Validation: reproduced the failure in Chromium using the actual handler, then verified a same-origin POST reaches the cross-origin callback after the fix. All 221 school Node.js tests passed, including rejection of null and hostile origins.

What changes:
- **The core finds the crumbs.** It walks the syntax tree for the named constructs around the caret: functions, methods, types, classes, modules, and impl blocks named by their type. Each comes with its named siblings, looking one level into unnamed wrappers such as Go's type declarations and Python's decorated functions.
- **Noise is left out.** A keyword argument or a short expression with a name field does not become a crumb.
- **Both status bars show them** after the branch. Each crumb is a menu of its siblings with itself marked, and choosing one is a jump Go Back returns from. No language server is needed.
- **GTK rebuilds only on change.** A caret move inside the same function rebuilds nothing.

The plan said over the editor. They are in the status bar under it instead: the same place on both shells, the text keeps its full height, and that is where GoLand puts them by default.

author: spshulem
body:
Known wrong-provider credentials currently reach OpenAI and produce opaque failures. Reject an OpenRouter key paired with the default OpenAI endpoint before saving it or opening model, embedding, transcription, or Realtime requests. Setup now exposes the explicit base URL; unrelated settings remain editable when an existing credential is misconfigured. Region restrictions and provider mismatches return actionable public chat/setup errors without exposing raw provider details.

Normalize trailing slashes before model/embedding requests and recognize the equivalent OpenAI hostname with a terminal DNS dot. Explicit compatible endpoints retain their existing path. Custom endpoints also retain the existing shared embedding configuration; a Responses-only service can reject best-effort embedding lookups.

Addresses the reproducible provider-configuration portion of #87; other reports in that umbrella issue remain separately evaluated there.

Validation: 104 focused provider, streaming, setup, onboarding, environment-persistence, transcription, and voice tests passed. An earlier run hit the existing 80 ms streaming-deadline timing assertion; complete focused reruns passed. Staged and commit-range Git safety checks passed. Hosted CI is tracked on the current PR head.

Non-blocking review limitations: model-settings and G2-specific mismatch responses can still use a generic error, and custom endpoint embedding capability is not independently configured. Their safety checks still reject mismatched credentials before connecting.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches credential persistence and all OpenAI-shaped outbound paths; misclassification of region heuristics or hostname checks could block or mis-message some setups, but changes are fail-fast validation rather than auth logic.
> 
> **Overview**
> OpenRouter keys (`sk-or-…`) paired with the default OpenAI host are now rejected **before** any network call or `.env` write, via shared `validateOpenAIKey`. That check runs on model (including streaming), embeddings, G2 transcription, voice Realtime sessions, and setup save; `/setup/save` returns **400** with the same user-facing message instead of persisting bad config.
> 
> Setup adds **`OPENAI_BASE_URL`** to the wizard and validates the effective key + URL when those fields or OpenAI/auto provider change, so unrelated settings can still be saved when a stored key is wrong until the user fixes provider config. Compatible third-party base URLs (non-`api.openai.com`) stay allowed; trailing slashes on base URLs are normalized for model/embedding paths.
> 
> **Agent failures** gain `provider-config` and `provider-region` codes so chat/setup show actionable text without leaking raw provider diagnostics (e.g. bearer tokens in region errors).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 084faac4d08044e1411b2d3a20d8f03884712aad. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

author: maleadt
body:
In Xcode GPU frame captures, Metal.jl workloads are hard to read: kernels only appear under their mangled entry point (`_Z10saxpy_loop14MtlDeviceArrayI7Float32Li1ELi1EES1_6UInt32`), all dispatches of a batched command buffer sit in one flat list under a single compute encoder, and buffers are anonymous (`MTLBuffer 1..4`). This PR labels what Metal.jl creates, so a trace says which Julia kernel and array you are looking at.

- **Kernel pipelines.** The library, function and compute pipeline of every kernel are labelled with a readable signature, such as `saxpy_loop(::MtlDeviceVector{Float32, 1}, ::MtlDeviceVector{Float32, 1}, ::Float32)`. Closures keep the name they were defined with (`broadcast_linear(...)`, `gpu_ka_fill(::KernelAbstractions.CompilerMetadata{…}, ...)`), and anonymous functions are named after where they were defined (`anonymous@script.jl:31(::Float32)`). Long argument types are abbreviated the way stack traces abbreviate them, and labels are capped at 256 characters. A pipeline can only be labelled through its descriptor, so pipelines are now created from an `MTLComputePipelineDescriptor`. The label is computed once per kernel and device, when the pipeline is linked.
- **Internal buffers.** The device malloc heap, the exception mailbox and a kernel's relocation table are always labelled (`Metal.jl device malloc heap`, `Metal.jl exception info`, `Metal.jl relocations of <kernel>`). These buffers are created once.
- **Debug groups.** When resources are labelled, every dispatch is wrapped in a debug group named after the kernel's pipeline label. This separates the kernels that batching puts into one compute encoder.
- **Default under frame capture.** Labelling of `MtlArray` buffers (e.g. `MtlArray{Float32,1,Metal.SharedStorage}(dims=(1024,))`), command buffers and the debug groups used to be enabled only by `-g2` or the `label_resources` preference. It is now also on by default when `METAL_CAPTURE_ENABLED=1`, which `Metal.@capture` needs anyway. The preference still overrides that default; it does not affect the kernel and internal-buffer labels, which are always set.

### What it looks like in Xcode

After replaying a capture of `saxpy_loop`, a second kernel, a broadcast, a KernelAbstractions kernel and an anonymous kernel (Xcode 27, M1):

- The outline under the batched `MTLComputeCommandEncoder` shows one folder per dispatch, named after the kernel (`saxpy_loop(::MtlDeviceVector…`, `scale_kernel(::MtlDeviceVect…`), holding `pushDebugGroup`, `dispatchThreadgroups` and `popDebugGroup`. The `useResource:` calls name the arrays (`useResource:MtlArray{Float32,1,…}`).
- *Bound Resources* of a dispatch lists the pipeline state and kernel function as `saxpy_loop(::MtlDeviceVector{Float32, 1}, ...)`, the residency set's buffers as `Metal.jl exception info` and `Metal.jl device malloc heap`, and the resident arrays as `MtlArray{Float32,1,Metal.SharedStorage}(dims=(1024,))`.

What stays unlabelled: the kernel state and by-value arguments go through `setBytes`, which takes no label, so Xcode keeps calling them "Compute Bytes / Buffer N (Bytes)".

### Launch latency

Host time per launch of a trivial one-thread kernel (`a[1] = 1f0`), 60 samples of 1000 launches each, `-t1`, M1, macOS 27. Each row is min / median in ns; the five configurations ran as separate processes, interleaved, three rounds.

| configuration | round 1 | round 2 | round 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| base (`tb/metallib-reflection-write`) | 3125 / 3302 | 2983 / 3302 | 3060 / 3278 |
| this PR, labels off (default) | 2960 / 3181 | 3158 / 3304 | 3050 / 3217 |
| base, `METAL_CAPTURE_ENABLED=1` | 3450 / 3560 | 3323 / 3562 | 3448 / 3534 |
| this PR, `METAL_CAPTURE_ENABLED=1`, labels forced off | 3497 / 3582 | 3443 / 3559 | 3403 / 3510 |
| this PR, `METAL_CAPTURE_ENABLED=1` (labels on, new default) | 3769 / 3868 | 3760 / 3885 | 3760 / 3926 |

With labels off, the launch path only gains the load of a `Ref`, and there is no measurable difference. With labels on, a launch costs about 0.3 µs more, for reading the pipeline label and pushing and popping the debug group. That only applies when capturing or running with `-g2`.

### Tests

`test/execution.jl` checks the pipeline labels, including closures, anonymous functions and abbreviated long signatures; `test/capturing.jl` checks that the frame-capture worker labels `MtlArray` buffers.

author: dimanyyar
body:
## What and why

On the request card, a video's tile showed only a play button, while in the form you already saw a frame from the video. Now that frame becomes the video's preview everywhere: in the request, in replies, in "All attachments" and in the viewer's strip. The play button sits on top. This is the last step of attachment previews (PRD: Attachments, previews; ADR 0013).

How it works, step by step:

1. **Browser.** It takes the frame for the form tile (#35). When the video is ready, the form also sends that frame, a small JPEG of about 6–20 KB named `<place among the files>.jpg` (`0.jpg` for the first file), in a hidden field `attachments_posters`.
2. **Form.** The frame is attached to the video by its place among the files, since two videos can share a name. It is kept only if it is a JPEG of 256 KB or less. Anything else is dropped quietly, and the video keeps its play button, as before. This is not an error for the client.
3. **Worker.** The frame waits in the private folder. The `make_previews` worker turns it into the usual WebP preview, then deletes the original frame. As with images, the site itself never decodes a client's picture: only the worker does (ADR 0013).
4. **Serving.** Before the worker finishes, `/files/<id>/preview/` answers 404. After that it serves the preview with the same access check as the file.

No FFmpeg and no new dependency. A video sent from a browser that could not show it (HEVC in Chrome before compression) keeps the play button.

## How to check by hand

1. `git fetch && git switch feat/video-posters && docker compose up --build`
2. Create a request and attach one or two videos (a short phone clip or a screen recording). Wait for compression and send.
3. Wait about 5 seconds for the `previews` worker and reload the card. The video tile shows a frame with ▶ on top.
4. Look at "All attachments" on the right and at the strip at the bottom of the viewer: the same frame.
5. Reply with a video in the thread. The small tile in the reply shows a frame too.
6. Sign in as a client of another company and open `/files/<that video's id>/preview/`: 404.

## Screenshot

Not a new screen; screenshots of the card and the panel are in the chat with Dmitry.

## Definition of done

- [x] Tests for the new behaviour, all tests green (274)
- [x] `ruff`, `mypy` and the migrations check green
- [x] Migrations included (none needed)
- [x] No new dependency, or an ADR for it (ADR 0013 updated)
- [x] PRD updated or flagged if behaviour changed (Attachments: video preview is the browser's frame)

body:
## Summary
- Adds an experimental `/esp32-lab` page using the MIT-licensed `mikroverk/esp32sim` browser emulator.
- Adds an ESP32 Lab entry in the code editor when an ESP32 DevKit is on the canvas.
- Adds a versioned ESP32 bridge message validator and unit tests for chip identity, GPIO pin/level validation, serial bounds, status payloads, and unknown messages.
- Adds a strict bridge-event guard requiring both the exact iframe origin and exact `event.source`, with tests for spoofed origins, wrong windows, wildcard origins, and invalid payloads.
- Adds a board-pin adapter mapping SolderHub's existing classic ESP32 DevKit and ESP32-C3 header labels to GPIO numbers, with warnings for classic ESP32 input-only and boot-strapping pins; includes unit tests.
- Adds `docs/esp32-firmware-integration.md` documenting the cross-origin boundary, licensing/asset cautions, staged GPIO bridge, compilation options, and validation gates.

## Important scope limits
This is **not yet real ESP32 simulation integrated with the SolderHub circuit canvas**:
- The embedded upstream emulator runs isolated in a cross-origin iframe. Its worker/GPIO events are not exposed to the SolderHub parent page.
- The bridge contract, strict event guard, and board-pin adapter are validation/mapping groundwork only; none is connected to the iframe or circuit simulation.
- The SolderHub `/api/compile` route still targets Arduino Uno only; ESP32 Arduino sketch compilation is not implemented.
- GPIO input injection, output observation, PWM, ADC, I2C, SPI, UART, and virtual sensor/component coupling have not been implemented.
- The current SolderHub board layouts cover classic ESP32 DevKit and ESP32-C3. ESP32-S3/C6 are not yet available as mapped SolderHub board layouts, even though upstream emulator support exists with maturity caveats.

## Next engineering milestone
Pin and build the upstream emulator, audit its assets, and expose a safe bridge from a same-origin hosted build or an explicitly origin-checked upstream fork. Then connect the tested board adapter to real canvas pins and implement digital input/output before expanding to analog/PWM and buses. A parent-side `postMessage` listener alone cannot access the upstream iframe's internal `EmuLink` or worker protocol.

## Validation
- GitHub Actions passed dependency installation, TypeScript typecheck, Vitest tests, and production build for current head `242d60029da13967692ae75c610720355834b5bd` (CI run 306).
- No browser end-to-end GPIO/component test has been run.
- Keep this PR draft until the hosted page, firmware loading, mobile layout, and eventual GPIO bridge have been verified.

## License and hosting
The upstream emulator core is MIT. Individual ROM and demo assets may have separate licenses; audit before vendoring or redistributing. Browser/Web Worker execution is preferred to avoid a continuously running VPS, but ESP32 compilation remains a separate unresolved engineering decision.

## 증상
레벨업 창을 띄웠을 때 캐릭터 체력창이 레벨업 창 위로 보인다.

## 원인
씬은 Canvas 하나(Screen Space Overlay)이고, 겹치는 순서는 **형제 순서(뒤에 있을수록 위에 그려짐)** 로만 정해진다. 레벨업 창(`LevelSystem` 아래 `Dim`·`Option_0~3`)이 HUD(`HudHealthBar`, `KillCountDisplay`, `TimerText`, `BossHealthBarUI`)보다 **앞**에 있어 HUD가 팝업 위에 그려졌다.

## 수정
Canvas 자식 순서만 바꿨다 — HUD 네 개를 `XpGauge` 바로 뒤(맨 아래)로 이동.

| | 순서 |
|---|---|
| 이전(GameScene) | XpGauge, CharacterSelectPanel, **LevelSystem**, TimerText, ResultPanel, …, BossHealthBarUI, …, RoyalWasabiPanel, KillCountDisplay, HudHealthBar, … |
| 이후 | XpGauge, **TimerText, KillCountDisplay, HudHealthBar, BossHealthBarUI**, CharacterSelectPanel, **LevelSystem**, ResultPanel, … |

- GameScene·BossScene 둘 다 같은 방식. 변경은 `m_Children` 목록의 순서뿐이다(diff 8줄씩, 이동만)
- 같은 이유로 **왕궁 와사비·호감도 대화·결과 화면 위로 체력창이 올라오던 것도** 함께 고쳐진다
- 코드에서 형제 순서를 바꾸는 곳(`SetAsLastSibling` 등)은 `IntroSceneController`의 배경 영상(Canvas 앞쪽 고정) 하나뿐이라 충돌 없음

## 협업자 소유 파일 알림
`GameScene.unity`, `BossScene.unity`를 수정했다 — Canvas 자식 순서 변경만.

## 확인
- EditMode 692개 중 691 통과 (실패 1개는 기존 `Portraits_AdelineAndKamarionHaveOne_InariHasNone`, 무관). 씬 로드 에러 없음(배치 테스트)
