author: vidigoat
body:
## What

`numericise()` (used by `Worksheet.get_all_records()` and `Cell.numeric_value`) no longer turns strings such as `"nan"`, `"NaN"`, `"inf"` or `"Infinity"` into `float("nan")` / `float("inf")`. They are returned unchanged, like any other non-numeric text. Finite numbers are converted exactly as before.

## Why

There is no existing issue for this, so here is the bug in detail.

`numericise()` falls back to Python's `float()`, which also accepts `"nan"`, `"inf"` and `"infinity"` in any case and with an optional sign. Google Sheets has no NaN or infinite numbers. A cell showing one of those words holds text. With the default `numericise_ignore`, a sheet like this:

| name | score    |
|------|----------|
| Nan  | Infinity |
| Ada  | 3.5      |

gives, on master:

```python
>>> ws.get_all_records()
[{'name': nan, 'score': inf}, {'name': 'Ada', 'score': 3.5}]
```

Problems this causes:

- Text gets changed silently. "Nan" is a real first name, and "Infinity" or "inf" can show up as a label or a product name.
- `nan != nan`, so equality checks, deduplication and lookups on these records break.
- The values can't be written back. Sending a record to `update()` / `append_row()` fails before any request is made, with `requests.exceptions.InvalidJSONError: Out of range float values are not JSON compliant`.
- `Cell("Nan").numeric_value` returns `nan` instead of `None`, even though the docstring says `None` is returned when the value can't be converted to a number.

The same applies to overflowing literals such as `"1e999"`, which `float()` turns into `inf`.

## How

A small helper, `_finite_float()`, calls `float()` and raises `ValueError` when the result is not finite (`math.isfinite`). `numericise()` uses it in place of `float()`, so a non-finite result goes through the existing "not a number" path. The function's complexity stays within the flake8 limit, and nothing else about numericising changes: ints, comma-grouped numbers, underscores, `empty2zero` and `default_blank` all behave as before.

## How tested

- New `UtilsTest.test_numericise_keeps_non_finite_values_as_text` covers `nan`/`inf`/`infinity` with mixed case and signs, `1e999`, `numericise_all`, and checks that finite floats are still converted.
- New offline `CellNumericValueTest.test_numeric_value_of_non_finite_text_is_none` covers `Cell.numeric_value`.
- Both tests fail on master (15 failing checks, counting subtests) and pass with this change. No new HTTP calls, so no cassettes are needed.
- `tox -e lint,py,build,doc`: all pass (168 tests). The full suite also passes on Python 3.8.20. The CI `bandit` command reports no issues.

Developed with Claude Code (AI) under my direction; the new test fails on master and passes with this change, and tox lint/py pass locally.

author: rafaellemus92
body:
## What this adds

Python side of the shared math library the convergence thesis in
`RESEARCH.md` depends on. Ports FFT, Hilbert transform (+ onset-
density + unwrap), and Kuramoto order-parameter machinery from the
TypeScript modules in sgrounds/lib/piano to numpy, under
`packages/stats/py/`. Shared JSON test vectors under
`packages/stats/vectors/` are the source of truth; both language
implementations must pass the same cases to the stated tolerance.

> **Base is `claude/research-spine` (PR #5)**, which carries the
> `packages/stats/` scaffold. GitHub will auto-retarget to `main` once
> PR #5 lands.

## The twin-implementation contract

```
packages/stats/
├── vectors/           ← shared JSON cases (source of truth)
│   ├── fft.json
│   ├── hilbert.json
│   └── kuramoto.json
├── py/                ← this PR
│   ├── stats/
│   └── tests/
└── ts/                ← sgrounds/lib/piano for now; mirror in follow-up
```

**Protocol:** add a case to `vectors/<module>.json`; both language
test suites load the same file through their own loader; if either
side fails, fix the implementation (never the vector). The vector is
the shared definition; the code is the implementation.

## Modules shipped

| Module | Public API | TS twin |
|---|---|---|
| `stats.fft` | `fft_in_place`, `ifft_in_place`, `next_pow2` | `fftInPlace`/`ifftInPlace` in `sgrounds/lib/piano/hilbert.ts` |
| `stats.hilbert` | `analytic_signal`, `instantaneous_phase`, `instantaneous_amplitude`, `onset_density`, `unwrap_phase` | `sgrounds/lib/piano/hilbert.ts` |
| `stats.kuramoto` | `order_parameter`, `order_parameter_series`, `kuramoto_from_onsets`, `live_frame`, `live_phase_from_onsets`, `KuramotoFrame` | `sgrounds/lib/piano/kuramoto.ts` |

Pythonic snake_case naming; same semantics as the TS. Non-finite
phases are skipped by `order_parameter` (NaN = "oscillator has no data
yet"). `onset_density` subtracts its own mean before return so DC
doesn't dominate the Hilbert phase estimate on sparse spike trains.
`live_phase_from_onsets` reports phase at `window_sec − margin_sec`
into the sliding window — same tradeoff as the live Kuramoto phasor
in the piano trainer (small display latency for a stable estimate).

## Tests

```
packages/stats/py/tests/test_fft.py          5 shared-vector + 3 property  cases
packages/stats/py/tests/test_hilbert.py      6 shared-vector + 2 property  cases
packages/stats/py/tests/test_kuramoto.py     9 shared-vector + 6 property  cases
                                             ────────────────────────────────────
                                             31 passing in ~0.1s
```

Reproduce locally:
```sh
pip install -e packages/stats/py
pytest -q packages/stats/py/tests/
```

## Shared-vector sample

`vectors/kuramoto.json` — three of the nine cases:

```jsonc
{ "name": "identical_phases_r_is_1_mean_is_the_phase",
  "input": {"phases": [0.5, 0.5, 0.5]},
  "expected": {"r": 1.0, "mean_phase": 0.5, "mean_phase_matters": true} }

{ "name": "three_phases_uniform_on_circle_r_is_0",
  "input": {"phases": [0.0, 2.0943951023931953, 4.188790204786391]},
  "expected": {"r": 0.0, "mean_phase": 0.0, "mean_phase_matters": false} }

{ "name": "N2_identity_r_equals_abs_cos_half_delta_delta_2",
  "input": {"phases": [0.0, 2.0]},
  "expected": {"r": 0.5403023058681398, "mean_phase": 1.0, "mean_phase_matters": true} }
```

The N=2 identity `r = |cos(Δ/2)|` is pre-encoded at three detunings
so a regression in either language that breaks the two-oscillator
limit fails on at least one specific case.

`vectors/hilbert.json` describes signals by *formula* (not by listing N
floats) so the TS twin can build the identical input the same way —
e.g. `{"signal_formula": "cosine", "N": 32, "k": 3, "A": 1.0}` means
`A·cos(2π k n / N)`.

## What's not here (deliberate scope)

- `stats.welch` (Welch PSD + log-log slope fit). The TS already lives
  at `sgrounds/lib/piano/onsetPSD.ts` and is in regular use for the
  piano trainer's IOI slope diagnostic. Follow-up PR will port and
  add shared vectors.
- `stats.pitch_histogram`. Mostly interesting on the TS/piano side;
  port when a second user needs it.
- `stats.stationary_phase`. Lives at `fluids/stationary_phase.py`
  because the fluids track needed it first (PR #6). Candidate for
  migration into `stats` once a second user emerges.
- The physical TS mirror into `packages/stats/ts/` so sgrounds imports
  from NICU-Math. That's a cross-repo change; separate PR against
  both repos once the Py side is settled here.

## Interaction with open PRs

- **PR #3** (baseline restructure) — orthogonal subtree; no collision.
  Its `.gitignore` is not on this branch so `__pycache__` dirs were
  manually excluded. Future branches inherit the ignore after merge.
- **PR #5** (research spine) — the base of this PR. `packages/stats/`
  scaffold + README table are updated here to mark Py-side modules as
  shipped.
- **PR #6** (`fluids/`) — orthogonal subtree.

## Validation checklist for review

- [ ] `pip install -e packages/stats/py` succeeds.
- [ ] `pytest -q packages/stats/py/tests/` reports 31 passed.
- [ ] `vectors/kuramoto.json` cases match hand calculation: `r=1`
  for identical phases; `r=0` for antipodal pair, 3-uniform, and
  12-uniform; `r = |cos(Δ/2)|` for N=2.
- [ ] The TS twin in sgrounds still passes its own vitest run
  (nothing in TS changed in this PR; the shared vectors here will
  only start affecting TS when the TS loader is added in a follow-up).

author: caresuiteapp
body:
Die bisherige Rechnungsverwaltung hatte unvollständige Vorschauen, verstreute Aktionen und nicht atomare Speicherabläufe. Dieser PR ersetzt die Office-Web-Ansichten durch einen kompakten hellen Arbeitsbereich und sichert den Rechnungslebenszyklus serverseitig ab.

- Suche, Monats-/Statusfilter, echte offene Beträge, responsive Liste und klare Lade-, Leer- und Fehlerzustände.
- Manueller Rechnungseditor mit mehreren Positionen und Entwurfsvorschau ohne endgültige Nummer; Leistungsnachweise als ausdrücklich gewählte PDF-Kopien, bestätigte Originale separat herunterladbar.
- Monatlicher, bewusst gestarteter Rechnungslauf mit nachvollziehbarer Eignungsprüfung, Einzelvorschauen, Auswahl und wiederholbarer Entwurfserstellung. Kein automatischer Versand.
- Endgültige Nummer und unveränderliche archivierte PDF werden gemeinsam freigegeben. Versandstatus dokumentiert einen tatsächlich extern erfolgten Versand; Zahlungen werden als echte Ledger-Buchungen erfasst.
- Zahlungsübersicht, vorhandene Mahnungen und Rechnungsmonatsübersicht mit vollständigen Datenabfragen.

Backend bereits bereitgestellt: Migration 20261018075737_office_invoice_workspace und bestehende Edge Function render-document-pdf v11. Alle 11 Rechnungsfunktionen stimmen im Live-Readback exakt mit der Migration überein; Spalten, aktive Guards, restriktive Leseregeln und private Tabellenrechte geprüft. Beide Rechnungs-RPCs weisen Aufrufe ohne Sitzung mit 42501 zurück. Bestehende Edge-Funktionsdateien ebenfalls exakt zurückgelesen; anonymer HTTP-Aufruf liefert 401.

Prüfung: 50 strukturelle SQL-Verträge und 50 isolierte Prüfungen des tatsächlichen Upload-Handlers bestanden; zusätzliche direkte Modell-/Serviceprüfungen und TS/TSX-Syntaxprüfung bestanden. Primärer Vercel-Build für ad6f6b2 erfolgreich: bestehende vollständige TypeScript-/Release-/Vitest-/Export-Kette inklusive Rechnungs-Gate bestanden. Die beiden Typfehler des ersten Checkpoints (Supabase-Cast und unvollständiger Testdatensatz) sind korrigiert und deren Review-Hinweise erledigt. Keine Live-Testrechnungen, Zahlungsbuchungen oder Nachrichten angelegt.

Grenzen: Authentifizierte visuelle Browserprüfung und echtes PDF-Rendering sind in dieser Arbeitsumgebung noch nicht nachgewiesen: der Prüfbrowser öffnet die Verwaltungsanmeldung und besitzt keine aktive Sitzung. author: macf-code-agent[bot]
dhruv2mars
body:
## Summary

A World version's primary record is now a **changeset**: the paths it changed relative to its parent, each with its new entry or a deletion. Full snapshots are derived on demand. Publish composes through indexed per-path lookups and writes only the change. Per-command paths validate only what they read; full-graph validation runs in `check()`, `history()` and `init()` on an existing store.

## What changed

- **Schema format 6** (`src/repository.rs`). Main took format 5 in #43, so this bumps to 6. There is **no migration from format 5 or 4**. Pre-GA formats aren't authoritative (`docs/build-contract.md`), and older stores are refused with `unsupported_format`.
  - `changes(path, version, kind, content)`: a `WITHOUT ROWID` table with PK `(path, version)`, plus `changes_by_version`. NULL `kind`/`content` means deletion.
  - `versions(number, id, operation)`: `id` is a hash chain, `SHA-256("javelin-version-v1\0" || id(V-1) || canonical changeset)`, computed in O(change).
  - `attempts.manifest` is NULL for Layer publications, which are bound through `publications`. It stays set for `compare_and_advance` (protocol full-manifest input). Main's `attempts_result` index is kept.
- **Engine-neutral logic** (`src/domain.rs`): `SparseChanges` is the changeset type. `intersections()` and `normalize()` run over a small `WorldIndex` trait (`entry_at`, `changed_under`, `check_entry`). The SQL implementation is `Index` in `repository.rs`. An in-memory `SnapshotIndex` lets `check()` reuse `normalize` to prove every stored changeset is canonical against its parent.
- **Publish compose** (`src/publish.rs`, inside main's prepare/CAS split from #43): for each Layer path, compare `entry_at(base)` with `entry_at(head)` for the path itself, each ancestor prefix, and each descendant with a change row in `(base, head]`. This gives the same exact, ancestor/descendant and end-to-end revert semantics as the old full-diff loop, now at O(changed paths × depth) plus descendant ranges. The new version's changeset is the Layer's changeset as is. No manifest is loaded or written.
- **Derived snapshots**: `Repository::manifest_at(version)`, `Repository::checkpoint_manifest(checkpoint)`, `Repository::changeset(version)` and `Repository::head()`. These are used by Stack merge, capture, clone-backed workspaces, the OverlayFS runtime and the protocol path.
- **Validation scope**: Layer, Stack and Publish commands stop calling full-state validation. They verify the head row and its attempt binding, the Layer rows and checkpoints they touch (shallow, no Stack-ancestry walk), the Layer's successful publication receipt, and new objects. `read_checkpoint` (deep ancestry) and `layer_history` (that Layer's events and attempts) still verify what they return.

## Deviations from the brief

- **Format 6, not 5**, because #43 already used 5.
- **Public API changes**:
  - `WorldVersion.manifest` → `WorldVersion.id`.
  - `LayerBase::manifest()` → `LayerBase::world()`.
  - `LayerCheckpoint::manifest()` is removed; use `Repository::checkpoint_manifest`.
  - The Publish guard now receives `(&WorldVersion, &SparseChanges)`, the exact changeset, instead of a full candidate manifest.
  - `javelin_protocol::Outcome::from_native(outcome, manifest)` takes the requested manifest, since versions no longer name one. The wire format is unchanged.
- **`compare_and_advance` stays O(repo)**: it derives the head snapshot to diff a full protocol manifest. It no longer re-validates unrelated history.
- **Corruption detection moved, not dropped**: test assertions that used `version()`, `layer_state()`, `capture_layer()`, `compare_and_advance()` or a fresh Publish to detect damage to *unrelated* records now assert through `check()`, `history()`, `init()`, `layer_history()` or `publication()`. All of those still fail closed. Damage to what a command reads (its head checkpoint, its content, its Layer's success receipt) still fails that command.

## Bench

`tests/publish_bench.rs` is `#[ignore]` and uses only APIs that exist on both sides:

```
cargo test --release --test publish_bench -- --ignored --nocapture
JAVELIN_BENCH_CASES=1000x10,100000x1000 JAVELIN_BENCH_SAMPLES=20 cargo test --release --test publish_bench -- --ignored --nocapture
```

It builds World 1 with N files, adds H-1 one-file publishes, then times one-file `publish_layer` calls (blob stored beforehand). It reports median latency, mean DB file growth, and mean bytes of 4 KiB DB pages the Publish rewrote (journal not counted). The machine is an Apple Silicon Mac, APFS, `synchronous=EXTRA` + `fullfsync`.

| one-file Publish | main df09800 latency | main growth / pages | **branch latency** | **branch growth / pages** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1k files × 10 versions | 45.6 ms | 133 KB / 184 KB | **28.1 ms** | **2.2 KB / 63 KB** |
| 1k × 1,000 | not finished in 23 min of setup | — | **29.8 ms** | **0.8 KB / 63 KB** |
| 100k × 10 | 3,795 ms | 13.5 MB / 13.5 MB | **27.4 ms** | **1.0 KB / 62 KB** |
| 100k × 1,000 | **extrapolated**: ≥3.8 s, ~13.5 MB per Publish, ~13.5 GB of setup | — | **17.3 ms** | **1.0 KB / 62 KB** |

Branch medians are over 20 samples; main medians are over 5. Pre-#43 main (88ae5ca) measured 4.7 s at 1k×10 and 26 s at 100k×1.

- **Bytes target (<10 KB excluding the blob): met** for logical growth (0.8–2.2 KB). Physical page rewrites are a constant ~62 KB: about 15 B-tree pages, one per table/index touched (versions, changes plus index, attempts plus indexes, publications plus indexes, the receipt object). This doesn't grow with repository size or history.
- **Latency target (100k×1,000 within 2x of 1k×10): met** (17.3 vs 28.1 ms). Per-Publish latency is dominated by fsyncs on two transactions and is noisy at ±10 ms.
- Main's 100k×1,000 cell was not run. Its setup alone writes ~13.5 MB per version (~13.5 GB total), and 100k×10 already took 9.5 minutes. Main's 1k×1,000 was stopped after 23 minutes of setup, so each 1k-file cycle there costs well over a second. The 100k×1,000 figure above is an extrapolation from 100k×10, not a measurement.

## Checks

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes.
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes on macOS, and with `--target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` (zig cross-compiler) so the Linux-only OverlayFS tests compile.
- `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features`: 245 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored (macOS). Windows was not run locally; CI covers it.
- New tests (`tests/world_changesets.rs`): indexed exact, ancestor, descendant and deletion conflicts; a net-revert non-conflict; a randomized 6-seed × 60-publish differential test of outcomes and derived snapshots against the old full-manifest algorithm; hash-chain stability across repos and reopen, plus `check()`/`history()` rejecting five kinds of change-row and version-id tampering; `compare_and_advance` changeset recording.

## Not done / follow-ups

- Capture and base materialization derive full snapshots (O(change rows up to the base)) before walking the tree. They are O(repo) anyway, but a cached per-base snapshot would remove the history factor.
- Physical writes per Publish (~62 KB of pages) could shrink by making the TEXT-keyed tables `WITHOUT ROWID`.
- Tree-structured manifests and the protocol's 65,536-entry cap remain separate follow-ups.

author: webbertakken
body: Walking the city has had a bicycle and a car parked by the landing since the tracer bullet, but the bicycle was an arcade sprite on two wheels: it turned on rails, leaned by formula and could not fall. This is the showpiece phase of exploring: a bicycle that rides like one, in a city that has vehicles standing about it. It solves three things. The bicycle now balances, steers and stops as a real one does, and stays fun on a keyboard. The city is no longer empty of vehicles beyond the landing. And riding has its own numbers, sound and controls on every device. What was done: - **Single-track physics** (`explore/bicycle.ts`): the linearised Whipple equations with Meijaard et al.'s benchmark bicycle, so self-stability (4.3 to 6 m/s hands-free), countersteering and turning by leaning come from the physics. A simulated rider balances it (assisted balance), helps with the body at walking pace, and wobbles the bars there. - **Drivetrain and brakes**: cadence, seven gears (Q and R, the wheel, LB and RB), freewheel, rolling resistance and air drag; back and front brakes with weight moving forwards, so a hard front brake lifts the back wheel, held short of going over the bars. Each tyre has a friction circle: braking hard while leaned over slides it out. - **The rider**: legs on the pedals and hands on the grips by two-bone reach, a foot down at a stop, thrown off by a hard knock or a slide, and back up after a moment. - **Parked vehicles from the plan** (`explore/parking.ts`): kerb places along every street filled by a hash of road and place, never in a junction; the 200 nearest the landing are kept and the nearest 16 drawn from a pool. The landing's car now stands across the street, clear of the bicycle's line. - **Bell, HUD and devices**: B or Ring rings a Web Audio bell; speed, gear and cadence in the walk's card; touch buttons for Brake, Ring and the gears; a standard gamepad walks and rides. - Spec, blueprint and defaults updated; unit tests stay at 100 % coverage, and the e2e suite rides, shifts, brakes and stops with a foot down on desktop, and uses the touch buttons on a phone. ![Riding through a left turn, the HUD in the card](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f9b9b83-2d36-44d2-bffb-0ec25ae7b606)

author: jkdreamr
body:
Adds **Grand Prix** (`chrome://games/grand-prix`), a 3D open-wheel racer where the driving comes from real physics, not arcade rules. It is first in the 3D section of the arcade.

## Driving model (`car.ts`)
- A rigid body on four tyres. Each tyre has its own grip curve that combines braking, acceleration and cornering, with grip that drops under heavy load and with tread temperature (best between about 90 and 110 °C).
- Each wheel spins on its own, so wheelspin and lock-ups actually happen. Without ABS, a full pedal locks the wheels as speed drops.
- Weight shifts under braking, acceleration and cornering.
- Downforce and drag, plus DRS and slipstream: less drag on straights, less downforce in dirty air.
- An 8-speed seamless gearbox, an auto clutch that slips on launches, a locking rear differential, brake bias, and an ERS battery with per-lap deploy and harvest limits.
- Checked against real-car figures in the tests: 0–100 in about 3 s, top speed about 344 km/h (353 with DRS), about 4.7 g braking at top speed, about 1.8 g in slow corners and about 3.5 g in fast ones.

## Circuit (`track.ts`)
- Monza, 5.77 km, run clockwise, built from straights and arcs and closed exactly: Rettifilo, Curva Biassono, Roggia, both Lesmos, Serraglio, Ascari, Parabolica.
- Kerbs, gravel traps, painted run-off, walls, catch fences, tyre barriers, track limits, three timing sectors and two DRS zones.

## Modes
- **Time Trial**: flying laps against your saved ghost, with a live delta and coloured sectors. Personal bests are saved per board.
- **Race**: 20 cars from a standing start behind five lights. 3, 5 or 10 laps, four AI levels, and a choice of grid slot. Track-limit warnings turn into 5-second penalties.
- **2P Split**: a race on one screen, side by side or stacked, with keyboard or two gamepads.
- **Online**: rooms with bots, built on the existing kit; the host sets the laps and bot pace.

## AI (`ai.ts`)
- Computer drivers follow a minimum-curvature racing line with a speed target from the car's grip and power.
- They drive the same physics as the player, using only steering, throttle and brake, and they pass slower cars.
- About 1:26 a lap at full pace; a 20-car race runs with no wall hits.

## Visuals (`scene.ts`, `model.ts`)
- **Cars:**
  - Lofted bodywork, front and rear wings with a working DRS flap, the halo and suspension arms.
  - Wheels that spin and steer, glowing brakes, and a rain light that flashes under braking.
- **Lighting and sky:** sun shadows, lighting and reflections from a sky with sun and clouds.
- **Track and scenery:**
  - Procedural asphalt with rubber laid on the racing line.
  - Grandstands with a crowd, the pit building, and a start gantry with working lights.
  - Bridges, braking boards and a forest.
- **Effects:** skid marks, tyre smoke and dust.
- **Cameras:** chase, T-cam, cockpit and nose, plus look back.
- **Performance:** about 340 draw calls with 20 cars on track. Touch devices get a lighter version.

## HUD (`hud.tsx`)
Rev lights, gear and speed, throttle and brake bars, ERS and DRS status, four tyre temperatures, lap time and delta, sectors, a timing tower, a minimap and the start lights.

## Controls (`input.ts`)
- Keyboard, gamepad (analog stick and triggers) and on-screen touch controls.
- Keyboard steering lock shrinks with speed to what the tyres can use, so a held key turns as hard as the car can and no harder. A test checks that a driver using only key presses can lap cleanly with the default assists.
- Optional assists: TC, ABS and auto gears. Time trial boards are split into **No Assists** and **With Assists**.

## Shared files touched
- `src/os/arcade/kit/three-lib.ts`: re-exports the extra three.js classes this game uses.
- `worker/src/specs.gen.ts`: regenerated with `npm run arcade:specs` (2 boards and the online spec).

## ⚠️ After merging
Redeploy the Worker (`cd worker && npx wrangler deploy`). Until then, the live Worker refuses online rooms and global leaderboard scores for `grand-prix`. Scores stay on the player's device and Create Room shows an error. Solo modes and split screen work without it.

## Not in this PR
Engine and revving sound, as you asked; that's planned for the next PR. There are also no pit stops, tyre wear, fuel or damage yet.

## Testing
- `npm test`: 1537/1537 pass, including 17 new tests in `tests/arcade-grand-prix.test.ts` (track geometry, physics against real figures, AI laps, a full race, time trial timing, packets, input).
- `npm run build`: passes (0 errors, 0 warnings), and the game is its own lazy-loaded chunk of about 92 KB.
- Checked in headless Chromium: Start card, grid, all four cameras, split screen, and phone and tall layouts. That browser renders in software at about 1 fps, so nobody has hand-driven the game at full frame rate yet. Driving was checked with simulated drivers instead.

body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

Resolves #5871.

### ❓ Type of change

- [ ] 📖 Documentation
- [x] 🐞 Bug fix (non-breaking)
- [ ] 👌 Enhancement
- [ ] ✨ New feature
- [ ] 🧹 Chore

### 📚 Description

When `UCheckbox` is the direct child of `UTooltip`, hovering its label does not open the tooltip because the trigger's pointer listeners are forwarded to the inner checkbox button.

Forward `pointermove`, `pointerleave` and `data-grace-area-trigger` to the existing outer Primitive so the box and label share the hover boundary. Keep focus, click, ARIA and form attributes on the inner control, and retain the `data-state` filter so tooltip state cannot overwrite checkbox state. Attribute splitting happens during rendering, including when tooltip listeners change after toggling `disabled`.

No public props, slots, emits or DOM wrappers are added. A playground example and eight integration regression cases cover default/list/card labels, nested label-slot content, movement within and outside the root, delayed opening/cancellation, touch, disabled changes, listener invocation counts, keyboard focus, ARIA, accessibility and label-click toggling.

author: juzaweb
body:
﻿Implements **F2 — Server-authoritative kill rewards (EXP / bac / drops)** from `BACKLOG.md` (EPIC F, P2). Spec gate: PASS (inline spec review).

## Why

F1 moved enemy HP, death and respawn to the server, but the reward for a kill was still minted by whichever client locally crossed `HP <= 0` (`CombatSystem.damageEnemy` -> `handleWolfKill`: `Phaser.Math.Between(3, 9)` bac, a flat +35 EXP, a `rollDrop` drop, then a save). The server's `enemy_hit` already carried `attackerId`, yet nothing a client received could contradict a doctored payout — the last client-authoritative step in the combat loop. Fine for the co-op demo, but it has to close before the economy items (B3 shop, C7 ren duc, C8 cuong hoa) treat bac/EXP as scarce.

## What changed

**Server**
- New `server/src/rewards.js`: `rollEnemyReward(attackerId, enemy, rng)` rolls EXP, bac and the drop from the shared client catalog (`src/game/items.js`), so both sides agree on the numbers and a client can recompute the payload.
- `server/src/websocket/gameSocket.js`: `handleEnemyHit` flags the kill from its own HP pool, broadcasts `enemy_hit` as before, then broadcasts `enemy_reward` exactly once per kill. The corpse-resync path cannot pay twice.

**Client**
- New `src/game/rewardSync.js`: `parseEnemyReward` validates the payload (finite non-negative EXP/bac, catalog-backed drop id; loot quantity comes from the local table, not the payload) and returns `null` for anything untrustworthy.
- `src/game/combat.js`: `handleWolfKill` keeps only presentation when connected and waits for the authoritative event; `applyServerReward` renders the shared drop on every client and pays EXP/bac/kill count only to the client the server attributed the kill to; `grantKillReward` holds the payout path (log, float text, level-up, quest, save). Drops carry a `collectable` flag set from that attribution, loot this client cannot take expires after 8 s, and the drop list is bounded. Offline play keeps the previous local roll unchanged.
- `src/game/game.js`: wires `enemy_reward` to `CombatSystem.applyServerReward` and passes the joined player id down for attribution.

## Verification

- `npm run build` — pass.
- `npm test` — **94 passed** (20 new: `rewardSync.test.js`, `rollKillReward` in `items.test.js`, and `CombatSystem` payout + drop ownership/expiry/bounds in `combat.test.js`).
- `npm run server:test` — **29 passed** (4 new: reward roll + attribution under a fixed rng; `enemy_reward` broadcast to both clients; only the killing blow pays).
- Verifier sub-agent (`code-review`) review history is in the comments: REQUEST CHANGES on the bystander-collectable drop (fixed in `9c9a4a3`), then a `code-review-and-quality` five-axis pass whose two Required findings are fixed in `1ec1ecf` with an **Approve** verdict.

## Policy notes

- Diff is 13 files, above `gate.yaml:maxFiles` (10), so this PR escalates to a **human merge** (no auto-merge into `develop`).
- No denylisted paths, no `humanMergeRequired` paths (`package.json`/`vite.config.js`/`.github/**` untouched).
- Known remaining local mint, out of scope: `collectDrop` still grants +5 bac / +5 noi luc to whoever picks a drop up.
- Follow-up filed: **E4** (`proposed`) — split the loot/drop concern out of `CombatSystem`.

author: tusanhomichi
body:
Peter chose this (option B in the dist-git decision note): store dist-git as a source kind in the public archive.

Before: CentOS 7's last glibc (2.17-326.el7_9.3), kernel (3.10.0-1160.119.1) and libX11 (1.6.7-5.el7_9) updates have no `.src.rpm` on the vault or on Red Hat's SRPMS. r2push therefore holds back their 8 binaries, and the public archive can't serve glibc for any CentOS 7 run.

After: when every other source fails for a CentOS 7 rpm, ingest stores the package's dist-git import as its source:
- it clones the tag `imports/c7/<nvr>` (gitlab.com/CentOS/archives/git.centos.org, where git.centos.org now redirects);
- it stores every file at the commit the tag names, with the spec first, which the binary's index entry names as its source;
- it stores each tarball the import's `.<name>.metadata` lists, fetched from `git.centos.org/sources/<name>/c7/<sha1>` and checked against that sha1.

It's all of it or nothing: if one tarball is missing, nothing is kept. Every entry is marked `live`, because nothing upstream signs the tag. git checks the files against the commit, and the archive's signature vouches for the rest.

How: `Store.distgit()`, called from `Store.fallback()` after the Red Hat and koji tries, for `vault.centos.org/7.*` only. The clone source can be overridden with `WEND_DISTGIT` for tests. test_archive adds two checks: a full import with its tarball stored and live, and an import whose tarball the lookaside lost, which keeps nothing.

author: kukks
body:
## Summary

The 50-browser Mutinynet test exposed a proving download failure: snarkjs received Cloudflare 429 HTML as a wasm or zkey file and reported bad magic or an invalid file format. Prefetch could also mark an unsuccessful HTTP response as fetched.

Check HTTP status before reading file bytes, retry transient network, 429 and server failures up to five attempts, and honor Retry-After seconds or dates. Share the in-flight download and successful bytes between prefetch and proving. Evict failed downloads so a later user attempt can recover. A Retry-After longer than 30 seconds rejects promptly and retains a per-URL cooldown, so a user is not left waiting for hours and another attempt cannot redownload before the server deadline.

Each attempt has a 120-second abort timer covering fetch and body reads; it is cleared in finally. Timeouts follow the same bounded retry and failure-eviction path.

Circuit selection, cryptographic verification, payment submission, and admission policies are unchanged. Existing immutable proving URLs remain compatible. Rollback: revert this PR; no data migration is involved.

## Validation

- Baseline: 522/522 tests passing. Current: 533/533 passing, no skipped tests.
- Eleven focused regression tests pass, including a real Groth16 proof verified after a mocked 429 HTML response, download coalescing, Retry-After seconds/dates, definitive 404 rejection, bounded retry exhaustion/recovery, prompt rejection with no early refetch for a long cooldown, and timeout/recovery for stalled fetch/body reads.
- npm run build and git diff --check pass.
- Live post-deploy verification remains pending. The separate load test has confirmed edge rate limiting; this change does not increase server capacity or bypass that protection.

author: gregpakes
body:
## Why

`lapsmith.gregpakes.co.uk` doesn't work from off the LAN over Tailscale. Two gaps:

1. **No DNS route for `gregpakes.co.uk`.** On the Mac, `tailscale dns status` shows no resolvers and no split-DNS route for the domain. The README said to set Pi-hole as a *global* nameserver with "Override local DNS" off, but in that mode clients keep their local resolver, so the global entry is never used. Pi-hole itself answers fine over the tailnet (`dig lapsmith.gregpakes.co.uk @172.16.51.67` → `172.16.51.66`).
2. **The target isn't routed.** lapsmith is on Traefik internal (`172.16.51.66`), and the subnet router only advertised Plex (`.70`) and Pi-hole (`.67`). `curl --resolve …:443:172.16.51.66` timed out.

## Changes

- `connector.yaml`: advertise `172.16.51.66/32` as a third host route. `.65` (external Traefik), the API VIP and the nodes stay off the tailnet.
- `README.md`:
  - Step 4 now sets up a split-DNS nameserver (`172.16.51.67`, restricted to `gregpakes.co.uk`) instead of a global one, and explains why.
  - Adds the `.66` autoApprover.
  - Adds a `grants` rule limiting the three routed hosts to `autogroup:member`. It only takes effect once the default allow-all grant is removed.
  - Adds checks that confirm DNS and lapsmith work.
  - Notes that resolving a name is not the same as reaching it.
- `values.yaml`: comment updated to list the three routes.

## After merge (console-side)

- [ ] **DNS → Nameservers → Add nameserver → Custom** → `172.16.51.67`, **Restrict to domain** `gregpakes.co.uk`. This works on its own, before the merge.
- [ ] Approve `172.16.51.66/32` on `ts-plex-subnet-router`, or add the autoApprover entry.
- [ ] Optional: replace the default allow-all grant with the members-only grant from the README.

## Test plan

- [ ] Off the LAN: `tailscale dns status` lists `gregpakes.co.uk. -> 172.16.51.67`
- [ ] `dig +short lapsmith.gregpakes.co.uk` → `172.16.51.66`
- [ ] `curl -sI https://lapsmith.gregpakes.co.uk/` → 302 to GitHub sign-in

Not tested end to end yet. The route only goes live after the Argo sync and route approval.

author: tannevaled
body:
Closes #47.

`ghmerge` refused `go-gfx/gfx#74`:

```
ghmerge: refusing to merge go-gfx/gfx#74 — arch loong64 (qemu) failure
```

It read each check row's own conclusion. But the workflow run that produced all
thirteen rows concluded **`success`**:

| source | says |
|---|---|
| check rows | 12 `SUCCESS`, 1 `FAILURE` (`arch loong64 (qemu)`) |
| run 38218557261, which produced all 13 | `status=completed` **`conclusion=success`** |

GitHub concludes a run `success` with a failed job **only** when that job carried
`continue-on-error`. So the run's conclusion is not a softer reading of the same
evidence — it is the **repository stating which of its own lanes gate**. The rows
cannot carry that, because a dispensed job still reports `failure` as a check
run, which is what makes the failure *visible*. That is the entire point of an
advisory lane.

That particular lane watches an open upstream compiler bug
(golang/go#81147, milestone Go1.27.3) and is meant to report rather than block.
Until now it — and every other advisory lane in the fleet — made its pull
request permanently unmergeable by this tool.

## How

For each row that is not green, ask which workflow run owns it, and treat the row
as dispensed only when that run concluded `success`. The join is
`check_suite.id` against the run's `check_suite_id`, the only link either object
carries.

**And it says so out loud.** A dispensation must never be silent, or a lane
quietly marked `continue-on-error` to get a merge through becomes invisible:

```
go-gfx/gfx#74: arch loong64 (qemu) failure — ADVISORY, the workflow run that
produced it concluded success, so the repository does not gate on it
go-gfx/gfx#74: 13 check(s), 0 status(es), green but for the 1 advisory lane(s) above
```

The extra call is made **only when a row is red**. The hourly REST budget is
shared with Renovate and every other session on this machine, and a green merge
cannot use the answer anyway.

## Five tests, and the three that matter are negative

| test | what it refuses to let happen |
|---|---|
| an advisory lane does not block | the bug itself (**the witness**) |
| a red lane in a **failed** run still refuses | widening the gate to everything |
| an unfinished run excuses nothing | a null conclusion read as a yes |
| a dispensation does not cross suites | joining on the sha instead of the suite |
| the green path asks for no workflow runs | paying for a call it cannot use |

**Proved by ablation, not by argument.** With `dispensations` returning an empty
map:

```
--- FAIL: TestAnAdvisoryLaneDoesNotBlockTheMerge
--- PASS: TestARedLaneInAFailedRunStillRefuses
--- PASS: TestAnUnfinishedRunExcusesNothing
--- PASS: TestADispensationIsNotTransferredBetweenSuites
--- PASS: TestTheGreenPathAsksForNoWorkflowRuns
```

The witness is sensitive to the feature; the controls are not sensitive in the
wrong direction.

## The fixture's own default arm earned itself again

Teaching it the new endpoint was *forced*: six existing tests failed with

```
the fake GitHub was asked for "/repos/o/r/actions/runs", which it does not serve
```

— all six of them tests that carry a red check, and **none** that do not. That is
itself the measurement that the call is made exactly when it is useful. The
comment on that `default` arm says a fixture agreeing with any path cannot tell
you that you asked for one it has never heard of; this is the second time it has
paid for itself.

Measured: **29 packages green**.

author: josh-complex
body:
## What changed

P2-8 part 3c-1a, the first slice of part 3c (sending). It adds the two pieces a send needs. Nothing calls them yet; part 3c-1b wires them into the cast's screens.

- **`apps/ballot/src/casts.ts`: this device's records of its casts** ([[revoting]], Client rule 3)
  - Records live in an IndexedDB database of their own, keyed by election and tier, so each tier is separate (rule 7).
  - Each record holds the version-3 ballot bytes, plus the operator's answer once it has been checked.
  - `recordCast` keeps a ballot only if it names a block strictly newer than every recorded one, and only beside casts that name the same definition. The check and the write happen in one transaction, so two tabs can never both keep a cast on one block.
  - The caller records a cast before the ballot leaves the device. A retry resends the recorded bytes.
  - `recordBoarded` keeps the first checked answer for exactly the recorded bytes.
  - A stored record is parsed as strictly as a decoder. Anything malformed is `unreadable`: it is never read as "no casts" and never replaced.
- **`apps/ballot/src/send.ts`: `POST /ballots` and the answer check**
  - `sendBallot` sends lowercase hex with no cookie, referrer or credential, and follows no redirect.
  - Each answer is read only in the route's own shape. Anything else is `unreachable`.
  - The read is capped by the size the ballot fixes.
  - `checkBoarded` passes a boarded answer only if all of these hold:
    - the entry is lowercase hex of exactly the fixed length;
    - it decodes under the pinned board-entry version;
    - it names the election and carries exactly the bytes sent;
    - the link is 32 bytes.
- **Refactors**
  - `withStore` moves from `identity.ts` to `store.ts`, shared by both stores. The identity store's behaviour is unchanged.
  - `readJson` (`answer.ts`) now takes a cap.

## Threats

- T-45, T-38: no self-tie, and no new ballot on a retry.
- T-25: a retry resends identical bytes.
- T-10: no credential is sent.
- T-31: strict decoding, lowercase hex only.
- T-52: capped reads.
- T-26: no signed receipt yet (known-weak).
- T-18: the records are unencrypted at rest (known-weak).

## Tests

- **`tests/casts.test.ts`:**
  - fast-check round trip;
  - copies are handed out, not the stored arrays;
  - malformed records are unreadable: version, keys, holes, extra properties, an undecodable ballot, another record type, two casts on one block, casts out of order, an answer of the wrong shape or length, an entry carrying other bytes, two definitions, answers naming two elections.
- **`tests/send.test.ts`:**
  - the exact request;
  - every defined answer, and the ones outside its shape;
  - a network failure;
  - the cap, both at the limit and one byte past it;
  - `checkBoarded` (fast-check): it passes any vector ballot at any index, segment, election and link, and refuses any flipped ballot byte, another election, another or resized ballot, another board-entry version, trailing or missing bytes, upper-case or odd-length hex, and a wrong-length link.
- **`tests/worker.e2e.ts`, in Chromium under the client's CSP:**
  - records persist across reloads, each tier separately;
  - a cast on a block that isn't newer is refused, including two concurrent tabs;
  - the first checked answer is kept, and `conflict` is returned for a different one;
  - entries that fail the check are refused;
  - a cast with another definition gets `other-election`;
  - a record of another version is unreadable and never replaced;
  - non-ballot bytes are refused.
- `vp run --filter @abolishus/ballot check` and `test` pass. The new unit tests also pass with `FC_NUM_RUNS=1000`.

## Known-weak

The full list is in `docs/status/P2-8.md`, Part 3c-1a:

- nothing calls these functions yet;
- the operator signs no receipt yet (P2-3);
- the records are unencrypted at rest;
- version-3 ballots only;
- no tie escape (rule 5) yet;
- a boarded entry's segment isn't range-checked;
- a lost casts database reads as no casts;
- the list of casts is unbounded.

## Independent review

An in-session subagent ran with the `crypto-review` checklist. It found nothing blocking, and its findings were addressed as follows:

1. **`recordBoarded` refused `checkBoarded`'s own output** (an exact-keys check against the extra `index` and `segment` fields).
   - Fixed: only the entry and link are passed through.
   - The e2e test now feeds the output of `checkBoarded` straight in.
2. **Nothing tied a stored ballot to its key.**
   - Fixed: casts under one key must share their definition hash (`other-election` otherwise), and every answer must name one election.
   - `recordBoarded` checks the entry's election against the key.
3. **No tie escape.** Added to known-weak; it gets its own path later.
4. **A stored entry was checked only by length.** Fixed: the length prefix and payload must equal the cast's bytes.
5. **`repeat` must not read as a failure.** Noted for 3c-1b in Next.
6. **Recovered client, and a lost casts database.** Added to known-weak.
7. **The segment range isn't checked.** Added to known-weak; the range needs the anchoring clock.
8. **`#PR` placeholders.** Fixed.
9. **The list is unbounded.** Added to known-weak.

CI's first run on the draft: `test` timed out in a fast-check property at `FC_NUM_RUNS=1000`. The heavy properties now have explicit timeouts. `e2e` died installing the toolchain (`curl: (56) Connection reset`) before any test ran.

No new dependencies.

author: sailmanseeulater
body:
## What

The person pastes their Google Calendar's **secret address in iCal format** into a new **Google Calendar** dialog on the Calendar page.
- **What's imported:** Mordi fetches the address and imports events from 30 days back to 6 months ahead, in the colour the person chose.
- **When it refreshes:** every 15 minutes for anyone active in the last 30 days, and whenever the calendar is opened with a stale feed.
- **Parsing:** biweekly 0.6.8 handles repeats, EXDATE, moved occurrences, cancellations and VTIMEZONE. Times are converted to the person's zone, sent from the browser and saved on the account.
- **Read-only:** Google events show a small link mark and open a read-only card. The server refuses edits with 409 "Change it there."
- **Limits:** up to 5 calendars, with sync-now, rename and disconnect.

## Security
- **The address is a secret.** It's AES-256-GCM encrypted under `MORDI_FEED_KEY`, never logged, and never returned (only a short hint). De-duplication uses a SHA-256 hash.
- **No SSRF.** The server only fetches `https://calendar.google.com/calendar/ical/<id>/(private-…|public)/basic.ics`.
  - The allow-list rejects user-info, ports, query strings and fragments, and the address is checked against it again before every request.
  - Redirects are never followed; timeouts are 10 s to connect and 20 s for the request; the body is read up to a 5 MB cap.
- **Off by default.** Without the key the feature is hidden, the API answers 404 and the scheduler does nothing.
- **Deletion.** Disconnecting, or deleting the account, removes the address and every copied event via the cascade.
- **Privacy Policy** updated; version `2026-10-18` on both the frontend and the backend.

## Setup after merge
1. Generate a key: `openssl rand -base64 32`
2. On the VPS: `echo "MORDI_FEED_KEY=<key>" >> ~/Mordi/.env`
3. Redeploy, or run `cd ~/Mordi && docker-compose up -d backend`; `.env` now pins the deployed tag.
4. Never change the key. Addresses saved under the old key can't be read with a new one.

## Testing
- **Backend:** 344 tests, 0 failures. The parser tests also pass with the JVM's default zone set to Auckland, UTC and Honolulu.
- **Postgres ITs:** 28/28 against Postgres 16, covering V21, every new query, Hibernate `validate`, and account deletion with connected calendars.
- **Frontend:** eslint clean; vitest 445/445; `vite build` ok.
- **In the browser** against a mock API: the dialog's states and errors; Google events are not draggable; the read-only card; the month view; one catch-up sync on open; mobile at 375px. One dialog bug was found and fixed with a regression test.

## Also in this PR
- **Calendar starts on Sunday by default.** A **Sun | Mon** switch sits in the Calendar toolbar beside Day / Week / Month, for the week and month views. It's the same preference as Settings → Appearance, and weekly goals still count Monday to Sunday. Checked at 1280×800 and 375px: no overflow, and the buttons are 44px.

A full redesign of `web/static/index.html`. **It includes #21, so merge this one instead.** No backend changes, and no build step: FastAPI still serves one HTML file, so Vercel needs nothing new.

## Design
An editorial "ledger book" rather than a SaaS template: Instrument Serif display type, Geist / Geist Mono, a warm paper and ink palette (light and dark, with a toggle), and one sindoor accent that only means "contradiction". Ledger rows have a date column like a real ledger, and rejected alternatives are struck through.

## Libraries (CDN, pinned)
- `alpinejs@3.14.1`: state and rendering (all user and model text goes through `x-text`, so it's escaped)
- `motion@11.11.13`: verdict reveal, row stagger, count-up (respects `prefers-reduced-motion`)
- `lucide@0.454.0`: icons
- Google Fonts: Geist, Geist Mono, Instrument Serif, Noto Serif Devanagari

## UX
- The check console is the hero, with labelled example chips (conflict / unrelated) and Ctrl/⌘+Enter.
- Verdicts read as citations: decision, verbatim quote, mono source line, explanation.
- **Inline forms replace `prompt()`** for replace, teach and reject (with focus handling).
- Ledger: status segments with counts, search, before/after precision bars, learned rules.
- Drag-and-drop import, copy button on the AGENTS.md block, toasts for results.
- Fallback labels (keyword / recorded / offline) and API calls are unchanged.

## Test plan (local, model unreachable)
- [x] MongoDB chip → cited contradiction (recorded fallback label); Keep, Replace (open/cancel) and Teach (open) all work; inputs focus on click
- [x] Unmatched text → "model offline" box with the local command; upload → friendly offline error
- [x] Tabs (8 settled / 4 rejected), search ("magic" → 1 row), stats 8 / 12 / 60%→71% with bars, 1 learned rule, AGENTS.md toggle, theme toggle
- [x] 375px: no horizontal overflow; order is check → ledger → side panels. Desktop: two columns, sticky side panel
- [x] No console errors; `pytest -q`: 31 passed

author: thinkingfish
body:
PR descriptions can retain a stale dependency blocker, overstate behavior in the opening, or leave the final implementation buried in historical commit messages. This change makes those checks explicit in `review-guide` while preserving repository conventions for required verbatim messages.

Five review scenarios cover consistency, current and unavailable dependency status, retained history, and distinct treatment of decisions, rationale, and validation gaps. Two prose scenarios cover repeated explanations and useful cross-references. The `technical-prose` instructions are unchanged because they already cover relevance and repetition.

The [evaluation record](https://github.com/iopsystems/skills-mcp/blob/7238720/docs/journal/2026-10-18-pr-description-consistency.md#evaluation) retains fictional inputs, source digests, baseline and revised outputs from separate fresh agents, and a third agent's critique. Both runs substantially satisfied the five requests. The critic found modest clarity gains, with no material factual failure in either run. This single comparison does not establish a general reliability improvement; two added scenarios were not executed, and both outputs implied a future re-review where the evidence only established that none had occurred.

Validation at `7238720`: 151 repository tests passed; formatting, strict clippy, debug and release builds, diagram checks, MCP smoke, review-bridge checks, and skill validation passed. Recorded input and skill digests were verified. The fixtures contain no private repository references.

author: sandeepannandi
body:
Fixes the visible polygon faceting on the cloth (user feedback: "too pixelated due to all polygons").

Causes:
- Web preview filled each triangle with one flat shade color, so brightness stepped per triangle.
- Native Skia texture sampling defaulted to nearest.
- The 17x12 mesh was coarse enough to read as polygons on folds.

Changes:
- Mesh 17x12 -> 25x17 (~12.5px cells) on native and web. Physics, wind, pins, drag and Reduce Motion behavior unchanged (clothMath is grid-agnostic; 9/9 math tests pass).
- Native: linear + mipmap sampling for the artwork texture, linear for the shade ramp.
- Web: per-vertex shade now fills each triangle with the exact planar gradient of its three vertex alphas (a plane through three values is a linear gradient), plus explicit high-quality image smoothing. Near-lit triangles skip the shade pass.

Verified locally: tsc, next build, node clothMath tests, playwright headless pass on the built site - rest drape, live breeze, drag, release recovery, Reduce Motion flat all render smooth (no faceting). Android emulator CI runs next via the parity branch before this counts as device-verified.

author: asafyish
body:
Addresses #415. Depends on #453; draft until that foundation lands. [Focused comparison against #453](https://github.com/asafyish/just-bash/compare/262a17b28b1729842720e348e5f860b32d5c7b08...bb1aef99).

`rg --files ... | head` currently enumerates the complete tree, and searches buffer all output. Discover files lazily, merge live roots with an ordered heap, read ahead in bounded batches, then match each file only as output is consumed. Preserve lexical order, duplicate operands, ignore rules and cleanup on downstream closure.

The stdin matcher and its encoding tests have moved to #638. Within-file line matching is separate in #639; existence-only early exit is #636. This PR owns file discovery and ordered per-file output only. The split removes the 154-line stdin module and reduces net added lines from 623 to 432 (31%); matching-loop reindentation still contributes to the displayed diff.

Validation: 581 rg/pipeline tests pass (82 existing skips), including complete output, overlapping roots, Unicode filenames, bounded read-ahead and downstream closure. Combined carried-runtime tests also pass (2,580 tests across interpreter/search/jq/du/ls/regex).

author: transfix
body:
## Why

`(while c a b)` ran only `a`. The rest of the body was dropped without an error, so a counter bumped in the second form never moved and the loop never ended. `(for x xs a b)` did the same. Every evaluator did it: the stackless one (and the async stackless wrapper), the tree-walking `evaluator`, and `async_evaluator`. The guide documented a single body, `(while cond body)`, but nothing enforced it. In the same way, `if` dropped forms after its else branch, and `return`/`yield`/`break` used only their first value.

The user decided: loop bodies of several forms run them all, as a `begin`; extra arguments to `if`/`return`/`yield`/`break` are an error.

## What

- **`while` and `for`** run every body form in order, as a `begin`. The loop's value is unchanged: nil, or `break`'s value. `break` from the middle of a multi-form body skips the rest of that iteration.
  - In the stackless evaluator, `loop_body()` builds the `(begin ...)` only for a body of several forms. A single-form loop keeps exactly the frames it had, so snapshots of in-flight loops are unaffected.
  - Under a restricted special-form set (the Ariadne predicate lane), a multi-form body counts as a `begin`; that set allows `begin`.
  - The tree-walking `evaluator` and `async_evaluator` evaluate each form in turn.
- **Arity errors.** `(if c a b d)`, `(return a b)`, `(yield a b)` and `(break a b)` now throw an error naming the form, in every evaluator that has that form. The other special forms already checked their arity.
- **Docs.** The developer guide's special-forms table shows `(while cond body...)` and `(for x collection body...)`, and says that extra arguments are errors.

## Audit

I scanned the 860 scripts that `gen_state_exec_corpus.py` collects from the tree: `.ari` fields, doc code blocks, C++ test strings and pycvc tests.
- No `for` or `if` has extra forms.
- One `while` does: the example in `docs/roadmap/DSL-GEOMETRY-VOLUME-ROADMAP.md:353`, `(while #t (set job (msg-recv ...)) (state-set ...) (process-brain ...) ...)`. It was written assuming every body form runs, and now they do.

So no script in the repo changes meaning, except for that example, which now does what its author intended.

## Tests

- `state_exec_stackless_evaluator_test`:
  - multi-form `while`, `for`, and `for` over a generator;
  - `break` in the middle of a multi-form body;
  - a loop's value is still nil;
  - each arity error names its form;
  - a multi-form loop under restricted special forms.
- `state_exec_evaluator_test` (tree-walking) and `state_exec_async_test` (`async_evaluator`, async stackless): multi-form `while`/`for`, and the `if`/`return` arity errors.

Local results (MSVC 14.38 Release, deps from the cvcpkg prefix):

- All 77 state_exec, Ariadne, `async_lane` and `state*` suites pass: 2106 tests, including the 13 new ones.
- pycvc (exec, exec_async, exec_coro, ari, state, app, async): 62 passed.
- clang-format 18 is clean on the changed lines, and `check_test_targets.py` is OK.

author: jan-kubica
body:
Pictures in WMF format are now drawn. The parser tries an embedded raster first, then a generated SVG from a bounded WMF subset (placeable and plain headers, pens and brushes with the format's default objects, lines, polygons, poly-polygons, rectangles and ellipses; device-unit, anisotropic and isotropic mapping), and keeps the existing placeholder otherwise. Unsupported records fail closed, every input is bounded, and the original bytes stay the source on save. EMF and WMF share the colour, transform and SVG helpers.

The converter is about 7 KB minified, so it loads with the parser.

Fixes #1692

author: fradser
body:
The Personal Agent now shows the Jev startup authentication check in a fixed header status. Ready requires a verified check. Missing credentials, rejected authentication, and service failures remain distinct.

Pi completion notifications use an authenticated Link subscription instead of progress polling. Stable event IDs prevent duplicate hints. Reconnects request one read-only catchup. The Pi Sessions snapshot exposes unsupported subscriptions without claiming automatic delivery.

Overview keeps a red dot beside the weekday. During refresh, the same indicator becomes a spinner. Retained briefing text stays unchanged, and initial loading uses the empty placeholder with an accessible busy state. Reduced motion keeps a static ring. Failure stops the spinner and retains the existing failure explanation. The dot does not indicate service health.

Automatic refresh already preserved conversation messages. New regressions retain that behavior alongside normal owner replies and task completion messages.

Validation:
- Latest complete Electron E2E: all reported statuses zero.
- Latest complete Agent Home fixture: exit zero; three themes, compact layouts, reduced motion, chat preservation, and fixed Jev status.
- Home preview: 11 captures; original text, geometry, scrolling, and 16px reading-floor gates retained.
- Independent Dashboard replacement: 8/8, including rejection cases. Lifecycle and frame tests: 11/11.
- Completion and Jev affected Node union: 220 passed, one existing skip. Four actual Main processes verified the IPC projection and subscription cleanup.
- Density: five runs without violations. Direct declared style compiler and UnoCSS checks passed.

Failure records remain available. The visible indicator initially exposed narrow-header overflow; removing the redundant header gap restored the existing gate. An intermittent preview floor failure led to explicit native resize and scrolling-geometry synchronization, without changing the floor. Updating the loading contract also required an exact empty-state mutation target in the independent negative fixture.

These checks use local synthetic fixtures and sockets. They do not establish live Jev authentication, device acceptance, or production completion delivery. The previous Code Terrier run ended with an infrastructure failure; the new head requires its own review.

author: renejordan
body:
Native cron gaps and restrictive discovery left the independent Buffer route empty. Add a renewable GitHub-hosted hourly clock, native recovery, prefetch and one-send-per-hour accounting. Target: up to 15 posts from 09 through 23 Berlin, capped by both calendar day and rolling 24 hours. No personal computer or paid model API is required.

Refresh the current German TwitchTracker top 50 daily, retain the last successful list through outages, and rank clips by views, view velocity and streamer rank. Lower-view clips remain eligible. Fresh broadcaster/original-age metadata, actual audio, usable source/final frames, title/subtitle rendering and full output decode remain checked. The user-requested practical policy does not demand perfect narrative/payoff scores. Uncertain words are omitted; version-3 receipts describe these basic checks without claiming human viewing or perfect storytelling.

Fix the reproduced cloud Whisper encoder failure by including the pinned required 128-bin preprocessor configuration and exercising both real encoders before service credentials. Reject unsupported caption density per candidate, checkpoint completed rejections, archive duplicate queue entries, retain permanent identities, and consult legacy history. Existing Auto20/Metricool code, Twitch tasks and the ChatGPT monitor are unchanged.

Validation: full offline suite and both self-tests pass; independent incremental reviews completed; latest GitHub PR checks pass. Real prepare #136 passes both actual CPU speech encoder health checks and is processing media. Public TwitchTracker fetch returned all 50 ranks and matched the saved page. Actual historical bad browser capture and real HUD/caption probes were inspected.

Automatic live publishing remains closed pending the first final-media commissioning. No new public post, successful renewable clock handoff or weeks-long throughput is claimed yet; those are deployment checks, not unit-test results.

author: abhinav-prabhakar
body:
## Summary
Fixes the seven reported UX problems, then redesigns the frontend (typography, layout, theming, and drawn visuals in place of text), adds a no-Docker way to run the whole stack, and installs the `taste-skill` design skills for this project.

**Heads-up for reviewers:** the diff is large (~126 files) because `.claude/skills/` now contains the 14 skills from `Leonxlnx/taste-skill` (copied in, project-only, ~37k lines of markdown/scripts). The application changes are under `frontend/`, `scripts/dev-local.sh`, and the rename touches in docs/services. If you do not want the skills committed, drop `.claude/skills/` and `skills-lock.json` from the PR.

## 1. The seven reported issues
| # | Issue | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hard to type in a single line | The fit-agent brief submits on **Enter** (Shift+Enter = new line, IME-safe). Room size fields are wider, select their text on focus, accept `3,5`. |
| 2 | Photo drag-and-drop not working | One shared `ui/photo-dropzone.tsx` replaces three copies (fit agent, single-piece simulator, product page). Drag state is counted (child elements no longer cancel the drop), a page-level guard stops a near-miss opening the image in the browser, it works by keyboard, and bad files show an error (non-image, over 12 MB). |
| 3 | Nothing simulated shown while processing | The live `SimulatingRoom` view now also shows on the main fit agent while it measures candidates (it previously existed only on the single-piece pages). Also fixed: the single-piece simulator never created an `AbortController`, so cancel did nothing. |
| 4 | Repo is "Before You Buy", site said "Buy You Before" | The UI already said "Before You Buy"; the reversed name was in the README, FastAPI service titles, pyproject/lock descriptions, MCP connector name and instructions, evals fixtures and `submission/` docs. All renamed. Also fixed a doubled tab title (`Store · Before You Buy · Before You Buy`). |
| 5 | Wrong input gave no error | `lib/validate.ts` (+ tests) validates room sizes (1–30 m, height 1.8–6 m), product links (http/https) and photos. Errors appear under the field and block submit. Before, a bad value was silently replaced by 4 × 3.5 × 2.4 m. The store's room bar blocks the sweep until valid. |
| 6 | Verdict was a small badge | `VerdictBanner` in the fit result: large icon + serif headline + tightest gap. Product cards show the engine's verdict as a full-width bar under the photo. |
| 7 | Theme | Real light / dark / system toggle in the nav (persisted, no flash on load via an inline boot script). Hardcoded `zinc/white/black` classes in the store, nav, cards, product detail and simulator were replaced with theme tokens. The 3D viewport and blueprint panels stay dark in both themes. |

## 2. Design pass (frontend)
- **Type:** Fraunces (roman, never italic) for headings, wordmark, verdicts and card titles; Geist body; Geist Mono only for copyable values (SKU, URL). `text-wrap: balance/pretty`.
- **Nav & footer:** masthead nav (wordmark + underlined current page + theme toggle + bag); the sparkle "AI First" pill and "Spatial AI Online" ticker are gone. New footer, skip-to-content link and a branded 404 page.
- **Hero (`/store`):** flat, no glow or gradient; two columns with an animated, themed floor-plan illustration (`hero-plan.tsx`, labelled as an illustration; sofa settles in, walkway flows, reduced-motion safe). The duplicate "Collections" pill row was removed.
- **Flat surfaces:** cards lose shadows and big radii (radius token 0.78 → 0.5 rem); icons removed from card titles; glows, blurs and nested boxes removed from the simulator, product page and workspace lists. Faint grain overlay on the body.
- **Product cards** are catalogue entries: photo → engine verdict bar → name/price → visuals → add to bag; "Schematic/Photo" toggle is a text link. Category index is a text-and-isometric-glyph index instead of icon tiles. Sticky room bar is a single row; the sweep note moved out of it.
- **Other pages:** workspace and fit-agent headers in the new voice; bag drawer heading; skeleton loader while the shop opens.

## 3. Text → drawn visuals (`components/visuals.tsx`)
- `FootprintPlan` – the piece drawn **to scale in the shopper's room** (door swing, gaps each side, tinted by verdict) replaces "180 × 89 cm" on cards.
- `StockDots` – dots for available vs held units replace "3 left · 2 held"; made-to-order shows a dashed marker.
- `LeadBar` – lead time on a 30-day track replaces "18 days · pallet freight".
- `PriceBand` – three coins for the € tier; `PriceSplit` – cost/margin stacked bar.
- `SpecFigure` – dimensioned plan + elevation (width/depth/height, clearance buffer) replaces the spec table on the product page.
- `Meter` – floor taken, usable floor and tightest gap (with the 0.60 m line) replace the four-number grid in the fit result.
All visuals carry `role="img"` + `aria-label` with the underlying numbers.

## 3b. Visual pass on every page beyond the shop
- **Fit agent run trace** is a timeline: one node per step on a rail, a bar as long as the step took (ms shown), parallel/skipped steps marked. The cost strip is four stat tiles (time, fits, model calls, passes).
- **Tested-against-this-room** attempts are cards with a verdict dot, price-tier coins, a floor-taken meter and a walkway meter with the 0.60 m line.
- **Delivery path** is a route (Door → Walkways → Margin), each stop lit by the fit report; original sentences are kept as short notes.
- **Fit-agent page** opens with a four-step flow diagram (reads → shortlists → fits → recommends); confidence is a meter instead of "confidence 82 %"; long card descriptions trimmed.
- **Returns calculator**: percentage fields are sliders, average-order is three price-tier coins, results are an orders → returned → because-of-fit → prevented funnel plus four stat tiles (all numbers still come from `returns_estimate`).
- **Agent surface**: a three-doors diagram (MCP / REST / this page) and icon tool tiles.
- **Holds & order drafts**: product thumbnails, status steppers (known statuses only; unknown ones print as text), cost/margin split bar; icon empty states keep the "needs the shopper's own yes" explanation.
- **Bag drawer**: photo rows, verdict dot, walkway meter, quantity stepper, lead-time bar; receipt shows the status stepper.
- **3D workspace**: piece list has photo + price-tier coins; empty viewer shows a drawn room.
Tests updated where assertions matched the old text (`fit-agent`, `delivery-path`, `value-panel`, `order-queue`, `reservation-list`).

## 4. Running without Docker
`scripts/dev-local.sh` starts the 7 services + Next.js on the host: SQLite instead of Postgres, direct HTTP instead of Dapr/Redis. First run creates `.venv-local` with `uv` (Python 3.12). Logs in `.local/logs`; Ctrl-C stops everything. Added `.venv-local/`, `.local/`, `.local-run.log`, `.taste-skill/` to `.gitignore`. AMD/vLLM and Evolus are not configured, so those paths use the built-in heuristic fallbacks.

## 5. Skills
`npx skills add Leonxlnx/taste-skill -a claude-code -s '*' --copy` → `.claude/skills/*` and `skills-lock.json`. (An earlier `hallmark` skill and its `design.md` were installed then fully removed.)

## Tests / verification
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; `vitest` 127/127 (new `validate.test.ts`; assertions in `store-grid.test.tsx` and `product-detail.test.tsx` updated to query the new visuals by accessible name; e2e selector for the photo input updated in `e2e/room-photo.spec.ts`).
- ESLint: no new errors over `main`'s baseline (the existing react-hooks errors in `live.ts`, `scene-viewer.tsx`, `store-grid.test.tsx` are untouched).
- Manually checked in a browser with the full local stack running: store, product page (ran a real simulation end to end), fit-agent form validation, light and dark themes.
- **Not done:** Playwright e2e not run; mobile widths were not reviewed after the redesign.

## Known / out of scope
- A simulation on SOFA-301 returned "Fits with room to move" with a tightest gap of 0

author: marco-pedron
body:
Replaces the cluttered "hard" receipt set with 30 simple, generated receipts, and fixes the generic parsing causes they exposed. Prompt untouched.

## What changed
- **Removed** `infra/fixtures/receipts/hard/` and `ai:eval:hard`; references updated (`docs/en/ai-pipeline.md`, `docs/en/development.md`, `eval.ts`, a test comment).
- **New set** `infra/fixtures/receipts/simple/`: `make-images-simple.py` renders 30 receipts (EUR 12, USD 8, VND 10, `random.seed(42)`) in the demo set's style (monospace 28, 800 px, 44 px lines) and writes `expected.json`. The script computes every amount and asserts `q × unit = line`, `items + tax + tip = total`. Split and hostile sentences use `eur-pizzeria-02` (4 items).
- **`pnpm ai:eval:simple`**; `eval.ts` prints `receipts: X/Y passed, mean extraction latency N ms, max N ms` and, for a failing receipt, its OCR rows.
- **Generic fixes in `receipt.ts`** (with unit tests):
  - amounts with OCR spaces around the decimal mark (`6 ,00`, `47 ,  00`), and a lost VND thousands dot (`10  000`);
  - the model's quantity is kept only when the row prints it (`Birra media 5,50` was read as 5 × 1,10);

author: toanmobile
body:
**Trạng thái:** gate `--full --diff origin/main` exit 0 (3/3) ở worktree; principal-code-reviewer không có P0/P1 (3 điểm P3 đã sửa); OCR trên diff cuối 0 lỗi.

### Problem
Ngày 18/10 main local dừng ở 7897399, tức 3 commit của PR #70 (06bb714, 75490e4, 7897399). Còn origin/main có squash 81e6c6e của #70, dựng từ head sau đó là 99114f1.
- Khi finish một worktree không liên quan mà PR của nó đã merge, luật "reset --keep khi gộp main vào origin không thêm gì" từ chối: nội dung của 7897399 khác bản squash cuối nên phép gộp có xung đột.
- finish báo "main local có commit origin chưa có", và main lệch origin mãi.
- Các repo symlink kit vào main checkout (GeelyEx2, …) không nhận được PR merge sau đó (#71).

### Solution
- Thêm `_extras_in_merged_prs`. Nó coi một commit thừa của main là đã tích hợp khi commit đó nằm trong danh sách commit của một PR MERGED vào trunk (không từ fork) và merge commit của PR đó đã có trên origin/<trunk> local.
- Commit được tra bằng `gh pr list --search <sha>`. Một PR phủ cả loạt commit của nó.
- Khi đó `_sync_main_to` reset --keep main về origin, vẫn qua đủ các kiểm tra an toàn cũ: không đang dở thao tác git, index không có gì stage, không có file bị ignore nằm đường.
- Gọi gh sau các kiểm tra rẻ, tối đa 5 × 15 s trong lúc giữ MAIN_LOCK.
- Từ chối như cũ khi gh lỗi, khi thiếu một commit, hay khi base hoặc fork không khớp.
- Đã đo trên GitHub thật: tra 75490e4 trả về #70 với commits [06bb714, 75490e4, 7897399, 99114f1] và mergeCommit 81e6c6e.

### AC + proof
- [x] Main giữ commit gốc của PR đã squash: finish đưa main về đúng origin/main và gỡ worktree (s7, ĐỎ trên code cũ với đúng câu từ chối đo được, XANH sau sửa).
- [x] Một commit thừa không thuộc PR nào: từ chối, main giữ nguyên (s8).
- [x] Merge commit chưa có trên origin local: từ chối (s9).
- [x] PR gộp vào nhánh khác, PR từ fork, gh thoát khác 0: từ chối (s10–s12; đột biến từng điều kiện làm test ĐỎ).
- `universal-agent-devkit/tests/worktree_git/test_worktree_discard.sh`: 71 ✔ / 0 ✖.

### Risk
Thấp, chỉ chạm nhánh đồng bộ sau squash.
- Ngoại lệ có chủ ý (đã ghi vào docstring và AGENTS.md): một commit giữa chừng mà chính PR revert sau đó cũng bị bỏ khỏi main, đúng ý người viết PR. Nó vẫn còn ở `refs/pull/<n>/head` và trong reflog.
- Chưa đo: PR có trên 100 commit thì `commits` của gh có thể thiếu. Trường hợp đó gh không liệt kê đủ nên luật từ chối, tức an toàn.

author: nicolascochin
body:
Ticket Kaneo : CCMM-9 « Outils listes de courses ».

## Contenu

- **`mealie_list_shopping_lists`** et **`mealie_get_shopping_list`** :
  - Une liste se désigne par son nom, sans tenir compte de la casse ni des accents. Si le foyer n'a qu'une liste, le nom est facultatif.
  - Les articles sont numérotés sur toute la liste, articles cochés compris. Ils sont masqués par défaut, mais les numéros ne changent pas.
  - Chaque article indique la ou les recettes dont il vient.
- **`mealie_add_shopping_items`** : aliments et unités résolus par leur nom via le catalogue (`resolveCatalogRefs`), pour que Mealie fusionne avec les articles existants.
  - Une note seule (texte libre) reste possible en dernier recours.
  - Un nom inconnu renvoie une erreur avec des suggestions. La création n'a lieu qu'avec `createMissing`.
  - La réponse indique combien d'articles ont été ajoutés et combien ont été fusionnés avec des articles existants.
- **`mealie_update_shopping_items`** : cocher, décocher, changer la quantité ou la note. Chaque article repart tel que Mealie l'a fourni, seuls ces champs changent.
- **`mealie_remove_shopping_items`** : suppression par numéro (annoté destructif).
- **Recettes** : `mealie_add_recipe_to_shopping_list` et `mealie_remove_recipe_from_shopping_list` passent par les endpoints dédiés de Mealie, qui calcule les articles à partir des ingrédients structurés.
  - On donne un facteur d'échelle, ou un nombre de portions converti selon les portions de la recette. Une erreur explique quoi faire si la recette n'indique pas ses portions.
  - Le retrait enlève toute la recette par défaut.
- **`CLAUDE.md`** : nouvelle section « Particularités de Mealie v3 » avec ce que les tests d'intégration ont révélé (identifiants des étapes, ordre des tags, « cuisinée le » par foyer, import d'URL).
- Les crêpes du Mealie de test sont pour 4 personnes, afin de tester la conversion des portions.

## Vérifications

- `npm run typecheck` et `npm test` (174 tests) passent en local, dont 12 tests des outils qui vérifient chaque écriture envoyée à Mealie.
- Tests d'intégration (job CI `live`) sur une liste créée pour l'occasion puis supprimée :
  - les crêpes pour 6 personnes donnent un facteur 1,5 : 375 g de farine, 6 œufs et 75 cl de lait, liés aux bons aliments ;
  - la farine de deux recettes est fusionnée en un seul article de 625 g, lié aux deux recettes ;
  - retirer la quiche garde la farine des crêpes ;
  - un ajout par nom est fusionné avec l'article existant ;
  - nom inconnu refusé ; cocher, changer une quantité, supprimer.

author: dante-sparras
body:
## Problem

A CI run took 3.5–5 minutes, and the pre-push check took about 64 seconds locally. Most of that was repeated work:
- The lint step built the solution in Release (~73 s). Then `scripts/test.ps1` ran `dotnet test` on each of the five test projects one after another, and each re-checked the build (~59 s).
- Every run installed the .NET SDK again (~31 s) and restored NuGet packages with no cache.
- The checkout fetched every file of every commit (~10 s).

## Change

- **`scripts/test.ps1`** builds the solution once, then runs every test project at the same time with `dotnet test --no-build`. Each project's output is printed whole when it finishes, so the logs don't interleave. Any failing project fails the run.
- **`-NoBuild`** is a new switch that skips that build. `scripts/check.ps1 -Test`, which the pre-push hook runs, passes it after building the solution. So does CI's test step after the lint step.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`:**
  - A blobless checkout (`filter: blob:none`). It keeps every commit and tree that the history and diff steps read, and fetches file contents only for the checked-out commit.
  - The .NET SDK is cached in `C:/dotnet` (`DOTNET_INSTALL_DIR`), keyed on `global.json`. `setup-dotnet` then skips the download.
  - NuGet packages are cached in `C:/nuget` (`NUGET_PACKAGES`), keyed on `global.json`, `nuget.config`, the props files and every `.csproj`.
  - CI also runs on the **push to `main`**. A pull request can only read caches its own branch or the default branch saved, so without this every pull request would start cold. The push run also checks `main` after each merge. It's free now that the repository is public.
  - The test step runs `./scripts/test.ps1 -NoBuild`.
  - `DOTNET_NOLOGO`, `DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT` and `DOTNET_SKIP_FIRST_TIME_EXPERIENCE` are set.
  - `actions/cache` is pinned by SHA (v6.1.0), like the other actions.
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`:** the CI section now says the push to `main` runs CI and that tests run on one build. Only those sentences changed. The maintainer's own uncommitted edits to that file are not part of this PR.

The header of `ci.yml` says it's shared with Winoma and Winshell, so those copies should get the same change.

## Scope and approval

The maintainer asked for CI to be as fast as possible (option A).

## Verification

- The pre-push check (`check.ps1 -Ref HEAD -Test`) on this machine went from **64 s to 31 s**. All five test projects pass.
- A deliberately failing test made `test.ps1` exit 1, with the failing project listed and the others still reported.
- actionlint 1.7.12 (the pinned build, SHA-256 checked) reports no problems in `.github/workflows/*.yml`.
- This PR's own CI run starts with empty caches. The run after the push to `main` saves them, and later pull requests show the full gain.
