author: sftwnd
body:
Implements #148 (milestone 2.1.0). The issue is closed after the merge into `develop`.

## Change

`MatchingTest.testLookupTablesOfThePool` needs a description of the algorithm that nothing else refers to: `newModel` first waits until the garbage collector has collected the description left by the earlier tests. The unit tests run in one JVM, so a test class that kept a model of CRC-32 in a static field and ran before `MatchingTest` made the test call `System.gc()` for 30 seconds and fail with `CRC_32_ISO_HDLC: the unused description has to be collected`, a message that pointed at the library (the experiment is in #148):

- **CRC-32/JAMCRC** instead of CRC-32/ISO-HDLC: `java.util.zip.CRC32` calculates it as well, so the model of the JDK still calculates the data without the lookup tables, and a test is much less likely to keep a model of it; a comment says why;
- **the failure of `newModel` names the cause**: `CRC_32_JAMCRC: the description of the earlier tests has to be collected, no other test may keep a model, a CRC or a checksum of the algorithm, in a static field for example`; the comment of `newModel` explains it;
- no change of the library.

## Compatibility

Tests only.

## Tests

A copy of the branch with a test class run before `MatchingTest` (`-Dtest=<class>,MatchingTest -Dsurefire.runOrder=alphabetical`):

| Test class run first | JDK | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `private static final CrcModel CRC32 = CrcModel.of("CRC-32")` | 25, 8 | pass (`develop`: failure after 30.0 s) |
| `private static final CrcModel JAMCRC = CrcModel.of("CRC-32/JAMCRC")` | 25 | failure after 30.0 s with the new message (`newModel:194`) |

- `./mvnw -B -o clean verify` passes on JDK 25 and 8: 167 unit tests (on JDK 8 the test of `Checksum.update(ByteBuffer)` of Java 9+ is skipped, as before), 25 integration tests of the default execution, 3 `SoftRetentionIT`, 7 `JdkIT`; `testLookupTablesOfThePool` runs on both.
- The workflow `build` of the branch (JDK 8, 11, 17, 21 and 25, the modular jar, SonarCloud) passes on the last commit, 4c29d3c.
- SonarCloud of the last commit: the quality gate passes, 0 issues, 0 security hotspots, coverage 100.0% (0 uncovered lines and conditions).

## What and why

Keyboard users had to Tab through six header stops (logo, Play Online, Play, Rules, Settings, Sign in) before reaching anything on the page, on every page.

Both layouts now render a "Skip to content" link as the first Tab stop. It stays hidden until focused, then shows in the top-left corner. Pressing it moves focus to `<main>` (`id="content"`, `tabIndex={-1}`), so the next Tab is the page's first control. author: filforce95
body:
Fixes #1001. Fixes #1546.

Implements the press-first model @grandixximo proposed in [#1001](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/issues/1001#issuecomment-6184287156). Replaces #1017 and #1059, and covers the case #1299 fixes (several clicks in one slow frame).

## Problem
Clicks were decided when the button came up. egui treats a press that moves more than a few points as a drag, so a click made while the mouse was moving was lost (object picks, the second window corner, CP points) or taken where the hand had got to (points, #835), so MOVE/COPY base points landed off the clicked spot.

## Change
- **A press acts at once, where the button went down**: it places the point (snapped as the cursor would be there), picks the object, or sets a window corner. Every press in the frame's events counts (#815).
- **Drag detection** (`canvas/press.rs`): once the pointer leaves a 6-point tolerance, a 0.25 s timer starts. If the button is still down then, it is a drag and the release closes the window the press opened. Otherwise it was a click and the window waits for the next press. Holding still never makes a drag.
- Grips (no command running), ZOOM Realtime, the Dynamic Input options menu, model tiles and double-clicks keep their release-based clicks.

## Behaviour change to review
A drag that **starts on an object** used to open a window; now the press picks the object and the drag adds nothing. This follows the model, but differs from #63 ("even over an object"). It should be checked against AutoCAD.

## Tests
- `tests/press_first_clicks.rs` (60 fps harness): MOVE base and second point, object pick idle and at "Select objects", both corners of a click-click window, two corners in one frame, CP points (#1546), hold still then release quickly, a real drag. 7 of the 8 fail on main; the drag test guards the unchanged behaviour.
- `canvas/press.rs` unit tests for the detector.
- `rapid_clicks.rs`: a moving click now places the point where the button went down, not where it came up.
- Checked in the running app with a real mouse (xdotool, X11): `ID`, MOVE, COPY, ERASE, window corners and SELECT CP, all clicked while moving.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

body:
## What

Beaten regular trainers come back. From the day after you beat them, each one turns up once a day somewhere in their range and can be battled again. The range is their class group in their region (e.g. Johto Hikers), a kind-of-place group (e.g. Johto caves), or just their home spot when their lines are about that place. Each free spot stands empty on 25% of days (0% for seven trainers whose presence is part of the place).

## Why

Cleared routes stay empty for good today. This is the trainer half of [daily world slots](.product/specs/daily-world-slots.md), after the item half in #161, and makes the open world worth re-exploring.

## Impact

- 659 of 901 ordinary trainers take part daily: 539 in class groups, 22 in place groups, 98 at their home spot. 242 stay out for structural reasons (story flags, ships, Trick House, Pokémon Tower, the Route 25 sequence…), listed with reasons in the generated report.
- A dialogue audit fails the build on any trainer whose line names or points at a place unless it's resolved; about 65 lines got minimal neutral rewording.

author: pranavjayakumar
body:
Closes #68.

## What
- **`/` command menu**: while the input is a bare `/command` (no space yet), a popup of up to 4 rows above the input lists matching commands (exact name, then prefix, then substring) with an argument hint and a one-line description. More matches scroll, with ↑/↓ marks.
- **`@user` / `#channel` completion**: an `@` or `#` word at the cursor gets the same popup. For `@`, members of the current channel come first, then everyone else, then user groups (`@oncall`). For `#`, channels you've joined come first.
- **Keys** (the owner's rules):
  - `↑/↓` and `Ctrl-P/N` move the highlight.
  - `Enter` or `Tab` puts the highlighted item into the input with a trailing space. **It never sends**, even when the text already equals the item. A second `Enter`, with the popup closed, sends as before.
  - `Esc` closes the popup without clearing the input. It stays closed until the next edit, and `Tab` reopens it.
  - `Esc` order: popup first, then the open mic, then the ring, then the usual chain.
- **One table** (`commandTable`, `internal/tui/commands.go`) drives both the menu and `/help`. The `/help` output is unchanged apart from one new key row. A test checks that every row is a command `runCommand` knows.
- Admin-only commands (`/disable`, `/group`) are hidden from non-admins. `/talk`, `/mute` and `/leave-huddle` are hidden in builds without voice; `/huddle` stays because it explains how to get voice.

## Things that don't change
- Normal messages send on the first Enter.
- Pastes and multi-rune bursts never open the popup.
- Cursor moves only hide the popup; they never open it, so ↑/↓ in a multi-line draft keep working.
- `fixed in #12` is not rewritten: substring matches for `@`/`#` need at least two letters and are never digits only.
- The popup does not follow a draft into another channel or thread, and its items are rebuilt when users, groups or channels reload.
- Select mode, the Ctrl-K switcher, `keyName` multi-rune handling and edit mode are all unaffected; `/` while editing a message is plain text.
- Keystrokes only filter a small in-memory slice: groups are cached and channel members are a cached set. Nothing touches the network.

## Tests
`complete_test.go` and `commands_test.go` cover:
- The menu opens, filters, scrolls and ranks results.
- Enter completes, then a second Enter sends or runs, including when the text is an exact command or an exact mention.
- Tab, the arrow keys and Ctrl-N/P.
- Esc closes the popup without clearing the input, and the following Esc behaves as before.
- Pasting `/notify all` runs it on the first Enter, and a pasted message sends on the first Enter.
- `@` and `#` completion: ordering, groups, a word with the cursor inside it, multi-line input, and inside a thread.
- Cursor moves don't open the popup.
- Digits are not completed.
- Switching channels doesn't carry the popup over.
- The Esc order is menu, then mic, then ring.
- Admin commands are hidden.
- Frames fit at 40x12, 20x6, 80x24, 100x14 and 200x60, including with a split thread.

`go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -race -count=1 ./...` all pass.

## Review
I ran tui-reviewer and fixed findings 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 9 in bee3ac7 and 4aa9ed0. Two findings are left for the owner to decide:
- **Exact `@mention` at the end of a message.** It still takes two Enters, which follows the owner's rule as written. A test pins this behaviour.
- **Ranking for `/join #` and `/add @`.** Already-joined channels and existing members still come first in those two commands.

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zwire"} -->
_Requested by **takumi** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01GsXisVr9WC4DUs8zvcYz79?thread=cmsg_01GsXisVr9WC4DUs8zvcYz792hp6rTk3WQZhmiHxJB8ykk)_

Before: a human gate passed only when the user typed a message starting with the bare word `approve` (or `reject`), and the rails were suspended only on `suspend`. The user had to know these words.

After: the agent asks the question as a choice and the user picks one. In Claude Code the agent shows Approve and Reject in an AskUserQuestion dialog, the user taps one, and Claude Code shows them a line confirming the pick. In other agents the agent ends its message with `1. Approve  2. Reject`, and the user replies `1` or `2` (or the name), with an optional note after it. A suspend request works the same way with Suspend and Reject. The free-text phrase matching from this PR's first commit is gone.

The pick still comes only from the user. Chat picks are read only from the user's own prompt. A dialog counts only when its options are exactly the question's choices, and only for the call the pre-tool hook saw without answers (matched by `tool_use_id`). A dialog that carries its own answers is refused, and one that resolved itself while the user was idle does not count. The nested-agent guard refuses prompts that start with a choice (`claude -p 1`, a cron prompt `approve`).

How:
- `lib/reply.mjs` (26 lines): the choices, `pick()`, and the one instruction sentence the agent gets.
- `lib/ask.mjs` and a Claude-only `PostToolUse` hook (matcher `AskUserQuestion`) read the dialog. Codex and Copilot use numbered choices in the chat or MCP elicitation. Copilot gets no answer when it runs Claude's settings.
- The suspend pick stays in `flow.mjs`, so it still works when `lib/` is broken.
- The audit found an existing gap: PowerShell `Start-Process claude -ArgumentList '-p','approve'` and `pwsh -c "claude -p 'approve'"` were let through. `shell.mjs` now reads both.

author: faetschi-bot
body:
## Summary

Collapses the PR-artifact workflow to fewer processes and browser launches. Measured warm-cache wall times on local pages; counts come from the command modules.

- **`diff` captures URL inputs itself** — `--wait`, `--wait-for`, `--element`, `--full-page`, `--header`, `--storage-state`, `--allow-console-error`, `--ignore-console`, `--save-inputs`. Both sides run through the capture pipeline in one process and one browser.
- **`capture --url` is repeatable** with `--name-prefix`: one browser launch writes numbered PNGs and returns `{ ok, captures }`, each with the error gate.
- **`recap` is multi-surface**: `--gfm-out`, `--html-out`, and `--png-filter <types|visuals>`; all outputs share one browser launch, and a filter that matches nothing skips the browser pass with a warning.
- **The cached-asset memo is persisted** (`.verified` sidecar), so the pinned 2.5 MB Mermaid (and highlight) assets are not re-hashed on every run.
- Docs + tests; `0.10.0 → 0.11.0`.

Deferred on purpose: `term` pair mode (no clean flag shape for two commands + outputs) and a pure-Node local diff (needs a PNG codec dependency, explicitly not low-risk).

## Artifact

![visual-shot latency recap](https://github.com/faetschi-bot/faetschi-bot-utils/blob/132d9fdb8dfdf13ccca39479288b5fa9ea50abfd/tmp/images/PRs/visual-shot-latency.png?raw=true)

| Cost | Where | Measured | Improved / saves |
|---|---|---|---|
| UI before/after path | `diff` + `capture` | 3 processes, 3 launches, 3.66 s | 1 process, 1 launch, 0.71 s |
| Before/after pair capture | `capture` | 2 processes, 2 launches | 1 process, 1 launch (`--url` ×2) |
| GFM text + visuals PNG | `recap` | 2 processes, 2 launches, 0.56 s | 1 process, 1 launch, 0.52 s |
| HTML + GFM + PNG | `recap` | 3 processes, 3 launches | 1 run, 1 launch |
| URL diffs | `diff` | viewport/scale only, no error gate | wait/selector/element/full-page/header/state/console gate + saved inputs |
| Asset digest | `shared` | 2.5 MB SHA per process | sidecar memo, ~1.5 ms/run |
| No-match PNG filter | `recap` | browser pass still ran | warning, no browser pass |

Full HTML report: [tmp/images/PRs/visual-shot-latency.html](https://github.com/faetschi-bot/faetschi-bot-utils/blob/132d9fdb8dfdf13ccca39479288b5fa9ea50abfd/tmp/images/PRs/visual-shot-latency.html) · GFM source: [tmp/recap/visual-shot-latency.md](https://github.com/faetschi-bot/faetschi-bot-utils/blob/132d9fdb8dfdf13ccca39479288b5fa9ea50abfd/tmp/recap/visual-shot-latency.md)

## How to verify

```bash
cd visual-shot
npm run check && npm run lint:sh
node --test test/*.mjs          # 152 tests, 0 fail (1 asset-gated skip)

# This artifact was rendered by the new one-run command:
node bin/visual-shot.mjs recap --from ../tmp/recap/visual-shot-latency.json \
  --format html --out /tmp/r.html --gfm-out /tmp/r.md \
  --png --png-out /tmp/r.png --json
```

## Risk and rollback

- Additive CLI surface. Two behavior notes: URL inputs to `diff` now run the capture error gate (a page error fails the diff unless whitelisted), and `capture` with multiple URLs returns `{ ok, captures }` (single-URL JSON unchanged).
- The `.verified` sidecar only memoizes `(size, mtime)` inside the cache dir; a changed file re-hashes, and a failed digest removes it.
- Revert the `0.11.0` bump to stop the release from firing.

author: mmatedavid-crypto
body:
Person review currently pays per mention row, can silently lose writes on role uniqueness conflicts, and can leave the displayed role stale. This makes backlog processing slow and unnecessarily expensive.

This change reviews up to six person–episode pairs per AI call, shares episode context, caches decisions before applying them, and reconciles each pair in one audited transaction. Accepted rows require exact names and source quotes; uncertain results go to review. Human decisions are protected. Run and pair leases prevent overlapping work, and source fingerprints reject stale updates.

Stored daily budgets and visitor-first gates remain in force. Requests cannot increase configured limits. Telemetry cannot undo a pause. Provider errors stop the run without paid retries. Cadence remains unchanged pending a live pilot.

Validation: 20 focused Vitest tests passed; isolated PostgreSQL/WASM tests passed for role conflicts, leases, audit backups, stale-source rejection, cache reuse, manual protection, person filters, pause controls, and privileges. Edge TypeScript bundles successfully. The repository model audit still flags three pre-existing references in bible-prefetch and weekly-editorial-post; this change adds none.

Migration pending: needs Lovable agent to apply via Cloud migration tooling, then deploy person-relevance-judge and run a capped live pilot. No operational records are included.

author: concepteur19
body:
# 009 — Micro-interactions et mini tuto

Rend le site plus vivant sans le ralentir, et apprend au visiteur à s'en servir dès sa première visite. Spec, plan et tâches : `specs/009-micro-interactions/`.

## Ce que voit le visiteur

- **Mini tuto au premier passage** : une bulle en 3 étapes, juste au-dessus des onglets (en haut à droite sur ordinateur) : explorer, ajouter à Mon séjour, recevoir son devis sur WhatsApp. Chaque étape encadre l'élément concerné à l'écran.
  - Sans voile, la page reste utilisable ; « Passer » ou Échap la ferme.
  - Elle ne revient plus sur l'appareil, et ne s'affiche pas si le séjour contient déjà une prestation.
  - Un ajout pendant le tuto mène directement à l'étape 3.
- **« Comment ça marche »** sur l'accueil, entre les univers du Tourisme et les expériences mises en avant.
- **Transitions entre pages** : fondu enchaîné ; la photo d'une carte d'expérience (univers, accueil, suggestions) glisse vers la photo principale de sa fiche ; un trait marque l'onglet actif et glisse d'un onglet à l'autre. Sur un navigateur qui ne les connaît pas (Firefox), la navigation est inchangée.
- **Apparition au défilement** : sections et cartes montent en douceur, en cascade dans les grilles. Le premier écran n'est jamais animé.
- **Survol et appui** : carte soulevée et photo légèrement zoomée (souris seulement), bouton qui s'enfonce, soulignement qui glisse sous les liens du pied de page.
- **Ajout au séjour** : « Ajouté ✓ » un instant, rebond du compteur, notification qui glisse depuis le bas, vibration de 15 ms sur Android.
- **Sélecteurs et Mon séjour** : les chiffres défilent dans le sens du changement ; une ligne retirée se replie.
- **Partager** sur les fiches : menu de partage du téléphone, ou « Lien copié » sur ordinateur.
- **Préchargement** des liens internes visibles, coupé en mode économie de données.

Garde-fous : aucune animation au-delà de 320 ms, cascade complète en 500 ms au plus, aucun écran de chargement. Avec « réduire les animations », plus rien ne bouge. Sans JavaScript, tout le contenu reste visible, sans tuto ni bouton Partager.

## Ce qui change dans le code

- **Tuto** : règles pures et testées à 100 % dans `src/features/guide/guide.ts` (quand l'afficher, étapes, cible à l'écran, mémoire avec repli sur le stockage de session puis la mémoire de page). L'îlot `FirstVisitGuide` est en `client:idle` et ne rend rien côté serveur.
- **Transitions** : CSS seul (`@view-transition` et noms `exp-<id>`, `tab-indicator`, `nav-indicator`), sans routeur côté client.
- **Apparition** : `src/scripts/reveal.ts` (moins de 1 kB). Rien n'est masqué tant que le script n'a pas tourné ; il fait aussi apparaître ce qu'un défilement rapide a sauté.
- **Survol et appui** : utilitaires `lift`, `media-zoom`, `press`, `link-slide` dans `global.css`.
- **Retours d'ajout** : branchés sur l'événement de sélection existant. La vibration part de l'îlot des notifications, présent une fois par page. Les sorties animées attendent `animationend` / `transitionend`, jamais un minuteur qui recopierait une durée.
- **Tokens** : `--duration-stagger`, `--distance-reveal`, `--shadow-lift`, `--z-guide`.
- **Notifications** : l'îlot s'active en 1,5 s au plus (`client:idle` avec délai maximal), pour qu'une confirmation n'attende pas que l'appareil soit inoccupé.
- **Préchargement** : `prefetch` d'Astro (`viewport`), sans dépendance ajoutée.

## Confidentialité

La nouvelle clé de stockage `kibreeze.guide.v1` (« tuto vu ») est déclarée dans la politique de confidentialité, en français et en anglais. C'est un stockage d'interface, sans consentement à recueillir.

## Tests

- Nouveaux : logique du tuto, notification « Lien copié », îlots du tuto et de Partager, retours d'ajout ; de bout en bout, le tuto (`guide.spec.ts`) et les mouvements (`motion.spec.ts`). Ces derniers vérifient : noms de transition uniques sur chaque page, photo partagée entre carte et fiche, rien de masqué dans le premier écran, aucune animation sous « réduire les animations », vibration, préchargement, partage.
- Les tests de bout en bout démarrent avec le tuto « déjà vu » (`tests/e2e/guide-done.json`) ; seuls ceux du tuto partent d'un stockage vide.
- Correctif d'un test instable préexistant : `seedSelection` écrit la sélection depuis `/robots.txt`. Sous charge, un îlot de la première page pouvait purger la sélection avant le rechargement. Avant : 1 échec sur 40 ; après : 100 passages sur 100.

## Vérifications

| Contrôle | Résultat |
|---|---|
| Tests unitaires et de composants | 216 + 58, couverture 100 % |
| Tests de bout en bout | 505 passés, 9 limités à Chromium par construction |
| Liens internes | 3 824, aucun cassé |
| JavaScript par page | 32,9 kB compressés au plus (budget 50 kB) |
| Lighthouse | 90 ou plus partout ; CLS 0,019 au plus, assertion ≤ 0,1 ajoutée |

Avant / après (Lighthouse simulé, médiane de 3 mesures) :

| Page | `main` | Cette branche |
|---|---|---|
| Accueil | LCP 3,01 s | 3,00 s |
| Fiche pirogue | LCP 2,78 s, CLS 0,000 | 2,70 s, CLS 0,001 |
| Village Mayi | LCP 3,38 s, perf 92 | 3,53 s, perf 90–91 |

Préchargement : en 4G lente simulée, une fiche ouverte depuis un univers s'affiche en 373 ms (362 ms sans préchargement). L'objectif de moins d'une seconde est tenu, mais le gain du préchargement n'est pas mesurable avec le serveur de prévisualisation, qui fait revérifier chaque page HTML. À re-mesurer sur l'aperçu Cloudflare de cette PR.

Détails : `specs/009-micro-interactions/quickstart.md`. Captures : `Elements/verification/009-*.png`.

## Reste à faire

- [ ] Les 16 scénarios manuels de `quickstart.md` sur un vrai téléphone (iPhone et Android), dont « réduire les animations »
- [ ] Re-mesure du préchargement sur l'aperçu Cloudflare
- [ ] Relecture des textes anglais (tuto, « Comment ça marche », Partager)

body:
Before: `/ai ダンジョン` のサイズの選択肢は 小 100x100・中 500x500・大 1000x1000・特大 2000x2000 マスでした。中以上は重すぎて実際には使いにくい大きさでした。

After: 選択肢は 小 20x20・中 50x50・大 100x100・巨大 200x200 マスになります。部屋密度カードに出る部屋数の目安もサイズに合わせて変わります (例: 小は 4 / 6 / 7 部屋前後、巨大は 40 / 70 / 100 部屋前後)。野外は 9 地点前後が入るよう、中から選びます。

これまでの「小」と同じ広さは「大」になります。シナリオビルダーの遺跡は 小・中・大 から選べ、既定は中 (50x50) です。注意: 以前「小」で保存した遺跡の下書きは、今後 20x20 で構築されます。

## How
- `gm_server/dungeon_scene.py`
  - `SIZE_PRESETS` を 20/50/100/200 に変えました。「特大」は「巨大」に改名しています (値 `dungeon_size:xlarge` はそのまま)。
  - PNG の 1 マスあたりのピクセル数は、小さいマップほど大きくしました (40/20/14/8)。
  - サイズカードは `SIZE_PRESETS` から組み立てます。野外では小を出さず、古いカードから小が届いても中にします (`size_key_for_mode`)。
  - 密度カードは `ROOM_COUNT_HINTS` から部屋数の目安を出します。
- `tools/dungeon_generator.py`
  - 20x20 では部屋が重なり、1 つの大部屋に潰れていました。そこで 60 マス未満のマップでは、部屋の最小辺を 3 マスまで下げ、部屋どうしを 1 マス空けて置くようにしました。
  - 小さいマップは配置の試行回数を増やし、部屋数の下限を 8 から 3 にしました。
  - `generate(min_room_count=...)` で部屋数の下限を指定できます。
  - 100x100 以上の生成結果は変わりません。
  - CLI の `--size` も同じ大きさに合わせました。
- `gm_server/builder.py` / `scripts/builder.js`
  - ビルダーの規模は 小・中・大 から選び、既定は中です。巨大は区画が多すぎるため選べません。
  - 遺跡は入口・最深部と中目標 (最大 3 件) のぶんの区画を、部屋数の下限として確保します。それでも置けなかった中目標があれば、チャットで知らせます。
  - 旅路の地点グラフは `size_key: "large"` にして、これまでどおり 100x100 で生成します (同じ seed で同じ地図になります)。
- 仕様書 (specification / dungeon_generator_spec / scenario_builder_spec) とテストを更新しました。

## テスト
- `python3 -m pytest`: 244 passed
- `npm test`: 104 passed

body:
## 배경 (비용)

AI 호출 비용을 줄이기 위해 사용자 결정(2026-10-18)으로 provider마다 가장 싼 모델 하나만 남긴다. Claude는 비싸므로 사용자가 요청마다 직접 고르는 채팅 기능에서만 허용하고, 워크스페이스 공용 설정에는 쓰지 않는다.

## 정책

| provider | 남긴 모델 | 채팅 질의·Agent | 워크스페이스 `ingest_lint` |
|---|---|---|---|
| openai | `gpt-6-luna` (채팅 기본값 `DEFAULT_MODEL`) | 허용 | 허용 |
| gemini | `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` (워크스페이스 기본값) | 허용 | 허용 |
| claude | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | 허용 | **불가 (400)** |

`ingest_lint`는 ingest, wiki lint/maintenance, 스킬 작성·게시, 회의록, 변환 repair가 함께 쓴다. 전사·TTS·임베딩 모델은 범위 밖이다.

## 변경

- `AiModelCatalog.SUPPORTED_MODELS`를 3개로 줄였다. 뺀 모델 요청은 기존처럼 `400 INVALID_AI_MODEL`("선택할 수 없는 AI 모델입니다."). `GET /api/ai-models`는 3개를 반환한다.
- `AiModelCatalog.resolveForWorkspace` 추가: claude면 `InvalidAiModelException("Claude 모델은 채팅에서 직접 선택할 때만 사용할 수 있습니다.")` → 기존 오류 형식의 400. `PUT /api/workspaces/{id}/ai-model-settings`가 이를 쓴다(access 호출 전 거절).
- `WorkspaceAiModelClient.get` 방어선: access 저장값이 허용 목록(openai·gemini 카탈로그 모델) 밖이면 `gemini/gemini-3.5-flash-lite`로 대체하고 warn 로그를 남긴다. ingest·lint·스킬·회의록·변환 repair와 설정 조회 API 모두 이 경로를 거친다.
- `ai_model_prices` 단가 행은 지우지 않는다(과거 청구 기록용).
- 문서: `docs/api/ai.md`, `api-specs/openapi.yaml`(스냅샷 재생성), `docs/data-model.md`, ADR-0028 후속 결정 절.

## 마이그레이션 규칙 (V79, V68 패턴)

미발행 `ai_command_outbox` payload의 top-level `provider`/`model`을 옮긴다.

| 대상 | 옮길 값 |
|---|---|
| openai, `gpt-6-luna`가 아닌 모델 | `gpt-6-luna` |
| gemini, `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`가 아닌 모델 | `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` |
| claude (아래 예외 제외) | `gemini` / `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` |
| 예외: `kind`가 `query`·`agent`인 `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | 그대로 (채팅에서 직접 고른 허용 모델) |

access `workspaces.ingest_lint_*` 값은 access 마이그레이션이 같은 규칙으로 옮긴다.

## 배포 순서

1. **document (이 PR) 먼저** dev에 머지 — access CI(`scripts/check-ai-model-catalog.py`)가 document dev의 카탈로그와 비교한다.
2. 그다음 **access** 카탈로그 사본·마이그레이션 PR 머지.
3. **ai**(pipeline 기본값·허용 목록)는 document·access와 동시에 배포 가능.

## 테스트

- `AiModelCatalogTest`: 3개만 반환, 뺀 모델 400, Claude Haiku 채팅 허용, `resolveForWorkspace` claude 거절, `isWorkspaceModel`
- `WorkspaceAiModelSettingsControllerTest`: claude 저장 시 `InvalidAiModelException`(400)·access 미호출, 뺀 모델 거절
- `WorkspaceAiModelClientTest`: claude·뺀 모델 저장값 → `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` 대체
- `V79ReplaceNonCheapModelOutboxSnapshotsTest`(Testcontainers): V78까지 migrate → 행 삽입 → V79 적용 결과 확인
- `AiModelCatalogPriceIntegrationTest`, `AgentTurnServiceTest`, `QueryControllerTest`, `DocumentApplicationTests`(OpenAPI 스냅샷), `scripts/test_ai_price_drift.py` 통과
- 전체 스위트는 로컬 colima 메모리 제약으로 돌리지 않았다 → CI 확인 필요

author: hyasin270
body:
## What it adds

A content security policy for the child pages the portal draws itself, **report-only** for now: nothing is blocked, the browser only reports what the policy would have stopped.

- **Pages:** the hub `/h/<link>` (plain and streamed), the quiz `/q/<code>` (plain, streamed, its class and schools views), the challenge `/c/<link>`, the finish card `/k/<link>`, the class link `/j/<code>`, the join page `/quiz/join/<link>`, and the closed pages these routes answer with.
- **Headers on those pages:** `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
  - Note for turning it on: `nosniff` is **not** report-only. Browsers enforce it from the first ON request. On these HTML documents it changes nothing the child sees (the ON rows check the body equals OFF), but it is the one enforcing header this switch sends.
- **Scripts:** this site's files only. The constant inline scripts are allowed by their sha256: the streamed quiz's ask-again line, the join page's early tap, and the designed wait's script, hashed from the module's own text. The streamed page's fixes line depends on the bot's answer, so it gets a fresh nonce per request. No `'unsafe-inline'` and no `'unsafe-eval'` for scripts.
- **Other directives:** `connect-src 'self'`, `object-src 'none'`, `base-uri 'none'` and `frame-ancestors 'none'`.
- **Report endpoint, `POST /api/wq/csp-report`:**
  - The body is capped at 8 kB. A larger body is read as nothing.
  - 120 reports a minute per address. The next one gets a 429 and is not logged.
  - Each report logs one line holding only the directive, the blocked origin (or its keyword: `inline`, `eval`, `data`, …) and the script's `file:line`. A report from an inline script logs `page:<line>`.
  - The page address is never logged. A child's link carries their token, so `document-uri`, paths, queries, the referrer and script samples are all dropped.
- **Known report sources as data:** `dashboard/tests/fixtures/child-csp-known.json` lists the sources the child scripts hold today, as (directive, file, text, count). These are the inline `onerror=`/`onload=` handlers, the recording upload to its signed address and the `no-cors` clip warm-up. A test scans `public/wq/*.js` and must match the list exactly, so a new inline handler, a new cross-origin upload or a new warm-up goes red until it is listed. The list may only shrink: it has fixed ceilings, and it is also checked against the merge-base with `sandbox`.
- **Page CSP ratchet (tests only, no switch):** `dashboard/tests/page-csp-ratchet.service.test.js`
  - **Route census:** every GET route of the child and teacher page routers is listed as report-only, meta or none. The documents with no policy (8 today) may only shrink, and a new page route must be listed.
  - **Header half:** the report-only pages are driven through the real routers, switch on and off.
  - **Meta half, for every variant of every page that builds a policy** (teacher home, maker with each addon combination, the role/pick/message pages, and the portal's own error pages on the wire):
    - script-src and style-src are the same in the header and the `<meta>`;
    - every inline script's and style's sha256 is in both;
    - the meta is the header minus `frame-ancestors`, and nothing else differs.
  - An unknown builder, option key, script/hash constant, addon, or file that sets the header is a red row that names it.
  - **Relay census:** a route that relays a bot page raw must carry the bot's security headers before the send (order, not presence). Today's 5 relays that do not carry yet are listed, and that list may only shrink.

## The switch

`app_settings` key `web_quiz_child_csp`, **default OFF**.

- It is ON only for the JSON boolean `true`. The string `'true'`, `'"true"'`, `1`, `{}`, `false`, no row, a read error and a thrown read are all OFF (one test row each).
- **It adds no settings read of its own.** The web quiz's switch reader (`web-quiz-brotli-flag.js`) now reads `web_quiz_brotli`, `quiz_edge_security_headers` and `web_quiz_child_csp` together, in one `app_settings` query (`.in('key', …)`) on its one 30 s cache. Each switch takes its own row's value. Never per request.
  - With the switch OFF, one hub page makes exactly **1** settings read, the same as before this PR (it was 2 with a separate reader). Ten child pages and a join page within 30 s still make 1.
  - `web_quiz_brotli` answers exactly as before. `createBrotliFlag({ key })` keeps its single-key read.
- **OFF:** every page's status, headers and bytes equal a golden recorded on the base, and the report path answers today's 404 JSON. The golden was recorded twice on the base with identical results, and the committed file is that recording.

## Evidence

- **Red, with the tests at the head and the four changed route files at the base:**
  `Tests:       40 failed, 96 passed, 136 total`. Every ON header row, the nonce rows, the page-run row, every report-endpoint row and the ratchet's header rows fail. The OFF and string-OFF rows pass on the base, as they must.
- **Mutations, each red on its own row:**
  - logging `document-uri` → the token row (2 failed);
  - removing the per-address limit → the 120-a-minute row (1 failed);
  - an `onclick=` added to `hub.js` → the known-list row (1 failed);
  - the designed wait's hash dropped → the wait and page-run rows (2 failed);
  - the maker's meta missing an addon's hash → the meta = header row (1 failed);
  - the full blocked URL logged instead of its origin → the token row (2 failed).
- **Green, head:** `Tests:       136 passed, 136 total` (`Test Suites: 3 passed, 3 total`).
- **One settings read** (`dashboard/tests/child-csp-reads.service.test.js`, 9 rows, real routers over a fake database that counts reads):
  - base: `Tests:       3 failed, 6 passed, 9 total`. The count is 1 there; the rows fail only because the base asks for one key.
  - the previous commit (separate reader): `Tests:       9 failed, 9 total`, with `Expected: 1` / `Received: 2` reads.
  - head: `Tests:       9 passed, 9 total`.
  - Mutation, the switch given its own reader again: `Tests:       8 failed, 1 passed, 9 total` (`Received: 2`).
- **Brotli suite** (`web-quiz-static-br.service.test.js`, unchanged file): `Tests:       64 passed, 64 total` before and after.
- **CSP suites + reads + brotli at head:** `Tests:       209 passed, 209 total` (`Test Suites: 5 passed, 5 total`). The OFF golden is unchanged (same sha256 as before).
- **Affected dashboard suites** (every suite that loads a changed router or the switch reader): head `Test Suites: 65 passed, 65 total` / `Tests:       1395 passed, 1395 total`; previous commit `Test Suites: 64 passed, 64 total` / `Tests:       1386 passed, 1386 total` (+9 = the new reads suite).
- **Shifted clocks:** the changed tests run with the clock moved +5 days and +400 days, `136 passed` both times; the reads and brotli suites `73 passed` both times.
- **Setup suites, head vs base:** circular-deps, unresolved-requires, column-completeness, table-usage-conformance, phone-shaped-fixtures, virtual-mock-of-existing-module, env-template-completeness and source-hygiene give identical counts and identical failing items on both sides: 0 new.
- `node --check` passes on every changed file and on the bot's entry points.

## Overlap with #2799 (edge security headers)

- **Text:** `web-quiz-brotli-flag.js` now conflicts with #2799 (that PR adds only the `key` option, which this file keeps). Whichever lands second takes this PR's version of the file and points `quiz_edge_security_headers` at the grouped read (`settingOn(KEY)` instead of its own `createBrotliFlag`), so that switch adds no read of its own either. Every other file merges cleanly.
- **Two header values:** this cannot happen. #2799 carries the bot's `Content-Security-Policy` on the raw relays (teacher home, maker, role page, report, stories). This PR sets `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` only on pages the portal draws from the bot's JSON. The t

body:
## What changed

- `bridge::remove_socket` removes the bridge socket only when this daemon bound it: the daemon records the socket file's device and inode right after binding, and on exit removes the path only if it still points at that file.
- Every kriyon-ptyd test that spawns a daemon now removes `KRIYON_BRIDGE_SOCKET` from its environment, as `stop_ends_the_whole_tree` already did.

## Why

A daemon removed whatever path `KRIYON_BRIDGE_SOCKET` named when it ended. Run `pnpm check` from inside a Kriyon session and the test daemons inherit that session's bridge path. Each one fails to bind it, because the session's own daemon is serving it, but on exit it still deleted the file. From then on the session's companion posted to a path nothing served: the Structured view stopped updating, and the session's daemon kept listening on a socket nobody could reach until the session was restarted.

Seen on 0.13.0-beta.1 and beta.2: a session's bridge spool stopped at the moment a `pnpm check` ran inside it, and later a test daemon was found serving the session's `.b` path.

## How I tested it

- New test `a_daemon_leaves_a_bridge_socket_it_did_not_bind`: a live listener holds the bridge path, a daemon is started with that path and shut down, and the listener must still be reachable. It failed before the fix ("the live bridge socket was removed") and passes now.
- `the_bridge_socket_goes_when_the_daemon_stops` still passes, so a daemon still removes the socket it bound.
- `pnpm check` passes.

A session whose bridge socket was already deleted stays cut off until it is restarted: its daemon survives app updates and never binds the path again. This change stops the deletion; it does not repair a session already hit.

## Checklist

- [x] The PR targets `dev`.
- [x] I wrote or updated tests, and `pnpm check` passes.
- [x] I read and tested every line, and I can explain it in review.
- [x] AI tools wrote most of this change. (Tick if true. See [Using AI tools](https://github.com/LeafyCode/kriyon/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#using-ai-tools).)

After this is merged, Renovate runs `go mod tidy` after each Go module update, so its update PRs carry a tidied `go.sum`. Before, superseded checksums stayed in `go.sum`, and the lefthook `go-mod-tidy` pre-commit check refused every following commit until someone cleaned them up.

## Cause

`config:recommended` does not enable `gomodTidy`; it is opt-in through `postUpdateOptions`. The cleanup has been needed three times: in 94becc2, in #865 and in #877.

## Changes

- `renovate.json`: `"postUpdateOptions": ["gomodTidy"]`.

body:
Zwei Änderungen am ISBN-Abgleich / an der Bestellliste.

### 1. Bereits bestellte Bände markieren
- Markiert wird nur, wenn genau der aufgeführte Band bestellt ist (`bestellt` = Bände bis + 1). Eine Bestellung eines anderen Bandes zählt nicht, „angekommen“ ebenfalls nicht.
- In der Bestellliste beginnt die Titelzelle mit `[bestellt]`, auch bei den „↳ Sonderausgabe“-Zeilen dieses Titels. Dadurch ist die Markierung auch in der kopierten Markdown-Liste erkennbar.
- Im Fenster ist `[bestellt]` hellblau hinterlegt (gleicher Farbton wie die Markierung „bestellt“, `colors.BESTELLT_COLOR`), dazu kommt ein hellblauer Balken am Zeilenanfang. Gold (Sonderausgabe) und Rosa (Fallback-Link) der Zeile bleiben erhalten, die Spalten bleiben bündig.
- Neuer Eintrag in der Legende. Die Zusammenfassung oben bleibt unmarkiert.

### 2. Monat und Jahr mit Pfeilen nach oben/unten (wie in V1)
- In der Auswahl sind Monat und Jahr Zahlenfelder mit ▲/▼ (neue Klasse `SpinBox` in `ui/isbn_dialogs.py`) statt Auswahlliste bzw. reinem Textfeld.
- Eintippen geht weiterhin. Die Pfeile ändern um 1 und bleiben in den Grenzen von V1 (Monat 1–12, Jahr 1900–2100). Bei „TBA“/„NA“ sind sie ausgegraut.

**Geprüft:** `ruff check .`, `pytest` (436 bestanden), beide Fenster in der Web-Vorschau ausprobiert (Pfeile, Grenzen, Ausgrauen, Rückgabewert beim Start). Mit echten Daten im Programm noch nicht getestet.

author: ksomang
body:
## 📌 한 줄 요약

**문제:** System Call에 잘못된 포인터를 넘기면 커널이 그 주소를 읽다가 PANIC
**해결:** 사용자 포인터 검증 함수(주소/버퍼/문자열)를 만들어 write/create에서 접근 전에 검사하고, create와 파일 시스템 전역 lock 추가

## ❓ 리뷰어 결정 필요
- 질문: 버퍼와 문자열을 **페이지 단위로** 검사하는 방식으로 구현했는데 괜찮을지 봐주세요.
  - `pml4_get_page`는 페이지 단위로 매핑을 확인하기 때문에, 같은 페이지 안의 주소는 검사 결과가 항상 같습니다.
  - 그래서 `check_buffer`는 버퍼가 걸친 페이지마다 한 번씩만 `check_address`를 부르고,
    `check_string`은 첫 글자와 새 페이지에 들어설 때(`pg_ofs (p) == 0`)만 검사합니다.
  - 예: `write (1, buf, 10000)`이면 1바이트씩은 10,000번, 페이지 단위는 3~4번 검사합니다.
  - page fault에서 접근 전에 처리 및 검사하는 것은 그대로이고 검사를 **몇 번 부르는지만** 다릅니다. 검사 횟수가 적으므로 시간 복잡도 측면에서 더 좋다고 생각하고 해당 방식을 사용해 구현했습니다.
- 선택지: A) 페이지 단위 (현재 코드) / B) 1바이트씩 검사
- **작성자 추천:** A (같은 결과를 훨씬 적은 횟수로 얻고, `create-bound`처럼 페이지 경계를 넘는 경우도 새 페이지마다 검사해서 놓치지 않기 때문)

## 🔄 전/후 흐름
- 전: `write (1, NULL, 10)` → `putbuf`가 NULL을 읽음 → 커널 모드 page fault → PANIC
  `create (NULL, 0)` → `case`가 없어 `default`에서 우연히 `exit(-1)` (검사 없이 통과한 상태)
- 후: `write`/`create` → `check_buffer`/`check_string` → `check_address`가 NULL/커널 주소/매핑 안 된 주소를 발견 → `exit(-1)`

## ✨ 변경 사항
- 검증 방식은 Introduction 문서 공부 중에 중요하게 짚고 넘어간 부분(`is_user_vaddr` → `pml4_get_page` 순서 (커널 주소가 `pml4_get_page`의 ASSERT에 걸리지 않게)과 이전 머지에서 합의한 접근 전에 검사하는 방식을 사용했습니다.
- `check_address`: 주소 하나 검사. 실패하면 `exit_status = -1` → `thread_exit`
- `check_buffer`: 버퍼가 걸친 페이지마다 한 번씩 검사 (같은 페이지 안의 주소는 결과가 같으므로)
- `check_string`: `'\0'`까지 따라가며 첫 글자와 새 페이지에 들어설 때만 검사. 검사 후에 읽어서 검사 전 접근이 없음
- `write`: fd와 상관없이 `putbuf` 전에 `check_buffer` (나중에 파일 쓰기도 같은 버퍼를 읽으므로)
- `create`: 검사 → lock → `filesys_create` → unlock → `rax`
  - 검사를 lock 전에 둔 이유: lock을 쥔 채 `exit`하면 lock이 영원히 안 풀림
  - 결과를 변수에 받고 unlock 후 `rax`에 넣어 lock 구간을 파일 시스템 호출로만 한정
- `filesys_lock`: 파일 시스템은 동기화가 안 되어 있어 전역 lock 하나로 보호. lock 대기 시 Threads 주차 donation이 동작
- TODO: Project 3 lazy loading 때를 대비한 주석을 적어두었습니다.
- `remove`는 테스트가 없어 `open`/`close` 때 함께 구현하면 될 것 같습니다.

## 🧪 테스트
- create-normal, create-empty, create-null, create-bad-ptr, create-long, create-exists, create-bound: PASS
- 회귀: args-none, args-single, args-multiple, args-many, args-dbl-space, halt, exit, bad-read: PASS
- 관련 이슈: #

<details>
<summary>📄 테스트·빌드 로그</summary>

```
pass tests/userprog/create-normal
pass tests/userprog/create-empty
pass tests/userprog/create-null
pass tests/userprog/create-bad-ptr
pass tests/userprog/create-long
pass tests/userprog/create-exists
pass tests/userprog/create-bound
```

author: aydosman
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:
The gateway-helm chart only creates one ClusterRole for the Envoy Gateway controller and binds it solely to the controller service account. There is no built in way for a cluster operator to grant a human user or group read only or read/write access to Gateway API resources (gateways, httproutes, grpcroutes, referencegrants, tcproutes, tlsroutes, udproutes, gatewayclasses, backendtlspolicies) or Envoy Gateway resources (clienttrafficpolicies, backendtrafficpolicies, securitypolicies, envoypatchpolicies, envoyproxies, envoyextensionpolicies, backends, httproutefilters, listenersets) without hand writing and maintaining custom RBAC outside the chart.

This PR adds a `rbac.aggregatedClusterRoles.enabled` flag to the chart. When enabled, it creates `view`, `edit` and `admin` ClusterRoles that use the standard Kubernetes aggregation labels (`rbac.authorization.k8s.io/aggregate-to-view`, `-edit`, `-admin`), so they aggregate into the cluster's built in `view`, `edit` and `admin` ClusterRoles automatically. `view` grants read only access, `edit` grants read and write access, and `admin` grants the same permissions as `edit` for these resource types.

The flag defaults to `false`, so existing deployments are unaffected. A golden file test (`test/helm/gateway-helm/rbac-aggregated-clusterroles.in.yaml` / `.out.yaml`) covers the enabled case.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #9750

author: bitmapasset
body:
CI/CD hardening wave (bg75): post-deploy production smoke, gated production database migrations, npm release provenance, and CI cache/concurrency/timeout hygiene. Every change is under `.github/`, `RELEASING.md`, `docs/RUNBOOK-CICD.md` and `.gitignore`.

## Commits

| Commit | What / why |
|---|---|
| ci: cancel stale runs on PRs only, add 15-minute job timeouts | A new PR push cancels its stale run; main runs are kept. 15-minute job timeouts instead of GitHub's 360. |
| ci: add a workflows job that runs actionlint + shellcheck | New `workflows` CI job lints every workflow and the scripts they call (pinned actionlint image). |
| ci: post-deploy production smoke test on every Vercel production deploy | `post-deploy-smoke.yml` probes 13 production routes/APIs after each `Production – app` success and opens/closes an issue on failure. |
| ci: gated production migrations via a production-db environment | `migrate-production.yml`: manual, main-only, behind a `production-db` environment with a required reviewer; a preflight refuses to run if the environment is missing or unprotected. |
| release: publish the CLI too, fix the trusted-publishing runtime, add GitHub Releases | `release.yml` on `v*` tags: Node 24 + npm 11 for OIDC trusted publishing with provenance, publishes connect, mcp and the CLI, then creates the GitHub Release. |
| docs: CodeQL default setup via one API call (no codeql.yml) | Runbook step to turn on CodeQL default setup instead of maintaining a workflow file. |
| deps: cover packages/bitmap-resolver in Dependabot | The resolver package gets dependency updates like the others. |
| docs: proposed required-checks list (every ci.yml job), applied after merge | Runbook section with the exact PATCH that makes all 12 CI jobs required on main. |
| ci: pin every action to a full commit SHA | checkout, setup-node and gitleaks-action pinned to verified SHAs. |

## Review fixes (separate commits, from the bg75 review)

| Finding | Fix |
|---|---|
| M1 | `migrate-status.sh` classified a diverged migration history as "pending" (exit 10), so mode `deploy` would have run `migrate deploy` on a mismatched database. Pending now requires Prisma's `Following migration(s) have not yet been applied` header and no `are different` / `not found locally`; everything else exits 1. Tested with stubbed outputs: up to date 0, pending 10, diverged 1 (was 10), unreachable 1. |
| m5 | Removed the bare `drift` grep and the header claim; `prisma migrate status` does not check schema drift (the CI `migrations` job does). |
| M2 | RELEASING.md: a new npm trusted publisher expires if its first publish is not within 2 days, so set it up in the same sitting as the first `v*` release and check the Provenance badge. |
| m2 | `migrate-production.yml`: the production DB variables now live only on the mask / status / migrate deploy steps, not job-wide, so `npm ci` install scripts cannot read them; removed the npm cache from that job. |
| m3 | Preflight job grants `actions: read` (with `contents: read`) and prints the real `gh api` error instead of assuming 404. |
| m1 | CI concurrency groups main pushes by commit sha, so a pending main run is never cancelled by a newer merge. PRs still cancel stale runs. |
| n1, n5 | `smoke-report.md` gitignored; runbook says to copy the exact `DATABASE_POSTGRES_URL_NON_POOLING` value from Vercel instead of showing a host pattern. |

## Scope

No `app/` change. No settings are changed by this PR. The `production-db` environment and its `DATABASE_URL` secret, and the npm trusted publishers, are manual follow-ups per `docs/RUNBOOK-CICD.md` / `RELEASING.md`.

Local gates on the head commit: actionlint 0 errors, shellcheck clean, all workflows + dependabot.yml parse, `prisma generate` + `tsc --noEmit` + `npm run lint` (0 errors) in `app/`.

## Post-merge plan

1. Wait for the push-to-main CI run on the merge commit to be green with all 12 jobs.
2. Turn on CodeQL default setup (`PATCH code-scanning/default-setup state=configured`).
3. Make every ci.yml job a required status check on main (strict, 12 contexts: sdk, mcp, resolver, cli, typecheck, app, migrations, lint, example, build, secrets, workflows), using the PATCH in the runbook. The previous list is recorded first for rollback.

author: kyle-sexton
body:
No related issue: owner-approved self-healing triage sweep

## Summary

Adds an hourly `triage-sweep` job to `maintenance-audit-lane-runs.yml`. It finds open issues that intake triage never reached and dispatches `intake-triage.yml` for them, using only the job's `GITHUB_TOKEN`. It spends no lanes App token.

## Fix

- **Schedule.** A second cron (`17 * * * *`) runs only `triage-sweep`. The daily cron and manual runs run all four jobs. The hourly run has its own workflow concurrency group, so it never waits behind the daily audit. The job also has its own concurrency group, so two passes never overlap.
- **Selection** (`triage-sweep.mjs`). An issue qualifies when all of these hold:
  - no `<!-- claude-lane intake-triage -->` comment from `github-actions[bot]`;
  - no label matching `needs-triage`, `needs-human`, `needs-spec`, `agent-ready`, `status: *`, `priority: *` or `work-class: *`;
  - it is not a pull request;
  - its body does not end with the born-triaged marker;
  - it is over an hour old;
  - its author is a listed human or the lanes App.
- **Dispatch.** At most 5 per pass, oldest first. Each dispatch's run id (from the 200 response) goes into one hidden-marker state comment on the issue, and later dispatches edit that same comment.
- **Give-up.** Once 2 dispatched runs have completed and the issue is still untriaged, the sweep files one `needs-triage` issue that names the issue and both runs. It then marks the state comment and labels the original `needs-triage`, and dispatches it no more.
- **Security review fixes** (review:security-reviewer, opus):
  - `github-actions[bot]`-authored issues are left out, because lane-sweep findings can quote log lines a fork controls.
  - An issue with more than 300 comments, where the state comment could be hidden, is labeled `needs-triage` and not dispatched.
  - Labeling the original issue on give-up stops it from crowding out newer candidates.
  - The pass stops before any dispatch or filing that the remaining call budget cannot record.
- **Accepted exposure.** Intake reads issue comments, and anyone can comment during the hour before the sweep dispatches. Intake treats comments as untrusted data, applies only allowlisted labels and never applies `agent-ready`. This is recorded in the script header.

Tokens: the sweep uses `GITHUB_TOKEN` only (`actions: write`, `contents: read`, `issues: write`). The dispatched intake run uses its own `GITHUB_TOKEN` plus `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, and its actor `github-actions[bot]` (41898282) is in intake's bot list (`.github/workflows/intake-triage.yml`, "Compose the bot id list").

API cost per pass, against the 1,000 requests an hour per repository that `GITHUB_TOKEN` gets:

- Today: about 8 calls (761 open issues and PRs make 8 list pages, and no issue currently qualifies).
- Ceiling: 120 calls, enforced by `CALL_BUDGET`. That covers up to 15 list pages; up to 20 candidates at 3 comment pages plus 1 run read each; 5 dispatches at 2 calls each; and 5 filings at 4 calls each.
- In the 06:xx hour the daily run adds its own budget of 350 + 50 calls.

Stranding: this changes no lane runner. The broker checks a run's caller and reusable files against main only for lanes in `docs/conventions/pr-pipeline.yaml` (azure-iac `src/lanes-token-broker/src/binding.mjs`, `checkBinding`). Those lanes are work-resolve-issue, pr-refine, pr-unblock, pr-merge and work-unblock.

## Verification

- `node --test` in `.github/scripts/maintenance-audit-lane-runs/`: 36 pass, 0 fail. The tests were written first, and the new tests failed before the code existed.
- `actionlint`: clean. `zizmor` 1.30.0 (offline): no findings.
- `scripts/check-affected.sh --tests`: 5 passed, 4 skipped.

Basis: dispatch returns `workflow_run_id` with a 200 status (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflows#create-a-workflow-dispatch-event). `GITHUB_TOKEN` gets 1,000 requests an hour per repository (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api). A `workflow_dispatch` sent with `GITHUB_TOKEN` still creates a run (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/github_token). The intake marker and the routing that drops the floor label come from ci-workflows `intake-triage.yml` at ff8cd36 (the comment-marker and floor steps).

## Related

- #7924 (intake-triage `workflow_dispatch` with `issue-number`)
- #7857 (the daily lane sweep this extends)

author: thpubs
body:
## What changed

`build_turns` no longer shows live rows that fell out of the part of the transcript that was read as if they were still to be written. A live row the transcript doesn't hold is now added after the transcript's turns only when it comes after the last live row the transcript does hold, and when it isn't older than the oldest row read.

## Why

The Structured view reads only the newest 12 MiB of a transcript (`TRANSCRIPT_TAIL` in `structured_cmd.rs`). Once a session's transcript grew past that, the companion's live rows from the session's start were no longer in what was read. They counted as rows the transcript lagged behind on, so they were placed after the newest turn: the view ended on the session's first turns instead of its latest one. Seen on 0.13.0-beta.2 with a 14 MB transcript.

## How I tested it

- `live_rows_older_than_the_transcript_read_are_not_shown_as_newest`: the transcript read starts mid-session, the live rows start earlier. It failed before the fix (the first prompt came after the second) and passes now.
- `live_rows_from_before_the_transcript_read_are_left_out_when_none_overlap`: live rows from an earlier run that share nothing with the transcript read. Failed before, passes now.
- The existing test for rows the transcript hasn't written yet still passes.
- I also ran `build_turns` on the affected session's real 12 MiB tail and live rows (a one-off check, not committed): 17 turns, oldest first, the newest turn last.
- `pnpm check` passes.

- [x] The PR targets `dev`.

PR head: 31d8fc2896fa528ba1268a22b3f870efc16fb3c7

Closes #795

## Summary

Five independent correctness/reliability defects in the optional (default-off)
LLM wiki curator pipeline are fixed: (1) quote verification compared the
quote's numbers against the whole chunk instead of the aligned window, so any
chunk with one extra number failed even a 96.7-scoring match — the fuzzy path
now aligns (`partial_ratio_alignment`, dest-span) and requires the quote's
numeric multiset to be contained in the window's; (2) the prompt schema
requested `entities`/`relations` (never read) and per-claim
`page_title`/`page_type` (zero consumers) — all dropped, ending the wasted
2048-token output budget and the largest post-claims truncation window that
turned a capped reply into a wholesale `json_parse_failed` claim loss;
(3) `active_if_verified` stamped `active` unconditionally (and fabricated
`chunks[0]` provenance for unknown chunk ids) — status is now computed per
candidate: active only when the quote check ran AND passed AND the chunk id
was fed to the curator; unknown-but-tolerated ids stay `needs_review` with
their own cited id; (4) `wiki_llm_curator_max_input_chars` was documented
"per call" but enforced as a per-document span — docstrings/comments across
config.py, wiki_compiler.py, and wiki_curator.py now state the two true
scopes (no behavior change); (5) every compile job built its own
`AsyncCircuitBreaker(fail_max=5)` while making at most ~3 calls, so the
breaker could never open — breakers now live in a module-level registry
keyed by (endpoint, model), failures accumulate across jobs, and outage
classification follows the repo's OPS-002 (#494) pattern (only 5xx/429 and
connection/timeout errors count). Every curator run now dispatches through
the single-worker wiki-curator offload executor, so concurrent jobs cannot
drive one breaker from concurrent event loops.

Audit findings closed: T1-35-K-05, TQ-instruction-batch-5-05,
TQ-instruction-batch-5-03 (+ T1-35-K-12), T1-35-K-11, T1-35-S-05 (+
T1-35-S2-05).

## Root Cause

See .agents/issue-traces/795-wiki-curator-quote-gating-breaker/04-root-cause.md
(five RCs at file:line level, all probe-verified at base e43ad1d3): wrong-
scope numeric comparison (wiki_curator.py `_quote_matches`), schema/consumer
drain (prompt requested unread sections whose ordering turned truncation into
total claim loss), verification-gate status assumed from the mode branch
rather than computed per candidate plus the `chunks[0]` fallback, one knob
serving two scopes with the docstring describing the wrong one, and a
persistence-meant breaker rebuilt per call site defeating its own threshold.

## Fix

- `wiki_curator.py`: `_quote_matches` window gate (dest-span alignment +
  multiplicity-sensitive containment; whitespace-only inputs no longer
  verify; `verify_quote` PUT-route consumer inherits); prompt schema drops
  entities/relations/page fields; per-candidate status gating; no
  `chunks[0]` fallback.
- `wiki_curator_client.py`: `_BREAKER_REGISTRY` + `_shared_curator_breaker`
  keyed by (endpoint, model) under a threading lock; `is_outage_status`
  classification (non-outage >=300 raises AFTER `breaker.call`, never
  counting toward fail_max); unused `breaker_name` param dropped (zero
  callers).
- `wiki_compiler.py`: curator runs always dispatch through the single-worker
  `_CURATOR_OFFLOAD_EXECUTOR` (inline `asyncio.run` branch deleted);
  `_build_curator_chunks` comment states the per-document span.
- `config.py`: docstring-only two-scope description.
- Tests: frozen `test_o05_wiki_curator_gates.py` (6 checks, arm's-length
  authored) + non-frozen `test_o05b_curator_gates_unit.py` (20 tests).

## Recurrence Prevention (defect class)

- Defect classes: C16 wrong-scope comparison (incl. the src/dest index and
  whole-chunk-containment variants), C18 docstring-vs-code, C9 flag-gated
  verification with unsafe fallback, C12 per-call rebuild of a
  persistence-meant resource, + cross-event-loop shared asyncio primitives.
- Sweep result: 11 disposition rows, all FIXED or NOT_APPLICABLE with the
  disqualifying property stated (08a-recurrence-sweep.md; predicates and
  counts reproducible verbatim).
- Guardrail: the frozen checks + unit battery; demonstrated to bite by 8/8
  executed mutation probes (M1a src/dest slice, M1b whole-chunk equality,
  M1c whole-chunk containment — the implementation-review round-1
  partial-fix survivor — M2 prompt, M3a status, M3b fallback, M4 docstring,
  M5 breaker), each killing its check, plus the base RED legs.

## Tests

- Frozen acceptance replays (both legs, repro/replay-final.log): 10/10 PASS
  at 31d8fc28 (C1-C6 RED→GREEN with exact frozen signatures; C7-C10
  GREEN→GREEN).
- `cd backend && python -m pytest tests/test_o05_wiki_curator_gates.py tests/test_o05b_curator_gates_unit.py -q -p no:randomly -p no:cacheprovider --basetemp=E:/tmp/...` → 26 passed
- `cd backend && python -m pytest tests/test_wiki_curator.py tests/test_issue515_wiki_curator.py -q ...` → 49 passed
- `cd backend && python -m pytest tests/test_wiki_compiler.py -q -k curator ...` → 13 passed, 17 deselected
- `cd backend && python -m pytest tests/test_settings_ssrf.py -q ...` → 25 passed (SSRF surface untouched)
- Isolation determinism (impl-review round 3): the exact three-file command
  → 71 passed on 9/9 runs across both orders (a double-patch race in the
  new battery's concurrency test was found and fixed before publication).
- `cd backend && python -m ruff check .` → clean; `python scripts/run_bandit.py` → PASS (128, all suppressed, flat);
  `check_settings_consumers.py` OK (258 fields); `check_config_contract.py`
  + `check_runtime_contract.py` pass; `scan-deferred.sh` clean.

## Regression Protection

- New: test_o05_wiki_curator_gates.py (frozen, arm's-length), test_o05b
  battery (window edges incl. quote-at-end and co-occurrence-outside-window
  discriminators, status matrix incl. empty/unknown chunk ids, breaker
  registry keying/OPS-002/concurrent-loops boundary, truncation residual
  pin, prompt page-field omission).
- Adversarial: 8 named mutations, all executed and biting (see above).
- Test drift review: existing curator suites (49 tests) pass unchanged.
  Two pre-existing behavior changes, both intentional: (1) unknown chunk
  under flag-off is now kept needs_review instead of fabricated-active;
  (2) under `active_if_verified` with `require_quote_match=False`, known
  chunks now also yield needs_review (the per-candidate gate requires the
  quote check to have actually run).

## External Checkpoint Anchor

- Receipt published before implementation (human-confirmable; local
  validation cannot attest timing): `issue-tracer-checkpoint-v1 slug=795-wiki-curator-quote-gating-breaker manifest=51acbc8ca4d4d1952e80ca9d7b93c348a22fee73 semantics=7ab19c9de898fab9eebb55ea895372d551933c5f tree=cc6f6489b2f4eac838ed2c271387e3f2108d8016`
- External artifact: https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/ragappv3/issues/795#issuecomment-6246185487
  (created 2026-10-18T05:39:46Z; first implementation commit 06:46:42Z —
  publication precedes implementation by ~67 minutes, independently
  gh-confirmed by the implementation reviewer and the final critic)
- Independent verification: `repro-check.sh verify-anchor --slug 795-wiki-curator-quote-gating-breaker --receipt '<literal>'` → OK (run by both gates)
- Local copy: .agents/issue-traces/795-wiki-curator-quote-gating-breaker/repro/anchor_v1.txt (non-authoritative)

| AC1 quote matches with unrelated number outside window | C1: base RED `assert False is True` (repro/C1.base.log) → head GREEN at 31d8fc28; mutation M1b kills |

author: talstilkol
body:
## Summary

Plan task **0.5: CI stable, retries 0.** Before changing anything I tallied the e2e annotations of the last **202 CI runs (588 e2e jobs)**. Most of the "known flakes" turned out to share **one root cause**, and that cause is fixed in config, not with retries.

**Root cause 1: Vite full-reloads the page in the middle of a test.** Vite's dependency scanner never follows `new Worker(new URL("./x.worker.ts", import.meta.url))`. So `@hpcc-js/wasm/graphviz`, `@ruby/wasm-wasi`, `@bjorn3/browser_wasi_shim`, transformers.js and web-llm were only discovered when a worker first started. Vite then re-optimised them and sent *"optimized dependencies changed. reloading"* to **every open page**. With parallel workers on a cold CI dev server, one graphviz or live-ruby test reloaded the tests running next to it.
- Reproduced locally against a cold server: `dependency optimized: @hpcc-js/wasm/graphviz` → `reloading` → the graphviz test failed. The CSV test's CI call log also shows `navigated to "http://localhost:5173/"` partway through the test.
- How often the other flakes appeared in the same job as a graphviz, live-ruby or CSV flake (base rate 61%, 358 of 588 jobs): template gallery **24/24**, LiveJS-throw **29/30**, ai-cancel **14/14**.
- Fix: `optimizeDeps.entries` now includes `src/**/*.worker.ts`. The cold scan then already contains all 5 worker-only deps.
- Plus `e2e/_warmup.ts` (globalSetup). It walks the module graph from `index.html` over plain HTTP, with no browser, so it works for every project, and compiles about 1040 modules before the first test. Before this, the first test of each worker paid for Vite's first compile and timed out in `beforeEach`. Any late dependency discovery now also happens before a page is open.

**Root cause 2: the command palette reset its query in a late `useEffect`.** The palette stays mounted while closed. The first frame of a reopened palette showed the old query ("Escape during palette typing": received `"Page View"`), and a reset that ran late wiped the first keystrokes ("a version is kept": the palette was unfiltered after `fill`). The reset now happens during the render that opens it. The new unit test fails on the old code.

**Fixes inside the tests**
| test | root cause | fix |
|---|---|---|
| vault zip export | raced a 10 s dialog wait against the download. When the dialog came late, the test stopped looking for it, and the download waited on an unanswered dialog | decide from `showDirectoryPicker` whether the dialog will come; no race |
| template gallery | collateral reload (24/24), plus a loose locator ("Template" also matches every `Templates: …` starter; it took the first non-palette dialog) | the reload is fixed above; it now asserts the option Enter will run and finds the dialog by its accessible name |
| OPFS in WebKit | **not a flake**: Playwright's Linux WebKit has no `navigator.storage.getDirectory`, so it fails every time | the probe moves to `e2e/_opfs.ts`. #217's new `wiki-autocomplete.spec.ts` calls OPFS without it and fails in WebKit every time; it should `test.skip(!(await opfsWritable(page)), …)` |
| CSV / graphviz / mermaid / 100 KB paste | their own waits (beforeEach + 15 s + 15 s) exceed the 30 s test budget by construction | `test.slow()` |
| pwa offline | the last `waitForTimeout(1500)` | wait until every chunk the page loaded is in a cache |

**CI**
- `retries: 0` (CI included).
- `npm run hygiene` now fails on any `waitForTimeout` in `e2e/`.
- The new **`.github/workflows/e2e-flake.yml`** runs nightly at 02:17 UTC and via `workflow_dispatch`. It is a 3-browser matrix running `npm run e2e:flake -- --times 5 --project <browser>`: red on any failure, a per-test table in the job summary, reports kept as an artifact. `e2e:flake` (from T23) gains `--all`, which loops over all 3 projects for local use. The nightly uses a matrix instead, so the browsers run in parallel and each gets its own setup (Xvfb for Firefox).
- Every `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` is now `ubuntu-24.04`, with a comment, because the label moves to Ubuntu 26 on 19.10.2026 (actions/runner-images#14748).

## Verification

| what ran | where | result |
|---|---|---|
| `grep -rn waitForTimeout e2e/` | local | **0** |
| base config, cold dev server, error-paths subset, 3 workers (3 cycles) | local chromium | reload `@hpcc-js/wasm/graphviz` in 2 of 3; graphviz test failed |
| fixed config, cold dev server (5 cycles, incl. error-paths + live-exec + data-safety + galleries + pwa + dynamic-blocks + ai-cancel) | local chromium | **0 reloads** in every cycle; scan includes all 5 worker deps |
| fixed, cold: 7 specs / 40 tests, 2 workers | local chromium | 37 passed, 2 skipped, 1 failed (data-safety beforeEach; the trace shows module requests getting no response for 15 s while the machine was at load 15). Next run 33/33 |
| data-safety + galleries `--repeat-each 3` | local chromium | 33/33 |
| palette tests `--repeat-each 8` | local chromium | 16/16 (the race does not reproduce here; the unit test does) |
| `CommandPalette.test.tsx` + `codeHygiene.test.ts` | vitest | 14/14; the new palette test fails on the old code |
| `tsc --noEmit -p .`, `npm run -s hygiene` | local | clean |
| Firefox / WebKit | — | **CI only**: the browser download is blocked in this sandbox |

## Open items
- ⏳ **3 nights in a row with 0 flakes**: measured after merge. The nightly only runs from the default branch.
- ⏳ CI on this PR with retries off is the first real test on Firefox and WebKit.
- #217 (`wiki-autocomplete.spec.ts`) needs the `opfsWritable` skip on WebKit (see above).

author: adithyakumarcr
body:
## Why
- **The browser saved cookies, logins and cache** (79 MB here), and on a Mac Chromium encrypts saved cookies with the "Kural Safe Storage" keychain item, which asks again after every update of the ad-hoc-signed app. Adithya wants the browser fresh every time.
- **macOS asked about Downloads, Desktop, Apple Music and Photos.** Found in a chat transcript: an Auto chat with no folder open ran `ls -d ~/*/ ~/*/*/` to look for a project, which opens every one of those folders. Auto let it run without asking.

## What changes
- `scripts/rebrand.py` `fresh_browser`: the workbench's `_resolveStorageScope()` always returns `"ephemeral"` (in-memory partition), for user tabs and `vscode.window.openBrowserTab`. A miss gives a `::warning::`; `package.json` sets `workbench.browser.dataStorage: "ephemeral"` as the fallback. `lib/browser/fresh.js` deletes `<user data>/Partitions/vscode-browser` and `workspaceStorage/*/browserStorage` once at start (only real folders, never a link's target).
- `lib/paths.js` `privateUse` / `privateFolder` + `decide({ privateFolders })` (Mac only): a command, Read/Glob/Grep/Write or upload into those folders, a wildcard in home, a walker (`find`, `rg`, `du`, `ls -R`…) over home or above, or a command started in one, gets a card **before the Auto shortcut**, with no "Allow all"; switching to Auto mid-answer doesn't answer it. Attached files and project roots (a project in ~/Documents) don't ask. `FORMAT` in `prompts.js` tells every mode not to look there.
- Limitation: Codex runs its own "safe" read-only commands (`ls`, `cat`…) without asking Kural, so only the instructions apply to those.
- README: two ways to install (`install.sh`, or the .dmg/.exe/.deb with the operating systems' warnings and permission questions); README, wiki and `guide.js` updated for both changes; the stale Pillow note for the Mac build fixed.
- Version `1.1.0-rc.4`; the "Not released yet" notes become its "What's new" block.

## Tests
- `npm test`: all 108 test files pass on macOS.
- New `test/private-folders.test.js` (every mode, attached files, a project in Documents, the chat's card handling) and `test/rebrand-fresh-browser.test.js` (stand-in, the real installed workbench file patched once and passing `node --check`, the cleanup).
- `test/permissions.test.js` pins `privateFolders: false`, so its table is the same on every system.
- Not checked live: a full `./install.sh` build started with the patch (Adithya is doing a fresh install next), and whether a Mac keychain prompt ever comes from the in-memory browser.

After merging: `git tag v1.1.0-rc.4 && git push origin v1.1.0-rc.4` on `main`.

author: techgopal
body:
## P2-T117: `FileFormat` trait, I/O layer and conformance suite

One trait that every file format implements once, plus the framework pieces around it (`krishiv-io`), and a generic conformance suite (`krishiv-testkit`) that the Parquet reader/writer and later formats must pass. Decisions: ADR 0014 (update 2026-10-18), P2-T117 design note.

### `krishiv-io`
- **`FileFormat`**: `read_metadata` (cached), `plan_units` (stage-1 statistics pruning, no I/O, midpoint rule), `open` → sans-IO **`Decoder`** (`step` → `NeedData(ranges)` / `Batch` / `Done`), `writer` → sans-IO **`Encoder`**. Async read-at libraries fit through `AsyncDecoder` over `PushReadAt`, so their reads also go through the scheduler. `FormatError` gets the redacted path from the framework. Public types are `#[non_exhaustive]` with constructors (unstable until a second columnar format).
- **`ScanRequest`**: nested projection, typed `PushdownExpr` (with collations), dynamic filters, `RowSelection`, `RowFilterPolicy`, limit, `_metadata` columns, field mapping. **Statistics** with exact/inexact bounds and NaN counts; `prune` returns `TriState` and is sound (NaN, signed zeros, nulls, inexact bounds and non-binary collations are unknown).
- **`IoScheduler` / `IoContext`**: coalesced ranges, per-store in-flight cap (reads and writes), full-jitter retries honouring `Retry-After`, per-attempt timeouts, per-query and process counters, `if_match` / `if_unmodified_since` on every read (`KRISHIV_FILE_CHANGED_DURING_READ`), one speculative tail read per footer, metadata reads reserved from the query pool, a byte-bounded metadata cache in its own memory pool keyed by file version and key fingerprint, per-query secret resolution cache, multipart uploads (parts as tasks, reserved while in flight, drained before abort on cancel/error/drop), and a fault-injecting store that flags requests not issued by the scheduler.
- **Split planning** reproduces Spark exactly: 84 cases planned by Spark 4.2.0 (`tests/fixtures/spark-4.2.0/file-splits.json`, generated by `tests/scripts/gen_file_splits.py`) match partition count and every split.
- **`SchemaMapper`**: case rules (Spark's duplicate-field error), field ids (with Spark's name fallback), Delta column mapping, widening, NTZ/LTZ, missing (nested) fields, predicates re-typed to the file before pruning; behaviour checked against Spark 4.2 probes.
- Typed options with an unknown-option warning (did-you-mean) and `krishiv.io.strictOptions`; `ScanStream` (per split) and `FileWriter` (per task, Spark file names, rollover).
- Storage failures after retries raise `KRISHIV_OBJECT_STORE_REQUEST_FAILED` and are never skipped by `ignoreCorruptFiles` (only real corruption is).

### `krishiv-testkit`
`file_format_conformance!(name, fixture)`: 12 checks (round trip of every Spark type incl. nested and a Variant placeholder, projection, pruning soundness property test incl. NaN/-0.0/nulls/collations/out-of-range literals/inexact statistics, selection and row index, split invariance, schema evolution, corrupt/truncated/changed files, memory accounting, cancellation, I/O behaviour, options and secrets, writer). A mock columnar format passes it with the sans-IO decoder and through the async bridge.

### Dependencies
`object_store =0.14.2` (pinned per ADR 0028, `default-features = false`); `async-trait` and `chrono` are already in the tree through it (+0 crates, budgets unchanged).

### Checks

## What and why
The owner asked me to review CI for speed. It is healthy: nothing is failing, flaky or run twice. A run takes about 6 minutes because the two jobs run in parallel and the emulator job is the slower one.

Step times from run 39115582525:

| Job | Step | Time |
|-----|------|------|
| Emulator | setup | ~40 s |
| Emulator | build debug, test and release APKs | 2 m 52 s |
| Emulator | boot, instrumented tests, smoke test | 2 m 15 s |
| Build | unit tests | 47 s |
| Build | lint | 51 s |
| Build | release (R8) | 1 m 42 s |

Changes:
- **The emulator boots in the background before the build**, not after it. The about one-minute boot now overlaps the three-minute build.
- **Smoke test waits less.** It used to wait a fixed 10 s after `am start -W`, which already waits for the first frame. It now waits 3 s. Monkey sends its 300 events at 100 ms apart instead of 200 ms, which saves 30 s.
- CHANGELOG line under 2.1.0.

Expected result: the emulator job goes from about 5 m 50 s to about 4 m 15 s, and the whole run drops to roughly 4–4.5 min. Test coverage is unchanged: the same unit tests, lint, both APKs, the signing check, all instrumented tests and the minified smoke test.

**Left alone on purpose:**
- **Both jobs build the release APK with R8.** Sharing one build would make the emulator job wait for the build job, which is slower overall.
- **`gradle/actions/setup-gradle`** would give a persistent build cache, but it is a new third-party action. It needs your approval under rule 5, so I haven't added it.

This PR's own CI run shows the timings.

body:
## What

New opt-in setting `[keyboard] apple_when_present` (default `false`).

While an Apple keyboard is connected, keyhub sets Toshy's `override_kbtype` to `Apple`, so every keyboard (including a laptop's built-in one) gets the Apple keymap. Unplugging it restores whatever `[toshy] override_kbtype` was configured (default `Auto-Adapt`).

- Detection: `/proc/bus/input/devices`, polled every 2s. A device counts if it has a `kbd` handler and its name matches `apple|magic keyboard`, so Apple trackpads/mice and e.g. AirPods' media-key device don't trigger it.
- Switching: keyhub writes `override_kbtype` into Toshy's preferences database, which Toshy already watches and reloads live. No restart, no change to the vendored Toshy.

Also: `ydotoold virtual device` (ydotool 1.x) joins `ydotool virtual device` (0.1.x) in the default ignore list; without it keyhub grabs ydotoold's device and remaps Handy's paste keystroke.

## Why

On a laptop with an external Magic Keyboard, Toshy treats the Magic Keyboard as Apple and the built-in keyboard as Windows. This makes the whole setup behave as an Apple keyboard whenever the Magic Keyboard is plugged in.

## Tests

`pytest`: 39 passed (new `tests/test_apple.py` covers detection, the fallback value, hotplug watching and the config round-trip).

author: phonedu
body:
## What this fixes

Two silent modelling errors that made the document (and every export) wrong while every call reported success.

### 1. A component set's editor outline was a real stroke

`Node::new` gave every `COMPONENT_SET` a purple dashed stroke (`#9747FF`, 1 px, dashes `[10, 5]`). That stroke lived in the document, so `file.export` and `screenshot` painted the canvas's dashed frame into the image. A set selected for export came out with the purple box around it, and the only workaround was to crop every preview.

New sets now start with no paint. The canvas draws the dashed frame itself in the UI overlay. Files written before this change carry no `editorOutlines` marker and lose exactly that stored decoration when opened (the exact paint and dash pattern). Files written by this fix carry `editorOutlines: true`, so a stroke someone chose is kept even when it looks exactly like the old decoration; an explicitly imported stroke is untouched.

### 2. `vector.create` ignored the requested width and height

For a vector with a `path`, the path's intrinsic bounding box overwrote `width`/`height`:

```json
{"command":"node.create","params":{"type":"vector","path":"M0 0 L24 0 L24 24 L0 24 Z","width":16,"height":8}}
```

exported as `<svg width="24" height="24">`. The same applied to `points`. Icons imported onto a 24 px grid could not be sized through the API.

The geometry is now scaled to the size asked for: both sides independently when both are given, the other side proportionally when one is. A path or point set that draws nothing (`M5 5`, or two identical points) is an error instead of an invisible 0×0 layer. So is a negative size, a size on an axis the geometry has none of (`width` on a vertical line), and a request that would collapse both axes.

## Reproduction

Component set, before:

```text
figcraft-cli run: create two components at x=0 and x=400, component.combineVariants
figcraft-cli export comps.figcraft -o comps.svg --node 4
```

The SVG contained a dashed `#9747FF` path spanning the set, and the PNG had 876 purple pixels. With this branch the same export has no `9747FF`, no `stroke-dasharray`, and 0 purple pixels; reopening the old file and exporting it gives the same clean result.

Vector, before and after:

```text
before: <svg width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24"> …  d="M0 0L24 0L24 24L0 24L0 0Z"
after:  <svg width="16" height="8"  viewBox="0 0 16 8">  …  d="M0 0L16 0L16 8L0 8L0 0Z"
```

## Notes

`variable.import` with a top-level `variables` map was a real silent partial import, but upstream already fixed it in #790 / #793 (`8629a6f`) by reading that shape and warning when nothing was read. This branch is rebased on that commit and does not duplicate it.

`component.combineVariants` preserving the variants' positions (and leaving a wide set when they were far apart), and the emoji fallback, were investigated too. The former matches Figma's behaviour (variants are not auto-arranged; the set frame is resized separately), and the latter renders correctly in this build, including `🟢` and `⚪`, so neither is included as a bug fix.

## Changes

- `crates/doc/src/node.rs`: component sets no longer get the decoration as a stroke.
- `crates/format/src/lib.rs`: files without the new `editorOutlines` marker drop exactly that stored decoration on open; marked files keep what they contain.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`: the dashed purple frame is drawn as canvas chrome, including for sets nested in ordinary frames (a visibility-aware subtree walk, since `boards` only visits top-level layers and sections).
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/create.rs`: scale vector paths/points to `width`/`height`; refuse geometry that draws nothing, a negative size, a size on an axis with no extent, and a request that would collapse both axes.
- Regression tests: `a_component_sets_editor_outline_is_not_exported`, `component_sets_draw_their_editor_outline`, `a_component_sets_old_editor_outline_is_dropped_only_without_the_marker`, `vector_paths_take_the_requested_size_and_refuse_empty_geometry`.
- `docs/mcp.md` and `docs/components-parity.md` record the behaviour.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy -p figcraft-engine -p figcraft-format -p figcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo test -p figcraft-engine --lib` — 1027 passed, 2 ignored
- `cargo test -p figcraft-format --lib` — 234 passed
- `cargo test -p figcraft-ui-egui --lib canvas_fixes_tests` — 5 passed
- CLI end-to-end: vector export is 16×8; new and 0.6.0 component-set exports both have 0 purple pixels.
