body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to master, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @ayu-sh-kr/dota-core@1.12.0

### Minor Changes

- d485d33: Pages can publish schema.org structured data through `SEO.jsonLd`, a JSON-LD object or array.

  - `updateDocumentSEO` (and therefore `DotaPageElement`) keeps one `<script type="application/ld+json">` in the document head in sync with it, and removes it when a page has no `jsonLd`, so structured data never carries over to the next route.
  - The managed script is marked with the new `SEO_JSON_LD_ATTRIBUTE` (`data-dota-seo`). JSON-LD scripts written by the application are left untouched, and server renderers can write the same attribute so the browser updates their script instead of adding a second one.
  - `seoHeadTags(seo)` describes every head element page SEO manages (title, meta, link, JSON-LD) in write order, with absent values marking tags to remove; `seoHeadTagSelector(tag)` identifies the element each one manages. `updateDocumentSEO` applies this list, and server renderers serialize the same one, so the head built on the server always matches the browser's.

### Patch Changes

- Updated dependencies [d485d33]
- Updated dependencies [d485d33]
  - @ayu-sh-kr/dota-rendering@0.2.0
## @ayu-sh-kr/dota-rendering@0.2.0

### Minor Changes

- d485d33: Add a DOM-free `@ayu-sh-kr/dota-rendering/server` entry that serializes `html` templates to HTML strings carrying the same durable hydration markers `hydrate()` adopts.

  - `serializeOutput(output, scope?)` renders a `TemplateResult`, a legacy string, or `nothing`; with a scope it emits element indexes, `data-dh-a` attribute tokens, and child-part and keyed-entry comments.
  - `escapeHtml(value)` escapes text and quoted attribute values.
  - `tokenizeHtml(source)`, `decodeHtmlEntities(value)`, the token types, `TEMPLATE_ELEMENT`, and `SHADOW_ROOT_MODE_ATTRIBUTE` expose the lexical HTML support that server tooling needs to read the same markup.

  The server entry imports the root entry, so both share one copy of values such as `nothing` and one set of types. The root entry and its bundled declarations are unchanged.

- d485d33: Export the durable hydration marker format so other emitters, such as Dota SSR's string renderer, produce exactly what `hydrate()` adopts.

  - `hydrationIdentity(tagName, strings, scope)` returns the four host attributes (`data-dh-c`, `data-dh-t`, `data-dh-v`, `data-dh-s`); `HYDRATION_IDENTITY_ATTRIBUTES` lists them for clearing.
  - `childPartMarkers`, `keyedEntryMarkers`, and `attributePartToken` build the comment and `data-dh-a` formats; `hydrationScope(n)` and `isHydrationScope` define the `h0`, `h1`, … scope shape.
  - The template conventions the renderer writes (`COMPONENT_START_MARKER`, `COMPONENT_END_MARKER`, `NODE_INDEX_ATTRIBUTE`, `COMPONENT_ATTRIBUTE`, `DYNAMIC_ATTRIBUTE`) are now public constants.

  The renderer itself uses these, so emitted markup is unchanged.
## @ayu-sh-kr/dota-server-dom@0.1.0

### Minor Changes

- d485d33: First release of `@ayu-sh-kr/dota-server-dom`: minimal, dependency-free browser stand-ins for rendering web components on a server.

  - The root entry exports pure constructors (`ServerElement`, `ServerShadowRoot`, `ServerDocument`, `ServerCustomElementRegistry`, the node, token-list, style, location, history, storage, media-query, and observer stand-ins) and `installServerGlobals()`. Importing it defines no globals.
  - `@ayu-sh-kr/dota-server-dom/install` is a side-effect import that defines `HTMLElement` and `customElements` when they are missing, for modules whose classes extend `HTMLElement` when they are evaluated.
  - `@ayu-sh-kr/dota-server-dom/node` exports `runInBrowserScope(url, task)`, which provides request-scoped `document`, `location`, `history`, storage, and window events isolated between concurrent renders with `AsyncLocalStorage`. It requires a Node-compatible runtime.

  Existing globals, from a browser, Happy DOM, or the runtime, are never replaced. Requires Node 22 or later.
## @ayu-sh-kr/dota-ssr@0.4.0

### Minor Changes

- d485d33: Routes declared `@Route({mode: 'ssr'})` are now rendered on the server automatically, in development and in production, with no server code to write.

  - `dotaSsr()` (from `@ayu-sh-kr/dota-ssr/vite`) renders `ssr` routes in `vite dev` and, on `vite build`, builds a self-contained server bundle and writes the deployment target's files: `node` (default, `node dist-server/server.mjs`), `vercel` (a function plus rewrites in `vercel.json`), `netlify` (a Functions API function), or `cloudflare-pages` (`_worker.js` and `_routes.json`). `github-pages` stays static and warns. Builds without `ssr` routes skip the server build.
  - Components and routes come from the application entry: `captureApplication()` loads it and receives what `initializeApp()` declares, so nothing is listed twice. `createApplicationHandler()` turns that into a web-standard request handler that renders `ssr` routes into the built `index.html`, inside the root element, with page or route `seo` in the head.
  - `createNodeServer()` from the new `@ayu-sh-kr/dota-ssr/node` entry serves built files (including prerendered pages), `ssr` routes, and the SPA fallback for client-rendered routes.
  - Request handlers accept a per-request document shell, and `PageRoute.seo` supplies head metadata for pages without their own. When a page provides SEO, the shell's own title, description, social, icon, and canonical tags are replaced rather than duplicated.
  - The server bundle is self-contained even when the application lists packages in `ssr.external`, and the shell is taken from the client build before SSG prerenders over `index.html`.
  - `createNodeServer` answers a render error with 500 and logs it instead of serving the SPA shell, and components whose `render()` returns nothing render empty on the server as in the browser.

- d485d33: Add a prototype request-time renderer at `@ayu-sh-kr/dota-ssr/server` that turns Dota pages into HTML strings in Node without Happy DOM.

  - `createStringAdapter({components})` renders a page and its nested light-DOM and shadow components from their `html` templates, awaiting an optional `serverLoad(context)` on each component first.
  - `createRequestHandler({adapter, routes, template})` matches `/path/:param` routes, gives components a request-scoped `fetch` and `state`, and writes page SEO and markup into a document shell. Page `seo.jsonLd` is written as a JSON-LD script the browser's `updateDocumentSEO` keeps in sync, and keywords are normalized as in the browser. `toNodeListener` serves it from `node:http` or connect middleware.
  - Loaded `@Property` values are written to host attributes, so the browser upgrades the same markup without a serialized state script.
  - Components declared `@Component({mode: 'csr'})` are emitted as empty `data-dota-csr` hosts, and Dota Core's server-render flag is set during a render.
  - Output carries Dota Rendering's durable hydration markers and the page route marker by default, so `dotaHydration()` adopts the server DOM and later updates patch it in place. Pass `hydration: false` for plain HTML.
  - Templates are compiled once per call site with an HTML tokenizer, which also finds nested component hosts. Tags inside comments, `<script>`, `<style>`, `<textarea>`, attribute values, and inert `<template>` content are never rendered as components.
  - During a render, `window`, `document`, `location`, `history`, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `matchMedia`, animation frames, and the observer classes exist as globals backed by the request, isolated between concurrent requests and removed afterwards. `runInBrowserScope` exposes this to custom engines. `customElem

body:
## What

A Raycast \`view\` command, **Mini Piano**, for checking a melody or a few notes without opening a browser.

- The search field is the keyboard: \`a s d f g h j k l ; '\` are white keys, \`w e t y u o p\` the black keys, Shift shifts up an octave, \`z\`/\`x\` move the typing octave (also a dropdown and ⌘[ / ⌘]). Typed characters stay in the field as the melody; ⌘R replays it, ⌘⇧C copies it as note names, ⌃X clears.
- Grid of drawn SVG key tiles (ivory / charcoal, amber while sounding) for the typing octave and the next one, with the key hint on each tile. Arrow keys + Enter also play.
- No audio assets: each note is synthesised once (additive partials, per-partial decay, slight inharmonicity, detuned second string) to a WAV in \`environment.supportPath\` and played with \`/usr/bin/afplay\`. Visible octaves are pre-rendered in the background (15–35 ms per note). Preferences: tone (electric piano / sine / organ) and tile style (drawn / plain colours).

## Verified

- \`pnpm build\` (ray build, incl. type-check) and \`pnpm lint\` (manifest validation against raycast.com, ESLint, Prettier) pass.
- Synth output checked numerically for all three tones at C2/C4/C5/C7: peak −2 dBFS, no DC offset, 120 ms end fade, 15–35 ms render time.
- Tile SVGs rendered in headless Chromium; icon PNG checked.

## Not verified (needs a Mac with Raycast and speakers)

- Listening test: afplay start-up latency per keystroke and the feel of the tone.
- Raycast's rendering of the SVG tiles (text in SVG). If it looks off, the **Key Tiles → Plain colours** preference is the fallback.
- Typing with a Japanese IME active goes into romaji composition; switch to English input to play.
## Follow-ups in this PR

- **Piano layout**: 7 white keys per row, black keys drawn on the upper right of their white key (⌘↩ plays the black key); two octaves fit without scrolling.
- **Shorter notes** plus a Note Length preference (short / medium / long).
- **Sustain by holding a key**: `assets/helper.swift`, an AVAudioEngine synth compiled with `swiftc` on first launch (~9 s, toast) and driven over stdin with note-on/off; release is a click-free damper envelope (checked offline with `helper --render`). Hold detection uses the user's macOS key-repeat settings; held notes are folded into the melody as `a–––` so replay reproduces them. `afplay` remains the fallback when the Command Line Tools are missing. Requires `defaults write com.raycast.macos ApplePressAndHoldEnabled -bool false` so vowels repeat instead of showing the accent popup.

body:
## Why
The API now stores the pause on the user's profile (brief #207, built in #210, API 0.34). The extension's pause only existed in one browser, so pausing in Chrome didn't pause Safari or the app.

The temperature and rain brief (#213, API 0.35 via #214) is already in use since #215. This PR finishes the remaining API work for the front end.

## What
- **Saving:** pausing sends `PUT /users/me/pause {until}` and turning it back on sends `DELETE /users/me/pause`. The change shows at once, then the server's `user.pause` replaces it. If a newer change is made before a save finishes, the newer one is kept.
- **Failed saves:** the previous state comes back, with a short inline message on the When card ("Couldn't save that…") or on the Rides status line ("Couldn't turn it back on…").
- **Other devices:** the panel reads `user.pause` every time it opens. If another device paused, the extension shows the pause and asks for no forecasts. If another device turned it back on, it fetches fresh scores straight away.
- **Panel closed:** a new daily `sync` alarm reads the profile. The existing `resume` alarm still fires at `resumesAt`.
- `User.pause` type added. The local `Pause` type now comes from `lib/types`.
- The e2e mock API serves `/users/me/pause`. The pause test covers:
  - the saved calls;
  - a failed save;
  - pausing and turning it back on from another device;
  - the daily alarm.
- `docs/api.md`: notes that the extension uses the pause endpoints now.

## Before merging
- Writes are last-write-wins, with no `expectedVersion`, as the API defines them.
- When signed out, the pause stays local, as it did before.
- The iOS/macOS app doesn't read `user.pause` yet.
- Checks: `bun run check` passes (63 unit tests). `bun run test:e2e` passed 26/26 three runs in a row. `build` and `build:safari` both build.

body:
## Summary

Codex GitHub 코드 리뷰가 영어로 달려서, 리뷰 규칙을 담은 `AGENTS.md`를 새로 둔다. Codex는 저장소의 `AGENTS.md`를 찾아 리뷰 규칙을 따른다([OpenAI 문서](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/third-party/github#customize-what-codex-reviews)).

```diff
+AGENTS.md
+## Code Review Rules
+- Write all review finding titles and descriptions in Korean.
+- Write review summaries and explanations in Korean.
+- Keep code identifiers, file paths, commands, and quoted code unchanged.
+- 리뷰 요약과 모든 리뷰 코멘트(지적 제목·본문·설명)는 한국어로 쓴다.
+- P0~P3 우선순위 표시와 그 형식은 그대로 둔다.
```

`homelab`, `homelab-app-template`, `files`도 같은 규칙 블록을 쓴다.

## Evidence

- **Before:** 이 저장소에는 `AGENTS.md`가 없었고, PR #1·#3의 Codex 리뷰가 영어로 달렸다.
  **After:** 이 PR의 Codex 리뷰부터 한국어인지 확인한다. 공식 문서는 언어 지정을 보장한다고 적지 않고, 어느 리비전(base·head)의 `AGENTS.md`를 읽는지도 적지 않는다. 그래서 효과는 실제 리뷰로 확인한다.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

파일 하나를 더한다. 되돌리기 PR 하나로 돌아간다.

**Blast Radius:** 리뷰

Codex 리뷰의 언어와 형식만 바뀐다. 빌드·배포에는 영향이 없다.

author: abhinavs1920
body:
## Description

Today `LexicalAutoEmbedPlugin` shows its embed menu whenever a pasted URL matches, even inside nodes that only accept inline content - in the playground, the `attribution` slot of `PullQuoteNode` and the `author` slot of `ReviewNode`. Inserting a block embed there bypasses the slot's own constraints.

This PR adds an optional `$disableMenuFor` predicate to the plugin. It receives the matched AutoLinkNode; when it returns true the menu is not shown and the pasted link is left as-is (the Tab/Enter/Esc handling is part of the menu, so it is skipped too). The predicate receives the matched link node rather than the plugin walking ancestors itself: `getParent()` stops at slot/shadow-root boundaries, so slot containment could never be detected that way. Callers walk ancestors with `$getNearestNodeOfType`, or with the slot helpers (`$getSlotFrame` / `$getSlotHost` / `$getSlotNameWithinHost`) for slot-aware checks.

The playground passes a predicate covering the two slots above.

Closes #9170

## Test plan

### Before

Pasting an embeddable URL inside the PullQuote `attribution` or Review `author` slot opened the embed menu and allowed a block embed to be inserted.

### After

Automated tests in `packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/LexicalAutoEmbedPlugin.test.tsx`:

- menu does not open (and `parseUrl` is never called) when a pasted link lands inside a node matched by the predicate
- menu still opens and embeds normally when the predicate does not match

`vitest --project unit LexicalAutoEmbedPlugin`: 18/18 pass. Flow libdefs updated with the `menuCommandPriority` and `$disableMenuFor` props.

author: sven-n
body:
## Summary

`LocalizedString` converts implicitly to `string`, but that conversion returns the **serialized value**, including all translations and metadata. For example, the map editor heading showed `Lorencia||zh-CN=勇者大陆||@src=MapNames/Lorencia||@stamp=47cb3df4`. The conversion is picked silently by Razor `@…` output, `StringBuilder.Append`, `string` parameters and `==` comparisons.

To find every usage, I temporarily marked both implicit `LocalizedString → string` operators `[Obsolete]` and built the whole solution, including the tests. That gave **55 sites**. I evaluated each one; the fix depends on what the text is used for:

| Purpose | Fix | Sites |
|---|---|---|
| **Captions in the admin panel / live map** | translation for the current culture (`ToString()`) | map editor heading, master skill root headers (`SkillListField`), merchant heading, map page title, live map names (`GameMapInfoAdapter.MapName`), cash shop item caption, socket option captions, and the `ToString()` of `Item`, `ItemCraftingResultItem` and `MiniGameReward` (used as captions in the admin panel) |
| **Messages to players** | translation for each player's culture | Blood Castle / Chaos Castle / … entrance opened/closed announcements (`MiniGameStartBasePlugIn`). They went out as one raw string to everybody, so configured translations were shown verbatim. The new `IGameContext.SendGlobalNotificationAsync(LocalizedString, params object?[])` overload formats the text once per culture, like `ShowGlobalLocalizedMessageAsync` does for resource keys. |
| **Published game events** (`GameEventPublisherPlugIn`) | neutral text (`ValueInNeutralLanguage`) | map, monster, item and mini game names in the events, which carried all translations and the `@src`/`@stamp` metadata |
| **Lookups in update plugins** (`x.Name == "Spirit"`, etc., 17 lines in 10 plugins) | neutral text | Once an admin links the captions (Captions page), the raw value becomes `Spirit\|\|de=…`. A still pending optional update would then not find its data, or throw in `Single()`. Applies the same pattern other updates already use. Behavior for not-yet-linked data is unchanged. |
| **Item drops search** (`EditItemDrops`) | displayed text **or** neutral text | It searched the raw value, so it also matched the metadata (searching `src` matched everything). |
| Debug message (`TerrainUpdateHelper`) | neutral text | — |

Left unchanged on purpose:
- `BaseInvasionPlugIn`: `string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(EndMessage)` is an emptiness check of the raw value, which is the right semantics.
- Test assertion messages in `GensRewardItemsTest` and `MasterSkillPassivePowerUpsTest`, and the operator tests in `LocalizedStringTests`.

## Noticed, not changed

`EventTicketItems` (Season 6 and 0.95d initializers) builds the drop item group descriptions as `name + "+" + itemLevel`. `name` comes from `LocalizedString.FromResource(...)`, so the result is `Scroll of Archangel||de=…||@stamp=abcd+1`. The level ends up glued to the stamp, and every level of a ticket shows the same caption. Fixing it needs an initializer change **plus** a configuration update plugin for existing databases (rule 4), so it belongs in its own PR.

## Testing

- Full solution build: no new warnings, no errors. A second run with the `[Obsolete]` marker only reports the intentional sites listed above (plus `EventTicketItems`).
- `dotnet test`: `MUnique.OpenMU.Tests` (1883 + 2 new), `MUnique.OpenMU.Web.Tests` (242), `MUnique.OpenMU.Persistence.Initialization.Tests` (643, 7 skipped as before) and `MUnique.OpenMU.PlugIns.Tests` (49) all pass.
- New `LocalizedCaptionTests` check that the captions of `ItemCraftingResultItem` and `MiniGameReward` show the German translation under a German culture. Both fail without the fix (e.g. `"Undefined 0 Spirit||de=Geist||@src=ItemNames/Spirit"`).
- The mini game announcement tests now capture the new localized overload. They passing shows that the announcements go through it.
- In the browser (`Startup -demo`, Playwright): the map editor heading shows `Lorencia`, and `勇者大陆` with the zh-CN UI culture. The merchant heading shows `Alex`.

author: darrinmc1
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
Preview (READY, not production): https://pm101topro-git-cursor-stripe-ttpn-rollout-darrinmc1s-projects.vercel.app

Inspector: https://vercel.com/darrinmc1s-projects/pm101topro/Bugi8VMUjHFozFf3g7nfiZQ1tY4f

Head commit `2f72c98`. Draft only. Do not merge. On that Preview, with the flags unset, `/` and `/pricing` show a disabled **Coming soon: $12/mo**, the TTPN sentence, the 3-day refund line, and the legal-example sentence. `/terms` has the refund paragraph and no 14-day or "all sales are final" line. `/llms.txt` lists $12/mo Pro and the refund policy. `POST /api/checkout` and `POST /api/stripe/webhook` return **503** `{ "error": "Payments are not enabled" }`.

`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_EMAIL` stays unset. Support-email lines are hidden rather than showing a blank or a fallback address. On this Preview, `/`, `/pricing`, `/terms`, and `/llms.txt` contain no `admin@pm101topro.com` and no `mailto:` link.

The first Preview (`d6e29c4`) failed at install with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE` because Vercel uses pnpm. `62d1dfa` updates `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `2f72c98` hides the support-email lines. That deployment is Ready.

Payments stay off. Currency is USD. Pro is **$12/mo** (the earlier $19/mo label is replaced everywhere it was shown). This wires Stripe Prebuilt Checkout behind flags that default to off. Nothing was created in Stripe, and no secret values are in this PR.

This builds on the disclosure from draft PR #50 (`cursor/merchant-of-record-disclosure-311e`) and does not close or delete that PR. The exact TTPN sentence now lives in `lib/merchant-of-record.ts` and is rendered by `MerchantOfRecordDisclosure` in the footer and under each Buy button.

## Price

| SKU | Amount | Checkout mode | Lookup key | On sale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pro | $12/mo | `subscription` | `pm101topro_pro_m_usd12` | Yes, once both Stripe flags are `true` |

The client sends `{ sku }` only. `POST /api/checkout` rejects a raw `priceId`. Lookup keys are prefixed with `STRIPE_SITE_KEY` (default `pm101topro`). Session metadata is `{ site, sku, userId }`. Checkout Sessions set `currency: "usd"`. The server accepts the Price only when `currency` is `usd` and `unit_amount` is `1200` on a monthly recurring price.

This repo never stored a Stripe price id. Nothing was deleted in Stripe.

## Product file inventory

Pro is a subscription to features that already ship in the app (the AI document generator and Status Cleaner). There is no paid download.

| Product | Expected path | Exists | Size | What it is | `available` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pro | none (no paid file) | The generator and Status Cleaner are in the repo | n/a | Real product: in-app access, not a file | `true` |

`available: true` matches the ExitCalc Pro subscription. While `NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_ENABLED` is not `"true"`, the button is still a disabled **Coming soon: $12/mo** and does not call checkout. `POST /api/checkout` returns **503** `Payments are not enabled` until `STRIPE_ENABLED` is `"true"`.

Free templates under `public/downloads/` are not the paid SKU. They are linked as free downloads on `/downloads`. They are real one- and two-page fillable PDFs, not empty stubs. They are public on purpose, so this is not a paid-file leak. Left in place (not deleted).

| File | Size | Signature / approval block | Notice on the product section |
|---|---|---|---|
| `public/downloads/project-charter-template.pdf` | 3,669 bytes | Yes (Approved By / Signature) | Yes |
| `public/downloads/business-case-template.pdf` | 3,660 bytes | Yes (Approved By / Signature) | Yes |
| `public/downloads/budget-tracker-template.pdf` | 2,110 bytes | Yes (PM and Sponsor approval) | Yes |
| `public/downloads/project-closure-template.pdf` | 3,206 bytes | Yes (final approval signatures) | Yes |
| `public/downloads/meeting-minutes-template.pdf` | 3,428 bytes | No | No |
| `public/downloads/raci-matrix-template.pdf` | 2,941 bytes | No | No |
| `public/downloads/risk-register-template.pdf` | 2,946 bytes | No | No |
| `public/downloads/stakeholder-register-template.pdf` | 2,562 bytes | No | No |
| `public/downloads/status-report-template.pdf` | 3,469 bytes | No | No |
| `public/downloads/wbs-template.pdf` | 4,956 bytes | No | No |

The notice is on the page, not inside the PDF bytes. Exact text: "Example only, not legal advice. Have a qualified lawyer check it suits your circumstances and meets your local laws (including signing and witnessing rules) before using it." The same sentence is on the Project Charter and Business Case tool pages, and under the Pro Buy button, because Pro drafts those document types.

## Refunds

The same paragraph is on `/terms`, the pricing FAQ, under every Buy button, and in `/llms.txt` (and `/llm.txt`, which uses the same generator). The 14-day window and "all sales are final" are gone. There is no separate refund route.

> One-off purchases can be refunded within 3 days. Subscriptions can be cancelled anytime and stop at the end of the paid period, with no refund for a partial period after 3 days. This doesn't limit your rights under the Australian Consumer Law.

## Flags and statement descriptor

Both flags must be the string `true` before a purchase can start, and the product `available` flag must also be true. Anything else, including unset, stays off.

- `NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_ENABLED` is baked in at **build time**. Buy buttons render a disabled **Coming soon: $12/mo**, plus the existing subscribe form, and do not call checkout. Changing it needs a redeploy.
- `STRIPE_ENABLED` is read at runtime. `POST /api/checkout` and `POST /api/stripe/webhook` return **503** `{ "error": "Payments are not enabled" }` unless it is `"true"`.

`/api/stripe/webhook` is excluded from the Clerk middleware matcher and returns before `auth.protect()`, so Clerk cannot block Stripe.

Subscription Checkout cannot set `payment_intent_data.statement_descriptor_suffix` (Stripe only allows that when `mode` is `payment`). For Pro, checkout writes `statement_descriptor: PM101TOPRO` on the Stripe Product. With the account shortened descriptor set to `TTPN`, the statement preview should read `TTPN* PM101TOPRO`. One-off sessions, if added later, set `statement_descriptor_suffix` to `PM101TOPRO`.

Pro is granted from `customer.subscription.*` (`active` or `trialing`) via `grantEntitlement` into Supabase `entitlements` (`user_id`, `product_id`, unique on that pair). It is revoked on delete / `canceled` / `unpaid` / `incomplete_expired`. Checkout completion alone does not grant Pro. There is no 7-day trial.

## Claims

- $19/mo is replaced with $12/mo Pro everywhere it was shown (pricing, FAQs, `/llms.txt`, courses, improvements, tools, Status Cleaner).
- The free plan no longer says "forever". There was no "lifetime" or "locked-in rate" pricing claim. A lesson line about a project constraint being locked in is unchanged.
- No "Most popular" badge and no 7-day trial (the current pricing page had already dropped both).
- The static `public/llms.txt` shadowed the generator and said pricing was not listed, with `hello@pm101topro.com`. It is removed. `/llms.txt` is generated and lists $12/mo Pro, the lookup key, and the 3-day refund policy. A support-email line is included only when `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_EMAIL` is set. Unset hides it. There is no fallback address.

## Env vars to set on the Vercel project (Preview first)

Do not commit values. Paste the TTPN **test** secret in the dashboard.

| Var | Set to |
|---|---|
| `STRIPE_ENABLED` | `false` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_ENABLED` | `false` |
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` | TTPN test secret (`sk_test_…`) |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | TTPN test publishable key (`pk_test_…`). Prebuilt Checkout does not require it. |
| `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Signing secret for this site's **test** endpoint `https://<preview-or-prod>/api/stripe/webhook` |
| `STRIPE_SITE_KEY` | `pm101topro` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_EMAIL` | Leave unset for now. Support-email lines stay hidden. No fallback addr

body:
## Summary

- Post and talk dates are now formatted in JST (`Asia/Tokyo`) instead of the build machine's local time zone. Cloudflare builds in UTC, so external posts published before 09:00 JST showed the previous day in production (e.g. a Bengo4 post at `2026-02-24T23:00Z` rendered as 2026年2月24日 instead of 2月25日).
- Every displayed date is now a `<time>` with a `datetime="YYYY-MM-DD"` attribute.

## Details

- New helpers in `src/lib/utils.ts`:
  - `formatDate(date, locale)` uses `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with `timeZone: "Asia/Tokyo"`. Output matches the previous date-fns patterns (`2026年2月25日` / `Feb 25, 2026`).
  - `toDateAttr(date)` returns the JST date as `YYYY-MM-DD` for the `datetime` attribute.
- `PostCard`, `BlogPostPage` and `TalkCard` use the helpers. `TalkCard`'s date `<span>` becomes a `<time>` with the same classes, so it looks the same.
- Pinning the time zone in code was chosen over setting `TZ=Asia/Tokyo` in the build script. The env var only covers commands that go through that script; the code fix also covers CI (which runs `astro build` directly), `pnpm dev`, and any build environment.

author: apojomovsky
body:
Closes #526

Ports the LVD driver for the PIC18F6520 family (LVDCON 0xFD2, PIR2<LVDIF>), with a host sim model and an mdb readback gate.

- `EPIC_LVD_Init/DeInit/Start/Stop/IsStable/EnableInterrupt` + weak `LVD_IRQHandler`; trip level is a raw LVDL 0..15 code (`LVD_TRIP_EXTERNAL` = 0xF for LVDIN). `EnableInterrupt` is refused with `EPIC_BUSY` until IRVST is set and clears the possibly-spurious settling flag.
- Dispatch (XC8 and epic-cc) calls the handler only when PIE2<LVDIE> is set, like EEIF, so a poller can own the flag.
- Host sim: IRVST rises after a fixed settle count (model constant) when LVDEN is set or LVDL changes, drops when LVDEN clears; `pic18_sim_drive_supply_low()` raises LVDIF once per above-to-below transition.
- `tests/example_lvd.c`: shared half checks the 0x05 POR image and LVDL/LVDEN readback through Init/Start/Stop; host-only half checks IRVST settling, BUSY gating, single-fire and re-fire callback, silence after Stop.
- Manifest: driver added to `hal_sources` and `epiccc_sources`, the 18F6520 sim stanza is now `lvd-readback`; reference `.X` project, CMake, MANUAL (new section 16, renumbered), README updated.

Verification limits:

- A real trip point cannot be stimulated headless, so the mdb gate asserts LVDCON readback only (MANUAL section 16 records it).
- XC8 and mdb are not installed on this machine (no vendor installers), so `make xc8-build` and the mdb gate were not run locally; CI runs them.
- Run locally: all 18F6520 host examples pass (epic-cc-dev image, cmake); ctest registers no tests for this module, so the examples were executed directly. epic-cc builds of the blink target and the `lvd-readback` sim variant succeed. `scripts/audit/mplabx-audit.py`, `scripts/tests` and `make pre-pr-check` are green.

Decision: one sim gate per variant is all the manifest supports, so `lvd-readback` replaces `timer4-match` as the 18F6520 mdb gate (same pattern #530 used for `irq-smoke`). Timer4 keeps its host test. Filed #532 to allow several gates per variant.

## Review

Reviewer: independent `reviewer` agent over the full diff. Question: real bugs in sim semantics, register handling, dispatch gating, ECAN variants, test vacuity, docs.

- Minor: `lvd_write` writes the read-only IRVST bit back (RMW). Declined: silicon ignores the write, and the memory-backed host sim needs the bit preserved to model it faithfully (dropping it would clear IRVST on every Start/Stop in the sim).
- No other findings in driver, sim, dispatch, ECAN variants, test, manifest/docs.

Fixed in place: none.

body:
| Q             | A       |
|---------------|---------|
| Bug fix?      | yes     |
| New feature?  | yes     |
| Deprecations? | no      |
| Issues        | Fix #120 |
| License       | MIT     |

При установке рабочий OAuth-токен ещё не подтверждал принадлежность заявленному приложению, порталу и пользователю. Добавлен общий `SdkAuthorizationVerifier`: secure `app.info` через настроенный OAuth-сервер SDK, проверка client/member/domain/user/expiry, затем `profile` на подтверждённом портале. Проверка обязательна в `Install` и `OnAppInstall` до изменения установки, аккаунтов, flush и событий.

- `Install` сверяет user ID и admin-флаг; сохраняет фактически проверенный access token и срок, включая обновление через SDK.
- `OnAppInstall` связывает подтверждённого пользователя с master-аккаунтом. Проверенные дубли сохраняют поведение no-op.
- Транспорт запрещает перенаправления: SDK самостоятельно обрабатывает 302, поэтому одного `max_redirects=0` недостаточно.
- Ошибки разделены на отказ авторизации и недоступность проверки; токены и SDK-ответы не включаются в публичные сообщения/цепочки исключений. Удалено логирование application token в изменённых обработчиках.
- Добавлены unit-тесты SDK-транспорта, подмены контекста, срока, refresh и сохранности состояния; функциональные тесты проверяют отсутствие изменений в тестовой БД при отказе. Внешние порталы не используются.

### Изменения контракта

Оба обработчика требуют пятый аргумент `AuthorizationVerifierInterface`. `OnAppInstall\Command` требует пятый аргумент OAuth `AuthToken`, отдельно от `applicationToken`. Миграций БД нет.

```php
$verifier = new SdkAuthorizationVerifier($applicationProfile, 'https://oauth.bitrix24.tech/');
$handler = new Install\Handler($accounts, $installations, $flusher, $logger, $verifier);
$eventCommand = new OnAppInstall\Command(
    $memberId, $domain, $applicationToken, $applicationStatus,
    AuthToken::initFromEventRequest($request),
);
```

ApplicationProfile и адрес OAuth-сервера берутся только из доверенной серверной конфигурации. Pending-установка допускается; `app.info.CODE` не сравнивается с OAuth client ID. Одноразовый токен события не заменяет сохранённый refreshable-токен.

Проверяется идентичность access token. Неиспользованный refresh token сохраняется без принудительной ротации и отдельно не удостоверяется. При последующем обновлении токенов вызывающему приложению необходимо проверить новую авторизацию относительно сохранённых member/domain/user до замены реквизитов; событие SDK о refresh само по себе этого не делает.

### Проверка

Проверки выполнены последовательно:

- `make lint-all` — успешно (лицензии, CS Fixer, PHPStan, Rector).
- `make test-unit` — 227 тестов, 486 assertions, успешно.
- `make test-functional` — 90 тестов, 246 assertions, успешно; пересоздана только отдельная БД библиотеки `b24phpLibTest`.
- `git diff --check` — успешно.

Проведено независимое ревью; обнаруженное SDK-перенаправление закрыто транспортной защитой и регрессионным тестом.

### Исправление CI

CI устанавливал плавающую вершину SDK с новыми обязательными методами `markAsNeedReinstall`, `findStaleInstallations`, `getCurrent`, ещё не реализованными в библиотеке. Совместимый SDK теперь явно закреплён в composer.json на `dev-v3-dev#398296d5d27dc9f09fb4d18a896a052d8bd795bd`. Миграция библиотеки к новому сценарию переустановки SDK остаётся отдельной задачей.

Обновлена конфигурация Rector: удалённый `PHPUNIT_110` заменён на `withComposerBased(phpunit: true)`, минимальная версия инструмента — `^2.7`. Временные локальные ограничения PHPStan/pcre сняты; `make composer "update --dry-run --no-audit"` и `make composer "update --no-audit"` прошли с актуальными зависимостями. Применены механические требования Rector в тестовых файлах. Старый тест `ChangePortalLicenseFamily` переименован с суффиксом `Test`, поэтому PHPUnit теперь выполняет ещё два ранее не обнаруживавшихся теста.

На этом наборе заново последовательно прошли lint, 227 unit-тестов и 90 функциональных тестов. GitHub Actions на коммите `a726984`: все 12 проверок успешны — unit, functional, PHPStan, Rector, CS-Fixer и licenses в обоих запусках (push и pull_request).

body:
Renames "ledger" → **the security record** across the AI Security Theory and web10 state, and names the `knowledge-base/security/` section **Written Security (WS)**.

The term "ledger" carried a blockchain overclaim (an append-only record of *value*) that contradicted the theory's own "not an oracle / bounded, evidenced uncertainty" framing. It is now **the security record** — a dated, agent-attributed log of what was scanned, by which model, when, against what commit, and what was found; it records *due diligence*, not a guarantee. The whole section is **Written Security** = strategy + record + knowledge, with the framing that having WS in the KB is what makes a project more secure (intent vs. evidence).

Renames: `scan-ledger.md` → `security-record.md`, `the-ledger/` → `the-security-record/`; the gate script's `ledger` var → `record_file` (also fixes a pre-existing empty-array-under-`set -u` bug it exposed); AGENTS.md WAKE-UP + tour re-pointed. No behavior change.

author: rwnq8
body:
## ISSUE-SLA-WINDOW-APPLIER-2 — record the live SLA trigger through the runner

The 120-minute window is **live** but **no `migration_runs` row describes it**. Both attempts to record it failed and are sha256-locked, so neither replays:

| run | what happened |
|---|---|
| 292 (12:45:31Z) | star-select INSERT probe refused → runner dropped the trigger → production had none |
| 296 (13:12:49Z) | explicit-column probe also refused → **restored** by `D1-TRIGGER-DEPTH-RESTORE-1`, nothing lost, file still failed |

**#2220 (13:20:01Z)** removed the veto: every zero-row `INSERT … SELECT` on `agent_issues` is refused by D1 whatever the trigger contains (star, explicit-column, and literal-source forms all 7500), while `DELETE`/`UPDATE` compile. So this file can apply.

### What it is

- the **same definition production already runs** — `DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS` + `CREATE`, idempotent, **no row read or written**
- `BACKUP: issue_triage` for the destructive rule (the applier counts `DROP TRIGGER` as destructive)
- the restore snapshot still protects production if the canary refuses
- `spof-review:` names the second path, already installed by #2145: `fleet_tasks issue-sla-invariant-guard` on `*/10`

### Verification (run locally)

- `apply_migrations.py --check` → `ok: true`, 3 statements, destructive 1, backup `issue_triage`
- `spof_review.py origin/main --enforce` → `ok`
- `workers_standards_guard.py origin/main` → `ok`

### What "success" means here

If it applies `ok`, production and `migration_runs` finally agree and the out-of-band drift is closed. If it is refused, the snapshot restores the trigger and the fleet is untouched — both outcomes are observable, and neither costs the SLA.

author: arpitjain099
body:
Follow-up to #291 and #305, in the half of the tree those did not reach.

`UnmarshalJSON` removes null relationships from the slice, but #291 chose `continue` for the other element types, so a `"packages": [null]` stays in the slice as a nil pointer and every consumer downstream inherits it. #305 fixed one consumer, `spdxlib` validation. The widest one left is the tag-value writer: `RenderDocument` panics on a nil element in any of the six pointer slices, in all three of v2_1, v2_2 and v2_3.

Four of those slices are reachable straight from `json.Read`, so the documented round trip of reading JSON and writing tag-value crashes on input the reader deliberately accepts. `json.Write` and `yaml.Write` are unaffected because `encoding/json` renders a nil pointer as `null`.

There are two defects per sorted slice, which is why the loop guard alone is not enough: the loop body dereferences, and the `sort.Slice` comparator dereferences before the loop runs at all. With two or more elements the comparator goes first.

Present at HEAD and in v0.5.7.

Each writer package gets `TestSaverDocumentSkipsNilElements`, which asserts the real element next to each nil still renders, so the skip cannot quietly swallow data. `spdx/v2/v2_3/tagvalue` additionally gets `Test_WriteNullElements`, which drives the genuine `json.Read` into `tagvalue.Write` chain through exported API only. All of them panic in the sort comparator on main. `go test ./...` is 30 ok and byte-identical to a pristine baseline once timings are stripped, and both fuzz targets pass at 100000 execs.

One thing left alone on purpose: with `files: [null]` and nothing else, `len(doc.Files) > 0` is still true, so an empty `##### Unpackaged files` header is emitted. That is a comment in tag-value, the output still parses, and reworking the header logic felt like gold-plating a panic fix. Happy to add it if you would rather.

Three more consumers of the same nil carry the same shape, `spdxlib.GetDescribedPackageIDs`, `spdxlib.FilterRelationships` and `licensediff.MakePairs`. I kept them out so this patch stays one coherent thing, and can send them separately.

AI assistance was used on this change and is disclosed in the commit trailer.

author: midhunxavier
body:
## Summary
Fixes the flaky "dark composer" color-contrast failure in `test/e2e/accessibility.e2e.ts` ("main screens, workspace tools and dialogs pass automatic accessibility checks…"), seen in Actions run 39125386212 (attempt 2) as `.config-note > span > b` with #445e5f (light `--muted`) on #0d1514 (dark `--sunken`), ratio 2.65.

**Root cause:** the test emulates `reducedMotion: "reduce"`, and `ui/styles.css:51` then applies `*, *::before, *::after { transition-duration: .01ms !important }`. `transition-property` defaults to `all`, so that rule gives every element an `all .01ms` transition. The switch to dark is a same-document hash change (no reload), so it starts hundreds of CSS transitions that finish only on the next rendered frame. axe caches computed styles per node during a run, so a frame landing mid-run let it read one property from before the switch and another from after it.

**Fix:** `audit()` now waits until `document.getAnimations()` has no running finite animation before injecting axe, so every screen is checked in its settled state. The contrast rule and the rule set are unchanged, and the UI isn't changed: once settled it renders dark `--muted` (#c9cbbe) on #0d1514.

## Evidence
- A probe that flips the scheme and runs axe color-contrast right away failed 9 of 30 flips unthrottled and 6 of 30 at 6× CPU throttling, including the exact CI node and colors. With the new wait it failed 0 of 50 in both cases.
- `test/e2e/accessibility.e2e.ts` passed 12 of 12 times in a row locally with 6 busy-loop CPU hogs running on a 10-core machine.
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean.

Fixes #1007

Turns on the cached machinist-review gate (`MACHINIST_REVIEW = MachinistReviewMode.ENFORCE`) for MHA-DT-014 `dt-pinion-bracket` and drives the sheet to SHIP on the farm leaf `check:machinist_review:dt_pinion_bracket`.

## Remote review

- Fixes #1007 (tracker).
- Refs #913: this sheet's duplicate centre marks are fixed; the issue lists other sheets.
- Refs #1217: this sheet's seat-leader/(43.0) crossing is fixed; the issue lists other sheets.

- Refs #155: the bracket's STRAP_T/STRAP_R_END/STRAP_C2C pair is already single-sourced (the assembly imports `dt_pinion_bracket_geometry`); other pairs remain.

## Decisions taken without owner ruling — please confirm

1. **Delete the 3.18 (cross hole to the hidden pivot-bore wall) and charge the implied zero at .X (±0.8).**
   - (a) Delete, letting the hole sit on the drawn pivot-axis line, budgeted at the coarsest grade. **Chosen**: it satisfies the machinist consensus and Codex P1, and there is no prose location per ruling (a)/Codex #858 P2.

2. **Material widened to `AISI 1018 or 12L14 cold-finished steel bar`.**

   - This may re-key the drive-train BOM.
3. **7.000 kept at three places with a function callout**, rather than loosened. The spec budgets 0.25 air on the follower/cam engagement. Loosening and moving the absorber to fit-up (rule 19) was not taken: the band is the engagement budget, not a thread-rescue band.

author: samgbafa
body:
# Description

When `disableSubDelegation: true` is requested, the delegation now carries the node's terminal marker: the UCAN fact `{"xyz.tinycloud.policy/delegationMode": "terminal"}` in `fct`. The node then refuses any delegation that cites it as a parent (`terminal-parent-cannot-redelegate`). The key and value come from tinycloud-node `tinycloud-core/src/util.rs` (`DelegationMode::FACT_KEY`, `read_delegation_mode_from_ucan_facts`).

- `createDelegation`, the `space.delegations.create` wiring and a new `delegateTo` option `disableSubDelegation` pass the request through to both session-key paths: the session path and the runtime-grant path. The returned `PortableDelegation` reports the value requested.
- The WASM `createDelegation` takes no facts. `markDelegationTerminal` (sdk-core) therefore adds the fact to the WASM-signed token inside `createDelegationWrapper`, re-signs it with the same Ed25519 session key, and recomputes the CID (CIDv1, raw, BLAKE3-256). Every other claim stays as signed. The key must be the token's issuer, otherwise it throws `session key is not the delegation issuer`. A token that already carries the fact is returned unchanged. Once the WASM builder takes facts, this step can go.
- Wallet-signed SIWE delegations cannot carry the fact. `disableSubDelegation: true` now throws on those paths instead of issuing a delegation that can still be re-delegated: `createSubDelegation`, `delegateTo({ forceWalletSign: true })`, and the `createDelegation` wallet fallback for capabilities outside the session.
- The delegate can still use a terminal delegation directly. A wallet-mode `useDelegation`, which chains a new session from the delegation, is refused by the node (checked on a local node).

## Testing

- `sdk-core/src/delegations/terminal.test.ts` covers:
  - the fact is added, every other claim is kept and the signature verifies;
  - the CID matches;
  - existing facts keep their order;
  - idempotency and no duplicate fact;
  - a non-issuer key, a non-Ed25519 key and malformed `fct` are refused.
- `TinyCloudNode.runtimePermissions.test.ts` covers the runtime-grant path: the marker is signed with the grant's session key, and the marked token is the one activated.
- `TinyCloudNode.terminalDelegation.e2e.test.ts` runs against a real node (`TC_TERMINAL_DELEGATION_E2E_NODE_BIN`). CI runs it in the Node SDK replication e2e job against the pinned tinycloud-node v1.20.6 binary.
  - `disableSubDelegation: true`: the delegate reads, and the node answers its child delegation with 401 `terminal-parent-cannot-redelegate`.
  - `false`: the delegate reads, and the child is accepted (200).
  - Wallet-signed paths throw.

  Before this change, the same e2e against the same node fails: the flag comes back `false`, and the node accepts the child (200).

Local results:
- e2e 3/3 on v1.20.6.
- sdk-core 988 pass.
- node-sdk 945 pass. The 2 failures are the existing OpenKey cross-repo harness tests, which need external paths.
- web-sdk size-policy scripts 121 pass.

## Bundle size

`TinyCloudNode` is part of the web-sdk root bundle, so this adds root bytes. Cuts were made first:
- one marker call inside the WASM wrapper;
- a 54-character error string;
- the issuer check replaces a separate public-key check.

CI went from +1,349 / +363 to +1,327 / +344 gzip bytes (index.mjs / index.cjs). A lazy import would be inlined (`LimitChunkCountPlugin({ maxChunks: 1 })`), and a browser stub would drop the feature for web-sdk callers. The remainder is admitted by this PR's own exact-delta `tc1436Ratchet` row at the canonical CI bytes of run 39134326448: root ceilings 1,465,995 / 1,395,719. If another root-growing PR lands first, this PR re-measures against the new base and replaces its row.

## Linear Ticket

TC-1436

## Changelog

`.changeset/terminal-delegation-marker.md` (minor: sdk-core, node-sdk).

author: nonamer777
body:
## Why

CONTRIBUTING.md asks for Conventional Commit pull request titles, and every commit in this repository follows the same format, but nothing checks either. Pull requests land as merge commits, so each commit in a branch ends up on `main` as written. A check has to cover every commit, not only the title.

## What

A `Pull Request` workflow runs commitlint against each commit in the pull request and against its title. `pnpm/setup` installs pnpm and Node.js on the runner, and `pnpm dlx` fetches commitlint at a pinned version, so the repository needs no `package.json` and contributors need no Node.js. That matters for a Minecraft mod, where everyone already has a JDK and Gradle but not necessarily Node.js. The Gradle alternatives were either too loose (a single regex with no length limits) or too young to depend on.

The config extends `@commitlint/config-conventional`, caps headers and body lines at 72 characters, lets footer lines such as source links run longer, and rejects subjects that start in upper case.

The job runs on `ubuntu-26.04`, which GitHub lists as generally available but actionlint 1.7.12 does not know yet. `.github/actionlint.yaml` declares the label until a release lists it. The workflow also runs when the pull request is edited, so a renamed title is checked right away.

## Test plan

- [x] All 101 non-root commits on `main` pass the config through `pnpm dlx` locally.
- [x] `foo: bar`, `Added a thing`, and `feat: Add Thing` fail; a footer with a 130-character link passes.
- [x] `actionlint` reports no problems.
- [x] The `Commitlint` check passes on this pull request.
- [x] Renaming this pull request to `Lint commits` fails the check, and restoring the title passes it again.

## Notes

After the first run, add `Commitlint` as a required status check in the `main` ruleset so a failing check blocks the merge.

`TAB-P0-01` requires negative tests of signed staff session authentication. Existing decoder ignored any third or later dot-separated component after a valid HMAC, accepting malformed aliases of valid tokens.

- Edited files: **only** `src/platform/http/staff-auth.ts` and `tests/unit/staff-auth.test.ts` (no overlap with another open PR).

author: postick414
body:
# Relates to

No issue. This is a parity fix between the two database adapters, `plugins/plugin-sqlite` and `plugins/plugin-sql`. The shared contract is `IDatabaseAdapter.upsertComponents`, exposed to agent code through `AgentRuntime.upsertComponent` / `upsertComponents` in `packages/core/src/runtime/data-mutations.ts`.

# Change

The two adapters resolve the upsert natural key in different ways.

- plugin-sql resolves it through `getComponent(entityId, type, worldId, sourceEntityId)`. In that lookup, an omitted `worldId` or `sourceEntityId` matches any stored value. The existing component is found and updated in place.
- plugin-sqlite compared both fields with strict equality. An upsert that omitted `worldId` or `sourceEntityId` did not match the stored row. The adapter then inserted a second component for the same entity and type, with a new id. The original row kept its old data, so a later read by entity and type could return the stale row, and the entity ended up with two components of one type.

The omitted-key lookup is a defined contract, not an artificial input. This adapter's own `getComponentsByNaturalKeys` already follows it, and `adapter.test.ts` tests it ("finds a component by entity and type when world and source are omitted"). Only `upsertComponents` did not follow it.

This change makes the SQLite upsert use the same rule: an omitted `worldId` or `sourceEntityId` matches any stored value. The stored row is updated in place, and its stored world and source are kept when the upsert omits them. The merged row also keeps the stored `createdAt`: the shared adapter contract says an upsert updates data, agent ID, and room ID, and must not update `createdAt`. One production file changes: `plugins/plugin-sqlite/records.ts`. A regression test is added in `plugins/plugin-sqlite/adapter.test.ts`.

# Why this implementation

The research is a direct comparison of the two implementations of the same adapter contract: `upsertComponents` and `getComponent` in `plugins/plugin-sql/src/base.ts`, and `upsertComponents` and `getComponentsByNaturalKeys` in `plugins/plugin-sqlite/records.ts`. The fix adopts the lookup rule that three of those four implementations already share, inside the one that does not. No new fallback is added: an upsert that names a different world or source still does not match, exactly as the natural-key read behaves today. No stored data changes shape.

# Testing

Setup: Bun 1.4.2 (the pinned runtime), the real `SQLiteDatabaseAdapter` imported from the package source, on a temporary SQLite file.

Probe: create one component with a world and a source, run a control upsert with the exact world and source, then upsert the same entity and type with a new id and with world and source omitted, then read all components for the entity back.

Results at the live head `c25a412eeef397e2d6ac4f2118b23cd7189f2451` (re-run for this head after the `createdAt` fix):

- Before the fix: the exact upsert updated the single row. The omitted-key upsert left two rows — the new row with the updated data and the original row with the control data. Result: `rows=2 singleRowUpdated=false pluginSqlContract=DIVERGENCE`.
- After the fix: the omitted-key upsert updates the original row. One row remains, with the original id and the updated data. Result: `rows=1 singleRowUpdated=true pluginSqlContract=MATCH`.
- `createdAt` at this head: the probe stores `createdAt: 1` and upserts with `createdAt: 2`. The updated row still reads `createdAt: 1`. Before the `createdAt` fix the same probe read `createdAt: 2`.
- `vitest run adapter.test.ts` in `plugins/plugin-sqlite` (under Bun) — 50/50 pass, including the new regression test "updates the stored component when an upsert omits world and source".
- `tsc --noEmit` for both plugin tsconfigs (`bun run typecheck` in `plugins/plugin-sqlite`) — pass, exit 0.
- `biome check plugins/plugin-sqlite/records.ts plugins/plugin-sqlite/adapter.test.ts` — pass, no fixes.
- `bun run verify` at the repository root was not run. The change is inside one package; the probe against the real adapter, the full adapter test file, the package type check, and lint above cover the changed files.

## How to test

1. On a SQLite-backed agent, create a component for an entity with a world and a source (for example a `form_session` component).
2. Upsert a component for the same entity and type without a world or a source, with new data. Before this change a second component row appears and the original row keeps its old data. After this change the original row holds the new data and it is still the only component of that type for the entity.
3. Read the components for the entity. The list holds exactly one component of that type, with its original id, world, and source.

- [x] Targets `develop` and has no conflicts with the latest `origin/develop`.
- [ ] Ran `bun install` and `bun run verify` after syncing; record blockers below.
- [ ] Updated relevant documentation.

No documentation change is needed. No documented contract changes; the adapter now follows the natural-key rule its own read path already documents and tests.

# Evidence Gate

Evidence must match the reviewed commit. `packages/scripts/pr-evidence.ts rows`
sets the marker from the live PR head; rerun after each push.
<!-- evidence-head:c25a412eeef397e2d6ac4f2118b23cd7189f2451 -->

Keep every row. Attach artifacts inline or write `N/A - <reason>` where
inapplicable. UI changes require desktop/mobile before-and-after screenshots,
an uploaded MP4 explainer and walkthrough, video proof of the changed flow,
logs, and OCR review. Screenshots do not replace video. Use JPG images where possible.
Keep generated artifacts out of source control.

author: sethdford
body:
## Problem (loops scorecard, 2026-10-18)

The prod loops audit (`voiceai-evidence/loops-scorecard-2026-10-18`) found two broken links:

- **Proactive check-in texts skipped the guarded sender.** `proactive-channels/default-deps.ts` called `sendSMS` directly, so a proactive text never checked STOP, texts-off, the per-kind gap or the atomic lock, and wrote no `feature_checkins` record. A member who had replied STOP could still get one. `PROACTIVE_CHANNELS` went on for the cohort on 2026-10-18, so this is now live.
- **The "How I reach you" history panel was blank.** It reads `bogle_users/{uid}/outreach_attempts` (`outreach-history-read.ts`). Only the orchestrator writes there, and it is off. In 30 days nothing was written. Proactive, follow-up, reminder and post-call texts never wrote a row.

## Fix

- Proactive texts now go through `sendGuardedText` with a new `TextKind` `'proactive'` and a 5-minute gap. `chooseChannel` still decides the channel; the guard only decides whether the text actually goes.
- A guard skip is logged to `proactive_outreach_log` and is never logged as sent:
  - `skipped` means never: STOP, texts off, no verified number, no hash secret.
  - `held` means a proactive text went to that phone moments ago. The entry can be claimed again, so a later run sends it.
  - Neither counts toward daily caps, unanswered back-off or reply matching (`sms-replies.ts`). A text Twilio refuses still falls back to a note in the app, as before. If the guard holds back the stand-in text for a failed call, the words go to the app.
- New `sent-history.ts`: every guarded text, sent or refused by Twilio, and every proactive note or call writes one `outreach_attempts` row through `recordOutreachAttempt`.
  - The row holds `type`, `channel`, `status`, `personaId`, a fixed reason (`"reminder by sms"`) and the sender as `triggeredBy`. It never holds the message text or the number.
  - `phone:` and `sponsored_` ids are skipped: there is no account to show the row on, and a phone id is the number itself.
  - Write failures are logged and never fail the send.
  - The panel has no in-app channel, so a note in the app is recorded as `push` (bell icon). Calls are recorded as `voice`: answered is `delivered`, a missed call is `sent`, a call that couldn't be placed is `failed`.

Side effect to know about: `recordOutreachAttempt` sets the Redis `recent_outreach` suppression for 2 h on a `sent` row. That suppression is read only by the orchestrator's decision engine, which is off in prod.

About 215 reviewable lines; the rest is tests. `guarded-text.ts` is exactly at the 500-line ratchet limit, so `GuardedText` now extends `TextSent` from `sent-history.ts`.

Daily outreach push (`OUTREACH_IN_APP_PUSH`) comes in a separate PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm vitest run src/services/outreach src/api/scheduled-jobs src/tests/reminder-sms-default.test.ts src/api/__tests__/outreach-history-route.test.ts`: 56 files, 590 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`: exit 0, 0 errors
- [x] Path tests now run the real guarded sender, with only Twilio (`sms-delivery.js`) and `recordOutreachAttempt` stubbed. New tests:
  - a number that sent STOP is not texted, gets no note, is logged `skipped/opted-out` and writes no history row
  - a text sent moments ago means the next one is logged `held`, then sent on a later run
  - one text writes exactly one row (`{type, channel:'sms', status:'sent', ...}`, no words); one note writes one `push` row
  - a reply is matched to the text that went out, not a newer skipped one
  - `sent-history` and `guarded-text` unit tests: field whitelist; skipped ids; never throws; no row on a guard skip; `failed` on a Twilio refusal
- [x] Mutation checks, each restored afterwards:
  - default-deps calling Twilio directly: 4 path tests fail
  - dropping the `recordText` call: the history test fails
  - `alreadySent` ignoring `held`: the held test fails
  - `markLatest` without the filter: the reply test fails

## Rollback

Revert this PR. There is no flag: honouring STOP is a safety fix, not a feature. A revert brings back the direct `sendSMS` and stops the history writes. Rows already written are harmless; the panel just shows them.

author: kato-hiro
body:
## 概要

SvelteKit 3 では組み込みの `$lib` が削除され、`kit.alias` も非推奨になります。Kit 3 へ移行する前に、`src/lib`への import を `package.json#imports` の `#lib/*` に置き換えます。現行の Kit 2.70.3 のまま動作します。

## 変更内容

- `package.json` に `"imports": { "#lib/*": "./src/lib/*" }` を追加
- 282ファイル・676箇所の `$lib/...` を `#lib/...` に置換（下記の codemod で生成）
  - 拡張子を明示します。TS モジュールは `.js`、コンポーネントは `.svelte`、runes モジュール（実体が `.svelte.ts`）は `.svelte.js` です。
- `$lib` の import を `no-restricted-imports` で禁止（`.ts` は oxlint、`.svelte` は ESLint）
  - Kit 2 は `$lib` をそのまま解決するので、規則が無いと新しいコードの `$lib` に Kit 3 移行まで気付けません。
- `docs/guides` の規約（architecture・testing・testing-e2e・server-cache・prisma-db）を `#lib` に更新

手で編集したのは `package.json`・`.oxlintrc.json`・`eslint.config.mjs` と `docs/guides` の5ファイルです。残りの282ファイルは codemod の出力で、そのうち1ファイル（`src/lib/clients/aizu_online_judge/clients.ts`）だけ `pnpm format` が行幅で整形しています。

## レビューの方法

置換部分は、この PR の base（`dc9f2471`）で codemod を再実行すると同じ結果になります。手での確認は、上記の手で編集したファイルに絞れます。

```bash
git switch --detach dc9f2471
python3 -I codemod_subpath_imports.py . lib   # 下記のスクリプトを保存して実行
pnpm format
git diff refactor/lib-subpath-imports -- src e2e prisma   # 差分なし
```

## 確認したこと

- `pnpm lint`、`pnpm check`（0 errors、警告数は変更前と同じ）、`pnpm test:unit`（2726件）、`pnpm build`
- E2E: signin / redirect_after_login / votes / workbook_edit / workbook_order（56件）
- seed の import 経路（tsx で解決できる）
- lint 規則が `$lib` を検出し、`#lib` を通すこと（一時ファイルで確認）
- Codex の cross-review: Critical・Severe の指摘なし

lint 規則は `vi.mock('$lib/...')` と `.svelte` 内の動的 `import()` を検出しません。specifier をまとめて変えるときは `rg -n '\$lib' src e2e prisma` で残りを確かめてください（`docs/guides/architecture.md` に記載）。

## 作業中の branch がある方へ

この PR のマージ後に rebase すると、`$lib` の import が残っている箇所は lint で止まります。rebase 後に codemodを再実行すれば、新しく追加したファイルも含めて置換されます。何度実行しても結果は変わりません。

```bash
python3 -I codemod_subpath_imports.py . lib
pnpm format
```

E2E の spec では `#lib` を使わず、相対 import のままにしてください。Playwright のランナーは `#lib/*.js` を `.ts` の実体に対応付けられないためです。

<details>
<summary>codemod_subpath_imports.py</summary>

```python
"""Rewrite alias specifiers to package.json subpath imports with an explicit extension.

Usage: python3 -I codemod_subpath_imports.py <repo-root> <lib|features>

- lib:      `$lib/...` -> `#lib/...`
- features: `$features/...` and `@/features/...` -> `#features/...`

The rewrite is idempotent, so it can be re-run on a branch after rebasing onto the change.
"""
import os
import re
import sys

root = sys.argv[1]
target = sys.argv[2]

# (specifier prefix, source directory relative to the root, replacement prefix)
RULES = {
    'lib': [('$lib/', 'src/lib', '#lib/')],
    'features': [
        ('$features/', 'src/features', '#features/'),
        ('@/features/', 'src/features', '#features/'),
    ],
}

if target not in RULES:
    sys.exit(f'unknown target: {target} (expected one of {", ".join(RULES)})')

rules = [
    (re.compile(r"""(['"])""" + re.escape(prefix) + r"""([^'"]+)\1"""), os.path.join(root, source), replacement)
    for prefix, source, replacement in RULES[target]
]

unresolved = []
changed_files = 0
changed_specs = 0
file_changes = 0
current_file = ''


def resolve(base_dir, path):
    # a `.js` specifier is kept as is because TypeScript and Vite map it to the `.ts` source;
    # other existing files keep their extension (e.g. `.svelte` components)
    if path.endswith('.js') or os.path.isfile(os.path.join(base_dir, path)):
        return path
    # `x.svelte` that only exists as `x.svelte.ts` is a runes module and becomes `x.svelte.js`
    candidates = [
        (path + '.ts', path + '.js'),
        (path + '.svelte.ts', path + '.svelte.js'),
        (path + '/index.ts', path + '/index.js'),
        (path + '.js', path + '.js'),
    ]
    for source, specifier in candidates:
        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(base_dir, source)):
            return specifier
    return None


def make_replacer(base_dir, replacement):
    def replace_specifier(match):
        global changed_specs, file_changes
        resolved = resolve(base_dir, match.group(2))
        if resolved is None:
            unresolved.append((current_file, match.group(0)))
            return match.group(0)
        file_changes += 1
        changed_specs += 1
        return f'{match.group(1)}{replacement}{resolved}{match.group(1)}'

    return replace_specifier


for base in ('src', 'e2e', 'prisma'):
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(os.path.join(root, base)):
        dirnames[:] = [name for name in dirnames if name not in ('node_modules', '.svelte-kit')]
        for filename in filenames:
            if not filename.endswith(('.ts', '.svelte', '.js')):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dirpath, filename)
            current_file = os.path.relpath(full, root)
            text = open(full, encoding='utf-8').read()
            file_changes = 0
            new_text = text
            for pattern, base_dir, replacement in rules:
                new_text = pattern.sub(make_replacer(base_dir, replacement), new_text)
            if file_changes:
                open(full, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(new_text)
                changed_files += 1

print(f'files changed: {changed_files}, specifiers changed: {changed_specs}, unresolved: {len(unresolved)}')
for item in unresolved:
    print('UNRESOLVED', item)
```

</details>

`features` モード（`$features`・`@/features` → `#features`）は、後続の PR で使います。

**Problema:** no iPhone, adicionar o painel (/dashboard) à Tela de Início criava o ícone com nome "Fidelize" e link `/carteira`, abrindo o app do cliente.

author: apexaiofficial
body:
Several tg processes routinely share one session directory: parallel commands, or two agents driving the same account. This makes the files they share safe for that.

**Torn reads.** gotd's `session.FileStorage`, the peer cache and the config truncated files in place, so a concurrent reader could load an empty or torn session or cache and fail. New `internal/atomicfile`: write a temp file in the same directory, fsync, rename over the target, fsync the directory. The cache skips the fsyncs, since it can be rebuilt. The file session store keeps gotd's on-disk format and path.

**Lost updates.** Atomic replacement alone doesn't stop two processes that both read, merge and replace the peer cache from dropping each other's entries: an overlapping-writers test (8 writers × 25 saves) lost 18–64 of 200. New `internal/filelock` takes an advisory exclusive lock on a sidecar `<file>.lock` (flock on Unix, `LockFileEx` on Windows, no-op where tg is single-process; released by the OS if the holder dies). The cache holds it across the whole read-merge-write cycle, and a corrupt cache is rebuilt instead of failing every command.

**Stale session keys.** gotd re-saves the session on every reconnect to the primary DC, writing its own auth key into the file. A long-running process (e.g. `tg watch`) that reconnected after another process ran `tg login` or `tg logout` therefore wrote its old key back, undoing the login or resurrecting the logged-out session. The store remembers the key it loaded and, under the lock, skips writing that key over a session someone else re-keyed or removed. Same-key writers stay last-writer-wins, which is safe because their copies differ only in volatile state such as the server salt.

**Config creation.** `writeConfig` stat'ed and then wrote, which raced. A crash mid-write also left a partial config that a retried `tg init` refused to replace. `atomicfile.Create` writes and syncs a temp file and hard-links it into place: atomic, and it fails if the target exists. It falls back to an exclusive synced create on filesystems without hard links.

Tests cover atomic replace and create, permissions, symlinked targets, lock exclusivity, overlapping cache writers, corrupt-cache recovery, and the session cases: re-login elsewhere, logout elsewhere, same-key writers, and this process re-keying. `go test -race` and golangci-lint v2.12.1 (Go 1.25) pass.

body:
Closes #2483

## What
Mistral Vibe `meta.json` carries session speed, cost and tool-outcome stats the adapter ignored. This reads them (parsing only, no view change; #2480 consumes throughput and duration later).

- `src/mistralvibe.ts`: new `getSessionStats()`; every numeric field is `undefined` when absent or malformed, never 0. `last_turn_duration` is seconds in the file (checked against a local session's magnitude only) and is converted to ms.
- `src/adapters/mistralVibeAdapter.ts`: `analyzeUsage` fills a new additive `SessionUsageAnalysis.vendorStats` and a **wall-clock** `sessionDuration` from `start_time`/`end_time` (documented as including idle; omitted when timestamps are missing or the range is not positive).
- `src/types.ts` / `src/usageAnalysis.ts`: `VendorSessionStats` (rates and durations as `{samples, sum}`, so they merge), summed into `UsageAnalysisPeriod.vendorStats`.
- Cost stays on `calculateEstimatedCost`; `session_cost` is stored as `reportedCostDollars` cross-check only.
- `docs/logFilesSchema/mistral-vibe-session-schema.md` added; Mistral Vibe added to `validate-session-schemas` (discovery of `meta.json` only, baseline entry, SKILL.md mirrored to `.claude/`, SECURITY.md line). It reports field paths, never values.
- Cache versions bumped (extension 84 to 85, CLI 13 to 14) so cached Vibe sessions are re-read.

## Deviation from the issue
Tool outcomes are session totals with no tool name, so I did not push them into `completedByTool`/`failuresByTool` (that would need a fake tool key and skew per-tool reliability). They live in `vendorStats.toolOutcomes` (`rejected`/`hookDenied` are the declined bucket).

## Tests
New `src/test/mistralvibe.test.ts`; additions to `ecosystemAdapters`, `parserRobustness`, `usageAnalysis` tests. Synthetic fixtures only. `pnpm run test:src` passes (1498). `pnpm run test:node`: 191/192 files pass; the one failure is `usageWebviewMessageFlow` "missedPotential keeps only well-formed workspace rows", a webview test unrelated to this change (not verified against main). Skill tests (18) and `validate-skill-security` pass; lint has no new warnings.

## Needs a maintainer
This touches `.github/**` and `.claude/**`, so `guard-agent-config` will fail by design. Please review those paths and add the `agent-config-approved` label.

Likely merge conflicts with sibling PRs (#2479 to #2482): `src/types.ts`, `src/usageAnalysis.ts`, and the cache-version bumps.

author: argszero
body:
Closes #2349

Part 2/2 of #2349: the GUI now recalls what the host typed in this session, from the
list the daemon owns.

## Why the client does not keep the list

#2349's problem statement was a list inside one client process: not per session (the
up arrow in a freshly opened session recalled the previous session's prompts), not
durable (closing the client discarded it), not shared (the other client had none).
Part 1 (#2370) put the list in the daemon — `<session_dir>/input_history.jsonl`,
written for every prompt the daemon accepts, surviving a rewind and a compaction.
This PR is the other client reading it, and it reads rather than keeps: the GUI asks
on every session switch and stores nothing of its own, so a prompt typed in the TUI
is recallable here and vice versa.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `emrg/gui/daemon_client.js` | `list_input_history` → `input_history` in the response map — without it the request waits for a frame type nobody sends and times out into "you typed nothing" |
| `emrg/gui/main.js` | `emrg:listInputHistory`, resolving `cwd` from the session as `emrg:listHistory` does |
| `emrg/gui/preload.js` | the channel, exposed |
| `renderer/src/lib/daemonBridge.ts` | `inputHistoryBySid` in the app store + `listInputHistory(sid)` |
| `renderer/src/components/Shell.tsx` | asks on every active-session change, passes the list down |
| `renderer/src/components/Composer.tsx` | ↑/↓ recall |

## The recall rules, and where each one is decided

They mirror the TUI's, and each is a case that looks like an oversight if it is
missing:

- **Only at the edge of the block.** `view.endOfTextblock("up" | "down")` asks whether
  the cursor can still move that way inside this block, so inside a multi-line draft
  the arrows stay cursor movement and recall happens only on the first line's ↑ and
  the last line's ↓.
- **↓ with no recall in progress does nothing.** Recall starts on ↑; a ↓ that grabbed
  the newest entry would swallow the cursor on the way to the next line.
- **The draft is captured before the first recall and returned past the newest
  entry** — walking down off the end restores what the host was writing, not the last
  prompt.
- **The pointer resets on submit and on session switch**; otherwise ↓ on a new session
  pushes the previous session's draft into an empty box.

## Two states that are deliberately different

`null` (nobody has asked this session yet) and `[]` (the session has nothing typed in
it) both leave the arrow keys to the cursor, but only the first is "unknown": a failed
read stores **no key** rather than an empty list, so "could not read" and "you typed
nothing" never become the same thing at the keyboard.

## Verification

- `emrg/gui` — 162 tests, 154 pass / 8 skip. New: `list_input_history → input_history`
  mapping test; `preload-api` surface 57 → 58 invoke methods.
- `emrg/gui/renderer` — typecheck clean, **698** tests pass (was 691): 5 Composer
  recall tests, 2 bridge tests.
- **The recall tests were armed.** Disabling the key branch turns the three
  behaviour-carrying tests red (`↑ 从最新一条往回走…`, `发送之后指针归零…`,
  `会话切换之后指针归零…`) and leaves the two negative controls green, which is what
  those two are for — they pin that the arrows must *not* be stolen when there is
  nothing to recall.
- Python — **5468 passed, 18 skipped** (239 s).
- `tests/test_doc_counts.py` + `test_agent_md_prompt_cap.py` — 87 passed. `Agent.md`'s
  derived counts moved with the tests (renderer 691 → 698 with Composer 65 → 70 and
  daemonBridge 52 → 54; GUI 160 → 161 with daemon_client 97 → 98); the file reads
  7,986 characters, inside its 8,000 cap.

## What this does not claim

The multi-line boundary (`endOfTextblock`) is measured by the browser's layout, and
jsdom has none — it answers "at the edge" for every position, so the tests cover
recall, restore, reset and the empty cases, and the edge rule itself is the
real-browser behaviour of a ProseMirror primitive rather than something this PR
pins. Stated rather than implied.

author: raudbjorn
body:
<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes release restriction validation semantics for multi-title operations (StateChanged vs cache miss) and adds bounded in-memory retention up to 128 MiB per operation; callers must adopt OperationEvidence for correct batch validation.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`OperationEvidence`**, a per-operation, bounded store of release term match results so large search/RSS cohorts can be validated inside a DB writer after the small global LRU cache evicts entries. Callers precompute with **`evaluate`** / **`evaluate_current`** (reusing **`PreparedTerms`** when possible), then **`validated`** checks digested media, profile terms, and title—misses or stale inputs return **`StateChanged`**, not empty matches.
> 
> Caps are **1024** entries and **128 MiB** (separate from the global cache). **`record`** only commits after async work completes; cancellation, worker errors, and byte/entry limits avoid partial publication. **`matches_heap_bytes`** is shared with **`write_cache`** sizing.
> 
> Tests cover eviction survival, identity checks, capacity limits, convenience path, and no partial state on cancel/failure.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit c4a9182b3f46ac984866f8c6e13e4c8f6ac42f7f. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

## Summary by Sourcery

Preserve bounded release-term match evidence for reliable validation throughout an operation.

New Features:
- Retain bounded operation-scoped term matches so validation remains available after global cache eviction.

Bug Fixes:
- Ensure cache misses, changed inputs, capacity limits, and cancelled or failed evaluations cannot produce invalid empty-match validation results.

Enhancements:
- Add identity-validated operation evidence with entry and memory bounds while keeping sensitive terms, titles, and results out of diagnostics.

Tests:
- Add coverage for evidence surviving global eviction, identity mismatches, capacity limits, cancellation, failures, and byte ceilings.

body:
## Problem and change

Scriptoscope has author previews, synthetic assertions and self-regression images, but no independently reviewed, version-matched original capture corpus. Those categories cannot establish historical fidelity merely by looking plausible or passing a browser comparison.

Add thirteen provisional empty-label capture requests: Windows 95 and System 7 normal/pressed/disabled/default states, Apple Lisa unequal face bands, 1990 unequal ring bands, and three Crayon experiments separating baseline, coordinate motion and fixed physical placement at two explicit port origins. Requests specify the control rectangle, state, text, background, full image size, scale and port-to-crop transform; original OS, installation/patch stack, bases/search order, font, palette and capture details remain unknown until supplied. These dimensions are experimental inputs, not historical defaults.

Request version **0.1.1** names the nonzero-origin cases as unresolved direct-drawing experiments: Apple documents an origin-zero precondition for ordinary Window/Control Manager calls. Both require independently reviewed actual invocation evidence and a matching hashed artifact. All three Crayon cases require observed pattern-origin API availability/state and separate review; no zero offset, valid bypass, expected phase or pixels are invented.

The compatibility contract advances to draft **0.1.2**. Intake checks its authoritative header and full-file hash, reuses the existing source/requirement authorities, and binds exact source pins, requirement wording, request inputs, PNG/artifact bytes and metadata to a separately maintained independent review. Missing, partial, rejected, unreviewed, qualitative, self-regression and synthetic evidence remain distinct. Known renamed golden/preview bytes are rejected as contamination; this is not authentication of unknown external images or human identities.

**The actual capture and review manifests are empty.** The report currently lists thirteen missing requests, 18 qualitative preview PNGs, 54 self-regression PNGs and two synthetic fixture registries. No original code was executed, no renderer output was synthesized as a reference, no fidelity percentage was calculated, and no ledger status or source-selection approval changed. The author-preview README now distinguishes attribution from missing version/capture conditions.

## Validation

- All **42 focused Node tests** pass. Negative cases cover missing source/component/version/hash/conditions, wrong state/rect/origin/crop/scale/text, swapped images/provenance, relabeled actual selfgoldens/previews, absent/self/stale/rejected review, incorrect contract ID/version, document-scope changes, redirected authorities and changed target obligations, inconsistent experiment transforms, missing/unsupported nonzero-origin invocation, absent pattern-origin state/review and swapped invocation artifacts.
- `build:themes`, `build`, `gates` and the installed-tarball consumer smoke pass on head **8f3c0d76**, based on main **69357dad**. All three package-negative probes pass too.
- The source-precondition amendment at **5ae6d5fe** passes all **42** tests and `gates`; Astra independently reviewed the primary-source interpretation and repeated those tests. It changes only intake/docs and preserves the prior build/package result.
- The CLI's generated empty intake template exits nonzero as partial evidence; the repository's honest missing-evidence report exits zero without claiming fidelity.
- No renderer, browser fixture or golden changed. Required CI retains the full browser contracts and exact pinned golden checks.

Reproduce:

```sh
npm ci
npm run build:themes
npm run build
npm run gates
npm run test:package
npm run test:references
node tests/reference-captures/run.mjs --template windows-95.normal
```

The report is written to `test-results/reference-captures/report.{json,md}`. The intake README documents the producer/reviewer contract and the remaining external evidence work.

Refs #190 and #221. Actual independently reviewed capture collection under #190 remains open and incomplete.
