body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work
> - `packages/kv-demo-mcp-server` is a small demo MCP server; `config.ts` builds its `KvDemoConfig` (port/host/optional token) either directly from an input object (`createKvDemoConfig`) or from env vars (`readConfigFromEnv`)
> - Neither function has a test file today, even though `createKvDemoConfig` has several small but easy-to-break rules: port defaulting on null/undefined/empty-string, strict integer/range validation that throws, host trimming with a default fallback, and token trimming that must collapse blank input to `null`
> - `readConfigFromEnv` also encodes an env-var precedence rule (`PORT` over `KV_DEMO_PORT`) that is easy to silently invert in a refactor
> - This pull request adds a narrow, dedicated unit test file for `config.ts`
> - The benefit is direct regression coverage for the server's startup config parsing, including its validation and precedence rules

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

**What existing behavior does this improve?**
Test coverage for the exported helpers in `packages/kv-demo-mcp-server/src/config.ts` (`createKvDemoConfig`, `readConfigFromEnv`).

**Current behavior**
`config.ts` has no test file. The port-validation throw path, the host/token trim-to-default/null rules, and the `PORT`-over-`KV_DEMO_PORT` env precedence are all untested.

**Proposed behavior**
A new `src/config.test.ts` asserts `createKvDemoConfig`'s default port fallback (null/undefined/empty string), numeric and numeric-string port acceptance, invalid/negative/out-of-range/non-integer port throws, host trimming with blank-to-default fallback, and token trimming with blank-to-`null`; and `readConfigFromEnv`'s default application, `PORT`-over-`KV_DEMO_PORT` precedence, and host/token env pass-through.

**Reason and benefit**
This config is parsed once at process startup and gates whether the server binds to the intended port/host and whether the token-required auth path is active. A silent regression in the port-validation or token-blank-to-null logic would only surface as a confusing runtime failure or a demo server unexpectedly left unauthenticated.

## What Changed

- Added `packages/kv-demo-mcp-server/src/config.test.ts` with 10 unit tests covering both exported functions in `config.ts`.
- No source/runtime code changed — test-only addition.

## Verification

Ran the narrow package test command (not a repo-wide test run):

```
pnpm --filter @paperclipai/kv-demo-mcp-server test -- src/config.test.ts
```

Result: `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 10 passed (10)`.

## Risks

Low risk. This is an additive, test-only change to a single package; it does not touch any source/runtime code, schema, or API surface.

## Model Used

Claude Sonnet 5 (model ID `claude-sonnet-5`), via Claude Code running in a Claude.ai cloud session. 1M-token context window. Standard agentic tool use (read/grep/bash/git); no extended thinking mode used for this change.

_Requested by **Madi** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01VLvBtRPHS7TA3eVMAaxQGT?thread=cmsg_01VLvBtRPHS7TA3eVMAaxQGTSyqWpY4D7Dw2M2VvoAQEDQ)_

Before: the Physics page went straight from notation to the Schroeder frequency, and covered mode geometry in one short closing section.

After: the page builds up from linear acoustics to sub placement. It covers the wave and Helmholtz equations, plane waves, the k-vector and particle velocity, and the rigid-wall boundary condition. It then shows the room's modes as a k-space lattice, with resonance shells at 39.9, 59 and 120 Hz and Weyl mode counting (29 modes below 150 Hz, which matches the Modes page). Finally, a new section, "Driving the room", derives the modal Green's function and uses it to justify mode coupling and point-source placement.

That section covers:
- the coupling ∝ ψₙ(rₛ) selection rule, and reciprocity for mics;
- a coupling table for corners, mid-walls, the floor centre and the pillows;
- why mid-wall and centre sources cannot drive (1,1,0) or (1,2,1);
- the rank and conditioning requirement on the coupling matrix.

How: the new text sits ahead of the existing passive-treatment sections, which are unchanged. The old "Modal geometry" section is folded into the new one. Two figures are added (`images/k-lattice.png`, `images/mode-coupling.png`), generated by the new `scripts/physics_figures.py`. The "Modal vs. diffuse regime" heading gets an explicit id, so the Modes page's existing link to it resolves. I rendered the page locally with Quarto: no warnings, and the math and tables display correctly.

Note for review: the "How many sources" subsection points out that the diagonal pair S1+S4 couples identically to (1,1,0) and (0,0,1), the two modes under the 59 Hz tone. This conflicts with the Layout page's two-degrees-of-freedom argument. Layout is not changed in this PR.

It resolves per-architecture base image digests (`resolve-bases`) and then builds and pushes the Linux release builder images (`build-images`) as two separately reviewed stages.

- Add `scripts/run_release_tool.py`, a runner restricted to `release.native_builder_bootstrap`.
- Add `release/aur_package_installer.py`, which the Arch builder image installs as a root-owned `pacman` wrapper. The unprivileged builder may run it through `sudo`, and it accepts only the canonical shared and static package files of one version from the build directory.

`release/native-builders/README.md` documents the two bootstrap stages.

body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** stacked on #467 (4/5). Retarget to `master` once the earlier PRs merge.
- **What changed and why (ADR-018 §3):**
  - **Storage.** Up to four exemplars (situation / owner line / agent line, at most 80 / 160 / 320 bytes, one line each) go in a new append-only table, `soul_tone_exemplar_revisions`, owned by `SoulProfileStore`.
    - They are not a new layer in `soul_revisions`, because master's export rejects unknown layers and would break after a downgrade. ADR-018 §3 is amended to say so.
    - Table constraints keep the table owner-only.
    - Revisions, CAS, history, rollback and export (`format_version` 4) work as in the other layers.
  - **Prompt.** Exemplars render inside `## Tone`, after the dials, under a fixed "copy the tone, never the facts" line. They are capped at 1,536 bytes, dropped one whole exemplar at a time.
  - **Owner only.** `PUT /api/soul/tone/exemplars` is the only write path. `propose_soul_change` refuses exemplars, reflection drops them, and their text never enters the reflection prompt.
  - **PWA.** An exemplar editor with byte counters. "Use as tone example" on a chat reply prefills a draft through router state. Nothing is saved until the owner presses save.
- **Scope boundary:** exemplars are not part of anchors or drift.
- **Blast radius:** soul.db (one new table), the Tone projection bytes, the review page and chat message actions.
  - Drive-by needed for phones: the chat message action row now also shows on keyboard focus and on devices without hover. This also applies to the existing copy and delete actions.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #380

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web`
- **Setup / preconditions:** a paired PWA and an agent with a chat history.
- **Steps to run:** in chat, choose "Use as tone example" on a reply, edit the draft to fit the limits, and save. Send the next message.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the exemplar appears in Review → My agent → Tone. The prompt's `## Tone` section ends with the exemplar block.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no exemplars exist.

### How I tested

- `fmt` and `clippy` (api, memory, runtime, gateway, tools, channels; `-D warnings`): clean.
- Tests: api 223, memory 635, channels 890 passed. gateway 439 passed with 1 failure, tools 1362 passed with 1 failure, runtime 2390 passed with 1 failure; all three failures are the known root-only read-only-dir tests.
- Web: build, `test:review` and the browser test (3 out of 3) pass. Editor screenshots at 375px were checked in zh.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. This adds owner-authored prompt text.
  - Each field must be one line (control characters and U+2028/2029 are rejected), so it cannot add headings.
  - The text is bounded and framed as tone-only.
  - The model has no write path.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Older binaries ignore the new table.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Core-Residency Rationale

N/A

## Rollback

`git revert` this PR.

## Summary
- Persist an atomic, private, attempt-scoped receipt when YouTube returns a video ID, before the worker commits the publish row.
- On worker restart, reconcile an interrupted `uploading` job to `uploaded` only when an exact job-and-attempt receipt proves the API returned a video ID; otherwise keep the job `uncertain`.
- Remove receipts only after durable DB commit/recovery, add file-permission and recovery regression tests, and document the remaining in-flight resumable-session limitation.

## Safety
This does not resume an interrupted transfer and never retries an uncertain upload. A receipt is written only after the provider returns a video ID. Live YouTube upload behavior is still unverified until credentials and a private test upload are exercised.

CI must pass before merge.

- `docs/dev-log/2026-10-18-collaboration-rules.md`는 다른 참여자가 베낄 예시 역할도 합니다

## 논의하고 싶은 점

규칙의 강제 수준을 **전부 권장으로** 뒀습니다. 참여자 숙련도가 다양하니 양식 때문에 기여를 포기하는 쪽이 더 손해라고 판단했는데, 더 조여야 할 항목이 있으면 알려주세요.

GitHub 레포 설정에서 `master`·`dev`에 branch protection을 걸지 여부는 결정이 필요합니다. 지금은 문서와 PR 템플릿 수준이라 직접 push를 기술적으로 막지는 않습니다.

이슈 템플릿(버그 신고 / 기능 제안)도 추가할지 의견 주시면 반영하겠습니다.

author: tylers2222
body:
Part 6 of 15 of the PR 7 stack.
Review rounds: 2 (r1 0B/0M/1m, r2 clean)

Size: +164/-53 non-test lines (217) in 5 files (monoCaller.ts, monoMessages.ts, monoRoute.ts, App.tsx, mono_messages.rs), unchanged in round 1; +883/-23 test lines (monoCaller.test.ts, monoRoute.test.ts, the `mono_messages.rs` test module, the Playwright spec `tests/browser/e7-session-callers.spec.ts` and its fakes in `tests/browser/app/backend.ts`). Whole diff: 9 files, +1047/-76.

## What changed

- `resolveCaller` takes the calling session (`id`, `blocks`, `cwd`, `leadSessionId`), not only its id. A Mono's chat or habit run is still a Mono caller, also after /operator. Any other session with a submitted /operator turn is a caller of kind `"session"`, with `access: "operator"`, its `cwd` and the window's copy of its lead. Only /operator gives app access at this point; `started` access comes with PR 9. A session with no app access still gets `not_a_mono`, with a hint that names app access.
- A row with no Mono now names its sender. `MonoQueueHost.sessionSender` (App.tsx) finds a lead or worker session with app access and gives its title and level. `renderMonoMessage` then shows `from="<title>" session_id="<id>" level="lead|worker"` in the queue item and in the hand-off text. A row whose sender is no such session still reads as a deleted Mono's. The stale `fromMonoId` doc comment (PR7-5b nit) now says a lead's or worker's row has no Mono.
- The submit's `live` list sends each session's `leadSessionId` copy (or null). Rust reads it only for a session that `sessions` has no row for, so a worker that is not saved yet is a worker to the gate, not a lead (PR7-5a nit n2).
- `get_message` gets the session party legs (PR I3 m1, decision 506): a session caller reads a row its session sent or handled. A Mono caller keeps only its Mono legs, and a session caller gets only its session legs.
- Inbox Ask sessions are no project session for messaging (`ownProject`), and `sessions.list` drops a loaded Inbox Ask and its saved record (PR 7 review r2 n5).
- `getMonos` sets `you` only for a Mono caller.

UI rule: waived by Tyler, in the Monocode General chat on 2026-10-16, for non-visual edits to src/app/App.tsx. The App.tsx edits are wiring only; nothing visible changes.

## Why

PR 5a and 5b put the level rules for lead and worker sessions in the Rust gate. This PR lets the web app send those callers, so a lead can brief its workers and a worker can report to its lead through Mono messaging.

## How it was tested

- monoCaller: "resolves a lead and a worker with app access to session callers", "refuses a session with no app access with not_a_mono", and "resolves a Mono's chat to that Mono" and "resolves a habit run to the Mono it works for" (both now with an /operator turn, so the Mono leg must win).
- monoRoute: "names a lead or worker sender by its title, session id and level", "names the session that wrote a row with no Mono when it is a lead or worker", "queues a refused hand-off of a session sender's row again under its sender", "tells the gate each live session's lead" (the 5a n2 case: an unsaved worker sends its lead copy), "answers a session caller's send with the level refusal Rust gave it" (`worker_scope`, one of the three codes 5b added), and the PR I4 n3 hand-off test "names a steer's target by its message id when its handle is from an earlier turn of the session".
- mono_messages: `get_message_lets_a_session_caller_read_a_row_it_sent`, `get_message_lets_a_session_caller_read_a_row_its_session_handled`, and `get_message_keys_the_party_on_the_callers_mono_not_its_session` (comment updated).
- Playwright on the app harness (`tests/browser/e7-session-callers.spec.ts`, Chromium and WebKit, with Rust and Pi faked):
  - "a lead's brief and its worker's report reach each other's turns named by title, session id and level" drives `monocode app messages send` from a lead and then from its worker through App.tsx. It checks the caller and live list sent to `mono_message_submit` and the text each Pi prompt gets.
  - "a worker's send that the gate refuses answers worker_scope with the gate's hint" checks that the gate's refusal reaches the worker's CLI call whole.
  - "a report from a worker this window has not loaded names the worker" reaches the `getSession` fallback of `sessionSender`.
  - "a row whose sender session is gone reads as a deleted Mono's".
  - "an Inbox Ask is no project session for the gate or sessions.list" opens a real Inbox Ask through the Inbox, then checks the `live` list (`ownProject: false`) and that `sessions.list` shows neither the loaded Ask nor its saved record. The new GitHub and `session_list_linked` fakes are in `tests/browser/app/backend.ts`.
- Mutations: `python3 /tmp/mc947/E/split7/e7-6-mutations.py` (25 mutations, 34 catches, 0 survived; output in e7-6-r1-mutations.out). Correction: round 0 had 18 mutations and 27 catches (23 in e7-6-mutations.out plus 4 Rust catches in e7-6-mutations.rust.out), not 30.
- `npm run check` and `npm run test:browser` pass.

## Risks

- The `getMonos` `you` guard has no test. It changes types only, because an undefined Mono id never matched.
- `sessionSender` repeats the caller rule (Mono chat, habit run, /operator) when a row is shown. Review r1 nit 1 asks for a simpler rule; it is left for the follow-up issue because this round changes tests only.
- `sessionSender` reads the window's copy of the lead to choose `level`. [Inference, not run] A worker whose lead was deleted while this window had it loaded can still show `level="worker"` until it reloads. The gate reads the stored row, so this changes only the tag the reader sees.

author: edwardh-jedi
body:
S14 from `todo.md` (Scope 3), repaired as R4 (Scope 4). **This PR now changes code;** see "Repair (Codex B2)" at the end. The text below is the original docs-only finding, kept for history.

## Finding

S14 asked to replace BookingComposer's free-text `YYYY-MM-DD` / `HH:MM` inputs (KNOWN_ISSUES NB-005) with `@react-native-community/datetimepicker`. Those inputs were already removed on 2026-05-05:

- `a5b187b` "improve session proposal date and time picking" replaced the text fields (+ `lib/sessionTime.ts`, +233 lines of `sessionTime.test.ts`);
- `e80456f` "refine session proposal date and time picker ux" added `components/CalendarPicker.tsx` and `components/TimeWheelPicker.tsx`.

What the item asked for, against what `main` already does:

| Item asks | `main` today | Pinned by |
|---|---|---|
| a real date/time picker, no free text | calendar grid + time wheel; the only `TextInput`s are location and notes | `BookingComposerScreen.test.tsx` "opens a calendar grid for date selection (no manual text entry)" |
| keep the `scheduled_at` ISO payload / W7-003 (local, no `Z`) | `startsAt = \`${date}T${startTime}:00\`` | "submits the default date + time…", "changing start time auto-shifts end time…" (`…T23:00:00`) |
| disallow past times in the UI | past days disabled in the calendar; same-day past start → "Choose a future start time." | `CalendarPicker.test.tsx` (yesterday `disabled: true`), `sessionTime.test.ts`, composer test at :414 |
| server-side validation untouched | untouched | — |
| default to the next whole hour | **tomorrow 09:00 → 10:00** (deliberate "date-stable defaults", `sessionTime.ts:96–111`) | "Send proposal is enabled out of the box thanks to valid defaults" |

This PR only marks NB-005 resolved in `docs/staging/KNOWN_ISSUES.md`, in the same format as NB-004.

**Not done, deliberately (owner's call):**
- **Swapping in `@react-native-community/datetimepicker`:** it would replace a working, tested picker with a new native module (and a new dev-client build) for no user-visible gain. That's a speculative change under `CLAUDE.md`.
- **Changing the default to the next whole hour:** the current default is a deliberate choice with its own test. Say if you want it changed and it's a two-line change plus a test.

## Verification

- `npx jest --ci src/__tests__/BookingComposerScreen.test.tsx src/__tests__/CalendarPicker.test.tsx src/__tests__/sessionTime.test.ts` → 82 passed
- `npm run typecheck -w @protin/mobile && npm run lint -w @protin/mobile` → clean (no code change)

## Review follow-up (Codex, APPROVE_WITH_COMMENTS → wording fixed in `bc365a0`)

Codex confirmed the calendar, the disabled past dates, the start/end wheels, that there are no date/time text inputs, the local timestamps with no `Z`, and both commit dates. One correction: "a same-day start in the past is blocked before submit" overstated it. `computeValidationError` is a `useMemo` on `[date, startTime, endTime]` (`BookingComposerScreen.tsx:67–70`) and `handleSubmit` doesn't re-run it, so picking today 15:00 at 14:55 and tapping Send at 15:05 passes the client check (the server accepts starts up to 1 h in the past). NB-005 now says exactly that. **Re-validating at submit is a small behaviour change, listed for the owner, not done here.**

## Repair (Codex B2)
Codex's independent verification (2026-10-19) found the S14 tick overstated. The picker premise was stale, but two acceptance criteria were still unmet. At 10:30 local the default sent `2026-10-20T09:00:00`, not `2026-10-19T11:00:00`. And a start that passed while the screen stayed open was still sent, because validation was memoised on the pickers and limited to today. Both of Codex's tests failed.

**Decision (owner, 2026-10-19):** keep the in-house `CalendarPicker`/`TimeWheelPicker`. A native module adds nothing user-visible, so `@react-native-community/datetimepicker` is not adopted. Recorded in `todo.md` R4 and in NB-005.

Changes (mobile only; payload and server validation untouched):
- `lib/sessionTime.ts`: **`nextWholeHour(now)`** replaces `defaultDate()`/`defaultStartTime()`. 10:30 → 11:00 today; 10:00 → 11:00; from 23:00 it rolls into 00:00 tomorrow, including across months. `computeValidationError` now flags a past start on **any** date: a start picked yesterday is past today.
- `BookingComposerScreen.tsx`: opens on the next whole hour → +1 h. Validation is computed every render (no longer memoised on the pickers), so it reflects the clock. **`handleSubmit` checks again at submit**; if the start has passed, it re-renders to show the existing "Choose a future start time." and makes **no API call**. The client requires start ≥ now, stricter than the server's 1-hour tolerance, so it never sends a start the server would reject as past. `startsAt`/`endsAt` are still local `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:00` with no `Z` (W7-003).
- `docs/staging/KNOWN_ISSUES.md` NB-005 describes the new behaviour and the picker decision.

Tests:
- **Codex's two regressions, as written** ("review original S14 acceptance"): fake clock at 2026-10-19 10:30 → the default payload is `T11:00:00`; then the clock moves past the start while mounted → Send makes no request. **Both fail on the old head `bc365a0`** (`Received: "2026-10-20T09:00:00"`; 1 call) and pass here.
- New: a start 5 minutes past (inside the server's tolerance) shows the error, disables Send, and clears once a later start is picked. After 23:00 the default is `00:00 → 01:00` tomorrow. In `sessionTime.test.ts`: `nextWholeHour` cases, and an earlier-day start counts as past.
- The composer suite now runs on a fixed local clock (Date only, timers real) at 08:30. Its existing 09:00 → 10:00 expectations are unchanged; only the date is today instead of tomorrow.
- Gates: typecheck, lint, **728 mobile tests**. Composer and `sessionTime` suites also pass with `TZ=UTC` on Node 20 (CI's runtime).

Rebased onto `main` `c03d014`; force-pushed `bc365a0` → `dca4c90`. The old S14 `todo.md` commit was dropped (main already has that text). **Re-titled** from "docs(staging): mark NB-005 resolved; S14 picker already shipped in May (S14)".

body:
## 基线与风险

当前 native 服务栈仍使用单次 CI 消费；独立确认尚未可见时会立即拒绝。本 PR 将 #1160 已修正的真实有界等待闭包接入包含负向恢复的当前栈，等待期间持续核验原 head/proof/期限，异常仍终止。

- **risk:high**：CI 消费控制流、请求/响应体/最终返回 deadline；仅 GET，默认关闭。
- Base #1170：`56aca50844ecd85aefe9818d8f9e4be0df063d8c`，`feat/cla-slot-negative-recovery-20261018`。
- Head：`f73a4b17b89f58e4595f3581afd2fe8ecaf6a90b`；tree：`c789030cfa5b58a859d060526062a81450150ec0`，与实际最终受测暂存树一致。
- 九个CI运行时/部署提案/测试文件逐字来自 #1160 `907af3f3920a62bbc52712c1e9fcf9da371f54d5`；新基线完整组合重新实跑，不沿用其旧CI或正式审查结论。
- 与 #1170 叠栈，保留其全部恢复及变异用例。保持 Draft，不合并/部署/启用，不改workflow、权限、凭据、资源或真实法律材料。

## What this changes

CLI调用真实有界等待入口，consumer与wait共同约束 transport、body、pause及最终返回。配置只来自可信输入，wait/provider默认关闭；只有完整owned-check枚举缺席或首次authority精确proof_not_confirmed可等待。其他错误及第二次authority pending直接终止。

每次重新读取可信main policy/正文、原事件head/base、run/attempt/proof并执行两次独立实时authority核验；不复用旧成功。原proof的到期会收紧单调deadline，保留亚秒wall-clock精度、初始化/回退检查和已验证快照的timer映射。

本片没有 #1163 timing planner，也没有真实CI接线。group仍在网络前拒绝，不新增Merge queues权限或移植未批准的完整前缀策略。等待不能代替独立恢复事件，不能让manual/unknown算confirmed或延长旧proof。

## How it was verified

[实际最终组合命令、退出码及逐文件SHA](https://github.com/Tavotto/Tavotto/blob/f73a4b17b89f58e4595f3581afd2fe8ecaf6a90b/docs/implementation/cla-ci-wait/evidence/verification.json)；[原文日志包](https://github.com/Tavotto/Tavotto/blob/f73a4b17b89f58e4595f3581afd2fe8ecaf6a90b/docs/implementation/cla-ci-wait/evidence/raw-logs.json)逐成员保存原始UTF-8及SHA256；[契约及边界](https://github.com/Tavotto/Tavotto/blob/f73a4b17b89f58e4595f3581afd2fe8ecaf6a90b/docs/implementation/cla-ci-wait/README.md)。

| 实际命令/核验 | 退出码 | 结果 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`（已记录完整展开argv） | 0 | 582/582，0 fail/skip |
| `python3 tests/migration.test.py` | 0 | 4/4 |
| `node tests/mutation-smoke.mjs` | 0 | 187项，保留父168及等待19 |
| CI专项 | 0 | 51 pass |
| 最终基线独立组合核验 | 0 | 14 pass；4唯一落点变异均AssertionError/1 |
| 实际转义regex标题见证反例 | 0 | 选中mutant实际AssertionError/1；标题兼容有效 |
| `git diff --cached --check` | 0 | 最终暂存树通过 |

独立组合实测manual/unknown耗尽仍不确认、不重发；新失败见证释放、撤销/429/503及短proof都能终止在途CI。每次真实native verification路径实测11 SQL、1个合成远端GET，两次authority核验仍独立执行。

这是**真实CI/native verification代码 + 固定预存合成confirmed记录 + 进程内GET Response**，不是实际GitHub HTTP、真实D1/浏览器端到端或法律验收。没有正向发布、时钟推进跨成功发布边界或被拒测试变体。服务真实token交换、配额、成本与延迟未验收。

## Hosted / review status

当前 head `f73a4b17b89f58e4595f3581afd2fe8ecaf6a90b` 的 [CLA Cloudflare offline checks #32](https://github.com/Tavotto/Tavotto/actions/runs/39142071154) 已成功；已读取 [job 原始日志](https://github.com/Tavotto/Tavotto/actions/runs/39142071154/job/117718361369)，核对真实 checkout SHA、`npm ci --ignore-scripts` 和 `npm run check` 的完整串行执行。

- typecheck `tsc --noEmit`：退出0。
- Node：582/582，fail/cancelled/skipped均0；migration：4/4。
- production build：20 inputs；未部署。
- mutation：187项均实际 selected exit1，harness退出0；job success且无error标记。
- 当前头首次完整[代码审查](https://github.com/Tavotto/Tavotto/pull/1171#issuecomment-6251953995)和自动[安全审查](https://github.com/Tavotto/Tavotto/pull/1171#issuecomment-6251955355)均已完成，均无发现；[汇总](https://github.com/Tavotto/Tavotto/pull/1171#issuecomment-6251924603)的两项完整 commit_sha 均为 `f73a4b17b89f58e4595f3581afd2fe8ecaf6a90b`，status=completed，has_any_findings/has_unresolved_findings=false。review_threads=0。仅一次首次完整请求，未用定向复核，未重复触发。

该运行验收此服务离线编译/构建/合成测试，不是完整main/full CI或真实GitHub/D1端到端验收。没有沿用父head或donor绿灯；父PR #1170有其自己的精确head成功运行。此前本地npm E403未重试，未配置替代凭据、代理/镜像或环境。

#1160/#1169无额外审查，#1163当前head正式覆盖不足仍保留。本PR不改写旧summary或把独立合成证据当正式覆盖。

## 剩余边界与人工决策

- #1170只解决可核实失败事实出现后的持槽恢复；永久缺失记录仍可能持槽。等待不解除该边界，也不以expiry清槽。
- 实际wakeup/deadline仍未闭合。D1 due不是事件；两分钟recovery可耗尽120秒proof，一分钟也不能覆盖现有最坏处理预算。新事件契约/更紧准入或Queue/DO等资源方案须另选并验收，本轮不配置。
- native merge-group成员策略、所需权限与真实实现未完成；用户尚未批准完整队列前缀或Merge queues权限。
- 可信main接线需先让受审源码落main，再另PR接线；完整main/full CI、真实平台/资源/密钥托管和最终启用仍待验收/批准。当前不合并、不改保护规则或生产。

## Contributor agreement

- [ ] I have completed the Tavotto CLA process, or this PR is made by an account explicitly exempt under the repository's CLA policy.

Closes #3

## 변경
- `src/lib/mdx-doc/split.ts`
  - `parseMdx(source, syntax)`: 파일 맨 앞 ESM을 문장 단위로 `import` / `metadata` / `export` 조각으로 나누고, 문장 사이 공백·줄바꿈·주석은 `gap` 조각으로 원문 그대로 보관. 나머지는 `body`
  - `printMdx(doc)`: 조각 원문을 이어 붙인다. 다시 생성하는 부분이 없다
  - 파싱 실패(`parse-error`), 본문 뒤 ESM(`esm-after-content`)은 `ok: false`로 원문만 보관 → 원문 모드 전용
- ESM 경계는 micromark mdxjs 파서 결과를 쓴다. estree 문장 위치가 파일 전체 기준 offset이고 `;`까지 포함하는 것을 확인

author: chrisdaltas
body:
Gap list §3 #28 (phone only, desktop unchanged).

## What you see now

- On the phone, tapping an AI expert's ranking in Community opens it in **Rankings**, on that expert's own ranking page. This works from every place the ranking appears: the Rankings tab rows, the "Rankings this week" shelf, the For you "Latest" shelf, the Latest page and the updated-by rows.
- The page shows the expert's card (avatar, name, title, note), then **Start my ranking from this**, then the tiered players.
- The card keeps **Like, Comments, Save and Share**, so opening the ranking from Community doesn't lose them. The Community detail and the Rankings card now share one action row.
- **Start my ranking from this** opens the editor with the expert's order. If you already have that ranking, it first asks whether to start from this one or open yours. The copy only reads the expert's saved players and never calls AI generation. A test checks this.
- **Back** returns you to Community on the tab you left (Rankings tab, or the Latest page).
- A ranking for one position opens at that position. An overall ranking opens at the position of its #1 player, the one its Community row shows. A chip for each position it ranks keeps the others one tap away. The link also carries the ranking's scoring, so the points shown match it.
- Small fix: the expert's tab used to be cut off at the right edge of the tab row. It now scrolls fully into view with the normal side margin.

## Calls made where the design was silent

- **A person's ranking still opens the Community detail.** People's rankings have no Rankings view yet.
- **When an expert is switched off**, their rankings also open the Community detail. They no longer show a "not available" page.
- **With Rankings switched off**, every ranking opens the Community detail.

## Open point for Chris

- **Scoring of a copy.** A copy starts your new ranking at Half PPR, following the "no scoring chosen = Half PPR" ruling. The design instead carries over the expert's scoring (e.g. PPR). On the app, a season ranking's scoring belongs to the whole board, so switching it would also relabel your other positions. This is left at Half PPR until you decide.

## Checks run

- `npm run type-check`: clean.
- `npm run lint`: no warnings or errors.
- `npx vitest run --project unit`: 412 files, 7,268 tests, all passed. New tests cover the Community links, the Rankings card's actions and the copy path, including a check that it never reaches AI generation.
- Production build: skipped locally, because it would overwrite the running dev server's build. Vercel's preview build covers it.
- Network: no request to any AI generation, quota or Anthropic URL during any phone run, light or dark.

## Screenshots (described, not attached)

Phone at 390×844, light and dark, compared with the handoff's S4 view:
- An expert's ranking from For you, Latest and the Rankings tab opens the Rankings page with the expert's tab active and fully in view. The page has no sideways scroll.
- @dev_user's own ranking and a person's list still open the Community detail, with Like, Comments, Save and Share.
- With the expert switched off, their ranking opens the working Community detail.
- Like and Save stay set after a reload. They were unset again after the test.

body: Creating or opening a document spent about 300ms on an empty page before the editor could start. React keeps a Suspense fallback on screen for 300ms after the real page is ready, and this route's fallback was a blank shell. The document page now renders the workspace directly. A document set in a built-in face (Arial, Georgia, Times, Courier) also no longer waits on the Google Fonts catalog. ## Measured Same machine, production build, click **Blank document** until the editor had a real size: | | Before | After | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Visible editor | 465ms | 183–207ms | | Playwright visible selector | 866ms | 275–280ms | The blank shell was on screen at ~75ms and the real workspace arrived at ~410ms. That gap was a 271ms timer inside React (`Throttled`), the remainder of the 300ms fallback hold. After the change the workspace and the editor show up together, and typing into the new document works. A cold download of Google's font catalog is 2.7MB and took 210ms from this network. It used to block the first open of a default (Arial) document. Those faces are not Google fonts, so opening one no longer asks for the catalog. Warm, that request was only a few milliseconds; the 300ms hold was the change a person would feel. ## Left alone Screenshot and PDF rendering, tool schemas, and document serialization. A headless page picture is still about 300ms of rasterizing, and the render route's own fallback does not add the 300ms hold on a full page load (its reveal script runs before that timer is armed). Home-page load was not on this path.

author: bkataru
body:
## What

The turn log records one line per HTTP request. An agent loop — one user turn — is served by MANY sequential requests: the model asks for tools, the harness runs them, the model asks again, and only the last request produces the answer. Nothing in a per-request record groups those, so "how many rounds deep did this turn go, and how long did it take" could not be answered from the log at all.

This adds session and loop identity, and a query surface to read the depth distribution.

## Changes

- **`loop_tracker`** groups requests into a loop keyed by a session id — an `x-nima-session` header, else a salted, non-reversible fingerprint of the conversation's first user message. A turn boundary is detected structurally, never by reading content: a request whose FINAL message is a `user` message begins a turn, because every later round ends with the client sending back a `tool` result.
- **A round is counted when its request BEGINS**, not when it completes. The proxy writes its error records from sites that carry no session, so counting at completion would drop every failed round — and 8.4% of live traffic returns 504. `loop_rounds - loop_completed_rounds` is therefore exactly "rounds that started and never reported", and `loop_model_ms` covers completed rounds only rather than inventing durations.
- **A `loop` record** is written when a loop closes, carrying rounds, wall time, summed model time, tool calls and the last finish reason. `ended_at` comes from the loop's own last activity, never the closing clock, so a swept loop does not report a wall time inflated by the sweep period. A sweeper thread closes each session's final turn, which has no successor request to close it.
- **`tool_call_distinct`** counts logical tool calls by the delta's `index`. `tool_call_count` is unchanged and still counts fragment ENTRIES, so its existing contract and test hold; it overcounts, which is now documented rather than silent.
- **`nimaproxy-query`** gains `loops` (per-loop table) and `depth` (percentiles plus a histogram of rounds).

## What was measured

`tool_call_count` overcounts badly. On live traffic a single logical tool call arrived as 4 fragment frames, and the production mean was 80.2 entries per response against `request_message_count` deltas implying 1–4 real calls. `index` is present on every fragment while `id` appears only on the first, so `index` is the only joinable key.

## Verification

- 391 lib tests plus the four CI integration targets (118 tests) pass; `fmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` are clean.
- The new tests were mutation-proved: reverting the boundary guard, the distinct keying, or the wall-time mapping each makes its test fail.
- Two defects were found only by exercising the tracker against a running proxy, and are fixed here:

  1. A boundary that depended on a completed round merges two genuine user turns when a round fails (a 504 never bumps it) or when its record lands after the next request has already begun. Reproduced live: two requests fired back to back made the second continue loop 1, while the identical pair separated by a 4s gap opened loop 2. The boundary now also compares the request's message count, which is what actually changes when a conversation moves on.
  2. `loop` records published `last_request_id`, which exists for exactly one purpose — letting the first-byte writer read back the id it generated so the completion record can share it. A loop summary has no such join, so publishing its id only overwrites the id a request is waiting to read. Measured consequence: `stream_observability` became flaky, asserting against another turn's `finish_reason`. Loop records no longer publish it.

body:
## Summary

The three client wrappers (`ssh`, `ssh-tailscale`, `scp-tailscale`) each carried their own copy of the same arg-parsing and session logic. That duplication is exactly how `ssh` and `ssh-tailscale` drifted apart before the v1.5 host-key fix — one verified host keys, the other auto-accepted them.

This extracts the shared logic into a new `extensions/sshk/bin/sshk-common.sh`, sourced by all three wrappers:

| Helper | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `sshk_known_hosts_flags` | emits `-y` only when `/root/.ssh/known_hosts` is unwritable |
| `sshk_identity_path` / `sshk_map_identity` | `-i <name>` → `kindle_<name>_key`, or absolute path passthrough |
| `sshk_lookup_alias` | resolve a `hosts.conf` alias into host/port/key without `eval` |
| `sshk_native_key_opts` | first-run native-key bootstrap |
| `sshk_inhibit_screensaver` / `sshk_restore_screensaver` | `preventScreenSaver` trap |

## Behaviour is unchanged

A differential harness runs the **HEAD** wrappers and the refactored ones against identical stubs and confirms **byte-identical `dbclient` argv across 43 cases**: plain targets, custom ports, `-i` name/absolute, `-L`, dangling flags, unknown flags, multiple positionals, aliases (with/without named keys, with `-i` override), missing `hosts.conf`, forced auto-accept, and all scp modes.

## Also fixed

Each wrapper now resolves its own directory with POSIX parameter expansion instead of the external `dirname`, so it still finds its sidecar files (the shared library included) when `PATH` is empty or `dirname` is unavailable. This is the case the existing sealed-`PATH` `ssh-tailscale` test exercises.

## Tests

Functional tests grow **47 → 64 assertions**: the library ships and defines each helper, all three wrappers source it, the known_hosts probe and the screensaver calls are defined in exactly one file (so a per-wrapper copy cannot creep back in), plus direct unit checks of the helpers.

- `./tests/run-tests.sh` → 64 passed, 0 failed
- `./tests/kindle-sim/run-sim.sh` → 23 passed, 0 failed
- `shellcheck -e SC2086,SC2016 …` → clean
- `sh -n` on all shipping scripts → clean

Docs updated: `ARCHITECTURE.md` (new component section), `CHANGELOG.md` (`Unreleased`), `.gemini/AGENTS.md` (file index + guidance).

body:
The finishing reduction now has a Mojo-native proof-term checker and a parameterized execution model. Checked proofs show that every complete legal modeled trace returns the same correlated rank, token, and Boolean invalid flag as an independent input fold, with counts, token bounds, register names, trees, and schedules remaining parameters.

## Changes

- Add the proof-term kernel, checked Nat/Done inductive definitions and eliminators, derived arithmetic/Base equations, and finishing-loop coverage and termination certificates.
- Add flexible reduction descriptors, a host event interpreter, provenance reconstruction, and whole-trace correctness proofs.
- Derive a total Nat join algebra and bounded rank/token record encoding, culminating in the 183-definition correlated-record trace theorem.
- Integrate the descriptors with token selection and its benchmark route; add compiler rejection fixtures, independent native oracles, and documentation of the remaining trust boundary.
- Keep the recorded inference explorer reproducible from hash-checked historical source snapshots, including its original reduction fixtures and compiler receipt inputs.

## Validation

- Sealed host qualifications passed for phase commutation, complete execution, derived join algebra, and correlated-record execution.
- The final record profile includes a compile-time positive and native controls, seven semantic compiler rejections, one resource-preflight rejection, and twelve constructor regression commands.
- The finite UInt32 oracle passed 25,145 cases / 36,937 result records. Documentation tests (5), package-boundary tests (3), the native oracle, and staged whitespace checks passed again for publication.
- Explorer generation checks and all 40 explorer integrity/provenance tests pass, including standalone rendering after current source changes and rejection of tampered or retargeted historical sources. The recorded HTML and compiler receipts are unchanged.
- Final record qualification resumed five verified historical commands plus five fresh commands; it is not a fresh uninterrupted full unittest run.
- Proof publication commit `5b79e0b` binds the 646 maintained source files to the sealed snapshot, with only audited terminal-blank-line normalization in 91 files. Historical receipts and source archives remain unchanged; generated binaries and full traces remain outside Git.

## Remaining qualification

The documented full `uv run --locked llm-mojo validate` workflow passed oracle preparation and frozen-anchor checks. It was stopped during Python test discovery after confirming that current `xcrun -f metal` exits 69 because the Xcode license is unaccepted. Complete numerical/device validation remains pending.

Universal native-word and source-to-model correspondence, collective memory visibility/progress, and full-model floating-point determinism remain open. No GPU performance claim is made. The new token-selection benchmark variants also need explicit Metal route checks; the existing general route-smoke loop does not cover them.

The generic proof kernel, admission specification, compiler/evaluator, and allocation implementation remain trusted. See `docs/finishing-executor.md`, `docs/finishing-join-algebra.md`, and `docs/finishing-record-execution.md` for the exact contracts and reproduction commands.

_Requested by **Jason** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01A5yQtY5a3RzSQuJ4aTm2sL?thread=cmsg_01A5yQtY5a3RzSQuJ4aTm2sLDapSefk6nufMVHUFcztVP2)_

Before: On a Mac, Option was always sent to the terminal as Alt, so a German keyboard couldn't type `@` (Option+L), and Option+digit switched tabs, so a UK Mac couldn't type `#` (Option+3). On Windows, AltGr arrives as Ctrl+Alt, so `@`, `€` or `ą` went out as a control code, and AltGr+0 (`}` on a German keyboard) reset the text size. Alt+Backspace sent a plain Backspace instead of deleting a word.

After: On a Mac or iPad, Option types whatever the keyboard layout puts on it, as the Mac's own Terminal does. A new setting, **Option works as Alt** (Settings, Hardware keyboard), brings back the old behaviour for emacs and shell word moves. On a Mac, tabs are Cmd+1 to Cmd+9, and the menu and help show that. On Windows, a Ctrl+Alt press that comes with a printable character types that character, ahead of any shortcut. Alt+Backspace, Alt+Enter, Alt+Tab and Alt+Escape send ESC first, as every other Alt key does.

Fixes review finding 20 (non-US keyboards can't type `@ [ ] { } | \ ~ #`).

How: `TerminalView` only treats Option as Alt on Apple platforms when `KeyOptions.optionAsMeta` is on; otherwise the key goes to the input method like any other character. On Windows, `TerminalView._onKey` types a Ctrl+Alt press with a printable character first thing, before the window's shortcuts, paste and the text size keys (unless an input method is composing). `KeyMapper.bytesFor` puts ESC in front of the five keys that had no Alt form. `AppShortcuts.tab` and `isReserved` use Cmd for digits on Apple platforms and Alt elsewhere; Alt+arrows for panes are unchanged. GUIDE.md, the help screen and the changelog are updated.

Tests: new tests in `key_mapper_test.dart` (Alt in front of the five keys) and `terminal_view_test.dart` (Option on a Mac with and without the setting; tab shortcuts per platform; on Windows, AltGr+0 and AltGr and + type `}` and `~` without changing the text size, AltGr+Shift characters win over paste and the tab shortcut, and Ctrl+Alt with no character is still a control sequence). Each fails with its part of the fix undone. `flutter analyze` is clean and all 253 Flutter tests pass locally. No Rust changes.

author: sharathsphd
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"SharathSPhD"} -->
_Requested by **S** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_014HQQb2TSwEX66QLPFLYM4D?thread=cmsg_014HQQb2TSwEX66QLPFLYM4DHdSCqnCHHU6D4tY3VBnH7f)_

Before: vocal tracks run about a minute and instrumentals two and a half, so the stream flipped between them and nothing settled.

After: with `STATION_SETS=1` the queue is arranged into sets. A block is 2 or 3 same-language vocal tracks (the next block changes language, so the "no more than 3 of one language in a row" rule still holds). Instrumentals sit between blocks and take at most 25% of the clock time (30% at midday and night). A new one is only added while the share is under 20% (25% midday and night), which lands the hourly share around 22%. At dawn no instrumental goes next to a devotional block. Ads never land inside a set. Language-locked listeners still get instrumentals, because they are language-neutral. Without the flag nothing changes.

Acceptance, checked by a simulation test over an hour of refills at six hours of the day: median uninterrupted block at least 3 minutes, instrumental share between 15% and 30%.

How: `lib/station/sets.ts` (`arrangeSets`, daypart policy), wired into `/api/station/queue`, which now also returns `set`, `fadeInMs`, `fadeOutMs` and `kind` on set tracks. The pool read tries the `kind` column (migration 0100) first and falls back to the old columns, so it works before 0100 is applied. The player ramps volume down over the last 2.5 s of a track and up over the first 2.5 s of the next one in a set (`lib/station/fade.ts`).

Honest limit: this is a dip-through-the-join, not an overlapping crossfade. A true overlap needs two audio elements or Web Audio, and iOS Safari ignores `audio.volume`, so there the tracks simply join with a hard cut. Please listen on a desktop browser and on a phone before turning the flag on.

Before turning it on: the pool needs admitted instrumental rows (migration 0100 applied, `kind = 'instrumental'`). With none, sets still group vocals and nothing else changes.

Tests: `tests/station-sets.test.ts` (grouping, language change, locked language, share caps by daypart, dawn devotional rule, the acceptance simulation, crossfade hints, volume ramps) and `tests/station-queue-sets.test.ts` (flag off, set fields, language-locked instrumentals, ads never inside a set). Lint, tsc and the full suite pass.

author: sakuya398-yamada
body:
## 概要
`weekday-issue-start` の手順 3 で作った `weekday-<番号>` への Edit/Write がブロックされていた。原因はプロジェクトの hook ではなく、Claude Code 組み込みの worktree 隔離だった。起動場所（worktree 内／メインチェックアウト）を最初に判定し、worktree 起動ならセッション自身の worktree で作業する手順に直す。

## 原因（実測で確定）
- `validate-edit-path` hook は、別 worktree 宛ての Edit/Write を exit 0 で通す（`.cjs` が `.claude/worktrees/` 配下を対象外にしている）。exit 1 が出るのはメインチェックアウト宛てだけで、これもブロックしない。一時リポジトリで再現スクリプトを使って確認した
- Claude Code の worktree 隔離（[公式「How Claude Code enforces isolation」](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md)）がブロックしていた。`isolation: worktree` のサブエージェント（Claude Code 2.1.302）で実測した結果:
  - 別 worktree への Write/Edit → 拒否（`This path is in a different worktree (...)`）
  - メインチェックアウトへの Write → 拒否
  - `git -C <メイン>` と `git -C <別 worktree>` → 読み取りだけでも拒否（`redirects git to the shared checkout via -C`）
  - `-C` なしで自分の worktree で打つ `git fetch` / `ls-remote` / `checkout --detach` / `checkout -b <name> --no-track origin/main` → 通る
- 手順 1-3（`weekday-sync-<PR番号>` の worktree 作成）も同じ制約に当たる。手順 1-1 / 1-4 の `git -C <repo>` も、今の版では同じ仕組みで拒否される（設計承認時に合わせて直すことを確認済み）

## 変更点
- `.claude/routines/weekday-issue-start.md`
  - 冒頭: `git rev-parse --git-dir` と `--git-common-dir` で起動場所（worktree 起動／メイン起動）を判定する。worktree 起動では git を `-C` なしで打つ、と明記
  - 手順 1-1 / 1-4: `git -C <repo>` をやめ、セッションの作業ディレクトリで打つ
  - 手順 1-3: worktree 起動ならセッションの worktree で `checkout --detach origin/<head>`、メイン起動なら従来どおり `weekday-sync-<PR番号>` を作る。detached にする理由と、push しなかった merge commit の扱いを更新
  - 手順 3: 起動場所ごとの表にする。worktree 起動ならセッションの worktree で `git checkout -b <branch> --no-track origin/main`、メイン起動なら従来どおり `weekday-<番号>` を作る（`--no-track` は #527 で Phase 2 に入った規約に揃えた）
  - 手順 3-2: `npm ci` は両方の起動場所で必要なまま。worktree には `node_modules` が無いことを実測で確認した。手順 1-3 で実行済みでも、ブランチを作ったあとにもう一度実行する
  - 手順 4: `<worktree>` を `<work>` に変更。needs-decision で終わるときの worktree 削除は、メイン起動のときだけにする

## テスト

author: nuwansh
body: ## What and why Roadmap **t02, "Make the production compose stack start"**. `docker-compose.prod.yml` had never been started; when it was, almost every part of it was broken (list below). It is now one complete file that comes up healthy from a fresh checkout, and a script and a CI job start it for real so it cannot go unnoticed again. - **One front door.** `web` (nginx) serves the web app and passes `/api` and `/cable` (live updates) to the API, on `HTTP_PORT` (80 by default). Plain HTTP; a TLS proxy in front is documented (HTTPS itself is d15). It looks the API up again every few seconds, so replacing the API container (an upgrade) needs no nginx restart (tried: recovered in about 8 s). - **The stack:** `web`, `api`, `sidekiq`, PostgreSQL 16, Redis, a Mosquitto broker with a login, and **SeaweedFS as the S3 file storage**. Only the front door and the broker's port 1883 are published; the database, Redis, the API and the storage are internal. - **Standalone, not an overlay.** The old file was meant to be combined with `docker-compose.yml`, which leaked the dev database and Redis ports to the network and merged dev settings in. `make prod` now uses it alone. - **Pinned versions** for every image in both compose files and both Dockerfiles (d04's "no latest tag" part; publishing images is still d04). - **`.env.example` is now the install file**: the required block first, each line with the `openssl` command that makes it; `.env` reaches the containers through `env_file`, so any setting in the README table works without editing the compose file. - **`make prod / prod-status / prod-logs / prod-stop / backup / restore`**, and a README "Install on a server" section. - **`bin/check_production_stack`** starts the stack from a fresh checkout (builds the images, waits for health, checks the front door, a WebSocket upgrade and refusal, first-run setup, sign-in, System Health, a backup and a restore) and removes everything. **A new CI job runs it.** ### Decision for review: SeaweedFS instead of MinIO `minio/minio` cannot be pulled from Docker Hub any more (`repository does not exist or may require login`; `quay.io` answered 401), and the old compose files used `:latest`. I chose SeaweedFS 4.48: Apache-2.0, official Docker Hub image, speaks the S3 calls this app uses (create bucket, put, list, head, get, delete, a streamed 300 MB download), takes its login from two environment variables, refuses a wrong or unknown key, and idles at about 95 MB. The `MINIO_*` setting names are unchanged. If you would rather use something else (Garage is smaller but needs a layout step at first start and is AGPL), it is one service in two files. ### Found by starting it, and fixed here 1. **The `Dockerfile` did not build** (no libyaml headers, so `bundle install` stopped at `psych`). It also sent 400 MB of `node_modules` as build context. 2. **Uploaded photos and the logo could not be opened by any browser.** Their links redirected to the storage server's internal address (`http://s3:8333/...`). They are now served through the app (`rails_storage_proxy_path`). Two existing specs asserted the redirect. 3. **Live updates were refused on every plain-HTTP install.** `assume_ssl` makes Action Cable take every request to be `https://`, so the same-origin check failed against `http://`. `APP_URL` and `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` are now the allowed origins (`FixflowOrigins`). 4. **Every sensor reading was stored twice**: the web server and the worker each subscribed to the broker. Now only the worker does; `MQTT_SUBSCRIBER=true|false` overrides. 5. The broker needed a password file that did not exist, and (once made) was unreadable by the user it runs as. 6. The README gave sensors the wrong MQTT topic and payload, the wrong HTTP route payload, and an `IOT_API_KEY` that nothing reads (the route authenticates with keys from Settings, API Keys). Corrected, and checked by publishing real messages. 7. `RAILS_LOG_TO_STDOUT`, `CORS_ORIGINS`, `RAILS_MASTER_KEY` and `IOT_API_KEY` were set in the compose files and read by nothing. Removed; a spec now fails on any compose setting the app never reads. 8. Redis was `allkeys-lru`, which can evict queued background jobs; now `noeviction`. 9. The development compose file could not start either (the image had no development gems; no secrets). It now runs with no configuration and uses the same storage image. 10. The bucket default differed between `storage.yml` and the setup task; the compose file now sets both bucket names. ### Not changed, but worth knowing - `Api::V1::Iot::IngestController` (the only reader of `IOT_API_KEY`) is not routed. Dead code; I left it. - Redis, the `postgres` service container and the dev `.env` handling in the CI `test` job still use floating image tags. ## How it was checked - **1,547 backend and 778 web tests** (was 1,520 / 778); rubocop, brakeman (0 warnings), bundler-audit, `tsc -b`, `npm run build`, `web:check_routes` pass. - **28 deliberate breakages each made a test fail** (a path on `proxy_pass`, `Host` without the port, a 1 MB upload limit, no WebSocket upgrade, a published database port, a `latest` tag, a missing bucket setting, Redis eviction, the broker's file ownership, a missing service, a setting nothing reads, no libyaml, the API address not set in the web build, an unpinned base image, a missing required setting, the origin list, the one-listener rule, both `MQTT_SUBSCRIBER` values, and both file-link redirects). One of my first mutations was invalid (a syntax error) and was redone properly. Every touched file was restored byte for byte. - **The stack, started for real from a fresh copy of the repo (no `.env`, no ignored files) with `bin/check_production_stack`: it passed**, including the Docker build, seven healthy services, WebSocket upgrade and refusal, first-run setup (and a second sign-up refused), System Health ok for database, Redis, worker, broker and storage, a nightly backup made and listed, and a restore that removed data added after the backup. - **By hand on the same stack:** a 2.4 MB photo uploaded through the front door (nginx's default would refuse above 1 MB) and fetched back byte-identical with no sign-in header, like an ``; WebSocket with the right origin connects, a foreign origin and a missing or bad token are refused; the broker refuses no login and a wrong password; a published reading becomes one row (two before the fix); HTTP ingest with a key made under Settings works and a wrong key gets 401; replacing only the API container recovered through the same front door in about 8 s; `down` then `up` kept the data, the photo and the broker; `make backup` and `make restore FROM= CONFIRM=yes` round-tripped; the images contain no `.env`, `spec`, `apps` or `node_modules`; a missing required setting is named by `docker compose` before anything starts. - **The development stack** (`docker compose up`, the README's `db:create db:migrate db:seed`) starts with no configuration and the seeded admin signs in. ## Not tested - **Never opened in a browser or on a phone.** The web app was fetched and its files, headers and caching checked with curl, and the WebSocket with a Node client; nothing was rendered. - **Not on Linux or a small server.** Everything ran in Docker Desktop on macOS (arm64); the CI job is the first x86 Linux run. First start builds both images (5 to 10 minutes here) and pulls about 1 GB; memory use was not measured against the 2 GB the README suggests (d18). - **No HTTPS** (d15) and **no published images** (d04): the images are built on the server. - **Not a real mail server**, **not a real sensor**, **not MinIO** (SeaweedFS only), **not a real company's data volume**. - The dev compose file was tested with host ports moved aside (my local Postgres and Redis use 5432 and 6379). - `make` targets were run on macOS; `make restore` with `FROM=latest` and a named backup went through the same path as the file form, but only the file form was run through `make`. ## Existing i

author: chris-beckman
body:
Models need accurate workspace paths, callable-tool guidance, and an explicit distinction between internal tool-step text and user-visible updates.

Explain workspace-relative paths when one folder is attached. Preserve implementation guidance while writing is loadable, so an initial read-only tool set does not reduce an implementation request to a prose proposal. Respect requested delegation and omit the guidance when writing is unavailable. Show exact loader calls for file creation, editing, and commands only while each tool is loadable; remove its hint once offered. Give `PROGRESS_MISSING` a valid JSON checklist example with escaped line breaks and retain the instruction to retry the rejected operation after saving progress.

Explain that assistant text alongside tool calls is hidden. Teach `surface_note` for meaningful updates and answers to mid-task check-ins; describe the wait boundary only when both tools are offered. Keep citation handles as strings, avoid routine tool narration, and remove the misleading prose distinction from wait resume. No tool-selection or Bialy changes.

Fixes #902. The history framing fix is separate in #956, and the wait guard is separate in #957.

Validation: all 405 prompt test and subtest results pass after the loadable-write role change, including transitions between offered, loadable and unavailable tools. Final size budgets pass without raising limits. Earlier recovery-example validation passed 1,064 guidance/OAR results. The OAR copy uses the upstream 1.0 binding grammar and changes no policy decision.

Fresh live runs on a local candidate containing these changes and the other isolated fixes exercised both models. Ministral loaded write and created the requested CLI and web files, but neither task passed: the CLI hit provider JSON errors and failed plain output and missing-file handling; the web app skipped browser interaction checks and failed completion persistence, accessible labeling and mobile layout. Three of five independent CLI probes and six of nine browser probes passed. This change does not establish end-to-end Ministral reliability.

GLM's final-candidate task-list app passed all eight independent browser checks, including completion persistence, deletion, keyboard entry and mobile layout. A preceding CLI smoke passed six independent probes and demonstrated the repository freshness correction. These are smoke checks, not statistical controls. Exact candidate trees, binary hashes and raw requests are retained with the local run manifests.

A focused GLM live check before the loadable-write role change ran a two-minute background build, answered a scripted check-in after a parked wait through a grounded visible note, resumed waiting, then read the output and reported success. This is a smoke check of communication behavior, not a statistical control.

Hold for review. Do not enqueue or merge.

author: harshanandak
body:
Pull requests here had a template, but it asked for "what and why" and a proof list, so descriptions came out in different shapes and were hard to skim. This rewrites the template so a PR written from it reads like T3 Code's own PRs: a plain opening, topic sections, concrete before and after, and a verification list with links.

## What the template asks for now

- **A short leading comment sets the rules.** Plain-words conventional commit title, no internal codes, written for someone new, and no machine-local paths or links.
- **The body follows one order.** Opening, 2–4 topic sections with bold takeaways, Before / after, What review found, Notes for review, Verification.
- **The closing lines are fixed.** "Reviewed with Codex code review: N rounds.", a Tracking line, and a Models section. There is no tool-branding footer.

## Before / after

- When someone opens a PR: before, they saw "What and why", "Before / after", "Proof", "Tracking", "Models" with one-word hints; after, they see the T3 Code order with short hints for each part.
- When a PR has review rounds: before, there was no place for them; after, "What review found" lists each blocker as a user-visible failure plus its fix, with minor findings deferred by issue id.
- When a PR links evidence: before, "Proof" took any link; after, "Verification" asks for test links pinned to the head commit and the CI run for the current head, and a **Not verified:** line.

## What review found

No review rounds yet; this is a template-only change.

## Notes for review

- Only `.github/pull_request_template.md` changes. No code, no tests.
- The template is meant to be short. Hints are one line each, so authors delete them as they fill in.

## Verification

- Compared against the descriptions of two T3 Code PRs (pingdotgg/t3code #18124 and #17082) for section order and tone.
- CI for the head commit: see the checks on this PR.

**Not verified:** the template has not yet been used for a real PR other than this one.

Reviewed with Codex code review: 0 rounds so far.

Tracking: Kernel issue c07a43a5

body:
## Summary
The whole site can now be switched between **English (default)**, **繁體中文**, **日本語** and **한국어** with a globe button in the header.

**How it works**
- `src/i18n/`: an `I18nProvider` with typed dictionaries. `en.ts` is the source of truth, and `zh-TW.ts`, `ja.ts` and `ko.ts` must match its shape (TypeScript enforces this).
- The visitor's choice is saved in `localStorage` (failures are caught), and `<html lang>` and `data-lang` update on switch.
- Noto Sans/Serif TC/JP/KR load from Google Fonts only when that language is picked. Per-language font stacks live in `index.css`.
- Covers every visible string: menus, landing page, all 18 demos, guides, legends, explanations, fact chips, aria labels, and `document.title` on demo pages.
- **Step narration** is produced by the algorithm logic through a messages object (`SORT_MESSAGES`, `SEARCH_MESSAGES`, `BST_MESSAGES`, `HEAP_MESSAGES`), English by default. The logic stays pure and the existing tests are unchanged.
- BST, heap and hash-table pages store *what happened* rather than the rendered sentence, so a language switch re-narrates the current state.
- The registry now holds only structure (ids, categories, icons, colours, components). Names, taglines and facts come from the dictionaries.
- `**bold**` markers in translated sentences are rendered by a small `Rich` component.
- Locale details:
  - lists use 、 in Chinese and Japanese; quoted words use 「」 there and “” in English and Korean;
  - Korean uses `word-break: keep-all`, with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` as a fallback;
  - on phones the language button shows only the globe icon.

**Tests**
- New `src/i18n/i18n.test.ts` walks the English dictionary and checks each translation has:
  - the same keys and the same array lengths;
  - the same arity for every function, and each function returns real text;
  - balanced `**` markers;
  - no more than 2% of sentences left in English.

## Testing
- `npm test`: 52 passed, 1 skipped (that skip is from #2). `npm run build` passes.
- Playwright, switching through all four languages:
  - `<html lang>` updates, headings and step narration change, and the choice survives a reload;
  - no console errors in any language;
  - no horizontal overflow at 360px on 11 pages × 4 languages;
  - the English pages and the scripted interactions from #2 still pass unchanged.

The translations were written by AI and checked mechanically, but not yet read by fluent speakers.

author: manas2297
body:
> **Stack:** `feat/ui-migration` ← #24 AI Monitor ← **this PR** ← remove Focus diagram.
> Review only the StitchDraw commit; the base moves forward as #24 merges.

## What

A new **Architecture** section in the sidebar with **StitchDraw**, a full whiteboard for system architecture diagrams. It's built on the MIT-licensed Excalidraw engine (`@excalidraw/excalidraw`, pinned to 0.18.1), so developers get the complete toolset: hand-drawn rendering, every shape and connector tool, keyboard shortcuts, shape libraries, image export, dark mode, and Mermaid-to-diagram.

- **Format:** drawings are `.stitchdraw` files, JSON tagged `"type": "stitchdraw"`. The engine's own Open / Save-to-disk items are replaced by **Import drawing…** and **Download .stitchdraw**.
- **Scoped per repo:**
  - local repos → `<repo>/docs/diagrams/` (versioned with the code)
  - remote-only repos → `~/.stitch/diagrams/<owner>-<name>/`
  - personal drawings → `~/.stitch/diagrams/personal/`
- **Drawing list:** create, rename, duplicate, delete; collapsible; reopens the last drawing per scope.
- **Autosave:** debounced, with a Saved / Unsaved / Saving / Failed indicator. Writes are atomic (temp file + rename), and rename/delete/duplicate wait for in-flight saves so a late save can't recreate a file.
- **Import:** header button, menu item, or drag-and-drop onto the canvas. `.stitchdraw` and legacy `.excalidraw` files become new drawings; dropped shape libraries merge into the shared library (`~/.stitch/diagrams/library.stitchdrawlib`).
- **Offline:** a small Vite plugin serves the editor's fonts locally, so it works in the desktop app without internet. The 12 MB CJK font is left out and falls back to the CDN.
- **Bundle:** the editor and its global CSS are lazy-loaded with the tab; the main bundle grows by about 6 KB.
- **Licensing:** the engine's MIT notice ships in `dist/licenses/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` (from `client/licenses/`).

The floating energy panel is hidden on this tab because it covered the editor's controls.

## API

`GET/POST /api/diagrams`, `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/diagrams/file`, `POST /api/diagrams/rename`, `GET/PUT /api/diagrams/library`. Names are validated (no path separators, max 100 characters), bodies must be `stitchdraw` / `stitchdrawlib` documents, and size is capped at 64 MB.

## Testing

- `go test ./internal/server/diagrams`: name validation and traversal, create/conflict/save/get/rename/delete, `.stitchdraw` extension and 0644 mode, rejection of raw Excalidraw documents, library round-trip.
- Headless Chrome end to end:
  - draw → autosave → `.stitchdraw` on disk with `type: stitchdraw`
  - a legacy `.excalidraw` file imported through the picker → converted `.stitchdraw`
  - the editor menu shows StitchDraw items only
  - layout checked at desktop and phone widths
- Each commit builds from a clean checkout.

## Known limitations

- Image export and **Download .stitchdraw** use browser downloads, which may not work inside the Wails desktop webview.
- The engine's Help dialog still links to Excalidraw's docs, and "Browse libraries" opens libraries.excalidraw.com.

author: joshka
body:
Follow-up to #771.

## Problem

`ObjectReadError::MissingReplacement { original, replacement }`, added in #771, holds two inline object IDs, which makes it the largest `ObjectReadError` variant (72 bytes on macOS). Windows paths are larger, so errors that embed `ObjectReadError` (`PushError`, `CloneError`) grow past clippy's 128-byte `result_large_err` bound there. The Windows all-features clippy run then fails, as seen on #773's full-ci jobs.

## Change

- `ObjectReadError::MissingReplacement` now holds only the absent replacement's ID, `MissingReplacement(ObjectId)`. The caller knows the ID it looked up, and `HistoryError::Read` already reports it.
- New unit test `read_error_stays_small`: no variant may outgrow the existing pack-pair variant (two paths and a box), on any platform.

## Public API

Changes the shape of a variant added in #771, which is not yet released. No new dependencies.

## Release notes

None; the variant hasn't been released yet.

## Validation

- `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --lib read_error_stays_small`, `cargo test --test replace_git`
- Labelled `full-ci` so the Windows clippy run confirms the fix.

| Test | 6 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​284 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​6 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​278 |
| Prod | 17 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​714 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​50 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​664 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## ELI5

On a phone turned sideways, the session title next to the tabs gets cut off ("brennanb2025/mobil…") and there was no way to read the rest. Now you tap the title and a small card drops down under it with the full name, the folder it lives in, and which computer it's on. Tap anywhere else to close it.

## What Changed

- **Before:** the title was plain text. Long worktree names were cut off with an ellipsis, most noticeably in landscape, where the title is capped at 160pt so the tabs fit beside it.
- **After:** tapping the title (in portrait or landscape) opens a card just under the top bar, lined up with the title's left edge. It shows the full worktree name, the worktree's path on its host, and the host's name with its connection dot. It fades in and slides down 6pt over 150ms. With Reduce Motion on, it only fades. Tapping anywhere outside it (including the title again) closes it with the reverse animation. The name and path can be selected for copying. Tapping the title again reverses the closing animation. Earlier QA found lost taps near the end of closing, so the title now stays the same button throughout the transition. The outside-dismiss area now follows the measured title if a live rename changes its width during closing. Source verification and checks have passed; actual phone-shell QA is still pending. Long details scroll inside the card, and long host names wrap. Turning the phone or moving the header closes the card so the next tap measures its new position; a keyboard-only height change keeps it open and resizes the available space.
- The card copies desktop's tab hover card: 256pt wide (narrower if the screen is), a hairline border, a raised background with a shadow, the name in semibold, then muted detail lines. A follow-up PR opens the same card under a tapped tab, so the phone's tab card and desktop's tab card match.

Mechanism: the title remains one button while the card opens and closes. The card and its outside-dismiss area render in a layer above page navigation, covering the visible phone page, including landscape side gutters. The card uses the existing Back handling until its closing animation finishes. The page keeps keyboard focus and screen-reader access within the title and details, then returns focus after closing; a later sheet takes precedence. Live title or header layout changes close the card and invalidate pending measurements. During closing, the dismiss area follows the current title bounds while the card stays in its original position; actual phone-shell verification is still pending. The status line still reconnects when retry is offered and the card is closed; while details are open, a tap outside the title text dismisses the card without activating the covered control.

Data: the desktop already sends the worktree's `path` and optional execution-host identity in its `worktree.show` reply. The phone now reads those existing fields. A workspace running on the paired computer uses its saved name; a workspace running on another server uses that server's existing label and connection state. The host line is omitted when the session cannot prove which machine to name. No wire change, new request, or new saved data. Older desktops still show the title and any available path.

## Why

Brennan picked "a small card under the title" from four mocked options, over moving the tabs aside, a middle ellipsis, or a centred sheet, because the same card can then serve the tabs and match desktop. author: aniruddhaadak80
body:
The `self-audit` job fails on `main` (run 37111121836) because `auditgen audit` exits 1 whenever it finds gaps — which is by design, and exactly what it does when auditing its own repository. The step only produces `auditgen-report.md`; it is not meant to gate the build.

Root cause verified locally on `main` HEAD: `npm run build` succeeds, all 85 tests pass, and the audit command reproduces the exit 1 after writing the report.

Change: add `continue-on-error: true` to the self-audit report step so the report is still uploaded while only `verify` acts as the required status check.

This matches the intent of PR #5 on a single, atomic workflow line so `main` can go green without taking the rest of that larger change.

author: rifont
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"rifont"} -->
_Requested by **Richard** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_014ARV5hjvNayk2mwUdCuZQm?thread=cmsg_014ARV5hjvNayk2mwUdCuZQmX4v4ErEgpHELh2Bz767APe)_

Before: each native kernel (Build123d in Python, PicoGK in C#) was wired by hand into about eight host files through typed `{ build123d?, picogk? }` slots. The Python and .NET plumbing lived inside each kernel package, so a second Python kernel meant copying about 3,500 lines. A third-party native kernel could not be added without editing Tau.

After: listing a native kernel's plugin in a runtime definition is enough for Tau to support it. The kernel carries its own deployment through `withNativeDeployment`:
- its `tau-plugin.json`
- the mapping from closure to options
- the seal
- the launch set

It finds its prepared closure when the runtime starts, or refuses with `KERNEL_NOT_PREPARED` naming `tau prepare <kernel>`. The CLI, daemon, MCP prepare tool, desktop, GeoSpec pool and examples discover native kernels from the runtime they run.

Two shared cores take the language plumbing. `@taucad/python-kernel-core` now runs Build123d and is ready for smlibpy. `@taucad/dotnet-kernel-core` now runs PicoGK. A Rust or other single-binary kernel uses `@taucad/native-process-core` directly. A third-party author edits no Tau package.

## How

- **Contract and store** (`@taucad/native-process-core`): `/adopter` gives `withNativeDeployment` and `nativeDeploymentOf`. `/store` holds the host-neutral machinery: deployments of a resolved runtime, preparation plugins, the closure resolver, verification and the payload store.
- **Python core** (`@taucad/python-kernel-core`): session, protocol base, shared worker modules, sealer, a generator with a `tau-python-kernel` bin, the project template and a reusable `python-kernel-tau-plugin.yml` workflow.
- **.NET core** (`@taucad/dotnet-kernel-core`): session, launch set, options and layer composition.
- **Kernels:** Build123d and PicoGK are now thin, with unchanged exports. PicoGK's `tau-plugin.json` is byte-equal.
- **Hosts:**
  - `tau prepare` gains `--plugin`/`--config`.
  - `tau mcp` and `tau serve` load skill bundles declared by `--plugin` packages.
  - The daemon answers each runtime child's closure request over IPC. It runs no user config, so it prepares only kernels the CLI ships.
  - The desktop keeps a static mirror of what it bundles, checked against its runtime factory.
  - The GeoSpec engine composes every prepared native kernel. Its optional peers are now the kernel packages.
- **Behaviour change:** the desktop now lists PicoGK on every host. Where no closure exists (for example Intel macOS), a `.cs` file refuses with `KERNEL_CAPABILITY_MISSING`. Before, PicoGK was simply absent there.
- **Checked decisions:** every host runtime (UI, CLI, desktop, GeoSpec, tau-examples, runtime-e2e, converter) asserts catalog coverage, or names an omission with its reason. Telemetry, skills and template tables are checked for first-party kernels only.
- **Goldens:** dispatch run 39146418155 re-recorded the Build123d golden receipts on all four targets. Every CPython and wheel row is unchanged; the four extra files are the shared worker modules.
- **Retired:** `TAU_PICOGK_RESOURCE_ROOT`, `TAU_BUILD123D_RESOURCE_ROOT` and the interim roster package.
- **Docs and skills:** `create-kernel`, `create-plugin` and `tau-example-packaging` are updated. The plugin generator emits native/Python kernels with a `/native` deployment. The runtime-architecture policy and runtime docs are updated.
- **CLI size:** the budget goes from 92 to 94 kB (92.91 kB measured, +1.31 kB net).

The new npm names `@taucad/python-kernel-core` and `@taucad/dotnet-kernel-core` need reserving before the next release. This PR publishes nothing.

author: keozx
body:
Home’s client previously returned raw Kotlin state, which the reducer converted and wrapped in another feature state. It now returns the existing native `HomeCounterLoadable` directly, and `.refreshResponse` carries that value. Kotlin mapping is private to the live client; Home’s presentation state no longer imports Kotlin. The five production files remove five lines overall, with the same cases, payloads, text and error fallback.

The native values and client closure container have checked `Sendable` conformance. **IOS-01 remains open:** the existing visitors still perform the private conversion. The live client retains its `@preconcurrency` import; this change does not qualify raw service isolation or async transport, retire a workaround, or select Swift export as the default.

The [first hosted run](https://github.com/Mekate-Studio/Mobi/actions/runs/39152328193) compiled successfully but hit the existing Nearby ordering test’s 60-second limit. A fresh local staged run reproduced the timeout, including with TCA’s normal-executor option. The pinned `TestStore` installs/restores a process-wide hook, so Home and Nearby now share one serialized Swift Testing parent, preserving TCA’s default executor while preventing overlapping store lifetimes. The ordering test still overlaps two requests, finishes the newer one first, and keeps its original time limit and exhaustive assertions. A scoped `defer` releases the earlier request if a later assertion fails.

**IOS-13 tracks this test-harness constraint separately from Swift export.** Its registry entry names TCA/Swift/Xcode rechecks, the per-test executor isolation needed for parallel suites, and the cold/repeated/negative-control retirement checks. The existing maintenance watch reports the entry and its native-dependency discovery gap.

Validation:

- Real Kotlin Home-service characterization covers initial/loading states, success, both repository failure reasons, and absent/retained previous values: 18 definitions / 22 parameterized runs.
- Local verification uses Xcode 27.1 / iOS 27.0; the original hosted failure used Xcode 26.6 / iOS 26.5. The [corrected hosted run](https://github.com/Mekate-Studio/Mobi/actions/runs/39157098188) passed every required check; the ordering regression completed in 0.028 seconds.

- Final serialized arrangement: all 220 repeated iOS runs passed; removing cancellation made the ordering test fail with an unexpected old response in 0.4 seconds. Production cancellation was restored before the staged gate.
- The update-watch contracts passed: 22 contracts, including IOS-13 source visibility and explicit native-dependency discovery coverage gaps.

- The normal staged hook passed all four selected jobs: Android/shared tests (38 cases), the iOS PullRequest plan (22 runs), Android debug packaging, unsigned iOS debug build, and owned-workspace cleanup. The feature-guide follow-up passed its documentation-only staged gate.
