body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"SmurfyHehe"} -->
_Requested by **Roy**_

Before: the benchmark said how long a frame took and how it split between CPU and GPU, but not which game system the CPU time went to.

After: `-- --benchmark --cpu_split=1` also prints, and saves to `user://cpu_split/`, a table of milliseconds per frame for each system (traffic cars, traffic manager, player car and each of its parts, HUD, camera, world streaming, the engine's physics step, the engine's render and other work). It gives the average, the slowest 1% of frames and the max, and lists the slowest frames with their three biggest costs. Without the option nothing is added, so normal play and plain benchmarks are unchanged.

How: Godot runs every node's tick in tree order, so `CpuSplit` drops timestamp nodes between the game node's children (and inside the traffic manager and player car) plus two at the very start and end of each tick. The gaps between them are each system's time; everything in a frame adds up to the frame's wall time. No game script is edited. The PR also brings in `tools/script_profile.gd` + `tools/script-profile.ps1` from the unmerged `claude/script-profile` branch (per-function shares inside one system), now forced into test mode with `NEON_TEST=1`.

Measured on Roy's laptop, 2026-10-18, main e0186e8, windowed 1152x648, medium tier, 60 s, alone on the machine, editor binary (debug GDScript), audio driver Dummy:

| ms per frame (avg / slowest 1%) | Empty road | Heavy A (60 cars, weave) | Heavy B (same) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Traffic cars (AI + GEVP + rails) | 0 / 0 | 4.9 / 27.1 | 3.6 / 10.0 |
| Traffic manager | 0.02 / 0.06 | 0.6 / 3.2 | 0.5 / 1.6 |
| Engine physics step | 0.2 / 0.5 | 1.1 / 4.4 | 0.9 / 2.0 |
| Engine render, GPU wait, other | 2.9 / 4.9 | 3.3 / 4.4 | 3.3 / 4.4 |
| Player car own tick | 0.2 / 0.5 | 0.5 / 2.4 | 0.4 / 1.1 |
| Camera + cockpit | 0.4 / 0.7 | 0.4 / 0.6 | 0.4 / 0.4 |

author: norvalbv
body:
Story: [sc-5071](https://app.shortcut.com/benordlabs/story/5071)

## Problem

A PASSing reviewer's `ADVISORY:` findings reach the ship log, one `advisory_result` sink row per reviewer (`gate: review:<name>`), and the ship digest. They never reach the PR. Someone reading the PR on GitHub does not see the "resolve before merge" items unless they open the ship log, so agents copy them into PR bodies by hand (#1133, #1179, #1118).

## Change

Ship now owns a second PR-body block beside the evidence block:

```

```

- **Source:** the `review:*` `advisory_result` rows of this ship's newest attempt. The detail goes in verbatim, one bullet per row. There is no ` | ` split (it would break on `string | null`) and no new row field, so the output stays right once #1046 moves to one row per advisory.
- **Text:** reduced to one line, with `<` escaped so no marker can survive inside a bullet. The home directory is shortened to `~/`; a root home (`HOME=/`) is left alone.
- **Publication:** after the PR exists, through the same head-guarded read → write → re-read loop the evidence block uses. `publishEvidenceBlock` is generalised into `publishBody(repo, pr, head, edit)`, the same name #1177 uses.
- **No advisories → zero gh calls.** A clean ship, a `--resume` and a gate-skipped run never touch the body.
- **Caller text:** an explicit `--body` keeps the PR's current notes, and a notes block pasted into a caller body is dropped. The owned-block helpers in `block.mts` now take a marker namespace, so evidence and notes share one implementation.

### AC3, restated

The story asked for a `--pr` re-push to *replace* the section. That would erase notes the re-ship never re-judged: an append `--pr` commits and reviews only the delta (`reship.sh:2-9`). So:

- **append `--pr`:** adds its notes to the earlier ones, de-duplicated on reviewer + text, so a cached PASS replaying the same advisory under a later commit adds nothing.
- **`--pr --base` rewrite:** the whole change is re-judged, so its notes replace the block.
- **Silence never removes a note.**

### Also

- `skills/using-devkit/SKILL.md` (synced): the block lists the advisories, so authors write only what they did about each one.
- Decision note on `ship-pr-evidence-block`: the ownership rule now covers a second marker namespace.
- New dist artifact `dist/cli/lib/ship/evidence/reviewer-notes.mjs`. Existing dist is left to `devkit release`.

## Proof

- **Unit:** `cli/lib/ship/evidence/reviewer-notes.test.mts` 13 and `block.test.mts` 14 pass. Revert proof: with `upsertNotes` made a no-op, 5 of the unit tests fail.
- **Integration (`cli/__tests__/ship-evidence.test.mts`, 15/15).** A fake pre-commit "reviewer" appends an advisory row:
  - the new ship opens with the section;
  - an append `--pr` keeps both notes in one block;
  - a re-ship with no advisories leaves the body byte-identical;
  - `--pr --body` with a forged pasted block gives `reworded` plus the carried notes, and the forged block is gone.
- **Rewrite:** `publish_reviewer_notes … replace` replaces the old notes. Revert proof: with the `body`-step carry removed, or the `--mode` flag broken, those integration tests fail.
- **Edge-case TDD:** with `HOME=/`, the old `replaceAll(homedir(), '~')` turned every `/` into `~`, and `HOME=/Users/ben` rewrote `/Users/benji/…`. Both cases were red, then fixed.
- **Coverage:** 66/67 added lines (98.5%). The one uncovered line is the usage-error throw.
- **fallow:** passes on measured coverage. The plain run estimates coverage and flags `noteLines`' callback and `publishBody`, which spawned tests do cover.

## Not done here (follow-ups)

- `--resume` after a failed push publishes no notes: it gets a fresh ship id and the gates do not re-run. Possible fix: carry the advisories on the per-sha `ship_gated` record (the `bypasses.mts` pattern). (sc-6818)
- The block grows with each append re-ship. Past GitHub's 65,536-char body limit `gh pr edit` fails; this fails open and only the notes stop updating. (sc-6819)
- Once #1024 lands, add a pointer line: "earlier attempts raised N more: `devkit ship --advisories <branch>`". (sc-6820)
- `reship.sh` `NOTES_MODE=replace` under `--base` is not exercised by a full rewrite ship, because the rewrite fixture's gh stub reports an empty `headRefOid`. The shell-function test covers everything downstream of it. (sc-6410)
- A `notes` failure prints with the `evidence:` prefix (cosmetic) (sc-6821). `redactSecrets` is not applied, because its assignment pattern rewrites `token: string` prose.
- Expect conflicts with open #995/#1177 (`run.mts`, `pr-body.mts`, `publish-evidence.sh`, `ship-branch.sh`, `reship.sh`). Both use the same `publishBody` name to keep the rebase small.

## Reviewer advisory dispositions

These respond to the Reviewer notes below. The block itself is this PR's live proof: this ship's own advisories, written by the feature.

- **A `--base` rewrite with no advisories keeps the earlier notes** (commit-guard, backend-performance, correctness). Deliberate: silence never removes a note. The way to tell "the fleet re-judged everything and found nothing" from "only completeness ran" would read `review_result` and cache-hit rows, and the pre-ship critique found that a `review:completeness` cache hit would make that check false-clear the notes. Rewrites are rare. Left as a follow-up: clear the block on a rewrite only when a non-completeness reviewer verdict is present. (sc-6822)
- **"Verbatim" vs the 500-char cap** (correctness, two advisories). This one is a real gap, and my first answer here was wrong. `reportAdvisories` joins a PASS's advisories with ` | ` into one row that `emitAdvisoryResult` caps at 500 chars. A reviewer with three or more long advisories therefore gets one bullet ending in `…`, and its later advisories are dropped. This PR shows it: the correctness bullet below ends in `…`, and its 4th advisory (this one) is missing. "Verbatim" means unsplit, not uncapped. The fix belongs in the emitter: one row per advisory (open #1046) or an uncapped list. It is listed as a follow-up. (sc-5823)
- **`reship.sh` grew 1257 → 1265 lines** (backend-performance). Shell scripts are outside guard-size's scan roots (the preflight listed only `.mts` files). The 8 lines are the `NOTES_MODE` assignment and the two publish call sites.
- **Dedupe filter `!seen.has(k) && Boolean(seen.add(k))`** (commit-guard). Readability only, no behaviour change. Left as is.
- **fallow advisory, 2 complexity introduced.** Scored on estimated coverage. `fallow audit` with this branch's measured coverage passes, because `noteLines`' callback and `publishBody` are covered by the unit and spawned integration tests.

## Android variant lab results — **completed successfully** (October 18, 2026)

[CI experiment #39152331866](https://github.com/jlingenfelter22-bot/Swole-Cat/actions/runs/39152331866) compiled all three variants from **identical Swole Cat Testing v0.93.3 / Android code 138 WebView JS and CSS**.

| CI-only variant | APK bytes | Uncompressed DEX bytes |
|---|---:|---:|
| Debug (current Testing build type, but ephemeral test signer) | 5,206,278 | 9,364,024 |
| Release, no R8 | 3,717,901 | 7,582,320 |
| Release, R8 enabled | 1,688,225 | 1,450,012 |

- R8 experimental APK **67.6% smaller** than debug wrapper. The native DEX size also decreases dramatically.
- Web asset bytes identical (**1,371,203**) in all three. JS SHA-256 `e9ec8dc99c0a872188e6612559e64a8a86fb8915277e720dc993c94dfe927346` and CSS SHA-256 `82ffbaeb66339f7517b379fb47bfc22cdd6c8c46f93eac104c8684d52d6a8d06` match across variants.
- No R8 compilation failure; warnings about Gradle flatDir and general tool deprecations, not evidence of missing classes.
- **Critical interpretation:** This is a package-size/code-shrinking experiment, *not measured Android startup, 60 Hz jank, WebView JavaScript speed, battery or stability.* It does **not** prove a speedup. R8 could still break plugin method discovery, updater/security callbacks or runtime behavior. Require an explicitly approved future **signed Testing-only** release and true device-level plugin/smoothness checks before switching release modes.

author: benthic-io
body:
## Title

qwen35: FP16 K/V cache by default, int8 with `--kv-q8` (262144 fits a 16 GiB card)

Issue: Resolves #

## Summary

The Qwen3.6 / `qwen35moe` engine stored its K/V cache in FP32 with no option to change it. At the model's
native 262144 cells that is **12.0 GiB** - the whole of a 16 GiB card before a single expert - so the context
had to stop at 192K. FP32 is also the wrong precision for this path, for a reason the code already made
obvious: **the prompt has always attended over FP16** while the decode of the next token read FP32.

FP16 becomes the default (6.0 GiB at 262144), matching what the main engine's `kKvF16` already does, and
`--kv-q8` stores int8 codes with one FP16 scale per 64 dims - the main engine's own `kv_q8.hpp` scheme
(`KV_Q8_GROUP`) - at 3.1 GiB.

This could not be reached with a configuration flag: **this engine path has no KV or precision option at
all.** Its parser has none of `--kv`, `--kv-resident` or anything else, and the allocation was a hardcoded
`dalloc(...)` (float) with the kernels reading `const float*` directly. There was nothing to set; the flag
and the storage had to be added together.

## What changed

`src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu`

- `k_attn_prep`, `k_attn_part` and `k_kv_f16` are templated on the cache format, so the FP16 path carries no
  branch and the prompt path's existing half-staging (`k_kv_f16`) becomes a pure compaction instead of an
  FP32→FP16 conversion.
- `--kv-q8` quantizes on write with `scale = fp16(max|x| / 127)`, `code = clamp(rint(x / scale), -127, 127)` -
  the main engine's scheme, so a cell is stored the same way in both engines.
- `k_attn_prep` loses its `if (i >= HD) return;` early return. The q8 group max needs a `__syncthreads()`
  that every thread has to reach, so the stores are guarded with `i < HD` instead. Behaviour on the FP16
  path is unchanged.
- `RowSel`, `Sess` and the batch rows' per-session pointer tables carry the scale arrays alongside the code
  arrays. The session-to-slot copy was sized in FP32 elements (`* 4`) and is now sized in the format's, with
  a second copy for the scales under q8.

`docs/QWEN36.md` - a section on the two formats with the numbers below.

## Extra Notes

**Why FP32 was never the right choice here.** `k_kv_f16` has always compacted `[kvh][ctx][HD]` into the
`[kvh][P][HD]` halves that the prompt chunk's Q K^T and P V GEMMs read. So a prompt attended over FP16
values while the split-K decode of the very next token read FP32. The cache format only ever gave the decode
a higher precision than the prefill sharing its sequence; FP16 makes the two agree.

**Measured**, Radeon VII (gfx906, 16 GiB), ROCm 7.1, `--max-context 262144 --chunk 4096 --expert-vram 8`,
two runs, back to back:

| cache | VRAM free | experts in VRAM | tg32 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| FP32 (before) | does not allocate | - | - |
| FP16 | 4.46 GiB | 49 / 256 | 41.4 / 45.0 tok/s |
| `--kv-q8` | 7.12 GiB | 91 / 256 | 49.1 / 52.6 tok/s |

q8 is both the smaller cache and the faster one, which is not the obvious outcome: the VRAM it returns goes
to the expert cache, and the q8 read also halves the bytes the split-K decode pulls across PCIe. The gap is
about +18%, with a few points of run-to-run spread.

**Parity** against an FP32 build of the same tree: 4 prompts of 4,000 tokens, greedy 96, `--mtp 0`, with both
binaries checked to place the same 81/256 experts so the comparison is the cache format and nothing else.
FP16 **383 / 384** generated tokens identical, `--kv-q8` **384 / 384**. The one FP16 difference is an argmax
near-tie at token 43 of the first prompt; no earlier token moves.

**A characteristic `--bench-pp` hides**, recorded in docs/QWEN36.md: it measures a 2,048-token prompt, nowhere
near the context's end, and throughput falls as a prompt fills the context. One 198,603-token prompt through
the server read 4,096 tokens at 1365 tok/s, 106,496 at 195, 172,032 at 72 - a steady decline that finishes,
about 17 minutes end to end. Worth knowing before filling a 262144 context in one request; irrelevant to a
conversation built up over turns.

**Not run here**: `tools/qwen35/q36_solo_gate.py` over the 10 parity prompts, `q36_batch_gate.py`, and the
vision gates. Those are the obvious next step on the project's own hardware.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Adds SysML v2 textual-notation input and output to the API by delegating conversion to a running [OpenSysML](https://github.com/Open-MBEE/OpenSysML) `sysml-grpc` service through its Java client (`org.openmbee:opensysml:0.10.1`), behind one setting.

**Merge order** — #28 → #29 → #33 → #31. This PR is based on `fix/review-findings-followup` (#33) so that its `page[after]`/`page[before]`, opt-in CORS and commit-changes fixes are already in; GitHub retargets it to `feat/spec-conformance` when #33 merges. `origin/develop` (#35, the `scan` job fix) is merged in.

**Setting** — `flexo.opensysml.url` / `FLEXO_OPENSYSML_URL` = `host:port` of a running `sysml-grpc`. Empty (default) = off: JSON routes behave exactly as before, notation input is `415`, notation output `406`. The client is opened with `ConnectionOptions.builder().service(host, port).autoStart(false)`, so the service never downloads or starts a binary of its own (`OpenSysml.kt`). An unreachable service is answered `502 Bad Gateway` in the `Error` shape.

**Input** — `POST /projects/{projectId}/commits` with `Content-Type: text/plain`, `application/vnd.sysml` or `application/vnd.kerml`. `CommitApi.receiveCommitRequest()` converts the body with `convert(body, "api-json", fromFormat=sysml|kerml, idForm=uuid)` and builds the same `CommitRequest` a JSON client would send (`DataVersion` per element, `identity.@id` = element `@id`), then the existing commit path runs unchanged. `branchId`/`replace` query parameters apply as for JSON; `description` sets the commit description. Ids are OpenSysML's name-based uuids — the spec requires UUID ids, and re-posting the same text updates the same elements rather than duplicating them (the default qualified-name id form would not pass `requireValidId`). The response is the JSON commit record even when the client only accepts `text/plain` (`respondCommit`).

**Output** — `GET /projects/{projectId}/commits/{commitId}/elements` with `Accept: text/plain`, `application/vnd.sysml` or `application/vnd.kerml`: the complete element graph is fetched as for the unpaged JSON route and written with `convert(jsonArray, "sysml"|"kerml", fromFormat="api-json")`. Page parameters are ignored for notation (no `Link` header, `page[after]`/`page[before]` not validated), since a page of elements cannot be written on its own. `acceptedNotationType()` gives each supported type the quality of its most specific matching `Accept` range (`text/plain` > `text/*` > `*/*`) and serves notation only when the best notation quality is strictly above JSON's — so `*/*`, `application/json, text/plain` and `text/plain;q=0.8, */*;q=0.8` keep JSON, `text/plain;q=0, text/*` refuses plain text, and `text/plain` or `text/plain, */*;q=0.8` selects it.

Notation output is on the commit-elements route only: the API reads elements by commit, and a branch read is "resolve the branch head, then read that commit's elements", which the existing branch route already supports.

**Diagnostics** — conversion errors (a `ConversionException`, or any `error`-severity diagnostic) → `400` in the spec `Error` shape, `description` listing each diagnostic as `error at line:col: message`. Non-error diagnostics do not block: `ApplicationCall.reportDiagnostics()` logs each and adds one `X-SysML-Diagnostic: <severity> at <line>:<col>: <message>` response header per diagnostic on the `200`, for notation input and output alike (the `Commit` record itself stays on the spec schema); the header is in the CORS `exposeHeader` list so browser clients on an allowed origin can read it. OpenSysML v0.10.1's `Convert` RPC reports only parser diagnostics, all `error`, so today the header is absent; it carries warnings as soon as the service emits them. Because notation requests carry a non-JSON `Accept`, error bodies are written as JSON explicitly (`respondJson`) rather than through content negotiation, which would otherwise answer with an empty body.

## Tests

`NotationTest` (Kotest, `ProjectAny`, 7 specs): 415/406/502 with the feature off or the service unreachable, and the `X-SysML-Diagnostic` mapping on constructed warning/info diagnostics through a test route on a CORS-allowed origin (always run); when `FLEXO_OPENSYSML_URL` is set, a round trip — `package P { part def A; part a : A; }` posted as `text/plain`, read back as JSON (`@type`s and `declaredName`s checked, no diagnostic header) and as `text/plain` / `application/vnd.sysml`, re-parsed through the OpenSysML client and compared as `(type, id, name)` sets, plus the `Accept` negotiation table, `page[size]` / invalid `page[after]` with notation (complete graph) and with JSON (400), and the `Accept: text/plain` POST — and `application/vnd.sysml`/`application/vnd.kerml` input and a syntax-error 400. The three round-trip specs skip with a message when `FLEXO_OPENSYSML_URL` is unset. Full suite with the URL set, on top of #33: 92 tests, 0 failures.

Test stack: `src/test/resources/docker-compose.yml` gains a `sysml-grpc` service built from `src/test/resources/sysml-grpc/Dockerfile`, which downloads the `sysml-grpc-linux-amd64` asset of the pinned OpenSysML release (v0.10.1), checks it against the `.sha256` sidecar and a digest pinned in the Dockerfile, and serves on `:50051`. `Dockerfile-Test` sets `FLEXO_OPENSYSML_URL=sysml-grpc:50051` so CI runs the round trip; locally run `FLEXO_OPENSYSML_URL=localhost:50051 ./gradlew test`. Once an OpenSysML image is published the `build:` can become an `image:`.

author: vishanth14
body:
## Problem Description

The current KESTRAL spatial-index visualizer does not expose the complete R-tree hierarchy in an interactive and inspectable way. Without explicit parent-child relationships, node types, and bounding-box information, it is difficult to understand the internal structure of the R-tree and correlate its nodes with the spatial visualization.

Additionally, the existing viewport and workstation layout have usability issues, including incorrect framing after resizing, HiDPI rendering inconsistencies, unreliable pan termination, and limited space for the hierarchy viewer. The Layer Visibility controls also occupy valuable vertical space in the sidebar, reducing the space available for exploring large trees.

This PR addresses these issues by:

- Exposing actual R-tree hierarchy relationships, node types, and MBR bounds through the state exporter.
- Adding an interactive hierarchy viewer with expandable nodes, node inspection, selection, and corresponding MBR highlighting.
- Improving canvas resizing, HiDPI rendering, panning, zooming, Fit All, and Reset View behavior.
- Making the workstation layout responsive across viewport sizes and browser zoom levels.
- Moving Layer Visibility controls into the top toolbar and expanding the R-tree hierarchy panel with independent scrolling.
- Adding regression tests for hierarchy export, validation, viewport behavior, and UI interactions.

### Testing

- Viewport math tests: 28 passed.
- Hierarchy validation tests: 21 passed.
- CTest suite: 10/10 passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Closes #2

author: zarubaf
body:
Closes #278.

Containers can now hold handles (`Reg[T]`, `Wire[T]`, `Input[T]`, `Mem[T, N]`, `Instance[M, args]`):

- A `handles` flag in the type metadata marks a type that holds a handle. A value of such a type is never static.
- Arrays, records and lists of handles work. A read in a data context gives the data of the handles.
- Formals, results and `mut` actuals check their handle leaves. A handle at a data leaf is S010.
- A handle at a static position is S011. `:=` targets walk through containers (S017 texts).
- `diagnostic` charges 0 for a handle, a flagged root pays the rebind charge, and Rust memoizes `data_ty` per type.

The spec (section 6.2) gets the new texts, each with its fix. Lean and Rust agree on the corpus, on `diff-si`, and on about 10,000 random comparisons at full and capped fuel. Six new scaling templates and the work counters in `tests_work_handles.rs` pass the judge.

A `:=` target now evaluates all its indices first and then walks once from the root, the same order as a `=` place write. The old order needed a new walk after each call index, and a deep target did quadratic work for linear fuel. Thus `w[1 / 0] := 1` on a wire is now S013, not S017, and a call in a later index runs before an S013 of an earlier one.

author: trissim
body:
P43: one lowercase-hex text family owns the identity, digest and token spellings.

- `LowerHexText` in `src/agent_comms/field_codec.py` is a `SpelledText` (#1530). It has no `from_text` or digits of its own; each member declares its spelling once:
  - `Id128Text` `[0-9a-f]{32}` (with `mint()`), equal to the bus-root spelling #1530 compares
  - `Hex256Text` `[0-9a-f]{64}`, with members `Sha256Text` (a digest) and `Token256Text` (a random 256-bit secret)
  - `GitCommitText` `[0-9a-f]{7,40}`
- Sites that restated a spelling now derive from the member: owner_protocol `ControllerTokenText` is a `Token256Text`; selected_tool_broker's `_TOKEN` regex is gone, the transport token goes through `Token256Text.decode`; pi_payloads' MCP acknowledgement checks `Id128Text.spelling`. `WireRootIdText`, `NativeInputIdText`, `StableLookupText`, `ACPInputIdText`, `_HEX32`, `_HEX64`, `_HEX_DIGEST`, `native_pi._DIGEST` and the per-character loop are deleted.
- No member overrides its refusal. A wrongly spelled controller token is now refused with SpelledText's `ControllerTokenText is spelled [0-9a-f]{64}` (the handshake test expects that text; a non-string still reports its type error).
- Left as is: `native_package.py` runs standalone from stack/ and keeps its `bytes.fromhex` check (no regex). The SQL `CHECK ... NOT GLOB '*[^0-9a-f]*'` table constraints are stored schema and are unchanged.

Check: `grep -rnE '\[0-9a-f\]\{(32|64|7,40)\}' src/agent_comms --include='*.py' | wc -l` prints 3.

body:
## What changed
Allow MCP OAuth consent submissions to complete callback redirect chains, including redirects from a registered loopback callback to another local port. The global security policy remains in place for other pages.

Changelog: docs/changelog/2026-10-18-mcp-client-authorization-redirects/

## Why
Browsers apply the consent page's `form-action` directive to every redirect after the form POST. A later callback hop outside the listed origins stops navigation after the authorization grant is created, making the Authorize client button appear inert.

## Before / After
Before: a browser POST received the authorization redirect and reached the first registered callback, then stopped when that callback redirected to another local port.

After: with only the consent page CSP changed, the same browser flow reached the final callback. The deployment browser gate in the SaaS change will exercise this two-hop flow on each production rollout.

## Risk
- Medium. Removing `form-action` from the consent document means it no longer restricts the destination of a submitted form. The rendered page has one hard-coded same-origin POST form, escapes client-controlled values, and has no scripts. Other pages retain the global `form-action 'self'` policy.

## Security
- Threat categories reviewed: TM-WEB-004, TM-WEB-005, TM-MCP, TM-AUTH.
- Findings and resolutions: retained `frame-ancestors 'none'` and all other CSP directives on the consent page; confirmed the form action is hard-coded to `/oauth/authorize`. The authorization endpoint still validates the registered redirect URI and CSRF token.

## Follow-ups
No follow-ups.

## Checklist
- [x] Tests added or updated
- [x] Backward compatibility considered
- [x] Security review performed against relevant threat model categories
- [ ] Final CI ran checks affected by this PR

Contributes to GEO-1361

## Description

A rebase rewrote every `fixed <sha>` commit, so no answer could pass. The reporter now maps a named commit the branch no longer holds to the one branch commit with the same patch, hunk line numbers left out.

- Acceptance 1, a rebased fix passes: `it confirms a fix whose commit a rebase rewrote and passes the check` and `it keeps a fix whose commit a rebase rewrote after a later delta without the fix commit`. Both fail on the old reporter.
- Acceptance 2, a sha that never touched the file fails: `it confirms no fix whose rewritten commit never changed the file the branch commits change`, with the reason `the commit bbbbbbb is not on the branch`.
- The match uses the whole commit, so a rebased test-only fix counts as an unrebased one does (`it confirms a fix whose commit changes only another file`).
- The named commit must descend from the head that posted the finding (compare status `ahead`), per finding.
- Each review and each check resolve the rewrite from GitHub inside the fix commits, so the summary marker gains no field.

# Coordinated dependency refresh: Hanami 3 + latest-or-close-enough across the stack

Plan: `notes/plan-20261018T173628Z-dependency-refresh.md` (space 20261014-all-fax-no-printer), ENTRY 1. Supersedes the 22 open Dependabot PRs (#2–#23) — they auto-close on merge. Parity refresh: dependencies move, behavior does not.

## What this does

One coordinated bump instead of 22 piecemeal PRs. The Hanami 3 set could never land piecemeal: the 2.3 metagem doesn't pin router/db/cli, and hanami-controller 2.3.2 (utils `~> 2.3.0`) is mutually exclusive with hanami 3.0.2 (utils `~> 3.0.0`) — hanami-controller is retired in 3.0 in favor of hanami-action.

### Lane hanami3 — Ruby stack + Hanami 3 migration

- **Hanami 2.3.2 → 3.0.2**: hanami-controller 2.3.2 → **hanami-action 3.0.1** (the retirement swap), hanami-router 2.3.1→3.0.0, hanami-db 2.3.0→3.0.0, hanami-cli 2.3.5→3.0.0, hanami-utils rides transitively at 3.x.
- **Body-parsing rewiring**: Hanami 3 ships NO implicit body parser (`use_body_parser_middleware` auto-append is gone). The explicit `Hanami::Middleware::BodyParser` registration (shipped by hanami-router in 3.0) is now load-bearing — without it JSON bodies never reach `req.params`. `IngestBodyPassthrough` preserved and re-verified against the 3.0 code paths: hanami-router 3.0's `_form_urlencoded_body` and `BodyParser#call` both short-circuit on `ROUTER_PARSED_BODY`, so the raw-body ingest stream stays untouched by construction.
- **Config parity**: `config.db.log_level = :info` (Hanami 3 defaults to :debug — would have dumped every SQL statement to the production log); memoization default audited against provider registrations.
- **Rest of the Ruby refresh**: sequel 5.105→5.109, pg 1.6.3→1.7.0, dry-monads 1.10→1.11, async-redis 0.13.1→0.14.0, falcon 0.55.5→0.57.0, vite_ruby 3.10.2→3.11.1, rom-factory 0.13→0.14.1, rack → latest 3.2.x. rom/rom-sql/dry-types/dry-validation/dry-operation/omniauth/minitest verified already-latest.
- **In-tree gems ported in place**: inertia-hanami's dev-dep moves hanami-controller `= 2.3.2` → hanami-action 3.0.1; both touched gem locks refreshed. Public interfaces survive; zero code renames.

### Lane frontend — toolchain majors to latest

typescript 6.0.3→**7.0.2** (the Go rewrite; the known `nightOwl` deep-esm export failure fixed with a per-theme import in `CodeBlock.tsx`), vitest 4.1.9→5.0.5, @testing-library/jest-dom 6→7, **@inertiajs/vite + @inertiajs/react 3.3→3.9.1** (traveling together — the react half was queued behind Dependabot's 10-PR npm cap), radix-ui 1.6→1.8, shadcn 4.11→4.22, plus axios, react-dom/@types, @vitejs/plugin-react, vite-plugin-ruby to latest satisfying versions.

### Lane hygiene — CI + Dependabot

actions/setup-node v6→v7, jdx/mise-action v4→v5 (all three jobs), checkout/cache already latest. `.github/dependabot.yml`: groups added (bundler minor/patch, npm dev-dependencies, github-actions all) so future waves arrive as ~3 PRs instead of 20; open-pull-requests-limit 10→5 (groups make the cap about noise, not coverage). No ignore rules — typescript 7 landed, so none needed.

## Gates (I14 judged CONTINUE, AC1–AC10 PASS cold)

- main suite **465 runs / 1385 assertions / 0/0/0** ×2 cold runs (base 445 — the delta is the Hanami 3 stack surfacing legitimate coverage motion, recorded not pinned per plan)

body:
Loading `Number` on PHP 8.1+ raises two deprecations: `Serializable` without `__serialize()`/`__unserialize()`, and `jsonSerialize()` without a return type.

- `__serialize()` / `__unserialize()` added next to the `Serializable` methods, so PHP 7.4+ uses them and older versions keep working.
- `#[\ReturnTypeWillChange]` on `jsonSerialize()`: read as a comment before PHP 8, no signature change.

Values serialized by the previous version (`C:18:"Thelia\Math\Number":…`) still unserialize, and `json_encode()` output is unchanged. A test covers both.

author: phantomic12
body:
# Fix episode titles being dropped or corrupted across playback paths

## Why

Episode titles reach the player through several independent paths, and most of
them lost or overwrote the title:

| Path | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| Episode drawer "Watch" | submitted a synthetic `Show S01E02`, discarding the episode name |
| Auto-advance / resume-next | reused the **previous** episode's title |
| `next_episode` endpoint | returned only coordinates, so "up next" had nothing to show |
| Watch history | fell back to the bare show title, so every episode looked identical |
| Continue Watching | rendered the show title plus `S01E02`, never the episode name |

The result was an episode playing under the wrong name, or under the show's
name, depending on how you got there.

## What changed

**One formatter.** `Playback::EpisodeLabel` builds `Show · S01E02 · Name` and
is used by every path. Synthetic catalogue placeholders (`"Episode 7"`, a bare
`"7"`) are dropped rather than displayed, so a missing name degrades to
`Show · S01E02` instead of a wrong one.

**The successor's own label.** `Playback::EpisodeSequence#next_episode_after`
returns the next episode with its label and runtime; `next_after` is kept as a
thin wrapper for existing callers. Auto-advance and resume-next now carry the
next episode's title instead of the finished one's.

**Server-authoritative titles.** `PlaybackStartService` resolves the catalogue
label when a caller sends a blank or position-less title, and trusts a title
that already carries the right `SxxExx` — so resume stays off the metadata path
while stale or bare titles still get corrected.

**The player shows it.** The chrome now leads with the episode name and shows
`Show · S01E02` as the context line, instead of hiding the title inside a back
button. This PR also adds skip ±10 s, a playback speed menu that survives
remux/transcode seeks, and names the next episode in the up-next card.

**Plain-HTTP self-hosting** (second commit, independent — happy to split it
out): production set `assume_ssl`/`force_ssl` unconditionally, so an instance
reached directly over HTTP redirected to `https://` and failed — even though
`docker-compose.yml` advertises `http://localhost:${PORT}`. Both now read
`ASSUME_SSL`/`FORCE_SSL` and default to `true`, so proxy deployments are
unchanged.

## Testing

- Regression specs: `spec/services/playback/episode_label_spec.rb` (label rules
  and placeholders), `spec/requests/episode_title_spec.rb` (drawer submission,
  stale client title, auto-advance, player chrome), plus updated
  `next_episode_spec`, `streaming_spec`, `playback_progress_spec` and
  `playback_resume_service_spec`.
- Full suite on this branch, in a clean compose project: **499 examples,
  4 failures**. All four are `spec/requests/age_restriction_spec.rb` examples
  that fail identically on a pristine `9b358aa` checkout; they are untouched
  here. Line coverage 91.27%.

## Notes

- No migrations, no new dependencies.
- `Playback::EpisodeSequence#next_after` keeps its old signature, so anything
  outside this repo build that calls it still works.

author: bgilbert1984
body:
## Summary

- Adds `capture_sessions` to `ScytheDuckStore` as the **operational persistence projection** of `scythe_mission.Session` — not a replacement domain object, and deliberately not named `sessions` (that name already means something else in `operator_session_manager.py` and `scythe_pg.py`). `scythe_mission.Session` itself was found to be fully dormant: it has a required, validated, frozen `mission_id` field designed in from the start, but **zero production callers anywhere** (confirmed via repo-wide grep, including its own tests). This PR makes the relationship the domain model already described operationally real, rather than inventing a new one.
- Adds a nullable `mission_id` column to `events` (guarded `PRAGMA table_info` + `ALTER TABLE`, the only existing precedent for a live-table schema change in this codebase, from `map_cache.py`) — picked up automatically by every existing per-instance `.duckdb` file on next startup, no separate migration step.
- `ScytheDuckStore.append_batch` now resolves and freezes session→mission ownership **before** any event row is inserted, inside one DuckDB transaction: a session with no binding yet accepts one; a matching rebind is a no-op; a *conflicting* non-null rebind raises `SessionMissionConflictError` (→ 409 at the API layer) and aborts the whole batch, not just the conflicting session.
- `/api/events/ingest` accepts an optional `mission_id` per event, validated against the existing `scythe_mission.is_valid_mission_id` (the same source of truth `create_mission()` already uses).

### Behavior change vs. purely additive

Purely additive for every existing caller: omitting `mission_id` reproduces prior behavior with `mission_id` simply `NULL`. The only new *rejecting* behavior is the 409 conflict case, which did not exist before this PR (there was no way to "conflict" before mission_id existed on events at all).

### Bug caught during testing (fixed in this PR, not a regression)

Backfilling a session's mission binding from `NULL` to a real value did **not** retroactively update already-inserted event rows still carrying `NULL` — exactly the split-brain identity problem this PR exists to prevent. Caught by the test suite before merge; fixed by having the backfill path also `UPDATE events ... WHERE session_id = ? AND mission_id IS NULL` in the same transaction. Covered by a dedicated consistency-invariant test (`events.mission_id` must always agree with `capture_sessions.mission_id`).

## Context

PR 2 of 3 in the ARR Mission identity propagation sequence (1: discovery → **2: ownership** → 3: data access). Branched directly off `origin/main`.

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m unittest test_scene_duckdb_store_mission_id` — 9/9 pass (new file: omission-preserves-behavior, accept+persist, backfill, conflict rejection incl. whole-batch and intra-batch, idempotent re-ingest, consistency invariant).
- [x] `python -m unittest test_rf_scythe_api_server_mission_identifier` — 9/9 pass (6 pre-existing + 3 new HTTP-layer: invalid mission_id → 400, valid → accepted, conflicting rebind → 409).
- [x] `python scene_duckdb_store.py` (module's own built-in self-test) — still passes unmodified.

author: kaividali
body:
Fixes from a full pass over the exchange. Each commit is one fix, with the reason in its message. Every fix was reproduced on a local copy first, then checked again after the change.

**Security**
- Anyone could log in as any user, including the operator, by setting the session cookie to a user id (ids are public in the holders list). Cookies are now signed with `SESSION_SECRET`.
- Two actions on `/api/auth` are removed: "switch" (log in as anyone) and "deposit" (free gold).
- The admin sign-up code was hard-coded and printed on the sign-up page. It now comes from `ADMIN_SIGNUP_CODE` (unset = off).
- The webhook API key was public, in the repo and in the served userscript. It's rotated at startup and the old one is refused; the userscript and watcher no longer contain a key.
- "Credit ledger entry" worked without logging in and could be repeated.
- The userscript rendered usernames as HTML in the operator's game tab.

**Gold created from nothing**
- Deposits credited the amount claimed, not the amount paid (claim 100,000, pay 5).
- Market buys paid sellers the full ask but charged buyers only the last price + 5%. "Infinity" was also accepted as a price.
- Dividends credited holders without debiting anyone. They're now paid from the founder's purse.
- Buybacks paid the sellers but left them their shares.
- Every cold start reset the operator passwords and zeroed admin and treasury purses. The seed now only creates missing accounts.

**Double spends** (with a networked database or overlapping requests)
These could each run twice: withdrawals, buy orders, two fills of the same ask, cancels, deposit approvals, ledger syncs from two tabs, buybacks and dividend payouts. Each one now claims its row before any gold moves.

**Smaller fixes**
- Fresh installs crashed until the server restarted.
- "Max" on a market buy always failed.
- The dividend total showed 0, and earnings rows had a placeholder title.
- The chart froze after 50 hourly candles.
- A new treasury account starts with 0 gold.

**Free database**
The app now also reads the variable names Turso's Vercel integration uses. `DEPLOY.md` walks through moving the site to a free Turso database. That ends the lost writes from each server keeping its own SQLite copy, and the Blob sync with them.

## Deploying
Merging deploys straight to production, so do `DEPLOY.md` steps 1–4 first: freeze the exchange, move the data to Turso, and set `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_AUTH_TOKEN` and `SESSION_SECRET` in Vercel. Then merge and do steps 5–6:
1. Change the JosephArora and CardinalSanjay passwords: both are in the repo history.
2. Copy the new webhook key from the Operator panel into the userscript.

Everyone has to log in once more, because sessions are now signed.

Checked with 24 before/after scenarios (races reproduced with simulated database latency), plus `tsc` and `next build`.

author: paramthakkar123
body:
## What

A common `WorldModel` protocol (`simulusion.world_model`) with one interface for every action-conditioned family:

```python
from simulusion.world_model import as_world_model, load_world_model

model = load_world_model("runs/iris/iris.pt", "iris")   # or as_world_model(agent)
state = model.encode(frames, actions)                    # real context -> state
traj = model.rollout(state, planned_actions)             # .frames / .rewards / .terminated
model.save("out/wm")                                     # load_world_model("out/wm")
```

- `encode` / `step` / `rollout` / `decode` / `save`, with the same conventions for every family: frame layout and range, actions between context frames, batch-first dict state, global-RNG seeding.
- Adapters for Dreamer (V1/V2), PlaNet, IRIS, DIAMOND, Genie and ConvVAE + MDN-RNN World Models.
- `WorldModelSpec` reports the action space (including Genie's latent actions), how many context frames a model needs, and whether it has reward and termination heads.
- `load_world_model` reads a saved world model or each family's own training checkpoint: PlaNet's bare RSSM weights, DreamerV2 (detected from its config), a full DIAMOND agent checkpoint.
- JEPA and DiT get no adapter: neither is action-conditioned, so `as_world_model` refuses them with an explanation.
- DIAMOND's networks are now built by one function shared with `DiamondAgent`; seeded init is identical to `main`. So a DIAMOND world model loads without the Atari emulator or the replay buffer.
- New guide: "One interface for every world model". API reference, exports table, type stub and changelog are updated.

## Verification

- `tests/test_world_model_protocol.py`: 72 tests. The contract tests run on all six families. The rest check each adapter against the family's own code path: IRIS against `imagine_rollout`, Dreamer against its stepper, PlaNet against its planner, the MDN-RNN cell against the trained sequence model.
- Existing type-stub, public API, DIAMOND, inference, web-export and CLI tests pass.
- Every trained checkpoint in `demos/runs` (Dreamer, DreamerV2, PlaNet, IRIS, DIAMOND, Genie) loads, rolls out and survives save -> load unchanged.
- Ruff clean; no mypy errors in the new code; docs build with zero warnings.

## Known issue (not caused by this PR)

The Sonic Genie checkpoint in `demos/runs/genie` predates 953ed690 (the causal-decoder fix). Under current code it reconstructs at ~0.47 mean error, i.e. noise. It needs retraining, and `Genie.CHECKPOINT_FORMAT` should be bumped so stale checkpoints refuse to load. That will be a separate PR.

L'accueil met en avant « Jouer contre le bot ». - **`/jouer/:id`**, l'écran de partie, conçu d'abord pour le téléphone : - le camp du bot : SI et SLA, Débit, main et pioche (en nombre de cartes), plateau en **jetons** compacts (cadre de rareté, nom, attaque et PV du moment) ; - mon camp : plateau, SLA, Débit, pioche, et ma main en cartes d'US-009, qui défile horizontalement ; - **actions au toucher et au clavier** : je choisis une carte, puis Poser, Faire évoluer ou Décommissionner ; ou je choisis un attaquant, puis sa cible (composant ou SI) ; enfin, je finis mon tour ; - le **journal** (`role="log"`) raconte chaque événement en français, ligne par ligne. Il s'affiche d'un coup avec `prefers-reduced-motion`, reste toujours dans l'ordre et ne prend jamais de retard ; - en **fin de partie**, l'écran annonce victoire, défaite ou nulle, avec le SLA final. author: lukekim
body:
## 📝 Summary

Upgrades local inference to `spiceai/mistral.rs` `ea48c06b`, the upstream v0.9.4 re-cut that merged as spiceai/mistral.rs#47. It also moves the workspace's `spiceai/candle` to `3af9fcd7` (spiceai/candle#18), the revision mistral.rs v0.9.4 builds against, so the workspace and mistral.rs resolve one candle. Together they add GGUF loaders for **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next** (`qwen4exp`), **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017** (`deepseek41`) and **GLM-5.3-Flash** (`glm5-next`).

Local models also now honor two request fields they used to ignore:

- **`max_tokens`.** A chat completion read only `max_completion_tokens`, so a request that set its limit with `max_tokens` had no limit. Many OpenAI clients and examples still send that field. The limit now comes from `max_completion_tokens` when it is set, and falls back to `max_tokens` otherwise. This is the rule `bedrock/chat/mod.rs` and `openai/responses_adapter.rs` already follow.
- **`reasoning_effort`** (#15272). Spice accepted it on chat completions, on `/v1/decisions` and as a model `params` default, then dropped it for local models. It now reaches the chat template. A value the template can't honor is refused (see the notes below).

Files:

- `crates/llms/src/chat/mistral.rs`:
  - `max_tokens`: `completion_limit`.
  - `reasoning_effort`: the mapping, plus the template check in `from_pipeline`.
  - The request and loader fields v0.9.4 added: `seed`, `queued_at`, `adapter`, `ignore_eos`, `video_preprocessor_config`, the scheduler batch limits, and model paths as `&dyn ModelPaths`.
- `crates/llms/src/chat/mod.rs` and `crates/runtime/src/model/chat.rs` pass each local model's name and its `reasoning_effort` default to the loader.
- `crates/llms/Cargo.toml` moves `mistralrs` / `mistralrs-core` from `2d15d171` to `ea48c06b`. The root `Cargo.toml` moves every `candle-*` pin from `efbb9a72` to `3af9fcd7`.
- `docs/dev/fork_patches.md`: I re-audited both forks against their new revisions. Every existing patch row is still present:
  - routed i-quant expert expansion;
  - the candle re-pointing;
  - the i-quant and MXFP4 kernels;
  - the `moe_gemm_wmma` rename;
  - the A10G flash-attention fix.

  Six new `mistral.rs` rows are added, all **GAP**: the ring all-reduce rotation, the three GGUF graphs, Jinja loop controls, the chat-template thinking default, the GGUF end-of-turn tokens, and single-node and queued requests in a `distributed` build. `scripts/check_fork_patches.py` passes: "30 pinned forks, all recorded".

## 🔗 Related

- spiceai/candle#18 merged as `3af9fcd7`; it contains spiceai/candle#17.
- spiceai/mistral.rs#47 merged as `ea48c06b`.
- #15269 was reviewed separately and squash-merged into this branch as `6d5c981c`.
- #15272 is the Enhancement for the thinking default and `reasoning_effort`, with PM/Design and DX/UX sign-off.
- #12371 asks for DeepSeek-V4 (`deepseek4`, the 0731 checkpoint). This PR adds `deepseek41` (V4.1-Flash-1017), a different graph, and does not close it.

## 👀 Notes for Reviewers

### Behavior changes

1. **`max_tokens` truncates.** A client that sends a small `max_tokens` to a local model now gets a truncated answer (`finish_reason: "length"`). Before, it got the whole answer. That is what the field is documented to do, and what every other provider in `llms` already does.
2. **An unset request uses the template's own thinking default** (#15272, from spiceai/mistral.rs#47). When a request doesn't set `reasoning_effort`, the model's chat template decides whether it reasons. This matches Hugging Face transformers. Before, mistral.rs rendered every template with thinking on.
   - **Now answer directly by default:** DeepSeek-V4.1 and Gemma 4, whose templates think only on request.
   - **Still think by default:** Qwen3, and GLM-5.3, whose template always thinks.
3. **`reasoning_effort` overrides that default** (#15272), per request or as the model's `params` default. `none` turns reasoning off, `minimal` asks for `low`, and the other levels pass through by name.

Some templates can't honor a value, and forwarding it as-is would invert the request:
- GLM-5.3-Flash takes only `low` and `high`, and renders anything else, `none` included, as `Reasoning Effort: Max`.
- gpt-oss ignores `enable_thinking` and reasons at `medium`.

So `from_pipeline` renders the generation prompt with reasoning off, with nothing set, and at each level, using the pipeline's own processor before the engine starts. Two cases are refused with HTTP 400, and a `params` default that can't take effect fails the load with the same message:
- `none` on a model that always reasons:

  ```text
  Model 'glm-5.3-flash' always reasons, so `reasoning_effort: none` can't turn reasoning off. Omit `reasoning_effort`, or set 'low' for the least reasoning. See: https://spiceai.org/docs/components/models
  ```
- a level that a template naming its levels doesn't name:

  ```text
  Model 'glm-5.3-flash' takes `reasoning_effort` 'low' or 'high', and ignores 'medium'. Set 'low' or 'high', or omit `reasoning_effort` for the model's default. See: https://spiceai.org/docs/components/models
  ```

A template with no reasoning control, such as Llama 3's, or one that fails to render, is left unchecked.

### Also from the fork

- Generation stops on a GGUF's declared `eot_token_id` and `eom_token_id`; GLM-5.3 ends its turn with `<|user|>`.
- Chat templates may use Jinja loop controls (`minijinja` 2.20 with `loop_controls`).

### Lock changes, kept minimal

Re-resolving also moved nine unrelated packages, all of them downgrades, and I restored those blocks verbatim from trunk's lock. `cargo metadata --locked` exits 0. What remains:
- the mistral.rs crates and the candle stack;
- `cudarc` 0.19.8 → 0.19.10 (candle needs `^0.19.10`);
- `cudaforge` 0.1.5 → 0.1.6 (pinned exactly by mistral.rs);
- `regex-automata` 0.4.14 → 0.4.16 (needed by candle-transformers' `fancy-regex` 0.19);
- new: `daachorse`, `fancy-regex` 0.17, `metrics` 0.24.6, `tokenizers` 0.23.2;
- removed: the old candle stack's own dependencies (`candle-ug`, `ug*`, `gemm` 0.18, `metal` 0.29, `cudarc` 0.17.8, `tokenizers` 0.22.2).

### Local embeddings are bit-identical across the candle change

I embedded the same 4 texts with `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` and `e5-small-v2` through the `TeiEmbed` in `llms`, on CPU (macOS, `--features local_embed`). I ran once at `51e14054` (candle `efbb9a72`) and once at `c43cb109` (candle `3af9fcd7`, the candle this head pins). All 8 vectors of 384 dimensions matched exactly:

```text
sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 text0: dims=384 bit_identical=True max_abs_diff=0.000e+00 cosine=1.000000000
…
intfloat/e5-small-v2 text3: dims=384 bit_identical=True max_abs_diff=0.000e+00 cosine=1.000000000
worst max_abs_diff=0.000e+00
```

The harness was a throwaway example and isn't part of this PR. I didn't compare the CUDA or Metal kernels. The ledger's TEI pooling GAP row stays open: this compares two candles, not Spice against a reference implementation.

### Evidence: `max_tokens`, on `spiced` serving a real model

The rig was spark-2d2c (DGX Spark GB10), single node, on 2026-10-18. The model was `mradermacher/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF` revision `68d514cd9f411c9d6b62f8a422102a202d57c18c`, file `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.Q2_K.gguf` (80,447,449,600 bytes). Both arms used the same model file, node and request:

```sh
curl -sS http://192.168.1.102:8090/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"qwen3.8-flash-next","temperature":0,"max_tokens":5,
       "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Count from 1 to 20, separated by commas."}]}'
```

| `spiced` build (enterprise CUDA, aarch64) | `usage` | `finish_reason` | content |
|---|---|---|---|
| before: sha256 `5f4fa81bc278…` (reads `max_completion_tokens` only) | `prompt 65, completion 306` | `stop` | `1, 2, 3, …, 20` (after 677 characters of reasoning) |
| after: sha256 `a41c26090f07…` (the `max_tokens` fallback) | `prompt 25, completion 5` | `length` | `1, 2,` |

author: mtlsnkai
body:
Characters' API calls fail on main: `api_call` is rejected with `not_logged_in` (e.g. `pull_mail`). The game's `api_call` goes through jQuery's `$.ajax`, which in caracAL runs on jsdom's XMLHttpRequest, and jsdom's page has no session cookie to send.

This gives each character a cookie jar, shared by its game page and its CODE's runner page (like a browser's tabs), with the session's `auth` cookie for the game's site. The game's own requests to its site are then logged in as they are in a browser: `api_call`, and `require_code` loading a slot.

It leaves the game's `api_call` itself alone, so caracAL doesn't have to follow changes to it. (thmsn's fork solves the same problem by reimplementing `api_call` in caracAL, in 19481f9; this fixes the missing cookie instead.)

The page's own `servers_and_characters` polling stays filtered (the coordinator polls it once for all characters). Now that the page is logged in, that filter also keeps the page from adding about 12 API calls a minute per character.

Tested (Node 24.13.1, Linux):
- jsdom with a cookie jar sends the `auth` cookie on the same `$.ajax` call the game's `api_call` makes, and sends none without it (offline, against a local test server).
- Live (MtlSnkRan on EU IV): `pull_mail` resolves (on main without this change it is rejected with `not_logged_in`); an invalid method is still rejected with `{failed: true, reason: "invalid_call"}`.

SYNTHETIC-DATA REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION. This is not CDF production.

Before: Administration showed only to user and role administrators, and its link always opened the user register. Since 2045 the database has listed Administration for every business administrator, but the application's floor hid it until its pages shipped, so the GRC Directors and the Compliance Section Manager had no Administration at all, and the committee, sector, notification, export-policy, corrective-action-policy and calendar registers had no page.

After: Administration shows wherever the caller's permissions open one of its pages, and its link opens the caller's first page; each page lists the caller's others. Six registers are read on their own pages, read only: the committees, the sectors, the notification rules, the export policy, the corrective-action policy and the business calendar. The calendar's administrator also adds a day (a holiday, a non-working day, or a working day on a weekend) and changes the working week from a later date, each asked first. Anyone else gets the same 404 as a page that does not exist. Arabic and English, from a 320 px phone to the desktop. No migration.

How:

- **The area (gap G1 of the P12-8 domain map).** The floor is now the pages themselves: `adminViews` in `@cdf/authorization`, in the order `api.my_areas` picks the area's default view. The export policy counts only where `authz.is_export_policy_admin` would allow it (DEC-F24), the gate 2045 already applies, so the floor can still only remove an area the database lists. `/admin` and the area's link open the database's default view; each page lists the caller's other pages, from `can()` until P12-8b gives the list from the database (F3).
- **One database check before anything shows.** Each page first asks the database for the caller check every command of its register starts with (`authz.has_permission`, or `authz.is_export_policy_admin` for the export policy). A caller without it gets the uniform 404, recorded as `ACCESS_DENIED` with the page's name only. A page the application pre-check would let through is still refused by the database (integration test).
- **Registers read past nothing (F2).** Each register is read in the caller's security context from tables whose row-level security returns exactly what that administrator keeps, with `api.authority_rule_coverage` and `api.export_approval_config_warnings` (2030, 2040). No table, policy or grant changes. A register carries ids, codes, dates, the reasons administrators wrote and names from the directory; never case content or a count derived from cases (§21), and every page says so. So a seat correction is read without the number of proceeding snapshots 2090 records with it, although row-level security would return it to `COMMITTEE_ADMIN`, and a static guard pins every table the registers read. Reading a register records nothing.
- **What each register shows.**
  - Committees (`COMMITTEE_ADMIN`): each committee's seats, in office, starting later and ended, with who appointed and ended them; seat corrections (AMB-045) beside the seat; every rule-set version with its source; the independent conflict authorities (DEC-F04); status changes; and which recommendation kinds have an authority rule in force. The rules list is now one component, shared with the committee page.
  - Sectors (`SECTOR_ADMIN`): sectors, positions and referral-approval delegations, revoked ones kept; the delegation limit is SOURCE_REQUIRED.
  - Notification rules (`NOTIFICATION_ADMIN`): what each notice does now on each channel (always for a mandatory rule, else the event rule in force, else no rule), changes that start later, committee defaults and ended rules.
  - Export policy (`authz.is_export_policy_admin`): approval rules with their source, purposes with legacy ones marked, approved external domains (SOURCE_REQUIRED), approver pools per stage and the configuration warnings (ids, stages and counts).
  - Corrective-action policy (`CORRECTIVE_ACTION_POLICY_ADMIN`; DEC-F25 to F27): each action type's due date, reminders, overdue notice and escalation, version by version, with an empty setting said as what the reminder job does with it; the kinds of evidence; the pools.
  - Business calendar (`BUSINESS_CALENDAR_ADMIN`; DEC-F02): the calendar's source (SOURCE_REQUIRED), every working-week version and every dated day, upcoming first, past and withdrawn ones kept.
- **Periods and sources.** Whether a row is in force, starts later or has ended is judged by the database's clock with `effective_to` exclusive. A governed value says whether it is the owner default, provisional awaiting the CDF source, or approved; a provisional one never reads as configured, and a value nobody has set says so, never a guess.
- **The calendar's two forms (F1, F4).** Each shows only where its command's own caller check, `authz.has_permission('BUSINESS_CALENDAR_ADMIN')`, passes when asked of the database. The service validates with the shared Zod schema, pre-checks the permission and runs `api.set_business_calendar_day` or `api.set_business_week_pattern` in the caller's context; every other check is the command's, on submit, and its refusal shows in the calendar's own words (a date that already has an entry, a week that does not start after the last version, a date in the past, no working day left). A new week starts at the beginning of its date in Riyadh and always records SOURCE_REQUIRED, since the form sends no source. Each confirmation says that a due date already set does not move and that no one is sent a message.
- **Also in the first commit.** AGENT-09's optional note on #109: the comment in `tests/e2e/security-csrf.spec.ts` now names the export preview as the second GET route with a side effect. The Rebase thread's correction to ADR-056: CDF-226 is fixed in 2117, not 2120.

## Change report (protocol §89)

- **Requirement / ADR:** ADR-051's P12-8a amendment; requirement CDF-UX-026 (new) and CDF-UX-005 (the shell); SECURITY_RULES §23 (new); Phase 12 plan §4 (P12-8); the P12-8 domain map's gap G1 and forks F1 to F13 (coordinator, 2026-10-18 12:27); DEC-F02, DEC-F04, DEC-F24, DEC-F25 to F27, AMB-045; UX-004, UX-028, UX-116.
- **Migrations added (Database Changes):** none.
- **Security controls affected (Security Impact):** no database control changes. The application floor for Administration widens to the pages the caller's permissions open, which `api.my_areas` (2045) already lists; it can still only remove an area. Six read-only pages and one server-action file, each through the administration service and the database's own checks. **RLS Impact:** none; the registers rely on the existing policies.
- **Access control enforced at:**
  - **Database:** each page's caller check (`authz.has_permission`, `authz.is_export_policy_admin`) before any read; row-level security on every register table; the two calendar commands decide every input again.
  - **Application:** `adminViews` pre-checks which pages open; the service validates with the shared schema, pre-checks `BUSINESS_CALENDAR_ADMIN` and records refusals. A form shows only where the database says its caller check passes.
- **Audit events created:** `ACCESS_DENIED` (a refused page, with the page's name only) and `COMMAND_DENIED` (a refused calendar command, with the command and outcome only), both SECURITY with the request id. The commands still write `BUSINESS_CALENDAR_DAY_SET` and `BUSINESS_WEEK_PATTERN_CHANGED` in their transactions, unchanged.
- **Privacy/Data Impact:** synthetic data only. No case content on any register; names come from the directory under its own row-level secu

author: marcioapm
body:
# lux: agent Runs park after an idle timeout

Agent-adapter Runs can now be parked instead of failing after they finish a turn. `workload.idleTimeout` stops a Run gracefully when it has been idle for the configured period and has no pending input. The Run is stopped, snapshotted and resumable; the stop reason is `idle`.

## Behaviour
- Valid for `acp`, `claude-code`, `codex` and `opencode` adapters. Generic workloads are rejected when they set it.
- Values are from 1 minute through 24 hours. Unset or zero disables it. `lux run --idle-timeout` overrides the spec.
- Busy activity, new input and a new placement reset the clock.
- Content-free interrupts move the clock but are not pending input. Interrupts with text or attachments remain pending until handled.
- Receipt-free deliveries settle at the following activity event, including short turns whose delivery record arrives after the idle event.
- Events and `stageReason: idle` distinguish this from a manual stop. The Run remains resumable; the existing total `timeout` still fails a Run.
- The reaper query is scoped to each candidate Run's current epoch and indexed event history rather than rescanning the entire event table.

## Verification
- Review loop: performance, code quality and test quality reviewers; R1 found the pending-input correctness defects and the per-tick query regression; R2 approved all fixes; final delta review approved performance, quality and tests.
- All requested mutation checks were killed by tests and restored.
- Rebased onto `main` at `8d719e77`.
- `gofmt`, `GOOS=linux go vet ./...`, OpenAPI comparison and diff guard: pass.
- Focused race server tests: 78 cases/subtests, 0 failures/skips; spec/CLI race tests: pass.
- Idle e2e: 4 passed, 3 skipped for missing real-agent API keys, 62 deselected.
- The idle reaper benchmark improved from 2.48s to 0.218s for 50 Runs × 1000 turns.

author: johncarl-30
body:
## Bug
`redactText` runs on every span attribute before export. A digit run of 9 to 13 digits counts as a phone number, and dashes count as separators, so a UUID whose middle groups are all digits loses them:

```
799ab1d1-7348-4105-9648-4d005768a7e6  ->  799ab1d1-[phone]-4d005768a7e6
```

Conversation ids are UUIDs and become `session.id`, so some Langfuse sessions got a mangled id that doesn't match the conversation. It also made `src/lib/langfuse-trace.test.ts` fail about 1 run in 10, depending on the random id. Found while working on #25.

## Fix
The digit-run regex now also matches a whole UUID as an alternative. When the UUID branch matches, the replacer keeps the text unchanged. Phone, card and email redaction are untouched.

## Tests
- A new `redact.test.ts` case covers digit-heavy, all-digit-middle and uppercase UUIDs, plus a UUID and a phone number in the same string. It fails without the fix and passes with it.
- `langfuse-trace.test.ts` passed 40 out of 40 runs. Before the fix it failed about 1 run in 10.
- `npm test`: 49 pass. `eslint` and `tsc --noEmit` are clean.

author: anarzone
body:
Refs EXP-113 · Work Log: https://docs.anar.to/books/work-log/page/exp-113-record-composer-runs-and-llm-calls-and-strip-identifying-fields-from-the-ranker-payload

## Why

- Composer slots kept no scores, ranker mode or candidate pool. LLM rankings lived only in a 10-minute cache, and token use only in a rate-limited log line, so there was no cost or fallback rate per feature and no way to compare LLM on and off.
- The ranker payload sent **exact travel minutes to up to 40 named places** (enough to triangulate the user), **companions**, and **affinities derived from immigration situation and a child's birth date**.

## What changes

**Privacy (ranker payload, `AnthropicCandidateRanker`):**

- `travel_minutes_from_origin` → `travel_band` (`≤10`, `≤20`, `≤30`, `≤45`, `>45`).
- `companions` is no longer in the request facts.
- `category_affinities` (from `CategoryAffinity`/`planAffinity`: situation and kids) is no longer sent. Only the behavioural `category_intent` / `category_dislikes` are. They still steer the deterministic scorer locally.
- `PROMPT_VERSION = 'rank-2026-10-18'` marks the new payload shape.

**Telemetry (new migration `2026_10_18_140000_create_llm_calls_and_composer_runs_tables`):**

| Table | One row per | Holds | Doesn't hold |
|---|---|---|---|
| `llm_calls` | LLM call: composer ranker, event classifier, event translation chunks, prompt parser | feature, model, prompt version, input/output tokens, latency, outcome (`success`, `fallback:<reason>`, `error:<class>`), `cost_usd` | any user link, prompt or response text |
| `composer_runs` | Composer plan | user (cascade-deleted with the account), ranker mode (`llm` / `llm_fallback` / `llm_disabled` / `bucket_off`), LLM bucket, candidate count, slot count, and per slot `{type, category, score, llm_rank}` | place or event ids |

- `cost_usd` is computed **only** from prices in `services.llm_pricing`, which is empty: I didn't want to guess prices. Unpriced calls record null; add the models' current prices to fill it.
- `SlotFiller::pickedScores()` exposes the score each greedily placed candidate won with.
- **Per-user LLM bucket**: `LlmRollout::allows($user, 'composer_llm')` is a stable crc32 bucket against `services.composer_llm.rollout_percent` (`COMPOSER_LLM_ROLLOUT_PERCENT`, **default 100**, so nothing changes until you lower it). An out-of-bucket user gets the deterministic ranker, and no LLM call is made.

## Pending decisions not pre-empted

- **Retention (EXP-117)**: neither table is pruned yet. Both have a `created_at` index ready for a prune job, and `composer_runs` already disappears with the account.
- **Event log (EXP-110)**: `composer_runs` is ranking telemetry, not the interaction/impression log. It holds no place ids and no user actions.
- **EU residency (EXP-118)**: this PR only reduces what leaves. Whether the ranker may run at all is still your call (it's off by default: `COMPOSER_LLM_ENABLED=false`).

## Checks (CI doesn't run on PRs into launch)

- **New privacy test**: *the ranker payload leaves out companions, situation-derived affinities and exact travel minutes* (asserts on the decoded outgoing request).
- Two existing ranker tests are updated to the new contract: the cache varies with `category_intent`, and grounding asserts `travel_band`.
- Pest: `tests/Feature/Composer tests/Feature/Events tests/Unit tests/Feature/Home`: **580 passed**.
- Pre-commit fast suite: **1812 passed, 1 skipped**.
- Throwaway checks (deleted, not committed), 2/2:
  - a success logs tokens, prompt version and a cost from configured prices;
  - a fallback logs a null cost, and `llm_calls` has no `user_id`;
  - the bucket is stable, and 0% makes **no** LLM request;
  - `/composer/compose` records a `bucket_off` run whose slots carry only type/category/score/llm_rank (no ids);
  - deleting the user deletes their runs.
- The migration rolls back and re-applies cleanly.
- Merges cleanly with #79, #68, #81, #76 and #78.
- No frontend files changed.

author: liblit
body:
Previously the build logic included four ad hoc tasks with `outputs.cacheIf { true }`. That's rather opaque: each predicate merely asserted that a task may be cached, without saying why, and offered nowhere to record why caching must not happen. Where caching is still not allowed, the `because` parameter to a `@DisableCachingByDefault` annotation now explains why.

`Exec` and `JavaExec` carry Gradle's own `@DisableCachingByDefault`, so making such a task cacheable requires a new task type. The `NpxTask` that the Node plugin supplies carries no cacheability annotation at all, so a task of ours built on it is cacheable by default and needs a type in order to opt out. Declaring tasks is good design even for tasks that are only used once: a type is where a task's contract, and what it knows about the tool it drives, are made explicit. Named task types could also eventually be exercised in unit tests, though we haven't added those yet.

Given the above motivations, `build-logic` gains three new task types, along with the Node-plugin dependency that lets `LintMarkdown` extend `NpxTask`. `@CacheableTask GenerateHelloHashJar` compiles `core:generateHelloHashJar`, copying the source, running the compiler, and checking the JAR in one task action. `@CacheableTask InstallAndroidSdk` installs `dalvik:installAndroidSdk`. `@DisableCachingByDefault(...) LintMarkdown` covers the root `lintMarkdown`, whose stamp records only that the linter ran. The fourth of the four, `cast:java:ecj:run`, keeps the task the `application` plugin gives it and simply loses its predicate, falling back to the annotation `JavaExec` already carries.

The scripts now name only where their inputs come from. `dalvik` combines the installed platform with the catalog version through `Provider.zip` when it locates `android.jar`, and the root script says nothing about `lintMarkdown` at all, the type naming the Markdown files it reads. `core` drops the injected-services interface it had been feeding the OCaml compiler, which now injects what it needs itself, and `OCAMLLIB` joins the project dictionary.

author: inglessemroteiro
body:
A maior peça que faltava no sistema. Ela entra em **duas camadas, e a separação entre elas é o ponto.**

O **syllabus** é da escola: por nível e por ciclo, as sessões do projeto, cada uma com objetivo, etapas, palavras e homework. É o que está nos guias do professor, e é igual para todas as turmas daquele nível.

O **plano** é da turma: começa como a sessão do syllabus e a professora ajusta — tira uma etapa que não cabe, muda o tempo, reordena, acrescenta a dela. Depois marca pronta e publica.

**O plano só passa a existir no armazenamento quando ela mexe nele.** Enquanto não mexe, a tela lê o syllabus direto. Isso resolve as duas coisas ao mesmo tempo: uma correção no syllabus alcança as turmas que ainda não ajustaram nada, e **não desfaz o ajuste de quem já mexeu** — que seria apagar o trabalho dela.

## As fases são as da ISR, não as do protótipo

O v5 mostrava `warm-up / listen / learn / practice / mission`. Lendo os guias de verdade, isso era dado de mentira do desenho: todo guia organiza a sessão em **Warm-up · Minds On · Language Focus · Hands On · Share Out · Wrap-up**, e a reflexão roda sempre no Wrap-up. É com essas seis que o sistema trabalha, e uma sessão nova nasce com as seis já postas.

## Duas regras que ficaram no código

- **Etapa do syllabus se desmarca, não se apaga.** Apagar daria à professora o poder de sumir com o que a escola planejou; desmarcar já resolve o caso dela ("não cabe nesta turma"), e a etapa continua à vista, riscada, para ela ver o que tirou. A atividade que ela mesma acrescentou, essa sim se apaga.
- **Roteiro sem nenhuma etapa marcada não publica.** Publicar uma aula vazia seria mandar a aluna abrir uma página em branco.

**Aula publicada continua editável, com o aviso à vista.** Não há versão guardada: o que ela mudar depois de publicar, a aluna vê na hora, e a tela diz isso em vez de fingir que existe um rascunho separado.

## A tela

Na Turma, a aba **Plano das aulas** entra entre Alunas e Chamadas: a tira das sessões do ciclo em cima com o estado de cada uma, e a sessão escolhida aberta embaixo — selo do estado, de onde o roteiro veio (igual ao syllabus, ajustado, ou com N atividades suas), porta para o guia do professor, o objetivo, o roteiro com o tempo somado, as palavras e o homework.

Turma de um nível cujo syllabus ainda não tem sessões diz isso, em vez de ficar vazia.

## Fica de fora, nomeado

- **A aula publicada ainda não chega ao caderno da aluna.** Para ligar uma aula a uma sessão falta a chamada guardar **qual sessão foi dada** — hoje ela guarda o tópico, não o número. É a próxima peça, e é pequena.
- **O conteúdo dos guias não está dentro do sistema.** Os títulos e os objetivos das dez sessões de cada nível continuam só nos documentos; o syllabus começa vazio e a tela diz isso em vez de inventar sessões.

## Testes

Duas suítes novas, 59 asserções.

`test-plano-motor.js` (25) guarda o motor sem tela: as seis fases são as dos guias; enquanto a professora não mexe a turma lê o syllabus e uma correção da escola a alcança; quando ela mexe o plano vira dela e o syllabus não a desfaz; etapa do syllabus não se apaga e a dela sim; desmarcar tira o tempo do total; roteiro vazio não publica; o planejamento entra na cópia de tudo.

`test-plano-tela.js` (34) guarda a tela: a tira com o estado de cada sessão, etapa sem descrição mostrando fase e tempo em vez de "sem título" seis vezes, **Ajustar devolvendo aos campos o que já estava gravado** (sem isso, ajustar e salvar em seguida apagava as palavras e o homework), acrescentar/desmarcar/reordenar/apagar pela tela, pronta → publicada, e o aviso ao reabrir uma aula publicada.

Rodados e verdes: `test-turmas-v5` (26), `test-porte-completo` (44), `test-painel-abas` (49), `test-aluna-caderno` (29), `test-historico-chamada` (15), `test-isr-dados` (6), `test-chamada-corrigir`. Verificadores de jargão, linguagem, nomes e identidade sem novidade; componentes em 96% (773 de 802), com os mesmos 29 escritos à mão de antes — os 24 elementos novos todos tomaram as classes do componente.

author: allanm-dev
body:
## Résumé
La quête « Les morts de Brumeval » passait directement de la maire à la crypte. Elle comporte maintenant une **enquête obligatoire** qui utilise les nouveaux quartiers du village :
1. **Josette, la meunière** (dans le moulin, à l'est de la rivière) : elle a perdu pelle et lanterne et a vu une silhouette gagner le cimetière ; un test de Perception sur la cour révèle des traces de bottes (indice `indice-moulin`).
2. **Hugues, le fermier** (dans sa ferme) : un loup décime ses poules ; il demande d'abattre le loup de la forêt (l'ennemi existant `wolf-1`) puis donne 10 pièces d'or et un indice : quelqu'un creuse la nuit au cimetière (`indice-ferme`).
3. **La tombe éventrée au cimetière** (nouveau lieu, au sud) : un **pillard de tombes** (nouveau monstre de carte `bandit-1`, rencontre « pillard ») a creusé un tunnel sous la crypte et fendu le sceau. On le combat, ou on le fait se rendre (Intimidation) ; dans les deux cas on récupère le **pendentif d'argent** de Gédéon (nouvel objet de quête). Le tunnel se visite.
4. La **porte de la crypte** ne s'ouvre qu'une fois les trois pistes suivies (la scène dit ce qu'il manque) ; ensuite la quête continue comme avant.
5. **Thibaud** reconnaît le pendentif, donne 25 pièces d'or ; Odile et la scène finale en tiennent compte. Odile, au fil de la quête, rappelle quelles pistes restent à suivre.

Détails : nouveaux lieux de carte `meuniere`, `fermier` (avec « ! » sur la porte) et `tombe`, l'habitante Josette et le fermier Hugues passent du décor aux personnages de l'histoire, 12 scènes ajoutées (`stories.ts`), objet `pendentif-gedeon`.

## Vérification
- [x] `npm test` (424), `npm run typecheck` et `npm run build` passent
- [x] Tests de l'aventure mis à jour : parcours pacifique complet (traces, loup, pillard qui se rend, clé, journal, prière, pendentif rendu, fin chez la maire : 85 pièces d'or au total), refus de la porte sans enquête, pillard affronté ou intimidé, fermier qui attend la mort du loup
- [x] Navigateur mobile : le pillard sort du cimetière et poursuit le héros (« Bandit vous poursuit ! »), la porte de la crypte réclame l'enquête

## Page Aide
- [x] « Suivre l'histoire » (déroulé en trois temps) ; fiche de l'objet dans Aide → Objets

## Limites connues
- Un personnage déjà au milieu de la quête, la porte de la crypte encore fermée, doit faire l'enquête (les personnages qui ont déjà ouvert la crypte ne sont pas concernés).
- Si le pillard prend la fuite (il est lâche et tireur), il disparaît de la carte sans laisser le pendentif : seul bonus perdu, la porte s'ouvre quand même.
- Pas de journal de quête dans l'application : les rappels se font par Odile et par la porte.
